# Decision log

One entry per architectural choice. Newest first. Add an entry whenever a new choice is
made; never rewrite an old one — supersede it with a new entry that links back.

Format: date, decision, reason, alternatives rejected.

---

## 2026-10-16 — W7.1 (#80): the Worker installer. One PowerShell 7 script, `tools/worker-install/Install-RestoreProofWorker.ps1`, run elevated on the Veeam server from the unpacked release package, copies `rpworker.exe` and its DLLs to `%ProgramFiles%\RestoreProof\`, makes `%ProgramData%\RestoreProof` and its six folders with the ACLs this entry fixes (the service account `NT SERVICE\RestoreProof` by its SID, `Users` nothing), asks for the Cloud URL, the install token, the Veeam URL and the Veeam account alone, writes `config.json`, fills the vault through `rpworker vault set` on stdin, makes the signing key with a new `rpworker signer new-key` and the Graph certificate with W7.0's script, grants the account the vault's Read entry and the Read ACE on every organisation certificate's key file (`rpworker veeam list` prints the thumbprints), runs `service install`, `cloud register` and `service start`, and prints the Worker's id; every step reads, compares and writes only what differs, so a stopped run is continued by running it again; the MSI (WiX) and code signing wait for a pilot and the certificate; one PR, `Closes #80` (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written on 2026-10-16: the package `0.1.0`, the certificate after the first pilot, the VM and the laptop for the Done-when, `Users` with no access, a machine without Veeam asked not refused, `tools/worker-install/`, the two Worker changes)

W7.1 (#80) is the installer. Done when, as the issue says: "The MSI installs on a clean Windows Server 2022 VM and the service registers within 2 minutes." This entry works from issue #80 and its two comments (2026-09-29 and W4.12's), the W4.3, W4.5, W4.6, W4.7, W4.8, W4.10, W4.11, W4.12, W5.1 and W7.0 entries and their Open points that name W7.1, the W5.1 code review (finding 10), `docs/worker-config.md`, `docs/tenant-setup.md`, `docs/onboarding.md`, `docs/environment.md`, the W4.8 and W5.1 live harnesses (which do by hand what the installer must do), and the code. No code is written yet; the build notes will record what the build finds. Out of scope and not built here: upgrades (W7.3), uninstall (W7.4), `rpworker doctor` (W7.2), the install guide (Q7.2), a silent or RMM-driven install, the MSI, the event source, alerts.

**The issue was written before W4.5 to W7.0; where it and the code disagree, the code wins.** Each such place:

- *"a first-run wizard (`rpworker setup`, a console prompt sequence)"*: there is no `rpworker setup` and none is added; the prompt sequence is the script's, and every answer goes where the Worker already takes it (`config.json`, `rpworker vault set`). A C++ wizard would duplicate in C++ what is one `icacls` line or one existing command in PowerShell, and could not be tested without touching the SCM.
- *"asks for ... Graph tenant id, client id, secret, test mailbox and location ids"*: none of these is asked. The Worker signs in to Graph with one certificate per Worker and never a secret (W1.5; W7.0's `New-WorkerGraphCertificate.ps1`), and a client's tenant, app id, mailbox and target ids are the client's profile, which the Cloud sends in every job (W4.10, W4.11) from the connector `manage.py create-connector` made of the profile W7.0's tenant script printed. The installer knows no client.
- *"Veeam URL and restore-operator credentials"*: the Worker runs in Veeam's admin mode (2026-09-26 entry), so the account is a local Windows account with the Veeam Backup Administrator role (`DESKTOP\rp-veeam` in the lab, W1.0), not a restore operator. Making that account and giving it the role is done in Veeam's console by the MSP before the install (no cmdlet or REST call sets the role); the installer asks for its name and password and checks them with `rpworker veeam list`.
- *"generates the signing key pair"*: no `rpworker` command makes or prints a private key (W4.3 point 4: "generating it at install is W7.1's"); point 4 adds `rpworker signer new-key`, which makes it straight into the vault.
- *"writes config.json and the vault"*: the vault is written by `rpworker vault set` alone, each value on stdin (W4.5); the script never holds a vault file.
- *"registers the service"*: `rpworker service install` makes the service with its fixed name, display name, virtual account, start type and recovery actions (W4.7), and refuses one that is already there; the installer runs it and does not describe the service a second time in WiX's `ServiceInstall`.
- *"Registers with the Cloud immediately and prints the worker id"*: `rpworker cloud register` (W5.1), as built; the installer runs it itself (point 9) so the service's account never needs to write the vault.
- *"Code-sign the MSI and the exe ... order in Sprint 6"*: no certificate was ordered. Point 2 says what happens without one.
- *"Fallback: install.ps1 ... for MSPs that refuse MSIs"*: here the script is first and the MSI is the later one (point 1).
- *Done when, "on a clean Windows Server 2022 VM"*: there is no such VM; point 11.
- *Comment 1 (2026-09-29)*: "installs on the Veeam server and refuses (or warns clearly) elsewhere": it warns and asks (point 3), not refuses, because the Done-when's clean VM has no Veeam on it.
- *Comment 2 (W4.12)*: the `icacls` line for the key file, as written; "re-grant when a thumbprint changes" is a second run of the installer (point 6) until W7.2's doctor names the line.

1. **A PowerShell script first; the MSI waits for a pilot and the certificate.** `tools/worker-install/Install-RestoreProofWorker.ps1` over `RestoreProofWorker.psm1`, the shape of W7.0's tenant script: every rule a pure function in the module, the script the sequence that calls them, tested through pytest over `pwsh` against a fake `rpworker` and a temporary root. *Why:* everything the install must do is already a `rpworker` command (`service install`, `vault set`, `vault grant`, `cloud register`, `service start`) or an `icacls` line the W4.8 and W5.1 harnesses run by hand, so the installer is those in order with a check before each and an `ok:`/`change:` line after; a script is testable on this laptop without installing anything (point 10), and a step that fails leaves a readable state (point 9). An MSI would have to either re-describe the service in WiX's `ServiceInstall` (a second copy of W4.7's choices, drifting from the first) or run `rpworker` from custom actions (the part of an MSI that is hardest to test, runs as LocalSystem, and is what SmartScreen and antivirus look at first); the ACLs for a virtual account whose SID WiX can't compute need a custom action too; and building one needs the .NET SDK and WiX, neither of which is installed here (checked 2026-10-16: `dotnet` host, no SDK; no `wix`). What an MSP gets from an MSI and not from this script is named and deferred: an Add/Remove Programs entry (W7.4, with the uninstall it would point at), an in-place upgrade (W7.3), a silent `msiexec /qn` push through an RMM (out of Stage 1 unless a pilot asks; the script's prompts can become parameters then, the secrets still on stdin). *Rejected:* both at once, as the issue wants (the MSI's testing needs the VM of point 11 for every change, and nothing in it would be proven that the script doesn't prove); an MSI that wraps the script in a custom action (the worst of both); a C++ `rpworker install` (point 0's first bullet).

2. **The package and what signing costs us while we have no certificate.** `worker/tools/package.ps1` builds the `ci` preset (Release; the `dev` build is Debug, with `fmtd.dll`, `spdlogd.dll` and seven more debug DLLs beside the exe, which no customer gets) and zips `rpworker.exe`, the DLLs from its build folder, `Install-RestoreProofWorker.ps1`, `RestoreProofWorker.psm1`, a copy of `tools/tenant-setup/New-WorkerGraphCertificate.ps1` (taken at packaging; no second copy in git) and `config.example.json` as `RestoreProof-Worker-<version>.zip`, `<version>` from `rpworker --version`. The version is `0.0.0` today; whether W7.1's package is `0.1.0` is one line in `worker/CMakeLists.txt` and the owner's call. The first Release build of the vcpkg dependencies on this laptop is the build's one-time cost. **Without a code-signing certificate:** a zip downloaded with a browser carries the mark of the web and so does everything Explorer extracts from it; under Windows Server's default execution policy (`RemoteSigned`) `pwsh -File Install-RestoreProofWorker.ps1` is then refused as "not digitally signed", and the guide's first line is `Unblock-File -Recurse <folder>` (or `pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ...`). `rpworker.exe` itself is run by the script and by the SCM, neither of which goes through SmartScreen (a shell feature), so an unsigned exe installs and runs; the UAC prompt for the elevated shell is the operator's own. An unsigned MSI double-clicked from Explorer is where SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", which is why the issue tied signing to the MSI; the script has the smaller problem. When the owner buys the certificate (an OV certificate must live on a hardware token or in a signing service since 2023; Microsoft's Trusted Signing service is the cheaper alternative to a token if the organisation qualifies), `package.ps1` gains one step, `signtool sign` on the exe and the DLLs and `Set-AuthenticodeSignature` on the two scripts, and nothing in the installer changes. *Rejected:* a self-signed signing certificate (worth nothing to a machine that doesn't have it, and installing it there is a worse habit than `Unblock-File`); shipping the Debug build.

3. **What the setup asks for, and what it no longer asks.** In this order, each skipped when the thing is already there (point 9): the Cloud URL (`cloud_url`, `https://`; `-CloudCaFile` for a Cloud behind a private CA, the lab's Caddy root, written as `cloud_ca_file`: never asked, since a deployment has a public certificate); the Worker's name (`-WorkerName`, default this machine's name, `cloud register --name`); the Veeam URL (`veeam_url`, default `https://localhost:4443` when Veeam's REST service is on this machine); **Veeam's certificate** (point 5); the Veeam account's name (`veeam_username`, `MACHINE\user`) and password (`veeam_password`); the install token (`cloud_install_token`) from `manage.py create-worker-token`. The three secrets are read at the console without echo (`Read-Host -MaskInput`) and each piped into its own `rpworker vault set <name>` process on stdin, as `fill-worker-vault.ps1` and W7.0's certificate script do: never an argument, an environment variable, a file, a transcript line or a log line; the script's variables are cleared after. The signing key and the Graph certificate are made, not asked (points 4 and 7). **Not asked, and why:** the Graph tenant id, client id, secret, test mailbox and location ids (the profile comes with each job from the Cloud; the certificate replaces the secret: the second bullet above); `poll_interval_s`, `heartbeat_interval_s`, `sample_*`, `log_level`, `screenshots_enabled`, `tsa_url` (the config's defaults; the samples are the plan's, the screenshots the client's, since W4.10/W4.11); `jobs_file` (a lab's key, never written by the installer). The config written is the two URLs, `veeam_ca_file` and `veeam_cert_sha256` when pinned, `cloud_ca_file` when given, and nothing else; the eight client keys are never written (the service never reads them). **Veeam on this machine:** the Worker runs on the Veeam server (2026-09-29 entry; confirmed by W4.12). The script looks for Veeam's REST service (`Veeam.Archiver.REST.Service`) and, absent, says so and asks before going on (`-AllowRemoteVeeam` answers it), because the key-file grants of point 6 can only be made on the Veeam server, so a Worker elsewhere runs no restore until W7.2 says what to grant where; the Done-when's clean VM is such a machine (point 11). *Rejected:* refusing outright (the comment's first option; the Done-when needs the second); asking for the Veeam account's role or making the account (Veeam's console alone sets the role).

4. **The signing key: `rpworker signer new-key [--vault <file>] [--replace]`.** Makes an Ed25519 key pair in process (OpenSSL's `EVP_PKEY_keygen`, already linked for `ed25519.cpp`), stores the private half as `signing_key_base64` in the vault's one form (64 characters of Base64 of the 48-byte PKCS#8 DER, W4.3 point 3) through `write_vault` in one write, wipes its copies, and prints what `signer public-key` prints: the public PEM on stdout and `key_id <sha256>` on stderr. A vault that already holds `signing_key_base64` is refused (`signer error: the vault already holds signing_key_base64; this Worker has its key (rpworker signer public-key prints it); --replace makes a new one, after which the Cloud must be told (manage.py revoke-worker, a new install token)`), exit 1, unless `--replace`. The private half reaches no stream, no log line and no recording (the secret audit gains the case). *Why in C++ and not in the script:* PowerShell 7.4 is .NET 8, which has no Ed25519, and `openssl.exe` is not on a client's server; the key must be made on the Worker and go into the vault by the one door W4.5 defined. `signer_command` is a strict file (100% line), the keygen's real call sits in `ed25519.cpp` outside the gate as `sign` does; the lab's `python -m seeder new-signing-key` and `fill-worker-vault.ps1` stay as they are. *Rejected:* the Cloud making the key (the private half never leaves the Worker); printing the private key for the operator to `vault set` (W4.3's reason: stdout).

5. **Veeam's certificate: found, shown, confirmed, pinned.** The script opens one TLS connection to `veeam_url` with a callback that records the server's certificate and accepts the handshake (nothing is sent), and then: (a) if that certificate is in this machine's `Cert:\LocalMachine\My` with its private key, it is Veeam's own REST certificate on this server (the thumbprint Veeam's General Options show): the script writes it as `%ProgramData%\RestoreProof\veeam-rest.pem` and sets `veeam_ca_file` and `veeam_cert_sha256` (the pin, which skips only the host-name check, `docs/worker-config.md` "Veeam's default certificate"), printing subject, SHA-1 thumbprint and SHA-256; (b) if it chains to the Windows store and names the host, nothing is set (the store is trusted); (c) otherwise (Veeam elsewhere, `-AllowRemoteVeeam`) it prints subject, thumbprint and SHA-256 and asks the operator to confirm the thumbprint against the Veeam console before pinning (`-VeeamCertificateFile <pem>` gives the certificate by hand and skips the question). Then `rpworker veeam list` runs (point 6): the pin, the URL and the account are proven together before anything is installed, and its one line is the script's error when they aren't. *Rejected:* asking the operator to paste a SHA-256 (the four-step recipe in `docs/worker-config.md` stays for the by-hand case); trusting the first certificate seen from a remote Veeam without a word (a pin taken blind is no pin).

6. **The organisation certificates' key files, and the renewal story.** `rpworker veeam list` gains a column, `APP CERTIFICATE`, the organisation's `applicationCertificateThumbprint` (already parsed into `Organization::certificate_thumbprint`, never printed; a small change under Catch2 with the recorded fixtures). The script reads the thumbprints from it, resolves each certificate in `LocalMachine\My` to its private key file (`UniqueKeyContainerName` under `%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Crypto\RSA\MachineKeys\` for a CAPI key, `Key.UniqueName` under `%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Crypto\Keys\` for a CNG key, as the W4.8 harness's `Get-W48KeyFile` does) and grants `icacls "<key file>" /grant "*<service SID>:(R)"`, one `ok:`/`change:` line per organisation. A thumbprint with no certificate or no key file on this machine is one `problem:` line naming the organisation and the thumbprint, and the install goes on (that organisation's restores will be `error` until it is fixed; the Worker's message names it, W4.12). **Renewal:** when Veeam gets a new certificate for an organisation the key is a new file with the default ACL and the next run of that organisation ends `error` (W4.12 point 4); the fix is to run the installer again, which grants what is missing and changes nothing else, until W7.2's doctor prints the exact line. A certificate Veeam no longer uses keeps its ACE (nothing is revoked here; W7.4). *Rejected:* granting Read on every key file under `MachineKeys` (Veeam's REST and operator-auth keys are among them, wider than the one ACE the account needs); reading Veeam's PowerShell module from the script (its load needs pwsh and Veeam's own cmdlets, and the Worker's REST access already answers the question with the credentials it has to have).

7. **The ACLs, as `icacls` lines.** `$R = "$env:ProgramData\RestoreProof"`; `$S` is the service's SID (point 8), written `*S-1-5-80-...` as `icacls` takes a SID; SYSTEM is `*S-1-5-18` and Administrators `*S-1-5-32-544` (by SID, so a localised Windows needs no name). Each line is run only when the state read back differs, and read back after.

   | Path | Line | Why |
   |---|---|---|
   | `$R` | `icacls $R /inheritance:r /grant "*S-1-5-18:(OI)(CI)F" "*S-1-5-32-544:(OI)(CI)F" "${S}:(OI)(CI)RX"` | The inherited `Users:(CI)(WD,AD,WEA,WA)` and `CREATOR OWNER` entries go: no local user can create, own or read anything under it (W4.5, W4.7, W4.8 and W5.1 Open). The service reads `config.json`, the two PEM files and `canaries\<tenant>.json` beside it through the inherited RX and can create nothing at the root. |
   | `$R\state`, `$R\runs`, `$R\outbox`, `$R\sent`, `$R\failed`, `$R\logs` | `icacls "$R\<name>" /grant "${S}:(OI)(CI)M"` | Made by the installer (Administrators' by owner), each with Modify for the account: the loop's records, marks and kept jobs (W4.8; the owner rule still holds a planted file to SYSTEM, Administrators or the account), the run folders, the outbox's three (W4.6; W5.1's `failed\` listable, so the review's finding 10 can't arise from the ACL), the log (W4.7). `logs\` is made before `service install`, which then finds it and leaves it. Delete is part of Modify: the Worker's prune of `sent\` and the move to `failed\` need it. |
   | `$R\vault.bin` | `rpworker vault grant $S` | The one Read entry on the vault's own protected DACL (SYSTEM, Administrators, OWNER RIGHTS), by SID. Never Modify: the service never writes the vault (point 9; W5.1's Open "the service writing the vault" closed as *no*). |
   | `$R\config.json`, `$R\veeam-rest.pem`, `$R\cloud-ca.pem` | none | Written by the installer, they inherit the root's entries: Administrators write, the service reads, nobody else. "Keep `config.json` writable by administrators only" (`docs/worker-config.md`) is now what the folder gives. |
   | `%ProgramFiles%\RestoreProof\` | none | `Program Files`' own inherited ACL (`Users:(RX)`, Administrators and SYSTEM full) is what the SCM and the virtual account need to read and run the exe (W4.7's error 5 line is for an exe somewhere narrower, a profile folder); the W4.8 and W5.1 runs ran the service from a folder with the same entries. |
   | each organisation certificate's key file | `icacls "<key file>" /grant "${S}:(R)"` | W4.12's one ACE; point 6. |

   `Users` get nothing, not the `RX` W4.5's Open suggested: the service's log holds what a console would have shown, tenant item names included (W4.8 point 12), `runs\` holds `items.csv`, and `sent\` the bundles, and an ordinary local user has no business with any of it; an operator runs `rpworker` elevated. On the lab laptop the folder already holds the lab vault and the hand-made run folders; the lines above change the folder's and the six subfolders' DACLs and no file's. *Rejected:* `(OI)(CI)M` for the account on the root (it could then create a folder or a file beside the config, which is what the owner rules exist to distrust); Modify on the vault (above); an ACL on each run folder of its own (they inherit `runs\`'s).

8. **The service account by its SID, before the service exists.** A virtual account's SID is a function of its name (`S-1-5-80-` and the five DWORDs of the SHA-1 of the upper-cased UTF-16 name; `sc showsid RestoreProof` prints `S-1-5-80-2410341749-1432216181-1010774729-1630443783-2912569396` on this laptop with the service uninstalled), and `icacls` and `rpworker vault grant` both take a SID string. So `Get-ServiceSid` in the module computes it, a test holds it equal to `sc showsid` for `RestoreProof` and for a random name, and every grant of point 7 is made by SID: the grants no longer wait for `service install` (the W4.8 harness's ordering), a re-run after `service uninstall` finds the same entries, and the tests grant to a service that doesn't exist on a temporary folder as a non-administrator. *Rejected:* `LookupAccountName` by name after `service install` (the harness's way; it ties the ACLs to the SCM's state and makes the tests need a service).

9. **The order, what a failure leaves, how a re-run continues.** Every step reads first and prints `ok: <what>` when nothing differs or `change: <what>` when it wrote, ending `changes: <n>`, as W7.0's script does; `-WhatIf` prints the plan with `would: ` lines and writes nothing. Nothing is ever undone by the script: a failed step stops it with that step's own line (rpworker's stderr line as it is, or the module's `problem:` line), the steps before it stay, and the next run finds them and goes on from the first thing that differs.
   1. **Checks**, nothing written: elevated; PowerShell 7.4 or later; 64-bit Windows 10 or Server 2016 or later; Veeam's REST service on this machine or the question of point 3; a `RestoreProof` service already installed from another exe path (`stop and uninstall it first; an upgrade in place is W7.3`) or from our path with a different command line (the same).
   2. **The exe**: `%ProgramFiles%\RestoreProof\` made; `rpworker.exe` and the DLLs copied from the package folder when absent or of another SHA-256 (a locked exe is a running service, refused in 1); `rpworker --version` run from there.
   3. **The folders and the ACLs** (point 7, the vault's grant in 5).
   4. **`config.json`**: when there and passing `rpworker config check --config`, kept as it is (`ok: config.json`), its URLs shown, nothing of it asked again; when absent, the questions of point 3 and point 5, the file written whole (UTF-8, no BOM, administrators-only by inheritance); when there and failing the check, the check's line and a stop (the operator's file is never rewritten by the installer; `-Replace` for a fresh one).
   5. **The vault**: `rpworker vault list`; each of `veeam_username`, `veeam_password` not there is asked and set; `cloud_install_token` is asked only when neither it nor `cloud_api_token` is there; then `vault grant` by SID. A registered Worker (`cloud_api_token` there) is asked for no token.
   6. **The signing key**: `signer new-key` when `signing_key_base64` is absent; its `key_id` printed.
   7. **The Graph certificate**: `New-WorkerGraphCertificate.ps1 -Worker <exe>` when the vault holds neither of its two names (the script refuses on its own otherwise; the installer asks `vault list` first so a second run prints `ok:`); its thumbprint printed.
   8. **Veeam**: `rpworker veeam list` from the installed exe; a failure is its line and a stop (the URL, the pin or the account is wrong, and nothing is installed yet); the key-file ACEs of point 6.
   9. **`rpworker service install`** (no `--config`: the default path is the one written); `already installed` with our command line is `ok:`.
   10. **`rpworker cloud register`** when `cloud_api_token` is absent: `registered worker <id> key <key_id>` kept for the summary. Exit 2 (the token refused: unknown, used or expired) removes the install token from the vault (`vault remove cloud_install_token`) so the next run asks for a new one, and stops; exit 3 (not reached) stops with the token kept, so the next run sends it; the half-way cases are `cloud register`'s own lines (`docs/worker-config.md`), and the way out is the one written there.
   11. **`rpworker service start`**; `already running` is `ok:`.
   12. **The summary**: the exe path, the folder, the Worker's id and `key_id` (from the line or `state\worker.json`), the Graph certificate's thumbprint, the organisations granted, `installed in <s> s` counted from the last answer typed to `started RestoreProof`, and the next two lines for the operator: `rpworker graph certificate > worker-graph.pem` (for each client's tenant script) and `manage.py create-connector --worker-id <id>`.

   *Rejected:* letting the first `service start` do the registration (W5.1 built it; an explicit step gives the token's refusal its own line and the summary its id without reading the log); asking every question first and writing afterwards (a wrong Veeam password would then be found after the service was installed); a transaction that undoes earlier steps on failure (an uninstall is W7.4's, and a half-installed Worker that says what is missing is better than one that is gone).

10. **Where it lives and how it is tested.** `tools/worker-install/` beside `tools/tenant-setup/` (the issue's `worker/installer/` was the WiX project's place; the script is an operator tool like W7.0's, not Worker source): `Install-RestoreProofWorker.ps1`, `RestoreProofWorker.psm1`, `tests/` (a uv project running `pwsh`, W7.0's `pwsh.py` and `fake_rpworker.py` copied in and the fake grown by `config check`, `vault grant`, `vault remove`, `signer new-key`, `veeam list`, `service install|start`, `cloud register` and `--version`, each answer and exit code chosen by a flag file). Tests first, failure paths first: not elevated (`-SkipElevationCheck` for the tests, which never are); pwsh 5.1; a service from another path; a config that fails the check; a `vault set` that fails; `veeam list` failing; a thumbprint without a key file; `cloud register` 401 (the install token removed and no second try), 503 (kept), 201; `service start` failing; a second run making `changes: 0`; `-WhatIf` writing nothing; every secret on stdin alone and in no argument, no output and no file (the fake's `argv.log`). The module's rules are pure and tested on their own: `Get-ServiceSid` against `sc showsid`, `Get-AclPlan`/`Test-AclState` against `icacls` output on a temporary folder (grants by SID to a service that doesn't exist; `/inheritance:r` on the test's own folder), `Get-ConfigPlan`, `Get-VaultPlan`, `Get-KeyFileCandidates`, `Read-OrganisationThumbprints` on `veeam list`'s recorded text, `Test-VeeamCertificate` on a certificate made in memory. `-Root`, `-ProgramDir`, `-Worker` and `-ServiceName` point everything at a temporary folder: no test touches `%ProgramData%`, `%ProgramFiles%` or the SCM. The Worker's changes (`signer new-key`, the `veeam list` column) are Catch2 and exe tests as every command's. CI: `.github/workflows/worker-install.yml` on `windows-latest` as `tenant-setup.yml` (`-m "not worker"`; the one test that runs the real `signer new-key` into a temporary vault is marked); `tests_touched.py` gains `tools/worker-install/` (but its `tests/`) held to `.py` or `.ps1` under `tools/worker-install/tests/`; `fixture_secret_scan.py` gains the folder.

11. **The live Done-when: a Hyper-V VM for the clean machine, the laptop for Veeam.** There is no Server 2022 VM. Hyper-V is on and running on this laptop (`vmms` Running, no VM defined; 16 GB RAM, 35 GB free on `C:`, Docker's WSL capped at 4 GB, Veeam's services running). The proposal: (a) **a Windows Server 2022 evaluation VM** (Microsoft's 180-day ISO, free; Generation 2, 2 vCPU, 4 GB dynamic memory, a 40 GB dynamic VHDX that a fresh install fills to about 12 GB, the default switch) made by `docs/api/veeam-lab/w7.1-harness/w71-vm.ps1`, with the laptop's Compose stack reached as `https://localhost:8443` through two `netsh interface portproxy` rules (the VM's `127.0.0.1:8443` to the laptop's address, the laptop's address to its `127.0.0.1:8443`), so Caddy's `localhost` certificate and its root (`cloud_ca_file`) hold without a change to the stack; the Veeam URL the laptop's `https://<laptop address>:4443` with the pin (which skips the host name) and `-AllowRemoteVeeam`; the Done-when measured as the script measures it, from the last answer typed to `started RestoreProof`, and the Cloud's `worker` row and the first heartbeat read as the W5.1 harness reads them. ## 2026-10-16 — W7.0 (#189) code review: findings 1 to 8 of fifteen fixed, 9 to 15 open (proposed)

The review (`/code-review xhigh`) of the branch `w7.0-tenant-setup` found fifteen. The owner asked for 1 to 8 to be fixed.

**Fixed.**

1. *A mail role assignment matched by name alone.* `Test-MailAssignment` now also requires the assignee (`RoleAssigneeName`, the service principal's object ID, as the lab recorded it) to be the app's service principal now. `Get-ExchangePlan` reads a pointer whose `ObjectId` is not that service principal as a deleted one's: it removes the assignments made to it first (`Select-AppAssignments` takes the old ID), then the pointer (`exchange.pointer-remove`, `Remove-ServicePrincipal`, added to `-CommandName`), then makes both again. `Test-ExchangeState` takes the pointer first and names a missing or stale one. Held by plan rows, check rows, the recorded lab answers read for another service principal, and two whole-script runs (the app made again; its service principal alone made again), each followed by a run with `changes: 0`.
2. *`-OneDriveUser` the restoretest mailbox.* The check skips a mailbox whose primary address is `-MailboxAddress` with a note, so a run on the lab's shape passes.
3. *The check stopped on an Exchange read.* Without a pointer the check tests no mailbox and lists the problem; each `Test-ServicePrincipalAuthorization` and each recipient read that fails is a `problem:` line (`Failed` in the authorization row).
4. *`-Worker` hid the Worker's reason.* rpworker's stderr is kept apart from the PEM and printed in the refusal, which no longer sends the admin to `New-WorkerGraphCertificate.ps1` for every failure and says never to `-Replace` a certificate the Worker has.
5. *No retry after the app was made.* The service principal's two reads and the three SharePoint grant POSTs go through `Invoke-WithRetry` (400 or 404, six attempts, ten seconds apart). The fake's `failures` takes `{status, times}`.
6. *Exchange in another organisation.* After `Connect-ExchangeOnline`, `Get-ConnectionInformation`'s `TenantID` is held to `-TenantId` before any Exchange read; the connect is inside the `try`, so a failed or cancelled sign-in still disconnects Graph (finding 10's case, fixed with it).
7. *Every Get-Recipient failure read as none.* `Read-Recipients` takes `-ErrorAction Stop`; only Exchange's not-found (`Get-ExchangeLookupFailure`) is no recipient, "matches multiple entries" stops the run (`names more than one recipient`), anything else is thrown in the setup and a problem in the check. The fake throws Exchange's own words.
8. *`-Replace` left a mismatched pair.* The script refuses `-Replace` while the Worker's service (`-ServiceName`, default `RestoreProof`) is not stopped, and a failed password set says what the vault now holds (the new PFX with the old password, or without one).

**Open.** 9 (two apps of the name read as none too), 10's rest (none: fixed with 6), 11 (`certificate_pem()`'s DER buffer and OpenSSL errors), 12 (the usage line in `docs/worker-config.md`), 13 (the whole role assignment table read twice), 14 (the check's copy of `MailboxKinds`), 15 (the module's function names that Exchange's cmdlets can shadow).

**Gates.** `uv run pytest` in `tools/tenant-setup/tests` with the built Worker, on the finished code: 359 passed (330 before the review). The live Done-when was not run again: `Remove-ServicePrincipal`, `Get-ConnectionInformation`'s `TenantID` and Exchange's not-found and ambiguous texts are from the module's documentation and Exchange's known messages, not recorded on the lab tenant.

## 2026-10-16 — W7.0 (#189): the client tenant setup script. One PowerShell 7 script, `tools/tenant-setup/Initialize-RestoreProofTenant.ps1`, run by the client's global admin, finds or makes the three restore targets and the "RestoreProof Worker" app with exactly its grants, checks them read-only, and prints the client's `restoreproof.client-profile.v1`; each step reads, compares and writes only what differs, so a second run makes no change; the Worker keeps **one** Graph certificate for all its clients, made in memory and piped into the vault, and only its public half goes to a tenant (a new `rpworker graph certificate` prints it); the deciding logic is a module tested through pytest on recorded and fake Graph and Exchange answers, failure paths first; one PR, `Closes #189` (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written on 2026-10-16: the live Done-when on the lab tenant, point 11 (A))

W7.0 (#189): "Client tenant setup script". Done when: "On a tenant that has never seen RestoreProof (a second test tenant, or the lab tenant with the app and targets removed first), the client's admin runs the script once; the grant check passes; the printed profile is accepted by `manage.py create-connector`; a Worker with that profile and certificate makes a `pass` run; and running the script a second time changes nothing." This entry works from the issue, `docs/security/graph-permissions.md`, the three lab scripts (`lab/entra/new-worker-app.ps1`, `check-worker-grants.ps1`, `fill-worker-vault.ps1`) and their tests (`lab/tests/test_entra_script.py`, `test_fill_worker_vault.py`), `lab/tenant.md`, `shared/schemas/client-profile.v1.json`, `docs/onboarding.md` step 4 and the code on `main` at `w7.0-tenant-setup`'s base. Nothing is built yet.

**What there is today (read in the repository, not taken from the docs).**

- **The lab scripts are the lab's alone.** `new-worker-app.ps1` holds the lab's tenant, admin, site, list, drive and folder IDs as constants, makes the certificate with `New-SelfSignedCertificate` in `Cert:\CurrentUser\My` and keeps the PFX in a file under `%LOCALAPPDATA%` with its password in Credential Manager; `fill-worker-vault.ps1` pipes both into `rpworker vault set` on stdin. Neither makes a target: the RestoreTarget library was made by hand, the OneDrive folder through Graph as alice, `restoretest` is a licensed user. `check-worker-grants.ps1` checks the canaries, which a client tenant doesn't have (canaries are an opt-in since W6.2), and its rules (`Test-PermissionRule`: `site-read`, `inherited-read-only`, `none`, `target-write`) are pure functions already tested row by row from Python through `pwsh`.
- **The Worker has one Graph certificate.** The vault holds one `graph_cert_pfx_base64` and one `graph_cert_password` (`rp/secrets.hpp`), while each client's profile names its own `graph_client_id` (W4.10) and one Worker serves two tenants (W6.2). So every client's app must accept the same certificate. The Worker opens the PFX with OpenSSL and refuses a legacy cipher, a key under RSA 2048, an expired certificate (`src/client_assertion.cpp`). No command prints the certificate's public half.
- **The profile** is nine keys, IDs only (`veeam_org_name`, the tenant, the app, `restoretest@…`, the site, the library's drive, the OneDrive drive and folder); the Cloud's `create-connector` holds it to the schema and its tenant to the client's.
- **This laptop** has PowerShell 7.4.21, ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.10.1 and Pester 3.4 (Windows PowerShell's, too old for PowerShell 7 tests); the Microsoft Graph PowerShell module is not installed in PowerShell 7 here.

**Decision.**

1. **Where it lives.** `tools/tenant-setup/` at the repository root, product code beside `worker/` and `cloud/` (not under `lab/`, which is the lab tenant's):
   - `Initialize-RestoreProofTenant.ps1`: the one script the admin runs; it reads, applies and prints, and holds no rule of its own.
   - `RestoreProofTenant.psm1`: every rule that decides, as pure functions over the answers read (the plans, the name checks, the grant rules, the profile), so the tests reach them without a tenant.
   - `tests/`: a uv project (`package = false`, `uv.lock` committed, pytest and jsonschema as dev dependencies, as `lab/` is), running `pwsh` as the lab's tests do; `tests/fixtures/` the answers.
   - `docs/tenant-setup.md`: the admin's page (what to have, the command, every line it prints, how to undo it).
   The lab scripts stay as they are (they set up the lab tenant and its canaries); the module copies `Test-PermissionRule`'s four rules and the lab's tests keep holding the lab's copy.

2. **What it takes.** Parameters, never a secret among them:
   - `-TenantId <guid>`: the client's tenant; the signed-in context must be that tenant, or it stops before anything is read.
   - `-SiteUrl https://<host>.sharepoint.com/sites/<name>`: an **existing** site that will hold the `RestoreTarget` library. The Worker app gets `read` on the whole site (grant #1), so `docs/tenant-setup.md` says to use a site made for RestoreProof and nothing else; the script refuses the tenant's root site and any `-my.sharepoint.com` (OneDrive) site, and prints the names of the site's other libraries as a note so the admin sees what `read` reaches. It makes no site (Graph v1.0 can't make a site without a group; a group-connected site would claim the mail alias, `lab/tenant.md`).
   - `-OneDriveUser <upn>`: a licensed user whose OneDrive gets the `/RestoreTarget` folder; the page recommends an account kept for this.
   - `-MailboxAddress`: default `restoretest@<the tenant's initial *.onmicrosoft.com domain>`; anything whose local part isn't `restoretest` is refused (the schema's rule).
   - `-VeeamOrgName`: default the tenant's initial domain, the name Veeam gives an organisation it adds; the Worker's client check (W4.11) refuses a wrong one at the first run, before anything is restored.
   - `-ProfileFile <path>`: where the profile is written as well as printed; `-WorkerCertificateFile <pem>` or `-Worker <rpworker.exe>` (point 4); `-AllowOrganizationCustomization` (point 6); `-WhatIf` (point 5).

3. **What the admin needs.** A **Global Administrator** of the client's tenant for the run (consenting application permissions, Exchange RBAC for Applications and SharePoint grants in one sitting needs it; a narrower set of roles, Privileged Role Administrator, Application Administrator, Exchange Administrator and SharePoint Administrator together, is left open until someone tries it); **site collection admin of the OneDrive user's OneDrive** (even a global admin can't write another user's OneDrive without it; the script can't set it without the SharePoint admin module, so it stops with the admin center's click-by-click steps, as `lab/README.md` has them, and says how to remove it afterwards). **PowerShell 7.4 or later** (`Test-Json -SchemaFile` reads draft 2020-12 there, point 8). Two modules and no other: **Microsoft.Graph.Authentication** (only `Connect-MgGraph` and `Invoke-MgGraphRequest`, not the whole SDK) and **ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.7.2 or later** (the lab's minimum, for `-DisableWAM`); a missing or older module stops the script with the `Install-Module … -Scope CurrentUser` line. The Graph sign-in is delegated with the scopes `Application.ReadWrite.All`, `AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All`, `Sites.FullControl.All`, `Files.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All` and `Organization.Read.All`, all for the admin's session (Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools), none for the Worker; the page says the consent prompt lists them and why.

4. **The certificate: one per Worker, its key never leaves the Worker's vault.**
   - **Making it** (once per Worker, on the Worker's machine, elevated, when the vault has no Graph certificate): `tools/tenant-setup/New-WorkerGraphCertificate.ps1` makes an RSA 2048 key and a self-signed certificate (subject `CN=RestoreProof Worker`, SHA-256, valid two years) **in memory** with .NET's `CertificateRequest` (no certificate store, unlike the lab's `New-SelfSignedCertificate`), builds the PFX with AES-256-CBC and SHA-256 (`Pkcs12Builder`, the ciphers the Worker reads) under a random 32-byte password, and pipes each value to `rpworker vault set graph_cert_pfx_base64` and `vault set graph_cert_password` on stdin, one process each, as `fill-worker-vault.ps1` does. Nothing is written to a file, an argument, an environment variable, a transcript or the screen; the byte arrays and strings are cleared after the pipe. It refuses when `rpworker vault list` shows either name set, unless `-Replace` (which strands every client app holding the old certificate until the tenant script runs again there: it says so).
   - **Giving a tenant its public half:** a new **`rpworker graph certificate [--vault <file>]`** prints the vault's certificate as PEM with its SHA-1 thumbprint and its end date, never the key or the password (the Worker opens the PFX as it does to sign in). The tenant script takes it by `-Worker <rpworker.exe>` (it runs the command itself, on the Worker's machine) or by `-WorkerCertificateFile <pem>` (the admin runs the script elsewhere with the PEM the MSP sent: a public certificate, safe to send). The script refuses a file holding a private key block, a key under RSA 2048 and a certificate that expires within 30 days.
   - The app's one credential is that certificate: `keyCredentials` replaced by it alone when they differ, every client secret removed (the lab's `Set-OnlyCredential`).

5. **A second run changes nothing.** Every step is read, compare, write: the module turns what was read into a list of changes (`Get-TargetPlan`, `Get-AppPlan`, `Get-GrantPlan`, `Get-ExchangePlan`), and only those are sent. Each step prints `ok: <what>` when nothing differs or `change: <what>` for each write; the run ends `changes: <n>`. A second run on the same tenant prints `changes: 0` and the same profile bytes. `-WhatIf` reads everything, prints the plan and writes nothing. A step that finds what it can't safely change (two apps named "RestoreProof Worker", a `RestoreTarget` list that is no document library, a non-empty folder of that name at the wrong place) stops with one line and writes nothing more.

6. **What it makes or finds, in order.**
   1. **Sign-in and the tenant:** `GET /organization` gives the tenant ID (held to `-TenantId`) and the initial domain.
   2. **The mailbox** (Exchange): a recipient with the primary address `-MailboxAddress` is taken if it is a user or shared mailbox; one of another kind, or an address that is another mailbox's secondary address, stops the script. With none, a **shared mailbox** `RestoreTest` is made (`New-Mailbox -Shared`: no licence). Whether Veeam restores into a shared mailbox and the Worker reads it back is not yet shown (the lab's `restoretest` is a licensed user): the live Done-when shows it only on a tenant that has none (point 11).
   3. **The library:** a list named `RestoreTarget` in the site is taken if it is a document library (`list.template` `documentLibrary`) whose address ends in `/RestoreTarget`; else one is made (`POST /sites/{id}/lists`, `documentLibrary`).
   4. **The folder:** `GET /users/{upn}/drive/root:/RestoreTarget` is taken if it is a folder directly under the root; else it is made (`POST …/root/children`, `conflictBehavior` `fail`). A file of that name, or a 403 (the admin isn't site collection admin), stops the script.
   5. **The app registration** "RestoreProof Worker": found by its name (more than one stops the script); single tenant (`AzureADMyOrg`), the certificate alone, `requiredResourceAccess` exactly the three Graph roles; the service principal; admin consent for `Sites.Selected`, `Files.SelectedOperations.Selected`, `Lists.SelectedOperations.Selected`, and **every other application consent on the service principal removed**, on Graph and on any other API, and every delegated grant (`oauth2PermissionGrants`) on it removed.
   6. **The SharePoint grants:** `read` on the site (a different role is set back to `read`); `write` on the RestoreTarget list; `write` on the `/RestoreTarget` folder. **Before each write grant the script reads the target again and refuses unless it is the one of step 3 or 4 by ID and named `RestoreTarget`** (the list: `displayName` exact and the address's last segment; the folder: `name` exact, a folder, its `parentReference` the drive's root, its drive the user's), the lab's `Assert-RestoreTargetList` and `Assert-RestoreTargetFolder` as pure functions over the reply.
   7. **Exchange RBAC for Applications:** the service principal pointer, the management scope `RestoreProof Worker - restoretest mailbox` with `PrimarySmtpAddress -eq '<address>'`, the one assignment `RestoreProof Worker - Application Mail.ReadWrite - restoretest`, and any other assignment of this app removed. **`Enable-OrganizationCustomization`** (tenant-wide, one way) runs only with `-AllowOrganizationCustomization`; without it a dehydrated tenant stops the script before any Exchange write, with a line that says what the switch does.

7. **The check, read-only, at the end of every run** (and alone with `-CheckOnly`): it reads everything again and stops (`grants: <n> problem(s)`, exit 1) unless:
   - the app is single tenant, has exactly one certificate (the Worker's thumbprint), no client secret and no federated credential, and asks for exactly the three roles;
   - the service principal holds exactly those three application consents, no delegated grant, and is in no directory role;
   - the site has exactly one grant of the app, `read`; the RestoreTarget list and the folder exactly one of their own, `write`; every other list of the site no grant of its own (an inherited `read` is fine); the OneDrive user's drive root and OneDrive site none (rules `site-read`, `target-write`, `inherited-read-only`, `none`; an unreadable list or a reply without a permission list is a problem, never a pass; another application's grant is a note);
   - Exchange holds exactly the one assignment for the app, with that role and that scope, the scope's filter exactly the address; `Test-ServicePrincipalAuthorization` gives `InScope` True for `restoretest` and False for the admin's own mailbox and the OneDrive user's.
   It ends `grants: ok`. That the app's token carries exactly the three roles is the Worker's side, for `rpworker doctor` (W7.2): the script never holds the key, so it never signs in as the app.

8. **The profile.** Built from what was read back, never from the parameters: the tenant ID, the app's client ID, the mailbox's primary address as Exchange gives it, the site's ID, the library's drive ID, the user's drive ID and the folder's ID, `veeam_org_name` as point 2. Validated with `Test-Json -SchemaFile shared/schemas/client-profile.v1.json` (the script stops on a profile the schema refuses, and when run outside the repository it carries its own copy, held equal to the shared one by a test); printed to stdout and written to `-ProfileFile` as sorted-key JSON, UTF-8 without BOM, LF. It is the same document `rpworker client check --profile-file` and `manage.py create-connector --profile-file` read; `docs/onboarding.md` step 4 points to it.

9. **What it never does.**
   - No write anywhere but: the app registration named "RestoreProof Worker" and its service principal, the three SharePoint grants, the management scope and the role assignment of point 6.7, and the three targets it made or found; it reads nothing else for a change and changes no other app, user, group, site, list, mailbox or policy.
   - No write grant but `write` on the RestoreTarget list and folder, each behind its name check; never `Sites.Selected` `write`, `owner` or `fullcontrol`; never a `*.All` application role, `Mail.Read`, `Mail.ReadWrite` or `full_access_as_app` as an Entra consent (each one found on its own app is removed, and its name appears in the script only in the list of what is removed); never a client secret.
   - No delete of a target, of anything in a target (it cleans nothing: that is the Worker's Cleaner) or of anything another application owns.
   - No secret printed, logged, written or passed as an argument: the script has no `Start-Transcript`, and the PFX, its password and any token are never in a variable the script prints; the tenant script never sees the key at all.
   - No canary: it seeds none and asks for no canary location; `docs/tenant-setup.md` says canaries stay an opt-in, seeded separately (`lab/`'s seeder in the lab; for a client a later task), with `manage.py create-plan --canaries`.
   - Nothing in Veeam: adding the organisation to Veeam (Veeam's own app) and its backup job are the MSP's, before the script; the page says so.
   - No change to the site collection admin membership, the tenant's sharing settings or licences.

10. **Tests first, on recorded and fake answers, failure paths first.**
    - **The fixtures:** the lab tenant's real answers, recorded **read-only** before the lab is changed (`tools/tenant-setup/tests/record/Record-TenantAnswers.ps1`: GETs and `Get-*` cmdlets only, as the admin), each a JSON file of the request and the reply; person names and addresses other than the test accounts replaced by placeholders (the W4.1 rule); the failure answers (a wrong-named list, a folder under another folder, a 403 on the OneDrive, a dehydrated tenant, an extra consent, an extra Exchange assignment, a `write` site grant) written by hand and saying so in their `source`. `fixture_secret_scan.py` gains the tree.
    - **The pure rules** (the module), row by row with `pytest.mark.parametrize`, refusals first: the list and folder name checks (the canary-shaped `RestoreTest` library, a renamed list, another list's address, a folder in a subfolder, in another drive, a file named `RestoreTarget`); the site refusals (the root site, a OneDrive site); the mailbox address and recipient kinds; the four grant rules; each plan from a state that differs in one thing, and **from the state the plan leaves, an empty plan** (the second run); the profile from fixtures, validated by Python's jsonschema against `shared/schemas/client-profile.v1.json` and by the script's `Test-Json`, which must agree on `shared/testdata/client-profile-v1/cases.json`.
    - **The whole script** against a fake tenant: `Invoke-MgGraphRequest` and the Exchange cmdlets replaced in the `pwsh` session by functions that answer from a fixture state, apply writes to it, and log every request. Held: the first run's writes are exactly the plan's; a second run on the state the first left sends no write and prints `changes: 0` and the same profile bytes; every write grant's request is preceded by its name check's GET of the same ID; no request writes to a path outside the allowed set; a failed GET is a problem, never a pass; the dehydrated tenant without the switch sends no Exchange write; and a sentinel certificate key and PFX password are in no output, no request and no file.
    - **The script's text** (as `test_entra_script.py` does): the only `write` roles are the two behind their checks, the only mail role is `Application Mail.ReadWrite`, no `Start-Transcript`, every Exchange call sets `-ErrorAction Stop`, the script parses, no comment runs as a command.
    - **The certificate script:** the PFX it would pipe, captured by a fake `rpworker`, opens with `cryptography`'s PKCS#12 loader and uses AES-256-CBC and SHA-256 (no RC2 or 3DES); the values reach the fake's stdin only; it refuses a vault that has them.
    - **The Worker's `rpworker graph certificate`:** Catch2 and an exe test (the PEM equal to the test PFX's certificate, the thumbprint, the end date, exit codes; a vault without the certificate exit 1), and a secret-audit case: the PFX's key and password in no stream.
    - "No test, no merge" holds `tools/tenant-setup/*.ps1` and `*.psm1` to a change under `tools/tenant-setup/tests/`.

11. **The live Done-when, by hand.** The lab tenant's trial ends on **2026-10-23**, so whichever is chosen runs before then; the fixtures (point 10) are recorded first, while the lab is as it is.
    - **(A) The lab tenant with the app and targets removed first (recommended for the date).** A lab-only harness `docs/api/veeam-lab/w7.0-harness/w70-teardown.ps1`, run by the owner, removes: the RestoreProof Worker app (and from deleted items), its three SharePoint grants, the Exchange assignment and scope, the RestoreTarget library and alice's `/RestoreTarget` folder (each only when empty and named `RestoreTarget`; the canaries never touched). It keeps `restoretest` (a licensed user whose deletion would lose its mail and the trial's licence), so the script finds the mailbox and makes the rest. Then `w70-live.ps1`: the script once (`changes: <n>`, `grants: ok`), `create-connector` with the printed profile on the Compose stack, the W5.1 harness's run with that profile and the vault's certificate (`pass`), the script again (`changes: 0`, the same profile bytes), `python -m seeder check-worker-app` with the new IDs. The new IDs go into `lab/tenant.md`, `lab/seeder/tenant.py`, the two lab Entra scripts, the lab config and the live test labs; the recordings and evidence that carry the old IDs stay as they were made. **Not shown live this way:** the shared mailbox and `Enable-OrganizationCustomization` (the lab ran it in 2026-09).
    - **(B) A second trial tenant.** Shows every create path, the shared mailbox and a dehydrated tenant, and keeps the lab's IDs; it needs a new trial, the organisation added to Veeam with a backup job and a restore point, a licensed OneDrive user and some real items to sample: about a day before the run.

12. **The build, in this order, each step's tests and code in one commit, red before green.**
    1. The read-only recorder and the fixtures, from the lab tenant as it is.
    2. The module's pure rules (name checks, site and mailbox refusals, the four grant rules) and their tests.
    3. The plans and the second-run tests; the profile and its schema tests.
    4. `rpworker graph certificate` and its tests; `New-WorkerGraphCertificate.ps1` and its tests.
    5. `Initialize-RestoreProofTenant.ps1` over the fake tenant: the whole-script tests, the text tests.
    6. The docs: `docs/tenant-setup.md`, `docs/onboarding.md` (a step 0 and step 4's profile), `docs/security/graph-permissions.md` (a client tenant, the shared certificate), `docs/worker-config.md` (`graph certificate`), `docs/testing.md`, `docs/glossary.md`, CLAUDE.md; the gates (the new tests, `ctest --preset dev`, coverage, `fixture_secret_scan.py`, the lab's tests unchanged).
    7. The live Done-when as the owner chooses in point 11, and the build notes with the real figures.

**Reason.** The grants are the one part of onboarding where a mistake either breaks the runs or opens a client's tenant wider than the rule allows, and every client tenant needs them again. One script that reads first, writes only differences and checks itself afterwards gives the same grants every time; the rules that decide are pure functions tested on real answers before any tenant sees them. One certificate per Worker matches the vault's one Graph credential and means the private key never travels: a tenant only ever gets the public half.

**Alternatives rejected.**
- *A certificate per tenant:* the vault holds one; a vault of many would be a Worker change for no gain in this stage, and every key would still live in the same vault.
- *The tenant script makes the PFX and the admin carries it to the Worker:* a private key in a file or an email.
- *A `.cer` file written beside the vault for the public half:* a second copy that can drift from the vault; `rpworker graph certificate` reads the one source.
- *Making the site:* Graph v1.0 makes no site without a Microsoft 365 group, and a group claims the mail alias; the SharePoint admin module would be a third module.
- *Making the admin site collection admin of the OneDrive by script:* the SharePoint admin module and a tenant-wide admin act for one step a person does once.
- *Running `Enable-OrganizationCustomization` without asking:* tenant-wide and one way.
- *Reusing the lab scripts with parameters:* they carry the canary checks and the lab's Credential Manager entries; the lab keeps them as they are.
- *Pester 5:* not installed; the lab's pytest-through-`pwsh` pattern is in use and gives jsonschema for the profile.
- *A licensed user for `restoretest`:* a licence per client for a mailbox only restores reach.

**Open.**
- The narrowest admin roles that can run it (point 3).
- Certificate rotation: a new certificate needs the script run again in every client's tenant, and runs fail there until then; a rotation that keeps two certificates for a while would break the "one credential" rule and is for a later task.
- Veeam's restore into a shared mailbox (point 6.2), unless the Done-when runs on a second tenant.
- `rpworker doctor` (W7.2): the token's roles from the Worker's side; `docs/install-guide.md` (Q7.2) points to `docs/tenant-setup.md`.
- Seeding canaries in a client's tenant (no command; the lab's seeder is the lab's).
- #154 (which SharePoint grant the library needs) stands; the script makes both, as the lab has them.

**Code, tests and docs with the build.** `tools/tenant-setup/` (`Initialize-RestoreProofTenant.ps1`, `New-WorkerGraphCertificate.ps1`, `RestoreProofTenant.psm1`, `tests/` with `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, the fixtures and the recorder); Worker: `src/graph_command.cpp` (or its header) for `graph certificate`, its tests, the secret audit; `worker/tools/fixture_secret_scan.py` (the new tree); `.github/workflows` and `tests_touched.py` for the new tree; `docs/api/veeam-lab/w7.0-harness/`; docs as step 6. The PR closes #189.

## 2026-10-15 — W5.1 (#66) code review: findings 1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11 to 15 of fifteen fixed, 3, 4, 7 and 10 open for the owner; a job that ended before its run line no longer holds the kept document (proposed)

The review of the branch `w5.1-worker-cloud` (Claude Code `/code-review max`, 2026-10-15) gave fifteen findings and eleven more cut by its cap. The owner asked for the eleven below to be fixed and the four that change an approved rule or need a proxy to happen left open. Each fix is test first; the numbers are the review's.

1. **The service stopped asking for jobs on Windows Server 2016 and 2019.** `kept_jobs_age` turned the file's time into the system clock with `clock_cast`, which in MSVC goes through `utc_clock` and loads `icu.dll`'s time-zone data; Server 2016 and 2019 have no `icu.dll`, so it threw at every poll after the first and the step's catch said only "a step failed unexpectedly". Now both times are the file clock's (`file_time_type::clock::now() - written`), which needs no time-zone data. The laptop has `icu.dll`, so no test can show the throw; `worker body: the jobs document is kept…` now holds the real age on the file clock, 0 to 1 h after a write and 7 to 8 h after the file's time is set seven hours back.
2. **One job that couldn't start kept every other client's runs at the Cloud for six hours.** A job that ends before its run line (no restore point yet, an unknown organisation, Veeam not answering) is never settled, so the kept document was read again at every poll and the Cloud not asked. Now such a job is kept in memory (`ServiceLoop::not_started_`, with when it first ended so) and holds the kept document no longer: the Cloud is asked at the next poll, its jobs run first, then each such job is tried again at every poll until it runs, a document names it again, or six hours (`kKeptJobsFor`) have passed since it first ended so, by when the Cloud has requeued or expired it. The case point 7 had in mind (Veeam down for minutes) keeps its retry at every poll; only the block is gone. A restart tries it once from the kept file. With `jobs_file` nothing changes: the file is read at every poll and is its own retry (an existing test held that). Two tests: the Cloud asked while job A keeps failing (`job-a, job-b, job-c, job-a, job-a` over three polls), and A tried until it runs, or dropped untried six hours later.
5. **The W5.1 harness removed a registered Worker's token.** Its `finally` removed both Cloud tokens even when the run had refused to start because one was there. Now the tokens are removed only after the run has seen that neither was there (`$vaultOurs`), and an install token already there is refused like an API token. `$since` is set before the `try`, so the `finally` no longer throws under `Set-StrictMode` when `sent\` holds a run, and the "targets after" warning reads the listing made after the run (it could never fire). Not run live again.
6. **The harnesses on the W4.8 stub could no longer pass** (C5.7's, so W6.3's, and W4.8's, W4.9's, W4.10's and W4.11's): since W5.1 the service sends nothing without `cloud_api_token`, takes a 2xx without `X-RestoreProof-API: 1` as no Cloud's, and the stub's port 8443 is Caddy's. Now the stub answers with the header and listens on 8444; `Start-W48Stub` puts 32 random bytes in base64url into the vault as `cloud_api_token` on stdin (refusing a vault that already holds one), and `Stop-W48Stub`, which `Remove-W48Harness` now calls before its own refusal, takes it out again only when the run put it there (a marker file in the run's temp folder). The scripts parse; none was run live again.
8. **A run the Cloud refused for good never became the loop's last error.** The loop took words only from `kept …` lines; the outbox reports such a run as `failed <run>: upload_http_<status>`. `kept_word` now reads that line too. Test: `cloud: a run the Cloud refused for good is the loop's last error`.
9. **No secret-audit case ran the registration**, the one path that receives a new API token. `secret audit M` runs `cloud register --record` to a 201 with the issued token, `service start`'s first start, a 409, and a vault that can't be written after the 201, on a real DPAPI vault in the temp folder, and searches both streams, the logger, every file under the temp folder (the vault, `state\worker.json`, the recording) and every request, the registration's body with the install token taken out after checking it is there once (the one secret the Cloud is sent there). It passed at once: no leak was found.
11. **`outbox flush` freed the vault's other secrets unwiped.** `rp::WipedSecrets` (moved from `cloud_command.cpp` to `rp/secrets.hpp`) holds the vault read and wipes every value when the command ends; `rp::wipe_secrets(secrets, "cloud_api_token")` wipes and drops the others at once; `CloudUploader` wipes its copy of the token in its destructor. Test: `wipe_secrets empties every value but the one kept`.
12. **A run in `failed\` dispatched again was started again.** `skip_job` now says `skipped <run>: already failed` for `OutboxHolds::failed`, as point 8 and `docs/worker-config.md` said. Test: the skip test's fourth job.
13. **After a 401 a move to `failed\` left by an earlier pass was not made.** The move is a rename and sends nothing; it now comes before the `token_refused` skip. Test: `outbox flush: after a 401 a move to failed\ left by an earlier pass is still made`.
14. **The age test passed on a negative age**, and a negative age kept the document. The test now checks the real file clock (finding 1's), and `cloud_jobs` takes an age below zero (a clock stepped back) as no age: the Cloud is asked. Test: `cloud: a kept document whose age is below zero is dropped and the Cloud asked`.
15. **The exe test of a flush without a token read a vault without `FIXTURES_REQUIRED exe-vault`.** It requires the fixture now, and main's `outbox flush with nothing queued` is back (exit 0, `0 queued, 0 sent, 0 failed`) on a fifth vault, `token.bin`, holding `cloud_api_token` alone.

**Open, for the owner:**

- 3. **A 400, 404, 409, 415 or 422 without the contract header moves every due run to `failed\`.** A wrong `cloud_url` that answers 404 (another host, an ingress default) would lose the queue for good. Point 8 approved the status alone; every recorded Cloud refusal carries the header, so requiring it before a refusal for good would lose none. The recommendation: require the header, and retry a 4xx without it. The owner's rule.
- 4. **A 401 from something in front of the Cloud** (a gateway, a proxy doing NTLM) stops the Worker until a new token, when a restart would have done. The Cloud's own 401s carry the header. The same recommendation as 3, for the 401; it needs such a proxy to happen.
- 7. **`service start` reads the vault before the Service Control Manager**, so an unelevated start says "the vault file can't be read" instead of "run this from an elevated prompt", and a missing vault refuses the start (point 2 said "with neither it starts as today"). The fix is to check the SCM's rights first, or to start without registering when there is no vault; which one is the owner's call.
- 10. **A `failed\` that can't be listed** (a file of that name, or a W7.1 ACL without it) makes the whole outbox unreadable, so nothing is uploaded. With W7.1's ACLs; the fix could count `failed\` as empty when it can't be listed, which hides the operator's archive.
- The cut list: the W5.1 harness's evidence gate can't see the Cloud tokens; `token_is_new` lives in memory (a run a 401 kept waits up to an hour after a restart); `cloud register --record` writes the request body (the audit found no token in it); the issued token isn't wiped on the key-mismatch path; `last_error` reads `upload_http_401` briefly before `token_refused`; `no_token_said_` never resets; the token names have no colon form in `redact()`; `state\jobs.json` read back right after it is written; `failed\` walked at every flush; `dispatched-run.wire` carries the lab tenant's IDs without saying so; `CLAUDE.md`'s strict names miss `cloud`.

**Build notes** (local, 2026-10-15): `ctest --preset dev -j 4` on the finished code: **2339 tests, 0 failed** (13 live tests skipped), the nine new Catch2 cases and the restored exe test among them; one run of the loop tests had failed first, on finding 2's retry reaching the lab's jobs-file mode (`what is said once of a job is forgotten…`), which is why the retry is the Cloud's jobs alone. `fixture_secret_scan.py`: 1266 files in 7 trees, 0 findings. **Coverage was not measured**: the OpenCppCoverage run was stopped by the session's low-memory guard and not started again, so the strict files (`outbox.cpp`, `service_loop.cpp`, `cloud_command.cpp`) are not shown at 100% line on this code; every new branch has a test. Nothing under `cloud/` or `shared/` changed; the harnesses parse and none was run live.
