## 2026-10-15 — W5.1 (#66): the Worker talks to the Cloud. `rpworker cloud register` turns the install token into the API token (the vault's one writer stays the operator's elevated console; `service start` runs it on the first start); `Authorization: Bearer` on the poll, the upload and the heartbeat; `GET /v1/jobs` replaces `jobs_file` as the service's source, its answer kept in `state\jobs.json` and read by the same reader; the upload's answers by status, the permanent ones to `failed\`; the header rule on every 2xx; the local Cloud reached over HTTPS through Caddy in the Compose stack at `https://localhost:8443`, its private root trusted through `cloud_ca_file`; the wire bytes of a Worker upload held by a Cloud test (C5.11's finding 3); one PR, `Closes #66` (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written on 2026-10-15)

W5.1 (#66): "Worker talks to the real Cloud". Done when: "The DB shows a pass run whose bundle was produced by the service on the Veeam VM." This entry works from the issue, CLAUDE.md's W5.1 bullet, the entries that recorded what W5.1 should do ("C5.5 and C5.6" point 10, "C5.7" point 15, "C5.8" point 12, "C5.11" point 8 and its review's findings 3 and 7), the W4.6, W4.7, W4.8 and W4.10 entries, and the code on `main` at `4254f26`. Nothing is built yet. The owner's plan holds throughout: everything runs on this laptop; C5.12 (a server) is the last task, so W5.1 talks to the Compose stack, and nothing here buys, proposes or depends on hosting.

**What the code has today (read on `main`, not taken from the docs).**

- **Secrets.** `kSecretNames` is five names (`rp/secrets.hpp`); `Secrets` has five fields; `secret_values` lists four values (the user name is no secret); `read_vault` refuses a name outside the five; `write_vault` writes the whole vault through a temp file and a move, keeps the DACL it finds, and refuses a file whose owner isn't SYSTEM, Administrators or the caller. The service's account `NT SERVICE\RestoreProof` gets **Read** on `vault.bin` (`rpworker vault grant`, W4.8's harness) and nothing more; the folder `%ProgramData%\RestoreProof` keeps its inherited ACL. **So the service cannot write the vault**, and a file it wrote would be owned by the virtual account, which every later `vault` command, run by an administrator, refuses by the owner rule. This decides point 2.
- **The upload** (`src/uploader.cpp`, not strict): `CloudUploader` POSTs the parts to `<cloud_url>/v1/results` with no `Authorization`; 202 is accepted, every other status is `upload_http_<status>`, transport failures `upload_unreachable` or `upload_timeout`, anything else `upload_internal`. The outbox (`src/outbox.cpp`, strict) retries every failure on its schedule (1, 2, 4 … 32 minutes, then hourly for good); there is no `failed\`; `OutboxHolds` is `none`, `queued`, `sent`; `outbox list` and `flush` end in `<n> queued, <m> sent`. `outbox flush` reads no vault.
- **The heartbeat** (`src/heartbeat.cpp`, not strict): five keys, canonical JSON, no `Authorization`; any 2xx is taken; the loop writes `heartbeat failed: <word>` once per change of word.
- **The poll** (`src/service_loop.cpp`, strict): `read_jobs()` reads `env.jobs_file` through `rp::read_jobs` (the owner rule of `read_trusted_file`, 1 MiB, five jobs) at every poll; without `jobs_file` the loop gets no jobs. The document is offered again at every poll: a job that ended before its run line ("the stub offers the job again at the next poll") and a job not reached in this poll run later because the file still names them; J2 skips a run whose folder, outbox entry or done mark is there. `parse_jobs` already takes `canary_cursor` (W6.2).
- **HTTP.** `HttpResponse` carries the headers; `HttpClientOptions::ca_file` replaces the Windows store by one PEM file and keeps the host-name check; `cloud_url` is `https://` only (`parse_config`), and `cloud_ca_file` (W4.6 point 7) exists for exactly this case. `redact()` already masks the `Authorization` header and `Bearer <token>`, and none of `api_token`, `install_token`, `cloud_api_token`, `cloud_install_token` as a JSON key or a `key=value` name. The recorder keeps three answer headers (`kKeptHeaders`), not `X-RestoreProof-API`.
- **The Cloud** answers as CLAUDE.md's rules say: registration 201 `{"worker_id","api_token","key_id"}`, 401, 400, 409, 413, 422; the poll 200 `restoreproof.jobs.v1` (with `canary_cursor` for a plan opted in, C6.8); the upload 202, 400, 404, 409, 411, 413, 415, 422, 401; the heartbeat 204, 401, 422; `X-RestoreProof-API: 1` on every answer the app sends. The stack is plain http on `127.0.0.1:8000`; nothing in it speaks TLS.

**Decision.**

1. **The local Cloud over HTTPS: Caddy in the Compose stack.** A new Compose service `proxy`: the official `caddy` image pinned by digest (as MinIO's are), `127.0.0.1:8443:443` (127.0.0.1 alone, like every port of the stack), and a `cloud/docker/Caddyfile` of a few lines: the global options `skip_install_trust` and `local_certs`; one site `localhost` with `tls internal` and `reverse_proxy api:8000`; no body limit of its own (the app's 96 MiB and 64 KiB caps stay the only ones; Caddy sets none by default). Caddy's internal CA makes a root (ten years), an intermediate and a short-lived leaf for `DNS:localhost`, renewed by Caddy itself and kept in a named volume `caddy-data`, so the root survives a restart and a `down` (not a `down -v`). **The host name is `localhost`**: the Worker checks it against the leaf's SAN as for any host (nothing skipped; `veeam_cert_sha256`'s pin is Veeam's alone), and no hosts-file entry or DNS is needed. **The Worker trusts the root through `cloud_ca_file`**: `docker compose cp proxy:/data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt <file>` gives the PEM (a public certificate; Caddy's root key never leaves the volume). `cloud_url` is `https://localhost:8443`. The plain `127.0.0.1:8000` stays for the Cloud's tests and earlier harnesses, which speak to the app directly; the Worker never takes `http`. A test in `cloud/tests` holds the Compose file: the proxy's image by digest, its one port on 127.0.0.1, `tls internal`, the upstream `api:8000`, no `request_body` limit. Behind Caddy `request.client.host` is the proxy's address (the audit rows' `ip`): C5.7's finding 7 and C5.12's item, unchanged here and named again under Open. Nothing else of the Cloud changes but point 10's wire test.

2. **First start: `rpworker cloud register`, the operator's one command, run by `service start` when the vault has no API token.** The issue says the Worker registers on its first start. The service can't write the vault (above), and making it able to (Modify on `vault.bin` and create rights on its folder for the virtual account, and an owner rule that takes the service's account) would widen the one file every secret lives in for one write. So the registration runs where the vault is already written, at the operator's elevated console:
   - **`rpworker cloud register [--config <path>] [--vault <file>] [--name <worker name>] [--record <dir>]`**, and **`rpworker service start`**: when the vault holds no `cloud_api_token` and does hold `cloud_install_token`, it runs the same registration first and asks the SCM to start only after it succeeded (the first start); with an API token there it starts as today; with neither it starts as today and the service logs point 6's line. So "first start" is the first `service start`, as the issue reads.
   - **In order:** the config (`cloud_url`, `cloud_ca_file`); the vault read; `cloud_api_token` there → `cloud register: already registered (cloud_api_token is in the vault); nothing was done`, exit 1 (the Worker never registers twice by itself; the operator removes the token with `vault remove` to register again); `cloud_install_token` absent → `config error: cloud_install_token is not in the vault`, exit 1; the signing key → its public key PEM (`rpworker signer public-key`'s text, which is exactly what `public_key_pem` takes) and its `key_id`; **then the vault written once with nothing changed**, before any request, so a vault this account can't write is found while the install token is still unused (`vault error: …`, exit 1); then `POST <cloud_url>/v1/workers/register` with `{"install_token", "public_key_pem", "worker_name", "version": rp::version()}` as canonical JSON, sent once (`max_attempts` 1), a 30 s timeout, at most 64 KiB of the answer read, redirects never followed.
   - **`worker_name`:** `--name`, else the machine's DNS host name (`GetComputerNameExW(ComputerNameDnsHostname)`), held to the Cloud's rule (1 to 128 characters, no control character) before anything is sent; a name that fails is a usage error naming `--name`.
   - **The answers** (the status first, the header on a 2xx, point 5): **201 with the header** → the body read with strict JSON as a closed object of exactly `worker_id` (a uuid), `api_token` (43 base64url characters) and `key_id` (64 lower-case hex), **`key_id` equal to the one the Worker computed** (else nothing is stored: `cloud register: the Cloud's answer is not this Worker's registration`, exit 4); then **one `write_vault`**: `cloud_api_token` set and `cloud_install_token` removed in the same write (whole or not at all); then `state\worker.json` (point 3); stdout `registered worker <worker_id> key <key_id>`, exit 0. **201 without the header** → nothing stored, `cloud register: the answer is not a RestoreProof Cloud's (no X-RestoreProof-API: 1)`, exit 4. **401** → `cloud register: the install token was refused (unknown, used or expired); make a new one (manage.py create-worker-token)`, exit 2, the install token left in the vault. **400** → `cloud register: the Cloud refused this Worker's public key`, exit 4. **409** → `cloud register: this Worker's key is already registered`, exit 4. **413, 422, any other status** → `cloud register: refused (http_<status>)`, exit 4. **5xx, a timeout, no connection, a TLS failure** → `cloud register: the Cloud couldn't be reached (<word>); run it again`, exit 3, the install token left. The exit codes are `rp/cli.hpp`'s (2 auth, 3 transient, 4 another refusal).
   - **Half way.** (a) The request failed before an answer: the install token is unused (the Cloud's one `UPDATE` is in the request's transaction); run it again. (b) **The answer was lost after the Cloud committed** (a timeout after the 201 left), or (c) **the vault write failed after the 201** (the pre-check passed, so only a fault between the two writes): the install token is spent and the Worker row holds this Worker's key, which `uq_worker_key_id` keeps across MSPs and revocations, so the same key can never register again. The line for (c) says exactly that: `cloud register: registered as worker <id>, but the API token couldn't be stored; revoke that Worker (manage.py revoke-worker) and register again with a new signing key and a new install token`, exit 1. (b) and (c) are recovered by hand: revoke, `python -m seeder new-signing-key` into the vault, a new install token. The token is never written anywhere else to make (c) recoverable: "shown once and stored nowhere" holds on the Worker's side too. A Cloud rule that lets an unused Worker re-register its own key is under Open.
   - **Never printed, logged or written elsewhere:** neither token reaches stdout, stderr, a log line, `worker.json`, a recording or a message; the request body is never logged (the HTTP client's rule); `--record` writes the 201 with `api_token` as `[REDACTED]` (point 4's names) and never the request body. The strings that held a token are wiped where the code owns them (the `Secrets` values, the parsed answer, the body text), as `RunSigningKey` does; what cpr copies is cpr's.

3. **`state\worker.json`: the Worker's registration, not a secret.** Written by the command after the vault, canonical JSON, `{"cloud_url","format":"restoreproof.worker.v1","key_id","registered_at","worker_id"}`, through the atomic writer, in the state folder (`%ProgramData%\RestoreProof\state`, made when absent). The service reads it at start for its first line (`scheduler started: … worker <worker_id>`, or `worker unknown`); `rpworker doctor` (W7.2) will print it. Nothing is decided on it: a missing or unreadable one is `worker unknown` and nothing else. A failed write after a stored token is `cloud register: registered as worker <id>; state\worker.json couldn't be written`, exit 1, the registration kept.

4. **The vault: two names, seven in all.** `cloud_install_token` (set by the operator with `rpworker vault set cloud_install_token` from the console or stdin, as the five are, never an argument; read and removed only by the registration) and `cloud_api_token` (written by the registration; settable by hand with `vault set` too, for a restored vault). `kSecretNames` and `Secrets` grow by two; `secret_values` lists both (six values); `read_vault` takes them (a vault holding them is refused by an older Worker by name, as any new name would be: the upgrade is one way, said in `docs/worker-config.md`); `vault list` and `config check` print `**** (set)` or `(not set)` for both. **`redact()`** gains `api_token`, `install_token`, `cloud_api_token` and `cloud_install_token` in its JSON-key and `key=value` forms. The secret audit (point 10) holds all of it.

5. **The header rule, one function** (`rp::cloud_answer_kind(const HttpResponse&)` in the new strict `rp/cloud_api.hpp`): for a **2xx**, `cloud` when `X-RestoreProof-API` (the name in any case) is there with the value exactly `1`; `not_cloud` when it is absent; `other_contract` when it has another value (named in the warning only when it is 1 to 9 ASCII digits, else "another value"). For any other status it isn't read (the C5.11 review's finding 7: uvicorn's own 400 and 503, and Caddy's 502 while `api` is down, carry none). On `not_cloud` or `other_contract`: **the upload** → the attempt is `upload_not_cloud` (a new `upload_code`, in `is_upload_error` and the manifest's vocabulary; retried by the schedule as `upload_unreachable` is), never `sent`; **the poll** → the document is not kept or read; **the heartbeat** → taken (it is the Cloud's only word of a revoked Worker and must keep going); **registration** → nothing stored. Each is one `warning` line once per kind (the service) or the command's one line.

6. **The service with the Cloud.** The service reads `cloud_api_token` from the vault at each use (the vault is already read per call), so a token registered or replaced while it runs is used at the next poll with no restart.
   - **No API token** → no poll, no upload, no heartbeat: `cloud: cloud_api_token is not in the vault; nothing is sent to the Cloud (rpworker cloud register)` once and then once an hour (`kServiceLineAgain`), the loop's last error `not_registered`; jobs from `jobs_file` (below) still run and are queued.
   - **A refused token.** A **401** from the poll or the upload → `cloud: the Cloud refused the API token (401); nothing is polled or uploaded until the vault holds another token` once; the loop keeps the SHA-256 of the refused token (in memory alone) and sends nothing with it again but the heartbeat; at every poll it reads the vault, and a token of another hash ends the state (`cloud: a new API token; polling again`). Nothing is retried with a token the Cloud refused, and nothing is lost: the queued runs stay queued. The loop's last error is `token_refused` while it lasts. The heartbeat keeps going at its interval with the same token, and its 401 is one `heartbeat failed: http_401` line once (C5.8 point 12).
   - **`jobs_file` stays as the lab's and the tests' source, and wins when set:** the loop then reads that file as today and never polls (the W4.8 to W6.3 harnesses and every loop test keep working; the upload and the heartbeat still go to `cloud_url` with the token). Without it, the source is the Cloud. `config check` prints `jobs: <file>` or `jobs: the Cloud`. The key's documentation says it is for a lab without a Cloud and not for a deployment.

7. **The poll: `GET <cloud_url>/v1/jobs`, kept in `state\jobs.json`, read by the same reader.**
   - **The request** (new `src/cloud_jobs.cpp`, not strict, the one HTTP call as `heartbeat.cpp` is): `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, `Accept: application/json`, sent once, a 30 s timeout, at most `kMaxJobsFileBytes` (1 MiB) of a 2xx read, redirects never followed. Its answer goes whole to the loop, which decides.
   - **When the Cloud is asked.** The Cloud dispatches a run once (it moves to `dispatched` in the poll's own statement) and gives it again only after the six-hour sweep; the file was offered again at every poll. So the answer is **kept**: the bytes of a 200 with the header are written whole to `state\jobs.json` (the atomic writer, replacing), then read with `rp::read_jobs` exactly as `jobs_file` is (the owner rule passes: the service wrote it; 1 MiB; five jobs; the same faults, J1 to J4, the same lines). At each poll the loop first reads `state\jobs.json`: while it names a job that **isn't settled** (J2's `skip_job` is false for it: no folder, no outbox, `sent\` or `failed\` entry, no done mark; an entry with no usable `run_id` counts as settled), the jobs run from it and the Cloud isn't asked; when every entry is settled, or the file is older than **six hours** by its last-write time (`DISPATCH_TIMEOUT`: by then the Cloud has requeued or expired what it holds), the file is removed and the Cloud is asked. A service restarted mid-document runs the rest of it; a job that ended before its run line (Veeam down) is tried again at each poll, as the file's was, until it runs or the six hours end.
   - **The answers.** **200 with the header** → kept and run as above; **a 2xx with no header or another value** → not kept, not read, point 5's warning; **a body over 1 MiB** → `jobs error: the Cloud's answer: over 1 MiB`, not kept; a kept body the reader refuses (not JSON, not the document, more than five jobs) is the reader's fault line as for a file, the word `jobs_unreadable`, and the file removed so the next poll asks again (the runs it named wait for the sweep: the line says so); **401** → point 6; **any other status** → `jobs: the Cloud answered http_<status>` once per word, the next poll as scheduled, the word `jobs_unreadable`; **a timeout, no connection, a TLS failure** → `jobs: the Cloud couldn't be reached (<word>)` once per word. An answer lost after the Cloud committed loses its runs until the sweep (six hours, at most three attempts): the cost of a dispatch made on a `GET`, the Cloud's design, under Open.
   - **J2 is unchanged** and is what makes a requeued run safe: the Cloud sends the same `run_id`, and a run the Worker already made is skipped.

8. **The upload: `Authorization: Bearer`, the answers by status, `failed\`.**
   - **The request** is W4.6's plus `Authorization: Bearer <cloud_api_token>`; `CloudUploader(http, cloud_url, token)`, built per flush from the vault. **`rpworker outbox flush` now reads the vault** for that one name: without it, `outbox error: cloud_api_token is not in the vault; nothing was sent (rpworker cloud register)`, exit 1, nothing tried and no attempt counted.
   - **The answers** (the table in strict `outbox.cpp`; the status alone decides; the body's `detail` is never read: C5.7 point 15 allowed logging it, and nothing gains from a Cloud text in the Worker's log):

     | Answer | The Worker |
     |---|---|
     | 202 with the header, first or repeated | `sent`, the move to `sent\`, as today |
     | any 2xx without the header, or with another value | `upload_not_cloud`, retried by the schedule; point 5's warning |
     | a 2xx other than 202, with the header | `upload_http_2xx`, retried by the schedule, as today |
     | 401 | `upload_http_401`, the attempt counted, `next_attempt_at` by the schedule; the pass stops (no other run is sent with that token); point 6's state; a new token makes every run whose `last_error` is `upload_http_401` due at once |
     | 400, 404, 409, 415, 422 | **permanent:** `upload_http_<status>`, the attempt counted, `next_attempt_at` null, then the folder moved by one rename to `failed\<run_id>`; never retried, never deleted by the Worker |
     | 411, 413, any 5xx, any other status, a timeout, no connection, a TLS failure | retried by the schedule as today |

   - **`failed\`** is a third sibling of `outbox\` and `sent\` under the root: a folder there is byte for byte what was queued but `manifest.json`, for the operator's `rpworker signer verify`. It counts under the 500 MB cap and is **never pruned**; it joins the "the outbox holds <n> MB" warning's sum. A move to `failed\` that fails leaves the run queued with `last_error` `upload_http_<status>` and `next_attempt_at` null; the next flush moves it without sending (`moved <run_id> to failed`), as an uploaded run's move to `sent\` is finished today. `OutboxHolds` gains `failed` (asked after `outbox\` and `sent\`); J2 skips it as `already failed`; `Outbox::prepare` refuses a run ID already there (`outbox error: <failed folder>: already failed`). The flush's line is `outbox error: <run_id>: refused by the Cloud (upload_http_<status>); moved to failed` on stderr; `outbox list` and `flush` end in `<n> queued, <m> sent, <k> failed`; `flush` exits 3 while a run stays queued, else 1 when a run went to `failed\` in this pass (an `outbox error`). The service logs the line as a warning, once per run, and its last error is `upload_http_<status>`.
   - **`folder_changed`** stays as W4.6 built it (no request, no attempt, the operator decides) and never goes to `failed\`: the folder is the evidence of what changed it.
   - **The heartbeat's `outbox_depth`** stays the runs under `outbox\`.

9. **The heartbeat:** `Authorization: Bearer <cloud_api_token>`, the body unchanged; `send_heartbeat(http, cloud_url, token, heartbeat)`. 204 (any 2xx) taken; the header absent or another value on a 2xx taken with point 5's warning once; **401** one `heartbeat failed: http_401` line (point 6), the heartbeat keeps going; **422** `http_422` as today; 5xx, a timeout, no connection as today. No API token: no heartbeat (point 6).

10. **The secret audit and the fixtures.**
    - **`[secret_audit]`** (`worker/tests/secret_audit_test.cpp`) gains two sentinels, an install token and an API token (43 base64url characters each, as the Cloud makes them), in its fake vault, and the paths that use them: `cloud register` (201, 401, 409, the vault write failing after the 201, `--record`), `service start`'s registration, `outbox flush` (202, 401, 409 to `failed\`, `--record`), the service's loop through a poll, an upload and a heartbeat on a fake Cloud, `vault set` and `list` of both names; everything they wrote (stdout, stderr, the log, the run folders, `outbox\`, `sent\`, `failed\`, `state\worker.json`, `state\jobs.json`, every recording) is searched for both sentinels and their shapes, as for the five. `redact`'s own tests take the four names in every form.
    - **`fixture_secret_scan.py`** gains the four names in `SECRET_KEYS` (a JSON key or `key=value` whose value isn't a placeholder is a finding); the committed trees (the new fixtures, the evidence, the wire vector) 0 findings.

The 413 and 5xx cases come from Caddy and the stack where it gives them (the `api` stopped: Caddy's 502 with no header) and otherwise are written by hand, saying so in their `source`. The recorder's `kKeptHeaders` gains `X-RestoreProof-API`, so a later `--record` keeps it. The Worker's tests serve them through `FakeHttpClient` with the test token in the placeholder's place.

A Worker test holds the file equal to what the uploader sends now, so a cpr upgrade that changes the framing fails one side or the other.

    1. Caddy in the Compose stack and its Cloud test; `curl --cacert <root> https://localhost:8443/healthz` 200 and `/v1/version` with the header.

The docs; the gates (Worker: `ctest --preset dev` whole, `run_coverage.ps1` and `coverage_gate.py --min-line 80` with every strict file at 100% line, `fixture_secret_scan.py` 0 findings; Cloud, since the Compose file and tests change: the full gate and `check_coverage.py`); the live Done-when; the build notes with the real figures.

**Reason.** The Worker has to reach the Cloud without loosening anything it already holds. TLS stays verified and `https`, so the laptop's Cloud gets a real CA and a real host name through the same `cloud_ca_file` a private Cloud would use. The vault stays writable by administrators alone, so the token is made at the console that already writes the vault, and the first `service start` is the first start. A token is never retried where it was refused. A signed run is never lost: a permanent refusal goes to `failed\` whole for the operator, a document the Cloud gave once is kept until its jobs are run, and nothing a 2xx says counts unless the Cloud's header says it is the Cloud.

**Alternatives rejected.**
- *The service writes the vault after registering:* Modify on `vault.bin`, create rights in its folder and an owner rule that takes the virtual account: a wider grant on the file every secret lives in, for one write. W7.1 may revisit it with the service account's whole ACL.
- *A second, service-writable store for the API token:* two places a secret lives, two owner rules.
- *An `http` `cloud_url` to the stack, or verification off for `localhost`:* refused by the TLS rule.
- *A self-signed certificate made by the harness (W4.6's stub):* a per-run artefact; Caddy's root lives with the stack, renews its leaf itself, and is the shape of a Cloud behind a proxy, which C5.12 will put in front of the app anyway.
- *A host name in the hosts file:* an elevated edit of a system file for nothing `localhost` doesn't give.
- *Polling the Cloud at every poll and holding dispatched jobs in memory:* a restart loses them for six hours.
- *Dropping `jobs_file`:* every loop test and the earlier harnesses use it; it wins only when set, and a deployment never sets it.
- *Logging the upload's `detail` word:* a Cloud text in the Worker's log for no decision.
- *Retrying a 401 by the schedule with the same token:* it can't succeed until the token changes.
- *Holding the token to the `cloud_url` it was registered at (`worker.json`'s `cloud_url`):* `config.json` is administrators' alone, so a changed `cloud_url` is the operator's act; the field is kept for `doctor` to show.

**Closes, from earlier entries.** "C5.5 and C5.6" point 10 (a) to (d); "C5.7" point 15 (the 4xx table, `failed\`); "C5.8" point 12; "C5.11" point 8 (a) to (d) with its review's finding 7 (the header on a 2xx alone) and finding 3's rest (the wire framing); W4.6's Open list for W5.1 (the token, the endpoint taking a bundle twice, which C5.7 does, the 4xx that never succeeds). W4.8's `folder_changed` run stays as built (kept, never sent, never moved).

**Open.**
- A Cloud rule for a registration whose answer was lost (point 2 (b)); today a new signing key.
- The dispatch on a `GET` (point 7): an answer lost after the commit costs six hours; an acknowledgement would be a Cloud change.
- `request.client.host` behind Caddy (C5.7's finding 7, C5.12).
- The ACLs of `failed\` and `state\` with W7.1; `rpworker doctor` (W7.2) reading `worker.json` and `/v1/version`.
- The plan's later 5-minute runs after the Done-when stay queued until a re-migration (no command disables a plan: C6.x).
- C5.11's finding 3 closes only if the wire vector's Cloud test passes; if `local_http_server` can't keep cpr's request whole, the build notes say so and it stays open.

**Code, tests and docs with the build.** Cloud: `cloud/docker-compose.yml`, `cloud/docker/Caddyfile`, a Compose test in `cloud/tests`, `tests/test_contract.py` (the wire vector). Shared: `shared/testdata/signing-v1/dispatched-run.wire` and `.wire.json`. Worker: `rp/secrets.hpp`, `src/secrets.cpp`, `src/vault.cpp`, `src/redact.cpp`, `src/recording_http_client.cpp`, `rp/cloud_api.hpp`, `src/cloud_api.cpp`, `rp/cloud_command.hpp`, `src/cloud_command.cpp`, `src/cloud_jobs.{hpp,cpp}`, `rp/uploader.hpp`, `src/uploader.cpp`, `src/heartbeat.{hpp,cpp}`, `rp/outbox.hpp`, `src/outbox.cpp`, `src/outbox_command.cpp`, `rp/service_loop.hpp`, `src/service_loop.cpp`, `rp/service_errors.hpp`, `src/worker_body.cpp`, `src/service_command.cpp`, `rp/cli.hpp`, `src/cli.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `tools/coverage_gate.py`, `tools/fixture_secret_scan.py`; the matching tests under `worker/tests/`, `fixtures/cloud/`; `docs/api/cloud-lab/w5.1-record/`, `docs/api/veeam-lab/w5.1-harness/`. Docs as point 12. The PR closes #66.

## 2026-10-15 — C6.8 (#184) code review: findings 1, 2, 3 and 5 of nine fixed, 4 not fixed (its premise was wrong; the real gap is the dispatch's, the owner's rule to give), 6 to 9 open; four report sentences changed (proposed)

The review of the branch `c6.8-real-data-report` (Claude Code `/code-review high`, 2026-10-15) gave nine findings. The owner asked for 1 to 5 to be fixed. 1, 2, 3 and 5 are fixed, test first; 4 is not, for the reason below; 6 to 9 stay open. Fixes 1 to 3 change what the entry "C6.8 (#184)" said the report prints, and are marked so: **the changed sentences wait for the owner's reading** (and the C6.5 reviewer's) like the entry's own; `tests/test_report_wording.py` holds them verbatim and the old Summary sentence under `RETIRED`. The by-hand run was not made again: the sample PDF is the wording before these fixes.

1. **Content counts took every item of a kind, compared or not.** A `backup_content` file the restore never brought back, or a canary nobody checked, counted under "Of those, compared by content" and earned the level 3 and 4 claims. Now `TypeCount` carries `compared`, the items found (`found` true) with `match` known, from the same one statement (`count(*) FILTER (WHERE …)`); `content_files`, `content_compared` and `file_content_compared` read it; "Client's own files tested" still counts every file sampled. A file found and differing is compared (a failed comparison). Changes point 1 of the entry (it counted by kind alone).
2. **The Method said every test sampled the client's own items.** A canary plan of one item per type takes one canary and no random item (`random_wanted = size / 2`). Now `ReportData.own_tests` counts the tests that passed or failed with an item of a kind other than `manifest`: when it is every such test, the sentence as before; when some, "In N of the tests that passed or failed, the sample included the client's own items, chosen at random from the backup's own listing."; when none, nothing; the canary sentence says "also" only after the first sentence. A month with no test that passed or failed keeps the first sentence (it describes the method and claims no test). Changes point 2.
3. **The Summary explained how files were compared in a month that tested none.** The sentence is now printed only when `own_files` is not 0, and reads "The client's own files tested are the files the tests that passed or failed sampled from the backup. A file counted as compared by content was found and compared by the SHA-256 of its content against the backup's copy; any other was compared by its name and, unless it is an Office document, its size, or was missing or not checked." (the second half follows fix 1). Changes point 4.
4. **Not fixed: the cursor's window is not the upload's.** The review said a poll during the upload's puts dispatches the plan's next run with the old cursor. True, but the window is far wider than the puts: `GET /v1/jobs` hands a Worker up to five runs at once, and a `--run-now` run beside the period's, or a requeued one, is dispatched with the plan's cursor while the first is still running on the Worker (minutes to hours). No reordering inside the upload closes that. The compare-and-set already keeps the cursor right (the second result moves nothing); the cost is a repeated canary sample. Closing it is a dispatch rule (for example, no second run of a canary plan dispatched while one is out), which changes what a Worker is given: the owner's to decide.
5. **The plan's row was locked while the objects were put.** The advance now runs after `put_all`, the route's last statement before the commit, so another upload of the same plan waits milliseconds, not the put of up to 96 MiB. A put that fails still rolls the cursor back (it never moved). Held by `test_the_cursor_moves_after_the_objects_are_put` (the order of the calls) and the existing rollback test. Changes nothing the entry said (point 11: in the upload's transaction).

Open: 6 (the template names the kinds as literals, not `data.py`'s constants), 7 (`CANARY_CURSOR_SCHEMA` in `routers/jobs.py` copies the shared jobs schema's rule), 8 (`cursor_advance` repeats `repo/plans.py`'s range rule) and 9 (`TestPlan.canary_cursor` tests three columns the CHECK makes all or none).

Build notes (local, 2026-10-15, focused runs only; the full gate was not run): `test_report.py`, `test_report_wording.py`, `test_repo_items.py`, `test_results.py`, `test_repo_isolation.py` and `test_report_checks.py` 430 passed and 2 failed on the first run: the canary sentence began with a space when no sentence came before it (fixed in the template), and the full-report test expected "each test" of a month where one of its two tests sampled a file of the client's own, which is finding 2's case (the test now expects the counted sentence). Then `test_report.py` and `test_report_wording.py` 208 passed. Coverage on `test_report.py` and `test_repo_items.py`: `app/report/data.py` and `app/repo/items.py` 100% line and branch. Two old tests changed because they held the bug: the canary-only month's sentence, and a level 4 claimed for a file never found (now a file found and differing). Nothing under `worker/` changed; no migration or OpenAPI change.

The red test (`test_a_canary_cursor_is_three_values_of_0_to_999999_or_none`, three of its six cases) showed it; every term of the second half is now `IS NOT NULL` first, so each half is true or false. `PlanRepo.create`'s rule check is the private `_cursor_in_rule` (the tenant-scope lint allows no public module function in `app/repo/` beyond its named ones).

## 2026-10-15 — C6.8 (#184): the report and the Cloud for real-data runs. The report says what the month's runs did, from the item rows the Cloud already keeps: canaries only when a test of the month sampled one, the content comparison against the backup's copy only when an item was so compared, level 3 only when an item was compared by the SHA-256 of its content; the Summary counts the client's own files tested and how many of them were compared by content ("n of m"); a sentence that a recovery time is a sample's; full item names in the Failures section held by a test; the canary opt-in on the **plan**, as three nullable cursor columns whose presence is the opt-in (`manage.py create-plan --canaries`), sent as the job's `canary_cursor` and advanced from the Worker's own signed `cursor_next` by a compare-and-set in the upload's transaction; migration `0001` edited in place; no Worker change (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written on 2026-10-15)

This entry works from issue #184, the 2026-10-14 entries "W6.3 (#183) and W6.2 (#182)" (points 6, 10 and 12 above all), its build notes, its live Done-when and its code review (finding 3 put the two interim Method sentences in), `docs/verification.md` "The Cloud's report", "The Cloud receives a bundle" and "A random file's content against the backup's copy (W6.3)", `docs/glossary.md` "Verification levels" and "Recovery time", and the code: `app/results.py`, `app/routers/results.py`, `app/routers/jobs.py`, `app/repo/{items,runs,plans}.py`, `app/repo/errors.py`, `app/report/{data,frameworks}.py`, `app/report/template.html`, `app/report/report.css`, `app/onboarding.py`, `manage.py`, `app/models.py`, `app/migrations/versions/0001_initial.py`, `shared/schemas/{jobs,result}.v1.json`, `worker/src/service_jobs.cpp`, `worker/src/worker_body.cpp`, `worker/src/sample_selector.cpp`, `tests/test_report_wording.py`, `tests/test_results.py`, `tests/results_lab.py`, `tests/test_repo_isolation.py` and `docs/api/cloud-lab/c6.5-c6.7-harness/c65-c67-live.ps1`. **What is there today, checked against the code.**

- *The Cloud already takes and stores `backup_content`* (issue step 1). `test_item.expected_kind` is `Text` with no CHECK (migration `0001`); `results.item_rows` copies `expected.items[].expected_kind` and `sha256` as sent and never reads a list of kinds; the verifier holds the result to `shared/schemas/result.v1.json` by path, which has the fourth kind since W6.3. Held today: `tests/test_results.py`'s first Done-when test posts the re-signed `signing-v1/bundle.json` and asserts its six rows, two of them `backup_content` (`report.pdf` by `bytes`, `Übersicht.docx` by `office-v1`) with their hashes; `tests/test_contract.py` posts the Worker-written `dispatched-run.json` (a run without canaries, two `backup_content` files) unchanged to 202; W6.3's live Done-when posted 14 `backup_content` rows, 202 twice. Not held: a `backup_content` item that failed (a `sha256` mismatch in a `fail` run) as a stored row and in the Failures section. **So step 1 is tests only**, and they are expected green at once (named as such in the build notes, not passed off as red-then-green).

That is enough: `expected_kind` `manifest` is a canary and only a canary (the expected-set table, `docs/verification.md`), `fields` a random mail, `metadata` a random file checked by name and size, `backup_content` a random file checked by the SHA-256 of its content against the backup's copy. No column is added to `test_item` and nothing of the result is re-read.
- *The report today.* The Method's two sentences are the W6.3 review's interim ones, true of any month ("The items of a test are a sample chosen at random from the backup's own listing; a test set up with canary items … samples some of those too." and "A canary is compared by the SHA-256 of its content. A random file is compared by the SHA-256 of the copy the backup gave of it … A random mail is compared by …"), never read by the C6.5 reviewer. The levels line is "Verification levels covered: 1, 2, 3" whenever a test passed or failed, with "; level 4 partially (files opened and read via Microsoft Graph)" when such a test sampled a file (`files_sampled`): level 3 ("Content integrity: the restored item matches its expected content (hashes and fields)", the glossary) is claimed for a month whose files were all checked by name and size. `gather` is eight reads; `ItemRepo.counts_by_type_in_period` answers `(run_id, type, count)`. The Failures section prints `item.name` whole; `report.css` lets `table.items td` break anywhere (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), and the layout test holds no text past the page.

A cursor the manifest can't take (`cursor_problem`: each type's cursor below that type's canary count, 0 for a type with none) and a manifest that isn't there both end the job before its run line, with no result; with the Cloud's jobs (W5.1), the run would then be requeued after six hours and `expired` at three attempts. The Worker computes `cursor_next = (cursor + c) mod M` per type (`sample_selector.cpp`) and signs it: a result with canaries carries `sample.manifest_sha256` and all three `sample.<mail|sharepoint|onedrive>.canary` objects (`cursor`, `cursor_next`, `wanted`, `ids`), one without carries none (the schema's two `if`/`then` rules). **Decision.**

*The report (issue steps 2 to 5).*

1. **The facts come from one changed read, not a new one: `ItemRepo.counts_by_type_in_period` groups by `expected_kind` too.** `TypeCount` becomes `(run_id, type, expected_kind, count)`, the same one statement over `period_filter` (grouped by `run_id`, `type`, `expected_kind`, ordered by the month's order, then type, then kind), so `gather` stays eight reads and `generate` stays nine, whatever the rows (the existing three-runs-and-sixty test holds it). The Test log's `mail / SP / OD` is the sum over kinds. `build` derives, **over the runs that passed or failed alone** (the `ran` runs, as the recovery times and the levels already are: an `error` is a test that could not run, and its items may never have been compared): `canary_tests` (runs with an item of kind `manifest`), `own_files` (items of type `sharepoint` or `onedrive` and kind `metadata` or `backup_content`: the client's own files, canaries never counted), `content_files` (of those, kind `backup_content`), and four flags for the Method: a canary, a `backup_content` file, a `metadata` file, a `fields` mail; and `content_compared` (an item of kind `manifest` or `backup_content`) and `file_content_compared` (such an item of type `sharepoint` or `onedrive`) for the levels line. The isolation table's `COUNTS` entry for this method stays (its answer gains a field; the two-MSP test is updated). Rejected: *a ninth read* (`ItemRepo.kinds_in_period`): the same join twice; *a `canaries` column on `test_run`* filled from `sample.manifest_sha256`: the items already say whether a canary was tested, and a run that asked for canaries and sampled none (a type of size 0) has none to name.

2. **The Method says what the month's runs did.** The sampling sentence, the targets sentence (unchanged) and one comparison sentence per kind that a test of the month used, each printed only when that kind is in the month's `ran` runs; then the levels line by the same rule. Written out in full:

   - Targets, unchanged: "A test restores each item into a restore target set aside for testing (the `restoretest` mailbox, the `RestoreTarget` library or the `RestoreTarget` OneDrive folder), reads it back through Microsoft Graph, compares it, and removes it from the target afterwards."
   - Canary, only with a canary: **"A canary is compared by the SHA-256 of its content."** (the existing sentence, now on its own and conditional).
   - Content, only with a `backup_content` file: **"A file of the client's own compared by content is compared by the SHA-256 of its content against the backup's copy, which the backup gave before the restore; for a Word or Excel document the SHA-256 is of the document's content, since the restore rewrites the rest of the file."**
   - Name and size, only with a `metadata` file: **"A file of the client's own that the backup gave no copy of is compared by its name and, unless it is an Office document, its size."**
   - Mail, only with a `fields` mail: **"A mail of the client's own is compared by its subject and received time, and by its sender's name when the backup lists one."**

   The two interim sentences of the W6.3 review go (from the template and from the wording list).

3. **The levels line by the same rule: level 3 only when an item was compared by the SHA-256 of its content.** With a `pass` or `fail` test and `content_compared`: "Verification levels covered: 1, 2, 3" (unchanged), with "; level 4 partially (files opened and read via Microsoft Graph)" (unchanged) only when `file_content_compared` (a file downloaded through Graph and hashed, an Office document opened as a package: what "opened and read" claims; a file checked by name and size is listed, not opened, so `files_sampled` goes). With a `pass` or `fail` test and nothing compared by content: **"Verification levels covered: 1, 2. No item of this period was compared by its content, so level 3 is not covered."** (this is the Done-when's "claims no content check", in so many words). With no such test: "No test of this period reached the comparison, so no verification level was covered." (unchanged). **This narrows a claim the report made before**: a month of random mails by their fields alone, or files by name and size alone, said "1, 2, 3" and now says "1, 2". The glossary's level 3 says "hashes and fields"; the report's rule is the stricter reading, since a subject and a received time are what the backup listed, not the item's content, and the issue's rule is "a month with no content comparison claims none". The glossary's row stays and gets one sentence saying the report claims level 3 only for a content hash. *The owner may choose the wider reading* (fields count for level 3); the entry recommends the strict one.

4. **The Summary counts the client's own files ("n of m").** Two rows in the Summary's facts, after "Tests run": **"Client's own files tested"** with `{m}`, and **"Of those, compared by content"** with `{n} of {m}` (a dash when `m` is 0, as the recovery times print one when nothing has a value). Below the facts, with the meaning sentences, one fixed sentence: **"The client's own files tested are the files the tests that passed or failed sampled from the backup, canaries not included; a file compared by content was compared by the SHA-256 of its content against the backup's copy, and any other by its name and, unless it is an Office document, its size."** "Tested", not "restored": in a `fail` run an item may be missing, and the count is of the files the tests sampled and checked. Mails are not counted (no content check for a mail; the Method says how one is compared). The counts are over every run of the month, not the listed 200 (the cap's rule).

The Test log's column keeps its heading.

6. **Full item names in the Failures section (the owner's decision of 2026-10-14).** Nothing changes in the code: `FailedItem.name` is the stored name whole (a mail's subject, a file's name), autoescaped, never shortened, masked or hashed. New tests hold it: a failed item with a 400-character name (spaces and none) is in both passes' HTML and in the PDF's text whole, and the layout test lays it out inside the page. This closes the C6.4 review's listed point "item names and subjects printed verbatim, so an address or a link can reach a PDF" **as the owner's rule**: they are printed verbatim by decision; `docs/verification.md` says so, and that the report is the MSP's to give its client, who owns the names.

7. **The wording list.** `tests/test_report_wording.py` takes every sentence of points 2 to 5 (and the two Summary row labels) verbatim in the same commit as the template, drops the two interim sentences, and runs each through `OVERCLAIMS` (none says "verified", "proves" or the four banned phrases; "compared" is the verb throughout). The four banned phrases test (`tests/test_report.py`) stays green unchanged. A new test renders three months and holds which sentences each prints: (a) no canary, files `backup_content` and `metadata`, random mails: no "canary" in the text, the content and the name-and-size sentences, "n of m" with its numbers, level 3 and level 4; (b) no item compared by content (files `metadata` only, mails `fields`): neither the content nor the canary sentence, "0 of m", the "1, 2. No item … level 3 is not covered." line, no level 4; (c) canaries and `backup_content`: the canary sentences with `k`, the canaries not in `m`. These are the Done-when's tests by name.

*The canary opt-in on the Cloud (issue step 6).*

8. **It lives on the plan, as the cursor itself: three nullable columns `test_plan.canary_cursor_mail`, `canary_cursor_sp`, `canary_cursor_od`, whose presence is the opt-in.** One CHECK, `ck_test_plan_canary_cursor`: all three null, or all three not null and each 0 to 999999 (the Worker's `kMaxCursor`). Null: the plan's runs have no canaries (every plan made so far, and the default). Not null: the plan's jobs carry `canary_cursor` `[mail, sp, od]`. **Why the plan and not the client:** the cursor is a rotation over a sequence of runs, and a plan's runs are one sequence (one run per period by `uq_test_run_msp_id_plan_id_scheduled_for`); a client with two plans would have two sequences reading one cursor. The opt-in sits beside the sizes it divides (W6.2: `ceil(N/2)` canaries and `floor(N/2)` random items per type with canaries, `N` random without), which are the plan's, and W6.2's entry put the choice "with the plan's sizes and the cursor". A client can then have a deep plan with canaries and a plain one without. **Why one fact and not a flag beside a cursor:** W6.2 point 10's own reason, two keys that can disagree; the job's rule is the key's presence, and the columns' rule is the same. What the client must have for it is on the Worker: `canaries\<tenant>.json`, seeded in that tenant; the Cloud can't see it, and a plan opted in without it gets runs that end before their run line (above) and expire. That is said in `docs/onboarding.md` beside the option. Rejected: *the client* (above); *a boolean and a cursor* (two facts); *one `integer[]` column*: a CHECK on an array's length and members is longer than three columns' and the sizes are already three columns; *the Cloud holding the manifest or its counts*: the Worker's file, never sent (W6.2 point 10).

9. **The CLI: `manage.py create-plan --canaries`** sets the cursor to `0,0,0` (in range for any manifest, since 0 is the Worker's rule for a type with no canaries too) and prints one more line, `canary_cursor 0,0,0`; without it the columns are null. `PlanRepo.create` takes `canary_cursor: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None` and holds each value to 0 to 999999 as a `RepoError` (`canary_cursor: not 0 to 999999`) before the database's CHECK, which `CONSTRAINT_WORDS` words the same (the table names every constraint an onboarding can meet: `tests/test_repo_errors.py`). `onboarding.create_plan` passes it; the `plan.create` audit row is unchanged (`plan:<id>`). **No command changes an existing plan's opt-in or resets its cursor**: there is no plan-update command (C6.x's "disabling a plan from a page" is open), and a plan opted in is made again to opt out. Open below. Rejected: *`--canary-cursor m,s,o`*: the operator can't know the manifest's counts, and a wrong value strands the plan's runs; 0 is always right.

10. **The job.** `app/routers/jobs.py`'s `Job` gets `canary_cursor: list[int] | None`, three items of 0 to 999999 in the response model, **left out of the document when null** (`Field(exclude_if=...)`, pydantic 2.14, so the key is absent, never `null`, which the Worker's reader refuses as a wrong kind); `job_of` fills it from `dispatched.plan` when the three columns are set. The poll's statements don't change (the plan is in the joined select already: held by the existing two-and-three statements test). `shared/schemas/jobs.v1.json` **does not change** (the key, its shape and its meaning are W6.2's); a test validates the poll's answer for an opted-in plan against it, and the existing one for a plain plan holds the key absent. `docs/api/openapi-v1.json` is regenerated (the response schema gains the optional key). **The Worker does not change**: its reader takes the key as it is (`service_jobs.cpp`, W6.2), so no `ctest` run is owed by this task; the jobs file and the Cloud's answer stay one shape.

11. **The cursor's advance rule: from the Worker's own signed `cursor_next`, by a compare-and-set in the upload's transaction.** When `POST /v1/results` files a bundle for the first time (after `RunRepo.receive` touched the row; never for the same bundle again, nor a refusal) and the result is `pass` or `fail` and carries the three `sample.<kind>.canary` objects, the route calls one new repo write, **`PlanRepo.advance_canary_cursor(msp_id, plan_id, *, sent, next) -> int`**: one `UPDATE test_plan SET canary_cursor_mail, _sp, _od = next WHERE msp_id = :msp_id AND id = :plan_id AND (canary_cursor_mail, _sp, _od) = sent`, where `sent` is the result's three `cursor` values and `next` its three `cursor_next`, answered as the row count and never read back. A pure function in `app/results.py`, `cursor_advance(result) -> tuple[sent, next] | None`, decides: `None` for an `error`, for a result without the canary objects, and for a `next` value outside 0 to 999999 (a manifest of a million canaries: the CHECK would refuse it as a 500, so the cursor is left as it is). Its rules:
    - *Why the Worker's `cursor_next`*: the Worker alone knows each type's canary count `M`; its `(cursor + c) mod M` is in range for the manifest the run used, and it is signed and verified before the Cloud reads it. The Cloud never computes a cursor.
    - *Why the compare-and-set*: two runs of one plan can be out at once with the same cursor (a `--run-now` run beside the period's, a requeued run); the first result advances the cursor, the second's `sent` no longer matches and it touches nothing, so the cursor never moves twice for one rotation step or back to an older one. A plan opted out meanwhile (null) never matches either. 0 rows is never an error.
    - *Why `pass` and `fail` alone*: those tests compared the canaries they sampled; an `error` run's canaries may never have been compared, so the next run takes them again. A run whose sample failed before the canaries were drawn has no canary objects either way.
    - *What it costs*: one statement more for a canary result's first upload, none otherwise; no audit row (the rotation is the system's own state, like the heartbeat's columns, and the run's stored `result.json` records `cursor` and `cursor_next` signed); it commits or rolls back with the run's rows and objects (a failed put rolls it back with the rest).
    - `advance_canary_cursor` goes in `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`'s writes (with A's `msp_id` it never moves B's plan: 0 rows), and the tenant-scope lint sees nothing new outside `app/repo/`.

12. **The migration.** Migration `0001` is edited in place, as the project does: the three columns on `test_plan` and `ck_test_plan_canary_cursor`; `app/models.py` the same; `alembic check` clean on the stack. **A database that ran the old `0001` needs `alembic downgrade -1` and `upgrade head` once** (`docs/testing.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), and the stack's `api` and `scheduler` need `--build`.

*The rest.*

13. **The sample PDF and the by-hand run.** `docs/api/cloud-lab/c6.5-c6.7-harness/c65-c67-live.ps1`'s `-Bundle` default becomes the kept W6.3 bundle, `C:\ProgramData\RestoreProof\c57\550fe89b-f96e-48e4-b902-bf7db53a7278` (24 items: 10 `fields` mails, 14 `backup_content` files, no canary), and its text calls it the kept W6.3 bundle. The SQL-made September month gets item rows of kinds a run without canaries has (each SQL run some `fields` mails, `backup_content` files and one `metadata` file; the fail's two unmatched items one of them a `backup_content` file mismatched on `sha256`), so the final report's Summary has a real "n of m". New checks in the harness, on the PDFs' text: September's names no canary, prints its "n of m" and the content sentence; the current month's interim report (the real bundle) prints "14 of 14" and names no canary. The harness is run once on the finished code (about six minutes; it re-migrates the stack's database, restarts the scheduler and replaces `c6.4-sample-report.pdf` and `c6.5-c6.7-done-when.txt`), and the owner reads the new sentences in that PDF: that reading is its own dated entry in this log (C6.5's form), and #184's last box.

14. **The docs.** `docs/verification.md` "The Cloud's report" (the Summary's two rows and sentence, the Method's rule per kind, the levels rule, the recovery sentence, full names as the owner's rule) and "The Cloud receives a bundle" (the cursor's advance), the jobs file's text in `docs/worker-config.md` (the Cloud sends `canary_cursor` for a plan opted in); `docs/testing.md` (the new tests, the harness's checks, the downgrade note); `docs/onboarding.md` step 5 (`--canaries`, and the Worker's `canaries\<tenant>.json` it needs); `docs/glossary.md` ("Canary item": the plan's opt-in on the Cloud; "Verification levels": the report's level 3 rule; "Canary cursor": what it is and how it moves); `CLAUDE.md` (Status, the open items, the code map, the Reports and Dispatch rules); the build notes here.

15. **Build order, test first at every step; each step's tests and code one commit once the owner says "approved".** (1) Step 1's tests through `POST /v1/results` (a `fail` with a `backup_content` item mismatched on `sha256`, stored and in the Failures section as "mismatch"; a run without canaries' rows), expected green at once. (2) The report: `TypeCount` by kind, `build`'s facts, the Method and levels, the Summary's rows and sentences, the recovery sentence, the Failures full-name tests, the wording list, the three months of point 7 (red first: the new sentences are absent). (3) The plan's cursor: the migration and the model, `PlanRepo.create`, `CONSTRAINT_WORDS`, `onboarding`, `manage.py create-plan --canaries`, the job's `canary_cursor`, `docs/api/openapi-v1.json` regenerated. (4) The advance: `results.cursor_advance`, `PlanRepo.advance_canary_cursor`, the route's call, the isolation row; tests on the re-signed `signing-v1/bundle.json` (a result with canaries: its `cursor` set to the plan's and `cursor_next` read back; the same bundle again moves nothing; a stale `sent` 0 rows; an `error` and a result without canaries move nothing; a `next` over 999999 moves nothing and is never a 500; a failed put rolls the cursor back). (5) The docs and the harness, the by-hand run, the sample PDF. (6) The gates, run locally, their figures in the build notes: in `cloud/`, `uv run --locked pytest --cov=app --cov-branch --cov-report=json:coverage.json --cov-fail-under=80` then `tools/check_coverage.py` (every guarded file 100% line and branch: `app/report`, `app/repo`, `app/results.py` are touched), with Postgres from Compose and GTK3's `bin` on `PATH`; `python worker/tools/fixture_secret_scan.py` 0 findings; `ctest` not run (no Worker code changes; said so, not implied); a run cut short is reported as cut short. Then the PR, `Closes #184`, not merged until the owner says so.

**Reason.** The report's claims should follow what the month's tests did, and the Cloud already holds the one fact that says it, each item's expected kind; a fixed paragraph either over-claims (a content check the month didn't have) or names canaries a client never opted into. The "n of m" makes the content check's reach visible on the first page, and its zero is as plain as its fourteen. The plan's cursor makes the opt-in the Cloud's to decide and send, as W6.2 meant, and taking the next cursor from the Worker's signed result keeps the one party that knows the manifest the one that does the arithmetic.

**Alternatives rejected.** *A ninth read or a run-level canary column* (point 1). *Level 3 for fields and names* (point 3: the owner's to choose otherwise). *"Restored" in the Summary's label* (point 4: a missing item was not). *The opt-in on the client, a flag beside a cursor, an array column, the Cloud computing `cursor_next`* (points 8 and 11). *Advancing at dispatch*: a run that never reports would skip its canaries for good, and two polls would advance twice. *Advancing on any result*: an `error`'s canaries may never have been compared. *A `--canary-cursor` option* (point 9). *Changing `jobs.v1.json`* (point 10: the key is W6.2's already).

**Open, before the build.** (a) The owner's choice in point 3 (the strict level 3, recommended). (b) The owner's choice in point 8 (the plan, recommended, or the client). (c) A command to opt an existing plan in or out, or to reset its cursor after a manifest was seeded again with fewer canaries (a cursor the new manifest can't take strands the plan's runs, which expire): **not built here**, recommended with C6.x's plan page; the C6.6 open items get it. (d) The new sentences wait for the owner's reading of the fresh sample PDF, and the C6.5 reviewer's (W6.3's interim sentences were never read and go). Not here: findings 11 to 14 of the W6.3 review; a body check for random mails; `office-v2`; the Worker's W5.1.

## 2026-10-14 — W6.3 (#183) and W6.2 (#182) code review: findings 1 to 10 of fourteen fixed, 11 to 14 open; the report's Method says what a run without canaries tests (proposed)

The review of the branch `w6.2-w6.3-real-data` (Claude Code `/code-review xhigh`, 2026-10-14) gave fourteen findings. 1 to 10 are fixed on the owner's word, test first, and finding 3 (the report's wording) in this branch rather than with C6.8, also on the owner's word; 11 to 14 stay open. Two fixes change what the entry "W6.3 (#183) and W6.2 (#182)" said, and are marked so: finding 4 changes point 5's warning message, and finding 6 adds one rule to `result.v1` (in place, before any result of this branch is kept: no valid result changes, the shared vectors are unchanged). The live Done-when was not run again: its kept evidence (`docs/api/veeam-lab/w6.3-*`) is of the code before these fixes, and its `content_export` message is the old one.

1. **`--record` wrote an export's bytes into the fixture folder.** The connector's Veeam client was recorded as `content`, so a UTF-8 file's text went into `<dir>/veeam/NNN-POST-…save.json`, against point 8. Now `RecordingHttpClient` takes a rule per request (`BodyRule`), and `record_connector` (moved to `src/run_pipeline.hpp` with it) records Veeam's exchanges by `veeam_recorded_body`: a `POST …/Documents/…/save` as `digest`, every other as `content`. Held by `recording_http_client_test.cpp` (the wrapped maker writes a sentinel file's text nowhere, keeps the request body, the size and the hash).
2. **Export time counted as recovery time.** `restore` and `recovery` began before `restore_sample`, which now holds up to 15 minutes of exports, so `timings.spans.recovery`, the Cloud's `recovery_ms` and the report's recovery times held them. Now `StepTimer::delay_start` moves the start of `restore` and `recovery` later by `RestoreResult::content_time`, held to the restore's own span (a connector's longer measure makes `restore` 0, never a clock that went back), and the restore line's elapsed time leaves them out too. A `restore_sample` that throws hands back no time, so its stopped spans keep the exports (rare: the exports end before the first restore request). Held by `step_timer_test.cpp` and a `restore_command_test.cpp` case on the harness's 123 s tick.
3. **The report's Method described the old test.** It said every test samples canaries and that a random file is compared by name and size, where W6.2 made canaries an opt-in the Cloud never sends and W6.3 compares a random file with the backup's copy. The two sentences are now true of any month, with or without canaries (the Cloud does not yet know which, C6.8's work): "The items of a test are a sample chosen at random from the backup's own listing; a test set up with canary items, seeded in the tenant for this purpose and whose content is known in advance, samples some of those too." and "A canary is compared by the SHA-256 of its content. A random file is compared by the SHA-256 of the copy the backup gave of it before the restore (for a Word or Excel document, of the document's content, since the restore rewrites the rest of the file), or, when the backup gave no copy, by its name and, unless it is an Office document, its size. A random mail is compared by its subject and received time, and by its sender's name when the backup lists one." `tests/test_report_wording.py` holds both verbatim; **they wait for the C6.5 reviewer's reading** like the review's other new sentences; the sample PDF `docs/api/cloud-lab/c6.4-sample-report.pdf` is the old wording until the C6.6 harness runs again.
4. **The `content_export` warning claimed a size check that never ran.** A docx or xlsx carries no size expectation, and an `invalid_package` file was exported. The message is now `<n> of <m> file(s) couldn't be compared with the backup's own copy (<word> <k>, ...): <s> checked by name and size alone, <t> by name alone` (point 5 said `couldn't be exported from the backup and were checked by name and size alone (...)`); `shared/testdata/result-v1/cases.json`'s one warning case carries the new text (a message the schema does not read).
5. **One export's 401 cost the run's whole content check.** `export_document` kept the token Veeam refused, so after a REST restart every export left was sent with it and refused. Now an empty 401 drops the token it was sent with, unless another caller replaced it meanwhile, and the next request signs in afresh; the export itself is still never resent (point 1). Held by three `veeam_client_test.cpp` cases (the next export signs in; a 401 with a message keeps the token; a token already replaced stays), and `veeam_m365_export_test.cpp` now expects the restore request after a 401 to sign in.
6. **A `metadata` file marked `exported` passed both checks.** `inconsistency()` now refuses it ("is metadata but its export gave its bytes") and `result.v1` has one more rule (`export` `exported` requires `expected_kind` `backup_content`), with the case `expected-metadata-export-exported` (invalid) in `shared/testdata/result-v1/cases.json`, read by both builds.
7. **`content_export` was "not reported" when nothing was asked.** Point 7 says `null`. The span is now reported only when the pipeline asked for an export (after the restore, or as not reported on a stop after the restore began), so a run that asked for none has it not run. The tables of five tests changed from "not reported" to "not run"; the shared vectors asked for exports and are unchanged.
8. **`canaries` defaulted to true.** `SampleRecord::canaries` and `ExpectedSet::canaries` now default to false, as a run does, and each `to_json` refuses `canaries` with an empty `manifest_sha256` (`std::logic_error`); the tests that build a canary record by hand say so.
9. **The replay lab named the manifest by the tenant as written.** `Replay::copy_manifest_for` lowers it, as the pipeline does, and the constructor uses it. Not shown by a failing test: NTFS finds the file in either case.
10. **No manifest was worded as an empty one.** `cursor_problem(nullptr, …)` now says `the <kind> cursor must be 0: the run has no canaries`.

Open: 11 (`want_content` on the selectors, with the hand-written `==` it forced; a set of indexes on `RestoreSpec` would keep `= default`), 12 (the "counts by word" text built twice, in `content_exports_line` and the warning), 13 (`ContentExport::size_bytes`, `ms` and `ExportAnswer::error_code` filled and never read, and no check of `size_bytes` against the digest's size) and 14 (the pipeline copies the selectors' names for `ContentHasher`; `content_rule`'s `name.size() > 5` repeats `ascii_ends_with_i`).

Build notes (local, 2026-10-14): `ctest --preset dev` 2245 tests, 2231 passed, 13 live tests skipped, 1 failed: `the shared result documents validate as they say`, whose pinned count of cases (229) the run's binary predated; both sides now pin 230 (171 invalid), and `rptests "[result_schema]"` passed after the rebuild (19 cases). The folder-permission test that fails on `main` on this laptop passed this time. Coverage was not run. Cloud, focused runs only (the full gate was not run): `test_report_wording.py` and `test_results_vectors.py` 118 passed, `test_report.py` 131 passed, `test_result_schema.py` 236 passed and `test_verify_bundle.py` passed. `fixture_secret_scan.py` 0 findings.
