## 2026-10-14 — W6.3 (#183) and W6.2 (#182): the content check of a real file against the backup's own copy, and runs without canaries. A fourth expected kind `backup_content` (the exported bytes' SHA-256 for a plain file, `office-v1` for a docx or xlsx, never bytes for an Office file), made by the connector inside its own explore session before the restore POST and recorded before anything is compared; a file the export can't give stays `metadata`, counted and named, never a `fail` or an `error` of its own; a run needs no manifest, canaries are an opt-in the job or the command line names, the whole sample is random items otherwise, and one Worker serves two tenants; `result.v1` changes in place in one edit, every result signed before invalid; one PR, `Closes #183` and `Closes #182` (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written on 2026-10-14)

Built together on the branch `w6.2-w6.3-real-data` from `main` at `09d2dc3` (the merge of W6.1). They are the second and third of the four tasks of the owner's decision of 2026-10-14 (after Q6.1): test real data only by default, check a real file's content against the backup's own copy, keep canaries as an opt-in, keep full item names in the report's Failures section; W6.1's spike (`docs/api/veeam-notes.md` §12) answered **go, with limits** (§12.5), and this entry builds under those limits. C6.8 (#184, the Cloud's side: the kind in the item rows, the report, the jobs the Cloud dispatches for an opted-in client) is not part of this and comes after. This entry works from the two issues, the W6.1 entries, the W3.1 entry of 2026-10-01 (where `backup_content` was deferred: no `office-v1` in C++ then, no real files in the lab, and "it makes the builder depend on `restore_sample`"), `docs/verification.md`, `docs/worker-config.md`, `shared/schemas/result.v1.json`, `shared/testdata/result-v1/cases.json`, `rp/connector.hpp`, `expected_set.hpp`, `checker.hpp`, `sample_selector.hpp`, `canary_manifest.hpp`, `run_status.hpp`, `src/run_pipeline.cpp`, `src/job_rules.hpp`, `src/veeam_m365_connector.cpp` and `worker/tests/export_spike_live_test.cpp`.

**Done when, restated.** W6.3 (#183): a live run in the lab restores real SharePoint and OneDrive files and reports them `backup_content`, verified by hash; a test with one byte changed in the restored copy is `fail` for that item; a test whose export fails is not `fail`; the result verifies in C++ and Python and the Cloud takes the bundle (202). W6.2 (#182): parametrised tests show that a job without canaries samples N random items per type and none is refused for a missing manifest; a job with canaries samples as today; two jobs of two tenants run on one Worker; the result of each validates and verifies in C++ and Python. W6.2 is not released without W6.3: a run of random items alone checks no file content.

**What is there today, checked against the code.** A random file is `metadata`: its name and, outside the Office family SharePoint rewrites, the size Veeam lists; nothing of its content (`expected_set.hpp`; `docs/verification.md` "The expected set"). The connector's `restore_sample` (`veeam_m365_connector.cpp`, `RestoreRun::run`) resolves every type first, each in an explore session of its own (`TypeWork::explore`, the items as `Resolved{container, id, name, document}` with Veeam's document object, its `sizeBytes` included), and only then sends the restore POSTs, one per type; so between the resolution and the first POST the connector holds every document's Veeam ID in an open session, which is exactly where §12.5 wants the export. `VeeamClient` has no octet-stream call: `get_json` refuses a 2xx that isn't JSON, `post_restore_once` is the one single-send POST and reads a `sessionId`. The spike sent `POST …/Documents/{id}/save` with `{"asZip":false}`, `Accept: */*`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, one attempt, a 120 s timeout and `max_body_bytes` 64 MiB, and held the answer to 200 `application/octet-stream` with `Content-Length` equal to the listed `sizeBytes` (`export_spike_live_test.cpp`, `export_document`). The recorder keeps a body as `content`, `digest` or `base64` (`recording_http_client.hpp`), and `FakeHttpClient` serves a `base64` fixture's bytes and refuses a `digest` one; the spike's `w6.1-recording/export/` is digests, so no export fixture can be replayed from it. The sampler takes `ceil(N/2)` canaries and `floor(N/2)` random items per type and the pipeline always loads `seed-manifest.json` beside the config (`run_pipeline.cpp` line 1373, `kManifestFile`); `choose_sample`, `build_expected_set`, `check_manifest_targets`, `cursor_problem` and the client check's `check_manifest_tenant` all take a `CanaryManifest` by reference, so today no run exists without one, and a Worker with two tenants can't serve both from one file whose `tenant_id` is held to the profile's. The `rp-canary-` prefix is refused by the lister (`veeam_candidates.cpp`) and the sampler (`sample_selector.cpp`) as a rule of their own; the manifest's list IDs, subjects, names and OneDrive folders are the query's `exclude`, built from the manifest. The job's `canary_cursor` is optional and the Cloud sends none (C5.6). `result.v1` requires `sample.manifest_sha256`, `expected.manifest_sha256`, each type's `sample.<kind>.canary` object, and the three counts in `expected.counts` and `status.verified`. The kept C5.7 bundle the three Cloud by-hand harnesses upload (`C:\ProgramData\RestoreProof\c57\…`, outside the repository) was signed under that schema.

**Decision.**

*W6.3, the content check.*

1. **The export is the connector's, inside `restore_sample`, between the resolution and the first restore POST.** The neutral header (`rp/connector.hpp`, no Veeam word) gets: on `SharePointSelector` and `OneDriveSelector` a flag `want_content` (default false; the pipeline sets it, point 4, on a random file whose name has a content rule, never on a canary and never on a mail); on `RestoreSpec` a `content_sink` (an `IContentSink*`, one call `on_content(kind, index, bytes)` per exported file, the caller's, so the connector moves bytes and keeps nothing, and knows no hash rule) and `content_max_bytes` (default `connector::kMaxContentBytes`, 64 MiB, held equal to `rp::graph::kMaxDownloadBytes` by a test: the read-back's cap, so a file the export may give is one the read-back can take); on `RestoreResult` a `content` list, one `ContentExport{kind, index, outcome, size_bytes, ms}` per selector that wanted content, in spec order, and `content_time`, the exports' span on the connector's steady clock (point 7). The outcomes, fixed words: `exported` (200 `application/octet-stream`, the bytes as many as Veeam listed for the document, the sink took them), `refused` (any other status, a 401 included: no resend of any kind), `no_answer` (a transport failure or the timeout), `size_mismatch` (the bytes aren't the listed `sizeBytes`; with no listed size the export's own count stands), `over_cap` (more than `content_max_bytes`: the body is cut at the cap and dropped), `not_in_backup` (the item wasn't resolved, Q3.1's own outcome: never asked), `budget` (point 2's run budget spent: never asked). An item that wanted content and isn't in `content` is the connector's bug, `error internal` (R1). **The Veeam side**: `VeeamClient::export_document(path, timeout, max_bytes) -> ExportAnswer{status, content_type, body}`: `POST /v8/RestoreSessions/{session}/Organization/Sites/{siteId}/Documents/{id}/save` and `…/OneDrives/{oneDriveId}/Documents/{id}/save`, body exactly `{"asZip":false}` (never `true`: §12.4, a ZIP of the same bytes), `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, **`Accept: */*`, as the spike sent it and was answered** (`application/octet-stream` was not tried live; the answer's type is held, not the request's), the token taken first as `post_restore_once` takes it, then **one `IHttpClient::send` with `max_attempts` 1 and `retry_on_status` off, never resent, after a 401 neither**, `max_body_bytes` the cap. `RestoreRun::run` calls it per resolved file item with `want_content`, in the type's own explore session, after every type is resolved and before the first restore POST, for SharePoint from the item's site and for OneDrive from its OneDrive as the restore body names them; a session the export finds gone is `refused` for that item and the restore goes on as it would (the restore's own call finds out). The sink is called on the connector's thread, with the whole body, once per `exported` item; a sink that throws ends `restore_sample` before any POST with a `connector::Error` ending in `kNothingRestored` (an `error internal`, the Worker's own fault). Why inside `restore_sample` and not a connector call of its own: the document IDs are found there and nowhere else (a separate call would resolve every item a second time, in a second session), and a session of its own would need its own Stop before the restore's preflight, which refuses while any session of the account is `Working`, and a Stop Veeam hangs on (seen 2026-09-30, 2026-10-01 and twice in W6.1) would then end the run before the restore. Why the sink and not hashes from the connector: the rules (`bytes`, `office-v1`, by name) are the verification layer's one list (point 3), and a connector that returned `office-v1` would hold a second copy of it.

2. **Time and size.** One attempt per file, `kContentExportTimeout` 60 s (§12.4 saw 0.5–1.5 s and one 9–15 s export per run; the owner's floor is 15 s), and one budget for the run's exports together, `kContentExportBudget` 15 minutes on the connector's clock: once spent, the remaining items are `budget` and nothing more is asked, so a Veeam that stops answering costs a run at most the budget and never 100 × 60 s per type. The sample's files are at most 64 MiB each by `CandidateLimits::max_file_bytes` already, so `over_cap` is a listing that lied or a body longer than listed. No export is retried, ever: §12.1 shows the call writes nothing in the tenant, but a second send is a second Veeam job on a session a restore is about to use, and the item has a kind without it.

3. **The fourth expected kind, `backup_content`, and its rule by name.** `ExpectedKind::backup_content`: a random file (`source` `random`, a `key`), its `name`, its `sha256` and `sha256_rule`, and for a `bytes` file its `size_bytes` (the export's byte count, which is Veeam's listed size by point 1); for an `office-v1` file no size (SharePoint rewrites it, §12.3's 19,995 → 22,594). The rule by name, one function in the verification layer (`verification::content_rule(name) -> optional<ContentRule>`): `bytes` for every name but the rewritten Office family (`rp::is_rewritten_office_file`), `office-v1` for `.docx` and `.xlsx` exactly (what `rp::office_v1_sha256` reads), **none** for `.docm`, `.dotx`, `.dotm`, `.xlsm`, `.xltx`, `.xltm`, `.xlsb`, `.pptx`, `.pptm`, `.potx`, `.potm`, `.ppsx`, `.ppsm`, `.doc`, `.xls` and `.ppt`: those are never asked for (no export) and stay `metadata` by name, the word `no_rule`, until a rule exists for them. The pipeline's sink hashes each body as it comes (`rp::sha256_hex`, and `rp::office_v1_sha256` for the two Office types; an `OfficeContentError` is kept, never thrown) and keeps the digests by kind and index; the expected set is **built before the restore as today** (`build_expected_set`, every random file `metadata`) and **raised to `backup_content` from the restore result's `content` and the digests, before the read-back and the check** (`verification::add_backup_content(ExpectedSet&, const RestoreResult&, const ContentDigests&)`, pure): an `exported` item whose digest by its rule is there becomes `backup_content`; an `exported` docx or xlsx `office-v1` refused is `invalid_package` and stays `metadata`; every other word stays `metadata`. The function refuses (`std::logic_error`) an export for an index that isn't a random file of the set, a digest without its export, or a kind other than `metadata` to raise. So the expectation still comes from the backup, never from what the read-back finds, and it is on record (the result's `expected`) before the check runs. The W3.1 reason for deferring ("it makes the builder depend on `restore_sample`") is answered by the two steps: `build_expected_set` doesn't change its inputs, and `add_backup_content` takes the restore's result as a value.

4. **Which items ask for content.** `want_content` is set on every random file whose `content_rule(name)` is one (the pipeline, right after `choose_sample`, from the selection's random candidates; a canary's hash is the manifest's, so a canary never asks; a mail has no export). The expected item carries the word under a new key `export` (`exported`, `no_rule`, `refused`, `no_answer`, `size_mismatch`, `over_cap`, `invalid_package`, `not_in_backup`, `budget`) for every random file, and no `export` key for a canary or a mail; `expected.counts` and `status.verified` count the four kinds. `rpworker test` prints one line after the restore's tables, `content exports: <exported> of <asked> file(s) exported from the backup (<word> <n>, ...)`, and its table's EXPECTED column says `backup_content`.

5. **An export's own fault is never a `fail` and never an `error`.** A random file whose export gave nothing is checked as today, by its name and the size Veeam listed (`metadata`), and the status table (`rp/run_status.hpp`) gets **no new row and no new code**: a `backup_content` item is `match`, `mismatch`, `missing` or `error` like any other, I1 to I5 and R1 to R8 unchanged, so **one byte changed in the restored copy is a `mismatch` on `sha256`, *failed* by I5, and the run is `fail` by R5** with the item listed. When every export failed, the table says what it says of a run of `metadata` items: every name and size right is `pass`, with `verified.backup_content` 0 and the words in `expected.items[].export`; nothing of the content was checked, and the result says so in two places. So that this is never silent, one new warning, `content_export`, the sixth of `warning_codes()` (at the end, so every result signed before stays valid for this enum): its indexes the random files whose export failed (`refused`, `no_answer`, `size_mismatch`, `over_cap`, `invalid_package`, `budget`; not `no_rule`, which is the rule, and not `not_in_backup`, which the restore result names), its message `<n> of <m> file(s) couldn't be exported from the backup and were checked by name and size alone (<word> <k>, ...)`. R8's message becomes `<n> of <n> item(s) verified: manifest <a>, fields <b>, metadata <c>, backup_content <d>`; `RunVerdict` gets `verified_backup_content`. Infrastructure is never `fail`: an export that failed is a weaker check, not a missing item, and the backup's own status never decides.

6. **The result, both verifiers, the vectors (one edit with W6.2's, point 12).** `expected_item.expected_kind` gets `backup_content` (at the enum's end); the item's rules in the schema: `backup_content` only for a random file with a `key`, `name`, `sha256`, `sha256_rule` `bytes` or `office-v1`, no `canary_id`, no mail field, `size_bytes` only with `bytes`; `export` an enum of the nine words, allowed on a random file alone (`metadata` or `backup_content`), required on neither (a result written afterwards has no items); `expected.counts` and `status.verified` require `backup_content`; `status.warnings[].code` gets `content_export`; `timings.spans` requires `content_export` (point 7). `to_json(ExpectedSet)` refuses an item whose fields don't back the kind, as it refuses the other three. The embedded copy in rpcore follows the file at build; `rpworker signer verify` and `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` change nothing of their own (they validate the schema and read no kind); the shared documents are rewritten by the hidden `[.write_shared_*]` cases: `result-v1/valid.json` (a run of the Worker's tests with two real-looking files as `backup_content`, one `bytes`, one `office-v1`, one file `no_rule`, no person named), `cases.json` (the new cases: `expected-backup-content-without-its-hash`, `-as-a-canary`, `-for-a-mail`, `-with-the-mail-rule`, `-office-v1-with-a-size`, `expected-export-unknown-word`, `expected-export-on-a-canary`, `counts-without-backup-content`, `verified-without-backup-content`, `warning-content-export` valid, `spans-without-content-export`, and W6.2's below), `signing-v1/bundle.json`, `closed-folder.json` and `dispatched-run.json` (its two files `backup_content`: the Cloud's contract test posts it unchanged to 202), `timestamp-v1` where it holds a result. **The format changes in place, as W4.2 and W4.3 changed it, and every result signed before is invalid under the new schema** (four required keys): no pilot bundle exists, the Cloud's stored results are never re-validated, and a verifier that holds the old schema answers `result_schema` for a new result, which is why `--schemas` travels. The one casualty is the kept C5.7 bundle the three Cloud by-hand harnesses upload: **the W6.3 live run's bundle becomes the kept bundle** (its path the harnesses' `-Bundle` default; `docs/testing.md`), and those harnesses are run again with it when their next task runs them, not here. Rejected: new keys optional so that old results stay valid: `counts` "always has all kinds so a report never claims more than was checked" is the W3.1 rule, and a reader taking a missing count as 0 is a second rule nobody wrote.

7. **`items.csv` and the timings.** `items.csv`: `expected_kind` `backup_content`, `sha256_rule` and `expected_sha256` its rule and hash, and **`found_sha256` the compared copy's hash by that rule**, as for a canary; the W4.2 sentence "a found hash only for a canary" becomes "for an item that carries an expected hash", since W6.3 puts a real file's hash in the result by the owner's decision, and a hash is what shows the match (the result's `check` object still writes no found value; a mail's body hash is still never written). One new span, `content_export` (the twelfth, `kSpanCount` 12, after `restore_wait` in the enum's order and the schema's list): the exports' time inside `restore`, reported from `RestoreResult::content_time` as `restore_submit` and `restore_wait` are, `null` when nothing was asked; `rpworker test`'s timings table shows it. Random mails stay `fields`: no body check (a spike of its own if wanted).

8. **Fixtures first.** `VeeamClient::export_document` and `RestoreRun`'s export step are built against `FakeHttpClient` fixtures: the JSON exchanges (the sessions, the site and OneDrive listings, the documents) are W6.1's recorded ones under `docs/api/veeam-lab/w6.1-recording/veeam/` copied to `worker/tests/fixtures/veeam/export/` (scrubbed already; `fixture_secret_scan.py` 0 findings), and **the export bodies are `base64` fixtures the tests write themselves** (a txt, a png-shaped byte string, a docx and an xlsx `rp::office_v1_sha256` reads, each under 2 KB, no tenant file: the spike's bodies are digests and a client's file never goes into a fixture), served by path with the status, type and `Content-Length` each case needs: 200 with the listed size; 200 with another size; 200 `application/json`; 404; 500; 401; a body over the cap; a timeout and a dropped connection through the fake's transport failures; a docx whose package `office-v1` refuses; a session gone. `--record` records the product's exports as `digest`, as it records every download (`RecordedBody::digest`), so a run's recording never holds a client's bytes.

*W6.2, runs without canaries.*

9. **A run needs no manifest.** `SampleSelector::select`, `choose_sample`, `build_expected_set`, `cursor_problem`, `check_manifest_targets` and the client check's `check_manifest_tenant` take `const CanaryManifest*` (null: no canaries), and the pipeline loads one only when canaries are asked for (point 10). Per type, with no canaries, random wanted is **N** (the whole plan size), the draw and the keys unchanged; with canaries, `ceil(N/2)` canaries and `floor(N/2)` random items as today, a canary shortfall still not moved to the random half (W2.6). Nothing is refused for a missing `seed-manifest.json`, because nothing looks for one.

10. **Canaries are an opt-in, named by the job or the command line; the manifest is the Worker's, one file per tenant.** The choice lives **in the job**: a job whose `canary_cursor` key is there (any value in its rule, `[0,0,0]` included) runs with canaries; a job without the key runs without, which is every job the Cloud dispatches today (C5.6 sends none), so real data only is the default by the Cloud's own answer and C6.8 opts a client in by sending the cursor. For `rpworker restore` and `test`: `--canary-cursor <m>,<s>,<o>` or `--manifest <path>` asks for canaries (`--manifest` alone with the cursor `0,0,0`, `--canary-cursor` alone with the default file); neither, no canaries, and the run line says `canaries: none`. The manifest's place: **`canaries\<graph_tenant_id>.json` beside the config file** (the profile's tenant, lower case; `%ProgramData%\RestoreProof\canaries\<tenant>.json` by default), or the `--manifest` path for a command; a job can't name a path. It is held as today: `tenant_id` the profile's (the client check), no canary in a restore target, the cursor below each type's canaries (`cursor_problem`), each refused before any Veeam call with today's words; a job that asks for canaries whose file isn't there ends before its run line (`config error: canary manifest: <file>: ...`) and is offered again at the next poll, as a manifest fault is today. The lab's `seed-manifest.json` beside the config moves to `canaries\<the lab tenant>.json` by hand (one copy; `docs/worker-config.md` and `lab/README.md` say so); the live tests keep reading `lab/seed-manifest.json` from the source tree. Why the job and not the profile: the profile is the client's identity and targets, a closed object the Cloud holds as the connector's `config_json` and both sides validate against `client-profile.v1`, so a flag there is a schema change on three vector sets and the Cloud's repo for a choice that belongs with the plan's sizes and the cursor, which is in the job already; and the cursor and its flag would be two keys that can disagree. Why a file per tenant on the Worker: the manifest is what the seeder wrote for that tenant, held to the tenant by its own `tenant_id`; one Worker serving two tenants needs two, and the Cloud has no reason to hold or send 40 items of hashes in every poll. Rejected: *a Worker config key* (`canaries_for: [<tenant>]`): the Cloud couldn't see it and a result couldn't say why a client had canaries; *the manifest in the job*: above; *"a file is there" as the opt-in*: a misplaced file would silently turn a client's canaries off, and `config error` is the honest answer when canaries were asked for and can't be had.

11. **The exclusions.** For a client with canaries nothing changes: the manifest's list IDs, subjects, names and OneDrive folders are the query's `exclude`, and the sampler refuses a candidate that is a canary's. For a client without, `exclude` is empty, and the sampler's manifest checks have nothing to check. **The `rp-canary-` prefix rule stays on for every client** (the lister's and the sampler's): it names nobody's real file, and a canary left in a tenant whose client opted out (the lab, where the RestoreTest library's canaries would otherwise be candidates once the manifest's list ID isn't excluded) must not pass for real data. `RestoreTarget` and `RestoreTest` stay skipped as folders and libraries by the lister's own list. The three restore targets' rule, the TargetGuard (layer 1 per item inside `restore_sample`, layer 2 on the exact POST body), the Cleaner (the one deleter, its three targets, `ListedItem`) and the app's grants **do not change**: the export reads the backup through Veeam, never the tenant, and the sample's items go where they went.

12. **The result for a run without canaries (the one edit with point 6).** `sample.manifest_sha256` and `expected.manifest_sha256` become optional and are **left out** (never null) when the run had no canaries, and so is each type's `sample.<kind>.canary` object (its cursor, next cursor, wanted and ids are facts of a rotation the run didn't have); `random.wanted` is N; `expected.counts.manifest` 0. `SampleRecord` and `ExpectedSet` carry `canaries` (bool) so `to_json` knows what to write, and `build_expected_set` holds the record's flag to the manifest given. New vector cases: `sample-without-canaries` (valid: no `manifest_sha256`, no `canary` objects), `sample-canary-without-manifest-sha256` (invalid: a rotation without its file), `expected-manifest-item-without-manifest-sha256` (invalid), `sample-manifest-sha256-null` (invalid). The `running.json` record keeps the job as given (`canary_cursor` present or not); `Job::canary_cursor` becomes optional and the reader's rule for the key's value is unchanged; `jobs.v1.json` and its vectors change in their description only. `rpworker test`'s header prints `canaries: none` or the cursor line as today.

13. **The service path and two tenants.** `worker_body` runs a job without `canary_cursor` with no manifest: the pipeline's one path, nothing special-cased. A jobs file with two jobs of two tenants (two profiles, two organisations) runs both in turn, each under its own profile, its own targets resolved through the guard, its own client check, and, when asked, its own `canaries\<tenant>.json`; the test (`worker_body_test.cpp`, two tenants' fixtures) holds that each run's result validates and verifies in C++ (`signer verify`) and that the two folders are queued; the Python side runs the rewritten vectors. The record, the close, the hold and the outbox don't change.

14. **The docs.** `docs/verification.md`: the expected set table's fourth row and the rule by name, the `expected` object's new keys, the two-step build, the warning, the R8 message, `items.csv`'s found hash, the span, "What of the tenant the result holds" (a real file's hash is in the result now); `docs/worker-config.md`: `--canary-cursor` and `--manifest` as the opt-in, `canaries\<tenant>.json`, the jobs file's `canary_cursor` semantics, `test`'s new lines; `docs/testing.md`: the new fixtures, the live test and the harness; `docs/glossary.md`: "Sample" (the whole sample random without canaries), "Canary item" (an opt-in), "Document export" (what the product does with it), "Expected kind" if there; `CLAUDE.md`: the Status, the pipeline line, the open items; the build notes here.

15. **The live Done-when of W6.3 and its harness.** `docs/api/veeam-lab/w6.3-harness/w63-live.ps1`, in the W6.1 harness's form (an elevated VS 2022 Developer PowerShell on the Veeam server, the vault, the run folder under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RestoreProof\lab\w6.3-<stamp>\`, the evidence writer's secret check on every text, the shape check, the copy into `docs/api/veeam-lab/` last and only when every step exited 0, the cleanup in its `finally` only once the live test has started, and the service uninstalled whatever happens): (1) `rpworker graph list`: the three targets empty. (2) One new live test, `worker/tests/backup_content_live_test.cpp` (`[live][writes]`, both switches, the run mutex held throughout, the lab profile, the 14 real files of L1.8 found through `list_candidates` as the spike found them, no canary, no mail), three restores through the connector's guarded path with the Cleaner's `before_run` clean between them: **(a)** `restore_sample` with `want_content` on all 14 and the pipeline's sink, `add_backup_content`, `TargetReader` read-back, `check`, `decide_status`: 14 `backup_content` (12 `bytes`, the xlsx and the docx `office-v1`), 14 `match`, `pass`; **(b)** the same restore, then **one byte of one restored copy changed in the RestoreTarget library** before the read-back: the test resolves the library through the guard's own check first and PUTs the copy's content with one byte flipped under the Worker app's own write grant on the RestoreTarget list (`docs/security/graph-permissions.md`: `write` there is the Cleaner's grant; the PUT is test code, the one write outside the Cleaner, on a restore target only, and it widens nothing: if the grant refuses it the test stops and says so, and the owner changes the byte through the browser as the admin); then the read-back and the check: that item `mismatch` on `sha256`, `fail` with its index listed, the other 13 `match`; **(c)** the same restore with `content_max_bytes` 1: 14 `over_cap`, 14 `metadata`, 14 `match` by name and size, `pass` with the `content_export` warning naming 14 and `verified.backup_content` 0: an export that fails is not `fail`. The test prints one table per restore and writes `RP_LIVE_EVIDENCE_FILE` (hashes, sizes, names, IDs, words and times; no credential). (3) `rpworker test --mail 0 --sp 7 --od 7 --evidence <dir> --outbox <root>` with neither `--canary-cursor` nor `--manifest`: a signed, timestamped run of the 14 as `backup_content`, `pass`, queued; `rpworker signer verify` and `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` on the folder: `verified`; the W6.3 recording's exports digests only. (4) The upload to the Compose stack: `rpworker outbox flush` against the stack's `cloud_url` from the Veeam VM as C5.7's live harness did, 202, the run's row `pass` and its 14 item rows `backup_content` (the Cloud stores the kind as text and reads no list, so no Cloud code changes; the pages show the word; C6.8 gives it its sentence). (5) The cleanup and `graph list` 0 in all three targets. Evidence `docs/api/veeam-lab/w6.3-*` (the texts, the JSON, the recording's scrubbed exchanges), `fixture_secret_scan.py` 0 findings, `audit-evidence.ps1` 0 hits.

16. **Build order, test first at every step; each step's tests and code one commit once the owner says "approved".** (1) `VeeamClient::export_document` and the connector's export step with their fixtures and unit tests, no product use yet (the pipeline doesn't set `want_content`). (2) W6.2's sampler and rules without a manifest, the opt-in, two tenants on one Worker. (3) The joint `result.v1` edit: the embedded schema, both verifiers, the vectors by `rptests "[.write_shared_*]"`, `cloud/tests` on the new shape (`uv run pytest -m "not db"` at least, and `tests/test_contract.py` on the rewritten `dispatched-run.json`). (4) The rule by name, the sink, `add_backup_content`, the pipeline's `want_content`, the warning, `items.csv`, the span, the R8 message. (5) The docs. (6) The gates, run locally, their figures in the build notes: `ctest --preset dev` whole (if the low-memory guard stops it, which tests were not reached, not restarted unasked), `worker/tools/run_coverage.ps1` and `coverage_gate.py --min-line 80` (100% line on the strict files; `expected_set`, `checker` and `sample_selector` aren't strict, `run_status` and `client_check` are), `python tools/fixture_secret_scan.py`, `[secret_audit]`, and in `cloud/` `uv run --locked pytest` with the coverage gate and `tools/check_coverage.py`. (7) The harness and the live test prepared, then the owner runs the live Done-when with the builder on the Veeam server.

**Reason.** A file restored with the right name and size and damaged bytes passes today; the backup's own copy is the one expectation for a real file's content that needs no read of any source through Graph and no wider grant, and W6.1 showed the export gives the restored copy's bytes. The kind is a fourth word beside three the report already keeps apart, so a report never claims more than was checked: a run whose exports failed says `metadata` and warns. Canaries as an opt-in make the client's own data the default evidence, which is what the owner's decision asks, and a manifest per tenant is what a Worker with two clients needs; the job as the switch keeps the Cloud the one that decides what a run tests.

**Alternatives rejected.** *A connector call of its own for the export* (`IConnector::export_content`): a second resolution in a second session, and a Stop before the preflight that Veeam may hang on (point 1). *The connector hashing the bytes*: a second copy of the rule by name (point 1). *`Accept: application/octet-stream`*: not what the spike proved; the answer's type is held instead. *A retry of the export*: a second Veeam job beside a restore about to run, for an item that has a kind without it (point 2). *Bytes for an Office file*: SharePoint rewrites the package on restore (§12.3). *A rule for pptx (`office-v2`)*: a new rule with its own vectors, not this task. *`backup_content` for canaries*: the manifest's hash is older and ours. *The export's fault as `error`*: infrastructure is never `fail`, and an `error` for a weaker check would hide a restore that worked; the warning and the words say it. *The opt-in in the profile, a Worker config key, the manifest in the job, a file's presence*: point 10. *Optional new keys so old results stay valid*: point 6. *Tampering the restored copy by intercepting the read-back's bytes*: it would show the checker, not a changed copy in the tenant. *`rpworker test` for the tamper case*: it has no step between its restore and its read-back, and a test seam in the product for one live demonstration isn't wanted.

**Open, before the build.** Whether the Worker app's `write` on the RestoreTarget list lets the live test PUT one changed byte onto a restored copy (point 15 b; the owner's browser is the fallback, and nothing is widened either way). Whether Veeam lists `sizeBytes` on every document the resolution keeps (the spike's 14 had it; a document without one has no size check and its export's count stands). The lab has no pptx and no legacy Office file, so `no_rule` is shown by a unit test alone. The numbers 60 s and 15 minutes (point 2) are the owner's to change. Not here: C6.8 (the Cloud's item rows and report sentences for the kind, the cursor in the Cloud's jobs for an opted-in client), the canary cursor's column on the Cloud, a body check for random mails.

## 2026-10-14 — W6.1 code review: findings 1 to 4 of eight fixed, 5 to 8 open (proposed)

The review of the branch `w6.1-export-spike` (Claude Code `/code-review high`, 2026-10-14) gave eight findings, none in product code (the task added none). 1 to 4 are fixed on the owner's word; 5 to 8 stay open. The test is a live one: the fixes were compiled (`rptests` built) and not run live again, so the kept evidence under `docs/api/veeam-lab/w6.1-*` is the third run's, of the test before these changes; the next run of the harness replaces it.

1. **The spike could fail after the exports with nothing compared.** Sessions A and B got one Stop each and were never read again before `restore_sample`, whose preflight refuses while any session of the account is `Working`; a Stop Veeam hangs on (seen twice in this task) answered late with the session still `Working`, and the restore thread's exception ended the test with the 14 exports recorded and no read-back. Now `SessionStops::stop_all_and_wait` stops them and reads each again every 5 s until none is `Working`, sends one more Stop after 60 s (the connector's own second try, `stop_working_session`), gives up at 180 s, and the test fails there, before any restore, naming the sessions and the sweep script (`REQUIRE`); the wait is in `notes.sessions_stopped`.
2. **The overlap poll depended on the server's default order.** `GET /v8/RestoreSessions?limit=50` with no order and no start time, on a server that holds 200 sessions (the kept page is exactly 50 long), and a 1,300-line fixture per 2-second poll. Now the poll asks `startTimeFrom=<the restore's start>&orderBy=CreationTime&orderAsc=false&limit=50`, as the connector's `own_sessions` does, so the page is this run's sessions alone, newest first, whatever the server holds, and the restore session is the newest of the two.
3. **Session C could cost the restore its verdict.** It was opened right after the restore POST, inside the connector's duplicate check (restore-flow §8: every `Working` `Vesp` session of ours created from `kDuplicateFloor` (5 s) before the POST is a candidate; two candidates and the restore is polled with no verdict, or, after a POST with no answer, ends in `connector::Error`), and the test could not tell that refusal from Veeam's behaviour. Now C is opened as soon as the connector's explore session is listed (so after its preflight) and before its POST, which the browse and the certificate export put about 15 s later in the lab; the export from C is made once the restore session is listed beside it; `notes.export_during_restore.session_c_before_duplicate_window` compares C's `creationTime` plus the floor with the restore session's, and the console says, when it is false, that a refusal of the verdict below is the connector's rule. Rejected: a wait after the restore session appears until the check must be over (the POST's timeout plus three looks 10 s apart), since the SharePoint restore ran 73 s and the overlap would be missed.
4. **The harness deleted what it had refused to touch.** Step 1's refusal of non-empty targets threw, and the `finally` ran the live cleanup test on them. Now `$spikeStarted` is set only when step 2 begins, the `finally` cleans only then, and the refusal says nothing is cleaned; the header says so.

Open: 5 (the build notes' title says the Worker's suite was green locally and points 4 and 8 "as written", where 319 tests were never reached, the export sends `Accept: */*` and matches the site by id, and the harness checks evidence by shape; the owner's to reword), 6 (`docs/testing.md` says `rptests "[live][writes]"` runs all three writing tests, and the spike, last and not cleaning, leaves 14 copies for the next writing test to fail on), 7 (`ascii_lower`, `form_encode` and four `VeeamClient` calls re-implemented in the test beside `src/text_util.hpp` and `VeeamClient`'s own) and 8 (the test's canary exclusion lists lower the list ids and not the folders, where `sample_selector.cpp` folds both).

## 2026-10-14 — W6.1 (#181): the spike on Veeam's document export in admin mode. One live test, run by hand from the vault as `rp-veeam`, exports the lab's 14 real files (7 SharePoint, 7 OneDrive) from an explore session, restores the same 14 through the connector's guarded path, reads them back through Graph with the Worker's own reader, and compares: SHA-256 for pdf, txt and png, `office-v1` on both sides for the xlsx and the docx; `asZip`, the time per file, an export during a running restore, and what `office-v1` cannot read are recorded; no product code changes; the verdict for W6.3 is go, go with limits or no-go (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written on 2026-10-14)

W6.1 (#181) is built on the branch `w6.1-export-spike` from `main` at `9c1f8e3`. It is the first of the four tasks of the owner's decision of 2026-10-14: a run proves the restore of the client's own data, content included, with nothing planted in the tenant; W6.3 (#183, the `backup_content` expected kind the W3.1 entry deferred) is built only if this spike passes, and #182 and #184 follow; none of the three is started here. Done when: `docs/api/veeam-notes.md` says, with the evidence named, whether the export works in admin mode for SharePoint and for OneDrive and whether its bytes compare with the restored copy; the build notes and a comment on #181 give the verdict.

**What is known, checked against the files.** The export is `POST /v8/RestoreSessions/{id}/Organization/Sites/{siteId}/Documents/{documentId}/save` and `…/Organization/OneDrives/{oneDriveId}/Documents/{documentId}/save`, body `{"asZip": bool}`, answer `application/octet-stream` with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=…` (`docs/api/veeam-feasibility.md` §1 "Item export", §2 d). It was run once, on 2026-09-26, as the **operator** account `rpoperator`, for **SharePoint only**, on two canaries: `rp-canary-01.pdf` 925 bytes, SHA-256 equal to Graph's and the manifest's (`w1.0-d-operator-sp-save-rp-canary-01-pdf.json`); `rp-canary-02.docx` 15,690 bytes, the bytes SharePoint stored and not the 3,263-byte original, `office-v1` equal to the manifest's, and its restored copy 15,563 bytes, rewritten again by SharePoint, `office-v1` still equal (`…-02-docx.json`, `w1.0-d-operator-sp-restore-docx.json`). No file records the export as `rp-veeam` (the account the Worker signs in as, `docs/decisions.md` 2026-09-26), and none records a OneDrive export. The document object Veeam lists carries `_links` (`self`, `library`, `versions`) and no `_actions` (`w1.4-sp-document-get.json`), so the save path is built from the IDs, as W1.0 built it. The lab holds the real files of L1.8 (`lab/tenant.md` "Real data for the random sample"): 7 in the root of the RestoreTest site's default "Documents" library (`team-meeting-notes.txt`, `supplier-contacts.txt`, `project-brief.pdf`, `budget-summary.pdf`, `office-floor-plan.png`, `brand-colours-draft.png`, `room-bookings.xlsx`) and 7 in the root of alice's OneDrive (`reading-list.txt`, `travel-notes.txt`, `expense-report-march.pdf`, `course-certificate.pdf`, `holiday-photo.png`, `whiteboard-sketch.png`, `weekly-status.docx`), each under 1 MiB, none a canary, none in a restore target; they have been in every nightly point since 2026-10-03. **No pptx and no legacy Office file is in the lab**, and this spike adds none (an upload is a tenant change outside its scope), so that part of question 4 is answered from the code: `rp::office_v1_sha256` and `lab/seeder/office.py` read exactly `docx` and `xlsx` (`CONTENT_FOLDERS`), nothing else. Today a random file is compared by name and, outside the Office family, by the size Veeam lists (`docs/verification.md`, the `metadata` kind); the W3.1 entry (2026-10-01, "Alternatives rejected" and "Open") deferred `backup_content` because `office-v1` did not exist in C++ and the lab had no real files; both are there now.

**Decision.**

1. **The harness is one live Catch2 test, not product code.** `worker/tests/export_spike_live_test.cpp`, tag `[live][writes]`, ctest name `live export spike: Veeam's document export in admin mode against the restored copy`, skipped unless both `RP_LIVE=1` and `RP_LIVE_RESTORE=1` are set, run once by hand from an elevated VS 2022 Developer PowerShell by `docs/api/veeam-lab/w6.1-harness/w61-live.ps1`. It is test code under `worker/tests/`, listed in `worker/CMakeLists.txt` beside the other live tests; **nothing under `worker/src`, `worker/include` or `worker/app` changes**, so "No test, no merge" is not touched and the strict files are not touched. Why a test and not a PowerShell script: the owner's rule that secrets come from the vault only. The lab scripts (`docs/api/veeam-m365/VeeamLab.ps1`) read Credential Manager or `RP_VEEAM_PASSWORD`, and `rpworker vault` has no read command; the live tests already read the vault as the Worker does (`worker/tests/live_secrets.hpp`, `rp::read_vault`), so the password reaches memory and nothing else. Why not a `VeeamClient` method for the export: a `download` on `VeeamClient` is the right seam for W6.3 and gets its unit tests there; a spike that may end "no-go" should not leave product code behind.

2. **The account and the credentials.** Veeam: `rp-veeam` in admin mode, user name and password from the vault's `veeam_username` and `veeam_password`; the pinned TLS of every run (`veeam_ca_file` from `RP_LIVE_VEEAM_CA_FILE`, `veeam_cert_sha256` the lab's), verification never off. Graph: the Worker app's certificate from the vault (`graph_cert_pfx_base64`, `graph_cert_password`), the app that reads the three restore targets and the rest of the RestoreTest site and writes nothing but the Cleaner's deletes (`docs/security/graph-permissions.md`); **no grant is added or widened**, and if a read the spike needs is refused the spike stops and says so. The restore's credential: Veeam's own organisation app certificate, exported in memory per restore call by the connector (`rp::make_local_machine_cert_exporter`, the elevated shell), as every live restore since W2.5.

3. **The items: the 14 real files, found through the Worker's own sampler listing.** The test makes the `veeam_m365` connector through `default_connector_registry()` (the vault's secrets, the exporter, the lab profile as `client`), takes the newest restore point of the lab organisation, and calls `list_candidates` for SharePoint and for OneDrive on it: the pool is the backup's own listing of the eligible containers with the canary library, the canary folder and every `rp-canary-*` name left out by rule (W2.6), so each candidate is a real file with its full selector (`site_id`, `drive_id`, `list_id`, `folder_path`, `name` for SharePoint; `user`, `folder_path`, `name` for OneDrive) and the size Veeam lists. The test keeps the 7 + 7 whose names are exactly L1.8's (ordinal), **requires all 14 to be there** (a shortfall stops the spike before any export: the point has not got the files), and uses nothing else. Mail is out of scope and no mail is listed, exported or restored.

4. **The export, in the test's own explore sessions.** The test opens its own Veeam HTTP client (`rp::HttpClient` with the same `HttpClientOptions` the connector uses: the CA file and the pin) wrapped in `RecordingHttpClient` over a `FixtureRecorder` (point 8), signs in once (`POST /v8/token`, `grant_type=password`, `disable_antiforgery_token=true`, the password from the vault, the token kept in memory), and logs out at the end. In a session **A** (`POST /v8/Organizations/{org}/explore`, `Vesp`, the point's `backupTime` byte for byte) it reads `GET …/Organization/Sites?parentId=root&limit=1000`, takes the RestoreTest site by `url`, lists `GET …/Sites/{siteId}/Documents?limit=1000` (every document of the site, all libraries), and matches the 7 by exact name, expecting exactly one each (the canary library's names differ, so a second match is a stop, not a guess). For each: `POST …/Documents/{documentId}/save` with body `{"asZip":false}`, one attempt, a 120 s timeout, `Accept: application/octet-stream`; recorded per file: the status, the `Content-Type`, the `Content-Length` against the `sizeBytes` Veeam listed, the bytes' SHA-256, for the xlsx its `office-v1` (`rp::office_v1_sha256`), and the milliseconds. Then once, on the pdf `project-brief.pdf`, `{"asZip":true}`: the status, type, size, whether the body is a ZIP (`PK` signature), how many entries it holds, and whether the one entry's bytes equal the plain export's. Then `GET …/Documents/{documentId}` of the first file again and `GET /v8/RestoreSessions/{A}`: the session is still `Working` and browsable after the exports. A session **B** (`Veod`) the same for OneDrive: `GET …/Organization/OneDrives?limit=1000`, alice's by `url`, `GET …/OneDrives/{oneDriveId}/Documents?limit=1000` (every file, flattened), the 7 by exact name, the docx's `office-v1`. **A and B are stopped before the restore** (`POST …/Stop`, in a `finally` whatever happens; a Stop that times out is read again and sent once more, as the connector does), because the connector's preflight refuses to start while any session of the account is `Working`. What the export can touch: the request names no Microsoft 365 credential (no `applicationCertificate`, no user; the recorded body is `{"asZip":…}` alone) and Veeam answers it from the backup repository, so it cannot write to the tenant; the spike shows it rather than argues it: before session A and after session B the test lists the default library's root through the Worker app (`GET /sites/{id}/drives`, the default drive's children: ids, names, `eTag`, `lastModifiedDateTime`) and alice's OneDrive root folder's metadata (what the app may read there), and both listings are equal, and the three restore targets, listed before and after, are empty both times.

5. **The restore, through the connector's guarded path.** One `restore_sample` with a spec of the 14 selectors from point 3 (`client_ref` the lab organisation, the newest point, `RestoreTargets::from_config` of the lab config): the run mutex taken first (the test holds it from before session A to its end), the connector's preflight, its own explore sessions, `TargetGuard` per item and on the exact POST body, the certificate exported in memory, the three targets only (the RestoreTarget library and alice's `/RestoreTarget`; no mail). Expected: `succeeded`, 14 of 14, two `Success` sessions; anything else is recorded and the comparison still runs on what was restored. **An export during a running restore (question 4):** `restore_sample` runs on a thread of its own (no Catch2 assertion on it; it hands back the `RestoreResult` or an `exception_ptr`); the main thread polls `GET /v8/RestoreSessions?limit=50` every 2 s until a `Vesp` restore session of `rp-veeam` created after the start reads `Working`, then opens a session **C** (`Vesp`), exports `project-brief.pdf` once more, records the status, the hash (equal to A's) and the milliseconds, and stops C; then joins. If the restore is over before any `Working` session was seen, the test records "no overlap seen" and makes no claim. Whether the restore sessions ended `Success` with 14 restored, with that export beside them, is the answer.

6. **The read-back and the comparison, with the Worker's own reader.** After the restore: `TargetReader::list_sharepoint()` and `list_onedrive()` with `hash_items` true on the two file targets (the Worker app's token, `download_item` without it from the tenant's own host, the W3.2 path), `on_file` computing `office-v1` of the restored xlsx and docx from the bytes. Per file: the restored size and SHA-256 (`FoundItem::sha256`, rule `bytes`), and for the two Office files `office-v1`. The comparison: **pdf, txt, png: the export's SHA-256 equals the restored copy's**; **xlsx (SharePoint) and docx (OneDrive): the export's `office-v1` equals the restored copy's `office-v1`**, and whether the bytes are equal too is recorded (W1.0 saw SharePoint rewrite a docx on restore; OneDrive rewrote nothing in W3.1's check). The test prints one table (name, kind, Veeam's size, export status and ms, export SHA-256, restored size, restored SHA-256, `office-v1` export and restored where it applies, equal yes/no) and writes the same as JSON to `RP_LIVE_EVIDENCE_FILE`; it holds no credential (hashes, sizes, names, IDs and times only). **The test does not clean**: the harness runs `rpworker graph list --hash` right after it, a second tool's reading of the same copies (its `bytes` SHA-256 must equal the test's restored hashes), then the live cleanup test (`cleaner_live_test.cpp`, which takes the mutex itself) in its `finally`, then `rpworker graph list` showing 0 in all three targets; a harness that dies leaves copies the next run's clean before takes up, as every run's does.

7. **What counts as a pass, per question.** (1) SharePoint, admin mode: every one of the 7 exports is 200 `application/octet-stream` with `Content-Length` equal to the size Veeam listed. (2) OneDrive, admin mode: the same for the 7. (3) The comparison of point 6 holds for all 14. (4) Recorded, not scored: the per-file time; the `asZip` observation; the session still `Working` and browsable after an export; the export during the restore and the restore's own outcome; the formats `office-v1` does not read, from the code (pptx and its family, doc, xls, ppt, and the macro and template types, which `rp::is_rewritten_office_file` names as rewritten and `office-v1` cannot hash). **The verdict for W6.3:** *go* when (1) to (3) hold; *go with limits* when they hold with a condition the notes name (for example a type whose bytes differ and whose `office-v1` holds, or an `asZip` that W6.3 must never send, or a time per file that bounds the sample); *no-go* when an export is refused in admin mode, answers other bytes than the restore, or disturbs a running restore, with what was seen. The verdict goes into the build notes, `docs/api/veeam-notes.md` (a new section "Document export", with each evidence file named) and a comment on #181. **If a check fails, the spike stops there and tells the owner**; nothing is worked around, and no Graph permission is widened.

8. **Evidence, scrubbing and the scan.** Under `docs/api/veeam-lab/`: `w6.1-1-graph-list-before.txt` (the three targets, empty), `w6.1-2-export-spike.txt` (the test's console, as shown: the point, the 14 candidates, every export's line, the restore's sessions and items, the table), `w6.1-results.json` (the table as the test wrote it), `w6.1-3-graph-list-hash-after.txt`, `w6.1-4-cleanup.txt` (the cleanup test and `graph list` 0 after), and `w6.1-recording/` (the `FixtureRecorder`'s scrubbed exchanges of the test's own Veeam calls under `veeam/`: the token answer's values `[REDACTED]` as `secrets_in` learns them, the `Authorization` header never written, each export's octet-stream body as a `digest` (its SHA-256 and length, never the bytes), the restore's own exchanges not among them since the connector's client is not wrapped). `w6.1-harness/w61-live.ps1` writes each text file through the W4.5 harness's evidence writer rule (checked against the vault's secret values read for that purpose into memory and for token, PFX and PEM shapes before it is written; a hit means nothing written) and **never replaces a committed file with a failed run's**: it writes to a run folder under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RestoreProof\lab\w6.1-<stamp>\` and copies into `docs/api/veeam-lab/` only when every step exited 0, the copy last. Before the commit: `python tools/fixture_secret_scan.py` (from `worker/`; `docs/api` is one of its trees) 0 findings, and `docs/api/veeam-m365/audit-evidence.ps1 -Path ..\veeam-lab\w6.1-*` 0 hits. Run folders, the exported bytes and the config copy stay outside the repository.

9. **The docs.** `docs/api/veeam-notes.md`: the new section with the two admin-mode answers, the comparison table, the limits and the verdict, each line naming its file; `docs/api/veeam-lab/README.md`: the W6.1 table; `docs/testing.md` "Live restore": the third writing test and its variables (`RP_LIVE_EVIDENCE_FILE`, `RP_LIVE_RECORD_DIR`, the same two switches); `docs/verification.md`: one sentence under the expected kinds pointing from the deferred `backup_content` to this entry's verdict; `CLAUDE.md`: the Status and the open items; the build notes here; the comment on #181. No sentence of the report, no schema, no shared vector changes.

**Why this shape.** The spike must show the four things the issue asks with the Worker's own pieces where they exist (the sampler's listing finds the items the product would find; the connector restores as the product restores; the reader reads back as the product reads back; `office-v1` is the product's rule), so that a "go" says W6.3 can be built from parts that already pass their tests, and the one new thing, the export call, is as small and as plainly recorded as it can be. The restore goes through the guarded path because the owner's rule allows no other, and because the question is whether the export's bytes match what *that* path puts in the target. Real files and no canaries because the decision of 2026-10-14 is about the client's own data, and a canary's bytes are known in advance, which is exactly what the export is meant to replace.

**Alternatives rejected.** *A PowerShell harness like W1.0's and W2.4's:* it cannot read the vault, and the owner's rule is the vault only; its Credential Manager path is the lab's, not the Worker's. *`rpworker restore --sp 14 --od 14` for the restore:* its canary half would restore 7 canaries of each type beside the real files, and its clean after deletes the copies before anything can read them back; the live test restores the 14 alone and leaves the copies for two readers. *Exporting from inside the connector's own explore session:* it would need the connector to hand its session out or take an export callback, which is W6.3's design and product code; the spike's own sessions answer the question "does an export in an explore session work and leave it usable", and session C answers "beside a running restore". *Uploading a pptx and a legacy file to answer question 4 live:* a tenant change and a change to `seed-real`'s plan; the code answers which formats `office-v1` reads, and a later task can seed one if W6.3 wants it shown. *A product `VeeamClient::download`:* W6.3's, with its unit tests, if the verdict is go. *Comparing with `rpworker graph list --hash` alone:* it has no `office-v1`; it is kept as the second reader.

**Open, before the build.** Whether `GET …/Sites/{siteId}/Documents` without `parentId` lists the default library's files in this version as it listed every document of the site in W1.4 (12 then); if not, the test lists `…/Libraries` and takes the library whose `id` ends in the default drive's list GUID (read through the Worker app from `GET /sites/{id}/drives?$expand=list`), the way the connector finds a library. Whether a 14-file candidate pool is drawn whole by `list_candidates` under the default `CandidateLimits` (the limits are the sampler's; the test raises them if the pool is cut, and says so).

## 2026-10-13 — Q6.1 (#74): the report checks. One reusable check, `app/report/check.py`, run by the tests and by `manage.py check-report` against a stored report: the file hash is the SHA-256 of the object the report's download link names, read back from the bucket (not the bytes that were put); every tested run of the month whose row says it was timestamped has its `timestamp.tst` in the bucket, over the `result.json` stored beside it (its SHA-256 the row's `bundle_sha256`), verifying under the Cloud's TSA root, its time the row's `tsa_time`, and that time not before the second the test ended and not more than the Worker's timestamp budget (120 s, from `timestamper.hpp`'s three constants) after it; a late result (received once its month had closed) is accepted when its arrival is the period's and counted, and the count is the Summary's line; for a final report every result was received before the report was generated; a run with no token or no bundle is counted as such and nothing is read for it. The 30-second check is the owner's: `docs/report-usability.md` holds the method and an empty result, so the PR says "Part of #74" (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written on 2026-10-13)

Q6.1 (#74) is built on the branch `q6.1-report-checks` from `main` at `2932df9` (the merge of the C6.5 and C6.7 readings). Done when: "Both tests pass and the 30-second check is recorded." The issue's two tests: "stored file hash equals SHA-256 of the downloaded PDF" and "for each run in the report, the TSA token in the bundle verifies and its time is within the period." This entry works from the issue, the entries "C6.4", "C6.6, C6.5 and C6.7" and their code reviews (finding 9 of the second settled below), `docs/verification.md` "The Cloud's report" (the part "A result that arrives late", which names Q6.1 twice), and the code (`app/report/{data,generate,render}.py`, `app/repo/runs.py` `period_time`, `app/results.py`, `app/scheduler.py` `tick_reports`, `app/routers/ui/reports.py`, `app/storage.py`, `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` `check_timestamp`, `worker/include/rp/timestamper.hpp`, `tests/{report_lab,results_lab,tsa_lab,pages_lab}.py`). No code is written yet; the build notes will record what the build finds.

**What is there, and what is not.** The first test is mostly there, in three places, and none of them reads the object back. `tests/test_reports_page.py`'s Done-when hashes the bytes "Generate now" **put** (the Stubber takes any body; a hook keeps what was sent) against `row.file_sha256`, and follows the download's 302 as far as the URL's key, not to the bytes. `tests/test_report.py` hashes `generate`'s put the same way and re-renders pass 1 to the content hash. `tests/test_scheduler.py` hashes the job's put. The by-hand harness `c65-c67-live.ps1` is the one place the object is fetched (through the api's own S3 client) and `Get-FileHash` compared with `file_sha256`, for the job's final report and the click's interim one, and it is run by hand. Nothing holds that the object under the row's key, read back, is the file the row describes, and nothing can be run against a report an MSP has already handed over. The second test exists nowhere: the Integrity section prints `tsa_time` from the row, the row's `tsa_time` is what `POST /v1/results` read from the token it verified (`app/results.py`: `check_timestamp` under the pinned root, refused with the verifier's word otherwise, so **a stored bundle's token always verified once**), and no test or tool reads `timestamp.tst` back from the bucket for a run a report lists. The period rule the second test must respect (`period_time`: a tested run by its end, a late result by its arrival; the review's finding 1) has every case tested on the rows, none on the tokens.

**Proposed.**

1. **One check, in the app, run two ways.** `app/report/check.py` (guarded at 100% line and branch like the rest of `app/report`): a pure `check_run(...) -> str | None` that words one run's finding from its row, the period, the two objects' bytes and the TSA root; a pure `check_file(report, pdf) -> str | None`; and `async check_report(session, storage, msp_id, report_id, *, tsa_ca) -> ReportCheck` that reads the report's row (`ReportRepo.get`, 404-shaped `report_id: no such report` for another MSP's), the month's runs by **the report's own read** (`RunRepo.period` with the row's `period_start` and `period_end`: the same `period_filter` the report was made from, so the set is the report's), gets the object under `storage_key` and, per run that has a bundle, lists its prefix and gets `result.json` and `timestamp.tst` (the lists and gets in a thread, never on the loop), and answers `ReportCheck(report_id, file_ok, runs, stamped, not_stamped, no_bundle, late, findings)`, `findings` a list of `(run_id | None, word)`. The tests call `check_report` on reports they made; **`manage.py check-report --msp-id --report-id`** prints one `<name> <value>` line per count, one `<run_id>: <word>` line per finding on stderr, exit 0 with no finding and exit 1 with one or more (`report: N check(s) failed` last), the CLI's own shape; it reads `DATABASE_URL` and the five `S3_*` as `generate-report` does and never `SECRET_KEY`; the TSA root is `app/results.py`'s `tsa_ca_pem()`, the image's one root. The recommendation is this (the owner's option 2), for one reason: the report is what an MSP hands to a customer or an auditor, and a pytest run proves the code of the day it ran, while `check-report` proves **a given stored report** on the day someone doubts it, and the test holds the command's rule because both are one function. Rejected: *pytest only* (option 1: the harness's fetch-and-hash stays a PowerShell line nobody runs on a real report, and the token check could never be run on a pilot's month); *a page or route* (`GET /reports/{id}/check` would read N objects per click; the admin routes are C6.x's remainder); *pypdf at runtime* so the check could read the Summary's printed counts (a dependency for four numbers; the check prints the counts it found and the operator reads them against the PDF's Summary, and the tests read the PDF through pypdf, which is a dev dependency already). No new dependency: `cryptography` and `asn1crypto` through the imported verifier, boto3's `get_object` and `list_objects_v2` through `Storage`.

2. **The file check.** `check_file`: the SHA-256 of the object under the row's `storage_key`, read back whole, equals `file_sha256`, else the word `file_sha256: differs`; an object that is not there is `storage: no object`. The test (the issue's first, by name, `tests/test_report_checks.py`): a month of real bundles (point 4), **a final report made as the job makes it** (`generate` with the job's arguments: the job's clock at 03:00 on the 1st, no user; `tests/test_scheduler.py` holds that `tick_reports` is that call and hashes its put) **and an interim one made by "Generate now"** through the real `POST /clients/{id}/reports/generate`; each downloaded through `GET /reports/{id}/file`: the 302's URL, its key the row's `storage_key`, and the object fetched by that key from the lab's bucket (the Stubber answers `get_object` with the bytes the lab saw put, a new helper `expect_get`), hashed, equal to `file_sha256`, and `check_report` saying `file_ok` with no finding for both. The content hash is not re-read by the check (it is inside the PDF's text, which the app has no reader for; `tests/test_report.py` holds it printed from the row, and pass 1 re-rendered to it). **The fault planted once:** one byte of the stored object changed, the download still 302 (the route signs; it never reads), the check `file_sha256: differs`; recorded in the build notes with what was seen.

3. **Which runs the second check covers (the owner's c and d).** "Each run in the report" is **every run the Summary counts**: the month's rows as `RunRepo.period` answers them, not the 200 the Test log lists (`MAX_LOG_ROWS`; C6.6's test holds the listed to be the first 200 of this set, so nothing is repeated here). Of those: a `pass`, `fail` or `error` run with `tsa_ok` true is **stamped** and checked in full (point 4); a tested run with `tsa_ok` null (an `error` written afterwards whose TSA gave no token, "not timestamped" in the Integrity section) is **not stamped**: the check lists its prefix and holds that no `timestamp.tst` is there, so the report's word is true, and counts it; an `expired`, `queued` or `dispatched` run ("did not run", "no result yet") has **no bundle**: nothing is read for it, it is counted, and its `bundle_key`, `tsa_ok` and `tsa_time` are held null (a row of that state with a bundle column set is the finding `state: no bundle expected`). The three counts are printed; the test holds them equal to `ReportData`'s (`tests`, `no_result`, `did_not_run`) and to the Summary's lines in the PDF's text.

4. **The token check (the owner's a, b, f).** For each stamped run, in this order, the first miss its word: `storage: no result.json` / `storage: no timestamp.tst` when either is missing under `bundle_key`; `bundle_sha256: differs` when the SHA-256 of the stored `result.json` is not the row's (the object is not the result the row names); then `check_timestamp(token, digest, tsa_ca)` with the verifier's own words (`timestamp_file`, `timestamp_mismatch`, `timestamp_invalid`; the Cloud's root, never one from the bundle); `tsa_time: differs` when the token's time is not the row's `tsa_time` second for second; then the time rule:
   - **The allowance (a).** The report dates a run by `finished_at`, the Worker's clock read **after the clean after and before the evidence is written** (`run_pipeline.cpp`'s `end_timings`; then the secret scan, the attachments' read-back, the signature, and only then the TSA is asked: milliseconds, then the request). The token's time must be **not before the second the test ended** (`tsa_time >= finished_at` with `finished_at` cut to the second, since a token's `genTime` is read in whole seconds by the verifier: the word `stamp_before_end`) **and not more than `STAMP_BUDGET` after it** (`stamp_after_budget`). `STAMP_BUDGET` is **120 s**: `kTimestampAttempts` (3) × `kTimestampTimeout` (10 s) + `kTimestampFirstWait` (30 s) + `kTimestampSecondWait` (60 s), the Worker's whole timestamp budget ("three attempts in all, about two minutes at worst", `worker/include/rp/timestamper.hpp`), held equal to those constants by a test that reads the header. So a test that ended at 23:59:58 on the last day and was stamped at 00:00:40 is in its month by its end and its stamp is accepted, up to 00:01:58 and no further. **No clock allowance** beyond that: the report prints the Worker's time as the test's date and the token is the trusted time; a Worker whose clock disagrees with the TSA by more than its own budget is a finding the operator should see, not noise to hide (Windows Time keeps a machine within a second of its source; a loose bound, an hour or a day, would hide a wrong clock, which is the one fault this check can catch that nothing else does). If a pilot's Worker shows a steady offset, the bound is the owner's to widen, in this file.
   - **A result written afterwards.** A tested run with `finished_at` null (the service's `close_run`: `interrupted`, `internal`, `job_invalid`, …) is dated by `tsa_time` itself, so the budget does not apply: the check holds the token's time equal to the row's and in the period (or late, below); nothing else.
   - **"Within the period" (b).** For a run that is not late, its date (`run_date`) is in the period by the filter, and the stamp follows the rule above, so the stamp is in the period or within the budget past its end. A **late** result is one whose `received_at` is at or after `RESULTS_CLOSE` past the last day of the month its end falls in (the same arithmetic as `period_time`, on the row: `month_of(end).end_at + RESULTS_CLOSE`): its end and its stamp are **before the period**, and the check accepts it exactly when `received_at` is in the period, counts it (`late`), and refuses a tested run whose end is before the period and that is not late by that rule (`period: not the run's`, which the filter should make impossible: a planted row shows the word). The test holds `late` equal to `ReportData.late` and to the Summary's "counted here: N".
   - **What the check proves (f), said plainly.** A token that does not verify is refused at the upload with 400, so every stored token verified once, under the same root, over the same digest. The second check therefore shows that **the object in the bucket is the token that was verified at the upload, over the result the row names, and that the row's `tsa_time` is that token's time and the test's date and that time agree**; a finding means the bucket or the row was changed after the upload, the Cloud filed the wrong object, or the Worker's clock disagrees with the TSA. The faults planted, each once in a parametrized test: the token under a run's key replaced by one of the same digest made `STAMP_BUDGET` + 1 s after the end (`stamp_after_budget`), one made 1 s before the end's second (`stamp_before_end`), one over another digest (`timestamp_mismatch`), one under the other test root (`timestamp_invalid`), the row's `tsa_time` moved by a second (`tsa_time: differs`), the stored `result.json` of another run (`bundle_sha256: differs`), the token removed (`storage: no timestamp.tst`).

5. **Finding 9 (the owner's e): received before generated.** For a **final** report the check holds, for every tested run with a result (`received_at` not null), `received_at < generated_at` (the word `received_after_report`): the rules give an hour (`RESULTS_CLOSE` two hours, `FINAL_AFTER` three; a late result of the period arrived before its own close, which is before the report), so a miss is a report made against the rules or a row moved afterwards. For an **interim** report it is not held: `generated_at` is the clock read before the month is read (the tick's start, the route's `at`), and a result committed between the two is honestly in the report with `received_at` after `generated_at` by milliseconds; holding it would be the loose-or-false choice. The check prints which rule it applied. **Finding 9 stays open:** closing it means stamping `generated_at` from the read's end or reading the month under one snapshot, a change to the generator beyond this task.

## 2026-10-13 — C6.6, C6.5 and C6.7 code review: findings 1 to 4, 6, 7 and 11 to 14 of fifteen fixed, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 15 open; finding 1 is fixed by a rule the entry did not have and the owner has not yet read (a result the Cloud receives once its month has closed is a test of the month it arrives in, by a new column `test_run.received_at`; no final report before 03:00 UTC on the 1st), with one new sentence in the Summary and one in the Framework mapping for the C6.5 reviewer and the C6.7 reader (proposed)

The review of the branch `c6.5-c6.7-reports` against `main` (`/code-review xhigh`, commit `056aa17`) gave fifteen findings. The owner chose 1 to 4, 6, 7 and 11 to 14 to fix now. Nothing is committed or pushed until the owner asks.

**Fixed.**

1. **A result that arrived after its month's final report was in no final report.** *This changes point 1 and the C6.4 entry's point 4, and it is the one fix here that is a new rule: the owner should read it.* A run that ended on 30 September 23:50 and whose Worker reached the Cloud on 1 October 03:05 was in September's report as "no result yet" (still `dispatched` at 03:00) and, once landed as a `fail` with `finished_at` in September, in neither month's report as a test; `docs/verification.md` and the entry said it was "the next month's test", which the code did not do. Now: `POST /v1/results` stamps the run with the Cloud's clock when it files the bundle (`test_run.received_at`, `RunRepo.receive(..., at=)`, the route's `now()`; migration `0001` edited in place, one nullable column), and `period_time` dates a tested run by its end **unless the Cloud received its result at 02:00 UTC on the 1st after that month, or later** (`RESULTS_CLOSE`, two hours): then by `received_at`. So the late run is October's test, a result received on 10 November is November's, and every result is a test of exactly one month; a row no bundle wrote (`received_at` null) goes by its end, as before. The four reads of a month share the rule through `period_filter`. In the report the late run keeps its own date (`_run_time`, the new order of `RunRepo.period`: by the tests' ends, so "a later test of the same plan" is one that ended later, held by a test with a late pass that must not count as a re-test) and the Summary counts it on a line of its own: **"Tests that ended before this period and whose results arrived after that period had closed, counted here: N"** (in `tests/test_report_wording.py`; a sentence the C6.5 reviewer has not seen). *Alternatives rejected:* correcting the docs alone (a `fail` missing from every report is the product's own failure); re-making a final report (the entry's rule, and the reader's copy would differ from the Cloud's); dating by the previous report's `generated_at` (an upload stamped before it and committed after it would still be lost: a clock rule with an hour's room between the close and the first final report has no such gap); holding a month's report until every run of it has a result (a revoked Worker's queued runs never get one).
2. **The start run finalised a month the minute it ended.** A scheduler redeployed at 00:00:30 on the 1st made every final report thirty seconds after the month, and the 03:00 run found them `existing`. `FINAL_AFTER` (three hours, `app/report/data.py`) is now one rule for whoever asks: `tick_reports` takes `closed_month(now)` (the previous month from 03:00 on the 1st, the one before it until then), `REPORT_HOUR_UTC` is derived from it, and `generate` refuses a final report of a month that ended less than three hours ago with `period: not closed until 03:00 UTC on the 1st` before any read (the CLI at 00:10 on the 1st hears it too). `RESULTS_CLOSE` is an hour shorter, so an upload stamped just inside the close has that hour to commit before the month is read; a test holds the two constants' order.
