## 2026-10-13 — C6.6, C6.5 and C6.7 (#72, #71, #73): the monthly report job, the reports pages and the framework text. The scheduler makes every client's final report of the previous month on the 1st at 03:00 UTC (and once at its start), one transaction per client, through `generate` as the CLI calls it, a month that has its report skipped and never a failure; `/reports` and `/clients/{id}/reports` list period, kind, generation time and both hashes with a download per row through a Cloud route that writes `report.download` and 302s to a URL pre-signed for ten minutes; "Generate now" makes an interim report of the current month in the user's name, one per client per ten minutes and one render at a time per process, every refusal the page's own words; the Test log, the Failures and the Integrity run list show at most 500 runs and say how many more there were; the four controls get their two sentences in `frameworks.py`, claiming what a `pass` shows and nothing else, and the SOC 2 row is named by the criteria's own words; the fixed sentences of the Summary, the Method and the mapping are held verbatim by one test so a reviewed wording cannot drift; the two outside readings close #71 and #73 by their own commits, not this PR's (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written on 2026-10-13)

C6.6 (#72), C6.5 (#71) and C6.7 (#73) are built together on the branch `c6.5-c6.7-reports` from `main` at `c160571` (the merge of C6.4 and its review), one PR, in the order C6.6, C6.7, C6.5. Done when: "An interim report is downloadable from the dashboard within a minute of clicking" (#72); "The table renders in the PDF and the wording has been reviewed by one outside reader" (#73); "The forbidden-phrase test passes and a reviewer confirms no claim exceeds what was tested" (#71). This entry works from the three issues and #74 (Q6.1, not built here), the entries "C6.4", its build notes and its code review (open findings 10, 12's rest and 13 settled below), "C6.1, C6.2 and C6.3" and its review (the pages' rules; open findings 6, 12, 13 and 14 named where they touch this), `docs/verification.md` "The Cloud's report" and "The Cloud's pages", `docs/testing.md` "The report" and "The pages", and the code (`app/report/{generate,data,render,frameworks}.py`, `template.html`, `app/scheduler.py`, `app/routers/ui/{clients,runs,workers}.py`, `app/audit.py`, `app/ui.py`, `app/repo/{reports,runs,audit}.py`, `app/storage.py`, `app/settings.py`, `cloud/docker-compose.yml`, `tests/report_lab.py`, `tests/pages_lab.py`, `tests/test_report.py`, `tests/test_pages.py`, `docs/api/cloud-lab/c6.4-harness/c64-live.ps1`). No code is written yet; the build notes will record what the build finds. The owner's six questions are points 1 to 6, in the owner's order; the rest follows.

**What is there.** `generate(session, storage, msp_id, client_id, period, *, now, user_id=, ip=)` reads the month (`gather`, eight reads), asks `ReportRepo.final` for a final report of the month *after* those reads, renders the two passes in a thread, writes the row and one `report.create` audit row, then puts the object; it commits nothing (the CLI's one transaction per command); a render or a put that fails is `ReportFailed` (a `RepoError`) worded by the cause's type. `interim_for(period, now)` is derived from the dates. The scheduler (`app/scheduler.py`) runs two jobs on an `IntervalTrigger` every 300 s, each once at start (`next_run_time=start_at`), `max_instances=1`, `coalesce=True`, `misfire_grace_time` 60 s; `_msp_ids` reads every MSP in its own transaction; the plans tick holds one transaction per MSP with one savepoint per plan; `main()` reads `DATABASE_URL` and `LOG_LEVEL` alone. The Compose `scheduler` service takes the `*app-environment` anchor, so it already has the five `S3_*` variables (the owner's "gains them" is already so; a test will hold it). `storage_settings_from_environment()` and `Storage.for_writing` exist (C6.4). The pages: every statement a repo method with `msp_id` first, a fixed count per page held by `before_cursor_execute`; another MSP's row 404; `SameOrigin` on every POST and on the bundle download; `LayoutDep` (the user and the MSP, two reads); `app/audit.py`'s `ACTIONS` closed at six words, `tests/test_login.py` holding the tuple; `base.html`'s nav is Clients, Workers, Audit (admin); `/runs/{id}/files/{name}` writes `bundle.download` then 302s with `Cache-Control: no-store` to `presigned_get_url(key, expires_s=600)` against `S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT`; `app.state.storage` is `Storage.from_settings` (the data, check and sign clients). `ReportRepo` has `create`, `get`, `final`, `list` (by `period_start desc, generated_at desc, id`; in the isolation table). `RESULT_WORDS`, `RAN_STATES`, `TESTED_STATES`; `build` is pure and runs on the loop. `frameworks.py`: `Control(identifier, name, demonstrates, not_covered)`, four rows with the two sentences `None`, `PENDING` the sentence the template prints under the table; the SOC 2 row's name is "Recovery procedures tested", the issue's gloss, not the criteria's words (the C6.4 review's cut list). The report wording test runs the four banned phrases against the template, the stylesheet, the controls, both passes and the PDF's text. The C6.4 sample PDF and evidence are the old template's (the review's "Not done"). APScheduler is 3.11.3 (`CronTrigger` available; a `MemoryJobStore`, so a process started after a missed occurrence does not see it as missed).

**Proposed.**

1. **The job: `tick_reports`, `CronTrigger(day=1, hour=3, minute=0)` in UTC and once at start; the previous month's final report for every client of every MSP with a run in it; one transaction per client; `period: already reported` is a skip, never a failure; the scheduler reads the five `S3_*` variables at start and never migrates; a final report is never re-made.** `app/scheduler.py` gains a third job, id `reports`, `CronTrigger(day=1, hour=3, minute=0, timezone=UTC)`, `max_instances=1`, `coalesce=True`, `misfire_grace_time` 3600 s (an hour: a scheduler busy or paused at 03:00 still runs it that morning), and `next_run_time=start_at` like the other two, so a scheduler restarted after a 1st it missed makes that month's reports when it comes up, and a restart on any other day finds them made (one read per client). `tick_reports(session_factory, storage, at=None) -> ReportsTick(msps, clients, created, existing, failed)`: the period is `previous_month(at.date())`; `_msp_ids` as the other jobs; then per MSP one read in its own transaction, **`RunRepo.clients_in_period(msp_id, *, start, end) -> list[UUID]`** (new; the distinct `client_id`s of the MSP's runs whose `period_time()` is in the span, any state, so a client whose only run was `expired` or has no result yet still gets its report with that line, as C6.4's rules say; one statement; `msp_id` first; in the isolation table as a read); then **one transaction per client**: `generate(session, storage, msp_id, client_id, period, now=at)` (no user, no address: the job's rows are the scheduler's, as the CLI's are) and commit; a `RepoError` whose reason is `ALREADY_REPORTED` is counted as `existing` and logged at debug; any other exception (a `RepoError`, a `ReportFailed`, the database) is rolled back for that client alone, counted as `failed` and logged by type (`report failed`, `msp_id`, `client_id`, `period`, `exc_info`), and the next client is made; a created report is counted and its `report created` line (`msp_id`, `client_id`, `report_id`, `period`) written after its commit, as the plans tick does. The tick line: `tick job=reports msps clients created existing failed duration_ms`. **`generate` asks `ReportRepo.final` first**, before the eight reads (the C6.4 review's cut finding "`ReportRepo.final` after the eight reads"): `interim_for` needs only the dates, so a month that has its final report costs the job one `SELECT` per client and no render; the nine-read count and the test that holds it stay, in the new order. **The scheduler's process:** `main()` reads `database_url_from_environment()`, `storage_settings_from_environment()` and `log_level_from_environment()`, a fault naming the variable and exit 1 as today; `serve(url, storage)` and `build_scheduler(session_factory, storage, start_at=)` take the `Storage.for_writing` made once; `cloud/.env.example` and the docs say the scheduler reads `DATABASE_URL`, `LOG_LEVEL` and the five `S3_*` and never `SECRET_KEY`; the Compose service is unchanged (the anchor), held by a test that reads the file. The scheduler never migrates (unchanged; the api did). The render runs in a thread (`generate`'s `to_thread`), so the two ticks keep ticking on the loop while a report renders. **A final report is never re-made, in Stage 1 or later by this design:** the final report of a month says what the Cloud knew on the day it was made, and C6.4's review settled what a late bundle is (a run with no result when the report was made is in it as such; its bundle is the next month's test by the time it ended), so nothing is lost and nothing has to be edited; a second final report of one month would be two documents with one name and the Q6.1 hash check could hold only one. A pilot that wants the late run in a report has the next month's interim report and the pages. *Rejected:* a daily cron (`0 3 * * *`) that makes any previous-month report still missing (the issue's and the owner's words are the 1st; the start run covers a missed 1st; a put that failed on the 1st is one `report failed` line naming the client and one `manage.py generate-report --period` by hand, where a silent daily retry would make a bucket outage invisible for a day); one transaction per MSP with a savepoint per client, the tick's shape (a report's object is put inside the client's transaction, so an MSP transaction that fails after three clients leaves three objects without rows, under keys the next run then overwrites; per client the window is one; and a report of seconds has nothing to share with its neighbours, where a plan's run is one insert); a persistent job store so a missed occurrence fires on restart (`next_run_time=start_at` does it for a job that is idempotent); `--replace` for a final report (nothing asks, and the hash rule above).
2. **The pages and the button: `/reports` (the nav entry), `/clients/{id}/reports`, `GET /reports/{id}/file`, `POST /clients/{id}/reports/generate`; a member or an admin may generate and download; one interim report per client per ten minutes and one render at a time per process; the request's transaction is held across the render and the put, bounded; every refusal is the page with one line; a fixed count of statements.** *Who:* **both roles** generate and download. C6.1's line between the roles was drawn at taking something away (revoke) and at seeing other users' actions (`/audit`); a report is the client's own evidence, made in the user's name on one audit row, and the pilot's day-to-day user should not need the admin role to get it. *Rejected:* admin only (widens the admin role for the wrong reason); a third role (nothing else needs one). *The list, `/reports`:* every report of the MSP, newest period first (`period_start desc, generated_at desc, id desc`), in pages of 50 by keyset (`?before=<report id>`, the rows alone for an htmx request, as the history does), each row the client's name (a link to the client's reports), the period (`YYYY-MM`), the kind ("interim" or "final"), the generation time, the content hash and the file hash (as `code`, both: the reader checks the file hash against the download and finds the content hash inside the PDF), and a **Download** link to `/reports/{id}/file`. **`ReportRepo.page(msp_id, *, client_id=None, before=None, limit=50) -> list[ReportRow(report, client_name)]`** (new; one statement joined to `client` on `(msp_id, client_id)`; `msp_id` first; the isolation table), `PAGE_SIZE` 50 as the history's. *The client's page, `/clients/{id}/reports`:* 404 for a client not this MSP's; the same rows without the client column, the **Generate now** form above them, and a line saying what the button makes ("an interim report of the current month, <month>, from the tests that have ended by now; the month's final report is made on the 1st"); the client page `/clients/{id}` gets a "Reports" link beside its heading and `base.html`'s nav gains **Reports** → `/reports` for every role. *The download, `GET /reports/{id}/file`:* `SameOrigin` (the one GET that writes, as the bundle's); `ReportRepo.get(msp_id, id)` or 404; one audit row **`report.download`** `report:<id>` with the user and the address, committed before the answer; 302 with `Cache-Control: no-store` to `presigned_get_url(report.storage_key, expires_s=600)` against `S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT`, as the bundle's route does; no bucket list (the key is the row's), so three `SELECT`s (the user, the MSP, the report) and one `INSERT`. The browser's file name is the key's last part (`2026-09.pdf`, `2026-10-interim-20261013T101500Z.pdf`); no `ResponseContentDisposition`. `report.download` joins `ACTIONS` (the seventh word; `tests/test_login.py`'s tuple and `docs/verification.md` updated). *The button, `POST /clients/{id}/reports/generate`:* `SameOrigin`, `CurrentUser`; 404 for another MSP's client; then **the cap**: `ReportRepo.page(msp_id, client_id=, limit=1)` answers the client's newest report, and if it is interim, of the current month and generated less than **`GENERATE_EVERY` = 600 s** before `ui.now()`, the answer is the client's reports page with the line "An interim report of this month was made at <time>; the next can be made from <time>." and **429** with `Retry-After`, no render, no row; then **the render slot**: `app.state.render_slot`, an `asyncio.Semaphore(1)` made in `create_app`, taken with `asyncio.wait_for(..., RENDER_WAIT_S` = 5`)`, and a slot not free in five seconds is the page with "A report is being made; try again in a minute." and 429 (`Retry-After: 60`); then `generate(session, storage, msp_id, client_id, month_of(today), now=ui.now(), user_id=user.id, ip=client_ip(request))` under **`session.begin_nested()`** (a savepoint, the scheduler's shape per plan), so a `RepoError` (`period: no run in the period` for a client with nothing this month; `storage_key: already used` for two clicks in one second) or a `ReportFailed` rolls back the report's rows alone and is answered as the page with the error's own line (`<key>: <reason>`, the CLI's words) and **409** for a `RepoError`, **503** for a `ReportFailed` (the Cloud's own fault; the type logged with the ids, never the message, never a traceback), while the request's transaction commits nothing of it (`get_session` commits at return; the savepoint was rolled back; the route calls neither `commit` nor `rollback`); on success **303** to `/clients/{id}/reports`, where the new row is first with its Download link. The page's POST is a plain form (no htmx: the render takes seconds and a 303 keeps a refresh from posting again). *The hold (the C6.4 review's finding 13, settled as kept and bounded):* the request's transaction, and its pooled connection, are open from `LayoutDep`'s first read until the 303, across the render (seconds of CPU in a thread) and the put (botocore's standard limits); the alternative, the reads in one transaction and the row and the put in a second after the render, is rejected because one request is one transaction by `db.py`'s rule ("a route calls neither") and because the row-before-object order is what makes a failed put roll the row back. The hold is bounded instead: at most one render at a time per process (the slot), a waiter waits five seconds and is answered, and the cap keeps one client to six renders an hour, so a process holds at most one connection across a render and the others for five seconds; the general case (a connection held across a slow bucket on any page) is the C6.1–C6.3 review's open finding 4 and C5.12's. *The count:* `/reports` three `SELECT`s (the user, the MSP, the page); `/clients/{id}/reports` four (the client); the download three and one `INSERT`; the POST, on success, the user, the MSP, the client, the cap's read, `generate`'s nine and two `INSERT`s then the put, the same for a month of three runs and of sixty; a test holds each. *Rejected:* a cap per hour or per day (a pilot showing the report twice in a demo would be refused; ten minutes is what two reports a minute apart would differ by anyway, since the PDF prints minutes and the same rows render to the same bytes, C6.4's build notes point 7); no cap (a render is CPU seconds; a signed-in user clicking in a loop would hold the slot and the pool); an htmx swap of the table after the POST (a wait of seconds with no page change, and a refresh that re-posts); a report made in the background and polled for (a queue, a state and a page of "pending"; the Done-when is one click and one minute, and the render is seconds); answering a `ReportFailed` as a 500 (the owner's words: never).
3. **The cap on a month of thousands of runs: the Test log, the Failures and the Integrity run list each show the first `MAX_LOG_ROWS` = 500 runs of the month in the month's order and one line says how many more there were; the Summary's numbers count every run.** `build` keeps `tests`, `passed`, `failed`, `errored`, `did_not_run`, `no_result`, the recovery times, the restore points, the workers and the plans over every row (`gather` reads them all: 8,928 rows of a `*/5` plan are one `SELECT` and milliseconds in Python), and sets `runs` to the first 500 lines, `failures` to the blocks of the first 500 `fail`/`error` lines, and new `runs_left_out` and `failures_left_out` counts; the template prints, under each capped table, "N more tests of this period are not listed here; the Cloud's pages hold every one." when N > 0 and nothing otherwise. The Integrity run list is capped with the Test log (the same 500 runs, so a run's hash is there when its row is). 500: a run is one Test log row and three to four lines of the Integrity table, so a capped report is about fifty pages; the C6.4 harness rendered three pages in seconds, and the build notes will record the two-pass time of a 500-run month measured once by hand (the figure the Done-when's minute depends on). Held by a test on `build` with 501 and 1,000 runs (pure, no render: the counts, the first 500 in order, the line's number) and by one render with `MAX_LOG_ROWS` patched to 5 on a month of 7 runs (the line in both passes and in the PDF's text; the Summary's "7" beside the five rows). *Rejected:* a page limit (WeasyPrint lays out the whole document, so a limit on pages is a cut after the fact through the middle of a table, and the cost is the layout); no cap (a `*/5` plan is 8,928 runs, 18,000 table rows, hundreds of pages and a two-pass render of minutes under a request's transaction and the slot; the cadence floor is an open item of C5.9 and does not make this safe); the failures alone (the Test log is the issue's evidence); the newest 500 (the month's order is oldest first everywhere else in the report, and the first 500 are the ones Q6.1's reader meets first in the pages too).
4. **The frameworks text: `frameworks.py` kept; the eight sentences below, under the wording rule; the SOC 2 row named by the criteria's own words; `PENDING` replaced by one sentence that says what the table is.** `frameworks.py` stays a Python tuple (held by the tests that scan the controls for the banned phrases and now for the sentences verbatim; typed; nothing parsed at run time; under `tools/check_coverage.py`); #73's `frameworks.yaml` is not made: a YAML file would be a second format for four rows, `pyyaml` a runtime dependency for it, and a file read at render time one more thing a test must hold. The `name` column is the control's own title, and for SOC 2, whose points of focus have no title, the criteria's own words shortened with an ellipsis, never a gloss: **"ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.13"** "Information backup"; **"SOC 2 (2017 TSC) Availability A1.2 and A1.3"** "A1.2: … data back-up processes, and recovery infrastructure to meet its objectives; A1.3: the entity tests recovery plan procedures supporting system recovery"; **"HIPAA 45 CFR 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(D)"** "Testing and revision procedures"; **"DORA, Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Article 12"** "Backup policies and procedures, restoration and recovery procedures and methods". Above the table, replacing `PENDING`: *"For each control, the left sentence says what a test marked pass in this report shows, and the right sentence what this report does not look at. A test marked fail or error shows nothing for the control; it is listed under Failures. The table describes this evidence; it is not an assessment of the control."* The eight sentences, each claiming only what a `pass` run shows (sampled items restored into a test location, read back and compared, on dates, with the outcome recorded), never a control met, an audit passed or a regulation complied with, and none of the four banned phrases:
   - **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.13.** *Demonstrates:* "On the dates listed, a sample of items was restored from the backup copy into a test location, read back and compared with what was expected, and the outcome of each test is recorded here." *Not covered:* "Whether every item in the backup can be restored, whether the backup policy is followed, how often backups are taken, or where and for how long the copies are kept."
   - **SOC 2 Availability A1.2 and A1.3.** *Demonstrates:* "On the dates listed, the restore of a sample of backed-up items was tested and what each test found is recorded here; this is a record of restore testing of items, not of a recovery plan exercise." *Not covered:* "Recovery of a system or a service, the recovery plan and its exercise, recovery time or recovery point objectives, and whether the backup process meets the entity's objectives."
   - **HIPAA 45 CFR 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(D).** *Demonstrates:* "On the dates listed, the restore of a sample of items from the backup was tested and the outcome recorded, which is one input to the periodic testing of a contingency plan." *Not covered:* "The contingency plan itself, its revision, its other parts (data backup plan, disaster recovery plan, emergency mode operation plan, criticality analysis), and whether the sampled items hold protected health information."
   - **DORA Article 12.** *Demonstrates:* "On the dates listed, the restoration of a sample of items from the backup was tested, with each test's outcome and the time the restore took recorded here." *Not covered:* "The backup policy, the restoration and recovery procedures and methods as a whole, the recovery of ICT systems, the testing of those procedures beyond the sampled items, and any register, report or notification the regulation asks for."
   The sentences are the C6.7 reader's to comment on (point 5); the build puts them in the PDF now so the reader reads them rendered. *Rejected:* one sentence pair for all four (each control asks a different question, and the right column is where the reader's experience is needed); the issue's "(recovery procedures tested)" as the SOC 2 name (a gloss that reads as a claim); leaving `PENDING` until the reader has read (the Done-when says the table renders; the sentence above the table says what it is).
5. **The two readings: the owner names the C6.5 reviewer and the C6.7 reader at approval, or is both; their comments are one dated entry each in this log; the PR closes #72 and the build halves of #71 and #73; each of the two closes on its own follow-up commit.** *The C6.5 pass, built here:* the fixed sentences of the Summary (the three meanings, the recovery-times sentence, the disaster-recovery sentence), the Method (the sampling, the targets, the comparison, the cleanup line, the levels line) and the mapping (point 4) are listed in a new test, `tests/test_report_wording.py`, **verbatim**, and held to the template and to `frameworks.py`, so a reviewed sentence cannot change without the list changing in the same commit; the test's docstring says the list is the reviewed wording and names the entry that records the review. The pass also settles two sentences now: the disaster-recovery sentence stays as the C6.4 review's finding 6 left it ("This report does not test full disaster recovery. It records what each test listed here found for the items it sampled, on the dates shown.") rather than the issue's "were restored and verified" (untrue of a month with a failure; the reviewer may say otherwise), and the Method's "Verification levels covered: 1, 2, 3" keeps "covered" (a level exercised by a test whatever it found), with the glossary's ladder named. *The readings:* the C6.5 reviewer reads the rendered Summary and Method of the sample PDF (point 6) against the C6.5 question, "does any claim exceed what was tested"; the C6.7 reader, someone with audit experience, reads the four rows rendered. Each reading is recorded as a dated entry "C6.5 review: <reviewer's role>, <date>" and "C6.7 reading: <reader's role>, <date>" in this log, with each comment, what changed for it (the template, `frameworks.py`, the verbatim list, the tests) and what was left and why; the reader is named by role unless they ask to be named. *How the issues close:* this PR says `Closes #72` and "the build half of #71 and #73" (the test and the sentences exist; the readings do not); after each reading, one small follow-up commit records the entry and any wording change with its test, and its PR (or the commit on `main`, the owner's choice) says `Closes #71` or `Closes #73`, so the batch merges on green without waiting for an outside reader. If the owner is the reviewer, the owner's reading of the sample PDF is the entry, written by the build in the owner's words. *Rejected:* holding the PR on the readings (the owner's words); recording comments in the issues alone (the issue says `docs/decisions.md`).

## 2026-10-13 — C6.4 code review: findings 1 to 9, 11, 14 and 15 of fifteen fixed, 10, 12 and 13 open; findings 2 and 3 change the entry's point 4 (a queued or dispatched run is in its month's report as one with no result yet, and a result written afterwards is dated by its stamp or its dispatch, never its queueing) (proposed)

The review of the branch `c6.4-report` against `main` (`/code-review max`) gave fifteen findings and a list cut by its cap. The owner chose 1 to 9, 11, 14 and 15 to fix now. Nothing is committed or pushed until the owner asks.

**Fixed.**

1. **An item the Worker could not check was printed "missing".** `found_word` looked at `found` first; the Worker's check outcome `error` (the item's target could not be read) is stored as `found` false with `match` unknown. `match` decides first now: `match` false is "missing" (`found` false) or "mismatch"; anything else is "not checked". An infrastructure problem never gets the word of a failed item.
2. **A run with no result was in no report, so a month whose Worker was off read as a month of passes.** *This changes point 4.* `period_filter` takes every state: a `queued` or `dispatched` run is the month's by `created_at`, shown in the Test log as "no result yet" with dashes and counted in the Summary ("Scheduled tests with no result when this report was made: N"), never as a test. A month of such runs alone is a report ("No test ran in this period"), no longer `period: no run in the period`. A run handed out on a month's last evening is in that month's final report as one with no result; if its bundle lands later it is also the next month's test, by the time it ended. Both statements are true on the day each report is made, and nothing is edited. `expired` keeps its line ("did not run").
3. **A result written afterwards was dated by the time it was queued.** *This changes point 4.* The Worker's `interrupted`, `result_invalid`, `internal`, `job_invalid` and `connector_unknown` results carry no `ended_at`; the fallback to `created_at` was written as one calendar corner case and was every one of them. `period_time` is now, for a tested run, `coalesce(finished_at, tsa_time, dispatched_at, created_at)`: the time it was stamped, else the time it was last handed out, and its creation only when nothing later is known; every other state by `created_at`. `app/report/data.py`'s `run_date` is the same rule on a row, held by a test.
4. **"No item was checked." under an error whose items all matched** (`restore_contradiction`). A failure block with no unmatched item says "Every item that was checked matched." when the run has items, and "No item was checked." only when it has none.
5. **An error's recovery span and restore point were in the Summary.** Average and maximum recovery time and "Restore points covered" are read from `pass` and `fail` runs alone (`RAN_STATES`), and the Summary says so in one sentence.
6. **Fixed sentences said what the month's rows did not.** C6.5's second sentence is now "It records what each test listed here found for the items it sampled, on the dates shown." (the issue's "were restored and verified" was untrue of a month of failures; C6.5 still reviews it). The Method is written as the method (present tense), names only the plans with a result in the period, says a random mail's sender is compared when the backup lists one and a random file's size unless it is an Office document (`docs/verification.md`'s own rule), prints the levels sentence only when a test passed or failed and its level-4 clause only when such a test sampled a file, and says in how many tests the removal from the restore target did not complete (`cleanup_ok` false).
7. **"Re-tested and passed" was any later pass of the client.** It is the nearest later `pass` of the same plan, worded "A later test of the same plan passed on <date>." (a later test samples anew, so "re-tested" claimed more than was done), else "No later test of the same plan passed in this period."
8. **A month without a test had its headline in the pass colour.** `overall_class`: `fail`, `error`, `pass` only with at least one test, else `quiet`.
9. **The Integrity tables ran off the paper.** The Runs, Workers and failed-items tables have fixed columns (`<col>` widths) and their cells, every `code` and every `dd` may break anywhere. Held by a test that lays the report out and looks at every text box's right edge (`tests/report_lab.py` `past_the_page`), seen to fail on the old stylesheet.
11. **`generate-report` blamed the database for a render or a put that failed.** `generate` raises `ReportFailed` (a `RepoError`, so one line and exit 1): `report: not rendered (<type>)`, `storage: put failed (<type>)`, the cause's type alone. `manage.py` words a storage client the library refuses to build as `storage: not usable (<type>)` (botocore's message quotes the endpoint), and `period_of` refuses the year 0000 as `period: not YYYY-MM`.
14. **The test for "no date, id or producer" could not fail, and the claim was untrue.** WeasyPrint writes the Info dictionary into a compressed stream; the test now reads it through pypdf: the title and `/Producer` `WeasyPrint <version>` alone, no `/ID` in the trailer, and the same read sees a date on a render that has one. The docs now say what holds: the same HTML is the same bytes by one WeasyPrint version, the one `uv.lock` pins; a stored report is never rendered again, so an upgrade changes no stored hash.
15. **`test_the_audit_reads_hold_on_a_moved_clock` would fail from 2027-06-01.** `make_world` moved the clock before the spare connector's audit row was written; the move and the hand-written row are now last, and the test also runs with a clock behind the real one (2026-01-01), which fails on the old order today. The C6.1–C6.3 review's finding 8 is closed by this, not by C6.4.

Finding 12's quadratic scan in `build` is gone as a side effect of 7 (the unmatched items are grouped once and the later passes found in one reverse walk); `build` still runs on the loop.

**Open.** 10 (DejaVu is the image's only font: a name outside it prints as boxes), 12's rest (`build` on the event loop), 13 (the transaction held across the render and the put; with C6.6's route), and the list the cap cut: item names and subjects printed verbatim (an address or a link can reach a PDF, against the Reports rule's "holds no person's address"), the SOC 2 gloss, two final generations at once answering `storage_key: already used`, `ReportRepo.final` after the eight reads, no index for the period predicate, `Storage.for_writing` run by no test with a usable endpoint, the partial index's predicate held by no test, the harness never failing on a mismatch, the docs still saying the CLI reads `DATABASE_URL` alone, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set process-wide, and the duplicated helpers.

**The gate.** `uv run --locked pytest` with coverage, once in full on the finished code on 2026-10-13: 2526 passed, coverage 99.80% combined, `tools/check_coverage.py` `OK` on every guarded file at 100% line and branch. The new tests of findings 9 and 15 were seen to fail on the old stylesheet and the old order.

**Not done.** The by-hand run on the Compose stack was not made again, so `docs/api/cloud-lab/c6.4-done-when.txt` and `c6.4-sample-report.pdf` are the old template's (the sample still shows finding 9's cut-off column).

## 2026-10-12 — C6.4 build notes: built as the entry says, with a ninth read (`ReportRepo.final`) before the two passes since Postgres names the key's unique first for a second final report, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` pinned in `render_pdf` since this laptop's WeasyPrint subsets fonts with fontTools and stamped each font with the render's time, `period_time` and `period_filter` as the lint's two further module functions, fontconfig's tool, a built font cache and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` in the image; the gate green locally once in full and once stopped by the low-memory reaper, the Done-when shown on the stack at the third run of its harness (proposed)

The branch `c6.4-report` holds C6.4 (#70), built test-first against the entry below (approved as written). Nothing is committed or pushed until the owner asks. Where the build left the entry:

1. **Point 1 as written**, plus `UniqueConstraint("msp_id", "id")` on `report`, and **`ReportRepo.final(msp_id, client_id, period_start)`**, a ninth read `generate` makes before the two passes: a second final report of one month violates both `uq_report_storage_key` (the issue's key is the month's) and `uq_report_final_period`, and Postgres reported the key's first, so the word would have been `storage_key: already used`; the read answers `period: already reported` before anything is rendered (a test patches the renderer to fail), and the index stays the line for two generations at once (shown on the model). `generated_at` has no default anywhere; `ReportRepo.create` refuses a naive one.
2. **Point 2 as written, and one thing the entry's probe could not see.** The GTK3 runtime 3.24.31 (the installer named in `docs/environment.md`) went on this laptop silently and the rendering tests run natively; but that runtime has **no HarfBuzz-Subset**, so WeasyPrint subsets fonts with fontTools here, and fontTools writes the time of the save into each embedded font's `head` table: two renders of one HTML differed by those bytes and the two-hash test went red (the Linux probe had `libharfbuzz-subset0` and was deterministic). fontTools takes that time from `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, the reproducible-builds convention, so `render_pdf` sets it to `0` when nothing set it (a test holds both halves); HarfBuzz-Subset writes no time and the image is unaffected. **The image** gained, beyond the four packages, `fontconfig` and `fc-cache -fs` in the same layer and `XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/cache` set after uv's layer and before the user switch: the service user has no home, and fontconfig printed `No writable cache directories` sixteen times per report into the CLI's stderr (the harness's second run); set before uv's layer, uv wrote its own cache there as root and the error stayed (the third run is clean). The image's packages as built: `fonts-dejavu-core 2.37-8`, `libharfbuzz-subset0 10.2.0-1+deb13u1`, `libpango-1.0-0 1.56.3-1`, `libpangoft2-1.0-0 1.56.3-1`, WeasyPrint 70.0.
3. **Points 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9 as written.** The Summary's overall line has a singular (`The 1 test passed`, `1 of 1 test failed`) and the case of errors alone (`N of M tests passed` beside the error line); `period_time` and `period_filter` are module functions of `app/repo/runs.py`, so `tests/test_tenant_scope.py`'s allowance for public functions that are no method names three (`constraint_refusal` and these two, which build a condition and run nothing).
4. **Point 5 as written** for `gather`'s eight reads; `generate` is those, `ReportRepo.final`, the row and the audit row, then the put (eleven statements, held for three runs and for sixty). `ItemRepo.counts_by_type_in_period` answers `TypeCount`s and sits in the isolation table's `COUNTS`.
5. **Point 7 as written**, with `Storage.for_writing(StorageSettings)` (the data client alone) and `make_s3_client` taking either settings object; `StorageSettings` has its own sources rule and validator (a classmethod can't be lent between pydantic models); `generate-report`'s period defaults to the previous month of `app/report/generate.now()`, which the CLI's tests move.
6. **Point 10 as written:** `make_world` places the hand-written audit row 30 days after the MSP's newest row and takes `clock=`; the moved-clock test runs the two `AuditRepo.page` reads of the table on worlds at 2027-06-01 and 2040-01-01. The world also gained a `fail` run with an unmatched item in `NOW`'s month, with its times given rather than the database's clock, so the report's three reads answer rows of their own MSP on any calendar.
7. **Testing's lessons, recorded.** The Stubber takes any body (`botocore.stub.ANY`) and a `before-parameter-build.s3.PutObject` hook keeps the bytes sent, filtered to `application/pdf` since the vector's landing puts five parts first. Two interim reports a second apart in one minute render the same bytes and hashes under two keys (the PDF prints minutes and never its key), which the test now says. pypdf reads a kerned heading as `T ests run`, so the PDF's text is held to sentences and hashes and the HTML to cells. The CLI tests' line rule gained digits (`content_sha256`). The harness needed three runs: PowerShell's names are case-insensitive (`$recovery` overwrote the parameter `$Recovery`), psql's command tag glued to a `RETURNING id` (`-q` now, and the ids checked), and the fontconfig lines above.

## 2026-10-12 — C6.4 (#70): the report generator. One UTC calendar month per report; a run is the period's by the time it ended; `pass`, `fail` and `error` are the tests and an `expired` run is counted as one that did not run; eight repo reads with `msp_id` first and a fixed count whatever the rows; a WeasyPrint A4 PDF from one autoescaped template in two passes, the first without the hash (its SHA-256 the content hash, printed by the second), the second the file (its SHA-256 the file hash), both in the `report` row (`content_sha256`, `file_sha256`), with `interim` for a period not yet over, one final report per client and period and no object ever replaced; the object at `msp/{msp_id}/reports/{client_id}/{period}.pdf`; Pango in the image and the GTK runtime on the laptop so the gate stays one `uv run pytest`; the Framework mapping section names the four controls and says the sentences are C6.7's; `manage.py generate-report` as the way to make one before C6.6; `app/report/` guarded at 100% (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written on 2026-10-12)

C6.4 (#70) is built on the branch `c6.4-report`, one PR closing it. Done when: "A PDF renders for a client with one failure and one error in the period and every section is populated." This entry works from the issue, the neighbours' lines (#71 C6.5 the wording review, #72 C6.6 the monthly job, the reports page, "Generate now" and `report.download`, #73 C6.7 the framework mapping text, #74 Q6.1 the report checks), the entry "C6.1, C6.2 and C6.3" and its code review, `docs/verification.md` "The Cloud's pages" and "The Cloud receives a bundle", and the code (`app/models.py`, migration `0001`, `app/repo/{reports,runs,items,workers,audit}.py`, `app/results.py`, `app/storage.py`, `app/ui.py`, `app/audit.py`, `app/onboarding.py`, `manage.py`, `app/settings.py`, `cloud/Dockerfile`, `tools/check_coverage.py`, `tests/pages_lab.py`, `tests/results_lab.py`, `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`). No code is written yet; the build notes will record what the build finds. The owner's list of seven things the code does not answer is points 1 to 7 below, in the owner's order, with the rest after.

**What is there.** `report` (`period_start`, `period_end` as dates, `storage_key`, one `sha256` under `ck_report_sha256_hex`, `generated_at` from the database's clock, a key to the client that starts with `msp_id`, no unique beyond its id); `ReportRepo.create/get/list`, each in the isolation table. `test_run` holds, per run, `state`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `created_at`, `restore_point_at`, `total_ms`, `recovery_ms` (C6.2, "the pages' and C6.4's recovery time"), `bundle_sha256`, `tsa_ok`, `tsa_time`, `cleanup_ok`, `error_code`, `error_message`, `worker_id`, `connector_id`, `plan_id`; `test_item` holds per item `type` (`mail`, `sharepoint`, `onedrive`), `name`, `expected_kind`, `found`, `match`, `reason`, `ms`; `worker` holds `name`, `key_id` (the SHA-256 of the key's DER, the signature's own `key_id`: the fingerprint the contract already has) and `public_key_pem`; `connector.type` is `veeam_m365`; `test_plan` the three sizes. `Storage.put(key, body, content_type)` writes one object, synchronous, run in a thread. `app/ui.py`'s Jinja2 environment autoescapes with `StrictUndefined` over `app/templates/` and carries the filters `utc`, `duration`, `colour`, `yes_no`. `app/audit.py`'s `ACTIONS` is the pages' closed list; the CLI's words are `app/onboarding.py`'s and each command writes its one row through `AuditRepo.write` with `user_id` and `ip` null. `manage.py` reads `DATABASE_URL` alone; the S3 settings are read by `load_settings` with the rest. `tools/check_coverage.py` guards `app/auth`, `app/results.py`, `app/repo`, `app/cadence.py`, `app/contract.py`. `cloud/Dockerfile` is `python:3.12-slim` with `uv sync --locked --no-dev` and no apt package.

**What the investigation found, since the points rest on it.**

- **WeasyPrint on Linux, shown today in a throwaway container** (`python:3.12-slim`, `apt-get install libpango-1.0-0 libpangoft2-1.0-0 libharfbuzz-subset0 fonts-dejavu-core`, `pip install weasyprint`): WeasyPrint **70.0** installs and renders. One HTML rendered twice, a second apart, gives **the same bytes** (5861 of them for a probe page). The PDF holds **no `/CreationDate`, no `/ModDate`, no `/ID` and no `/Producer`** unless asked: a date comes only from the document's own `<meta name="dcterms.created">`, and an identifier only from the `pdf_identifier` option (given, the trailer gets `/ID [(the value) (an md5 of the content)]`). So the two-hash scheme needs no scrubbing: the same HTML is the same file, and the hash cell is the one difference between the passes. The bytes differ between machines whose fonts differ, which the scheme never needs (both passes run in one process on one machine).
- **WeasyPrint on this laptop:** there is no GTK runtime (no `gtk-update-icon-cache` or `pango-view` on `PATH`, no GTK3 install, no MSYS2). The wheel is pure Python and installs under uv on Windows; `import weasyprint` then fails at the first use for want of `gobject`, `pango` and `harfbuzz` DLLs. WeasyPrint's own Windows instructions are the GTK3 runtime (the "GTK for Windows Runtime Environment Installer", which puts the DLLs on `PATH`) or MSYS2's `mingw-w64-x86_64-pango`, with `WEASYPRINT_DLL_DIRECTORIES` when they are elsewhere.
- **What the issue's words read from.** Test log "date": `finished_at` (`created_at` for a run that never finished, as the pages do); "restore point time": `restore_point_at`; "items tested (mail/SP/OD counts)": `test_item` rows grouped by `type` per run, which no column holds; "result": `state`; "recovery time": `recovery_ms`; "run id (short)": the first eight hex digits of `test_run.id`. Failures "what was missing or mismatched (item names and reason)": the `test_item` rows of the run whose `match` is not true (`found` false is missing, `match` false is a mismatch, both null an item that couldn't be checked), with `name` and `reason`; an `error` run also has `error_code` and `error_message` (the Worker's fixed words). Integrity "Worker ids and public key fingerprints": `worker.id`, `worker.name`, `worker.key_id`; "list of run ids with each bundle_sha256": `test_run.id`, `bundle_sha256`; "TSA status per run": `tsa_ok` with `tsa_time`. Summary "restore points covered": the distinct `restore_point_at` values, their count, first and last; "backup source": the connector's `type`, worded (`veeam_m365` is "Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365"). Method "sample sizes": the client's plans' three sizes (`PlanRepo.list(client_id=)`). Nothing the report prints needs `result.json` from the bucket.
- **Which time puts a run in a month.** The strip and the history page a run by `created_at`; "date" on the pages is `finished_at`. Q6.1's test holds that "for each run in the report, the TSA token's time is within the period", and `tsa_time` is the token's `genTime`, seconds after `finished_at` (the Worker stamps the result it has just written): a run queued at 23:58 on the 31st and finished at 00:40 on the 1st would, by `created_at`, sit in a report whose period its token's time is outside. So membership is by the time the test ended, with the one fallback below.
- **A month of runs.** `check_spacing`'s floor is five minutes (the C5.9 review): a `*/5` plan makes 8,928 runs a month, every one a Test log row; the stack's revoked-Worker MSP has 168 and counting, `queued`. A daily plan is at most 31 rows, a weekly one 5. Nothing in this task caps the log; the floor is already an open item.
- **The second report of one period.** C6.6's "Generate now" makes a report of the current period "marked interim in the PDF title", for a pilot that won't wait, so one period has interim reports and then the final; the issue's key `{period}.pdf` holds one object per period, and a row's hashes stop matching the object the moment a second generation overwrites it (Q6.1's first test, "stored file hash equals SHA-256 of the downloaded PDF", would fail for every older row). Nothing about a report is ever edited or re-signed (the rule for runs), and nothing deletes one but C7.3.
- **No settings reader but `load_settings`** gives the S3 values alone; the scheduler (C6.6's job will run there) and the CLI read `DATABASE_URL` and `LOG_LEVEL` and nothing else today, and `Settings` has no default for `SECRET_KEY`.
- **Reading a PDF's text in a test:** WeasyPrint writes text as glyph ids inside compressed streams, so a hash printed on a page is not a substring of the file; `pypdf` (pure Python) extracts the text.
- **Finding 8 of the C6.1–C6.3 review:** `make_world` plants its hand-written audit row at the fixed `NOW + 30 days` (2026-11-09 12:00Z) so that `AuditRepo.page(since, before=that row)` has the connectors' rows before it; the connectors' rows take the database's clock, so from 2026-11-09 they are after the planted row and the read answers nothing: `assert rows_of(own)` fails with no code change.

**Proposed.**

1. **The `report` row: `content_sha256` and `file_sha256` replace `sha256`; `interim`; one final report per client and period; migration `0001` edited in place.** The columns: `content_sha256 text NOT NULL` (`ck_report_content_sha256_hex`), `file_sha256 text NOT NULL` (`ck_report_file_sha256_hex`), `interim boolean NOT NULL` (no default: the generator always says), `period_start date NOT NULL`, `period_end date NOT NULL` with `ck_report_period_order` (`period_end >= period_start`), `storage_key text NOT NULL` with `uq_report_storage_key`, `generated_at timestamptz NOT NULL` (the generator's clock, given, no longer the database's default), `UniqueConstraint("msp_id", "id")` as every table another may point at (C6.6's `report.download` row names a report by its id in `target`, not a key, but the unique costs nothing and keeps the rule), and **`uq_report_final_period`: a partial unique index on `(msp_id, client_id, period_start) WHERE NOT interim`**, so a period has one final report and as many interim ones as were asked for. `constraint_refusal` words the two: `period: already reported`, `storage_key: already used`. A database that ran the old `0001` needs `alembic downgrade -1` and `upgrade head` once (`docs/testing.md`); the `UtcDateTime` count stays nineteen. **A second generation of one period:** an interim one is a new row and a new object (point 8's key carries its time); a final one is refused by the index, with no object written (the row is flushed before the put, as the upload writes rows before objects), so a final report is made once and its object is never replaced; `Storage.put` still replaces by its nature, and the unique on the key is what keeps a key from being written twice. A late bundle (an `error interrupted` landing after the month's final report) is not in that report and nothing regenerates it in Stage 1; the owner may add a `--replace` (a new row and the old one kept) later. *Rejected:* one row per period updated in place (the rule against editing evidence, and Q6.1's test); the report id in every key (the issue's key is `{period}.pdf`, and a final report is the one a reader looks for by month).
2. **WeasyPrint: a runtime dependency; Pango and a font in the image; the GTK runtime on this laptop, so the gate stays one `uv run pytest` with nothing skipped.** `weasyprint>=70` in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`; `pypdf` as a dev dependency (the tests read the PDF's text). The Dockerfile gains one `apt-get install --no-install-recommends libpango-1.0-0 libpangoft2-1.0-0 libharfbuzz-subset0 fonts-dejavu-core` (the four packages the probe rendered with; the lists cleaned in the same layer), before `uv sync`, so a code change doesn't reinstall them; `tests/test_schemas.py` holds the four names in the Dockerfile and `weasyprint` among the runtime dependencies. **On this laptop the build installs the GTK3 runtime once** (the installer WeasyPrint's documentation names, per machine, adding its `bin` to `PATH`; recorded in `docs/environment.md` and `docs/testing.md` "Cloud" with the version installed), and the rendering tests then run natively under `uv run pytest` like every other test. The renderer imports WeasyPrint inside the one function that calls it (`render.py`'s `render_pdf`), so the suite, the app and the scheduler import nothing of it until a report is rendered, and a machine without the runtime fails the rendering tests with the library's own `OSError` and **never skips them** (the rule for the database). The stylesheet names `DejaVu Sans` with `sans-serif` as the fallback: the image renders with DejaVu, the laptop with whatever Windows gives for the family, and the bytes differ between the two, which nothing depends on; the deployment's PDF is the image's, and the Done-when below is shown on the stack. *Rejected:* running the PDF tests in the container alone (a second gate command, a dev image with pytest and the tests mounted, and the coverage figure split in two; kept as the fallback if the runtime can't be installed here: a `test` Compose profile running `pytest -m pdf` in the image); MSYS2 (a 1 GB toolchain for three DLLs); vendoring a font into the repository (1.4 MB for a look the apt package gives); a `pytest.importorskip` (a green run that rendered nothing).
3. **The Framework mapping section before C6.7: the four controls by identifier and name, and one sentence that says the mapping sentences are not in this report yet.** The table has the issue's four rows (ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.13 "Information backup"; SOC 2 Availability A1.2 and A1.3; HIPAA 45 CFR 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(D) "Testing and revision procedures"; DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Article 12 "Backup policies and procedures, restoration and recovery procedures and methods") with the two columns the issue names, "What this evidence demonstrates" and "What it does not cover", and under the table one sentence: *"The sentences relating this evidence to each control are being written and reviewed by an outside reader (C6.7) and are not part of this report yet."* The two columns hold a dash until C6.7 fills them. The identifiers and titles are the controls' own names, not claims; the section is populated and claims nothing. The rows live in `app/report/frameworks.py` as a tuple of four entries (identifier, name, demonstrates, not_covered), the last two `None` now; C6.7 decides whether its `frameworks.yaml` replaces the constant (a YAML file needs `pyyaml`; the task that wants it adds it) and fills them. *Rejected:* leaving the section out until C6.7 (the Done-when says every section); placeholder sentences in the two columns (text in a customer's PDF that a reviewer hasn't read).
4. **The period is one UTC calendar month, named `YYYY-MM`; a run is the period's by the time it ended; `pass`, `fail` and `error` are the tests; an `expired` run is counted as a scheduled test that did not run; `queued` and `dispatched` are never in a report.** `period_start` is the month's first day and `period_end` its last (both inclusive, dates), the span `[start 00:00:00Z, end + 1 day 00:00:00Z)`. A run in `pass`, `fail` or `error` belongs to the month of **`coalesce(finished_at, created_at)`** (`finished_at` is null only for a result whose `ended_at` the calendar refused, C5.7; the fallback keeps every finished run in exactly one month). An `expired` run belongs to the month of `created_at` and is **not a test**: it appears in the Summary as one line, "Scheduled tests that did not run: N", and in the Test log as a row whose result is "did not run" with dashes, so a client whose Worker was silent all month reads why the log is short; it counts in neither "tests run" nor "N of M". A `queued` or `dispatched` run is not over and is in no report (an interim report of the current month lists what has happened; what hasn't is C6.6's page's to show). **`tsa_time` never decides membership** (null for an untimestamped run); it is printed per run in the Integrity section and is Q6.1's to hold against the period, which closes the open item "`tsa_time` against a report's period" for C6.4's half. *Recorded for Q6.1:* a run that ended at 23:59:58 on the last day with a token at 00:00:03 the next is this month's by its end and its token is a few seconds outside; Q6.1's test should allow the stamping's seconds. Interim: a report is **interim when its period's end is not before the generation day** (`period_end >= generated_at.date()`), derived, never a flag; the PDF's title says "Interim report" and the Summary says the period is not over. A month that hasn't begun is refused (`period: has not begun`); a month with no run of the client in it is refused (`period: no run in the period`; C6.6 generates only for clients with a run, and the CLI's operator is told). *Rejected:* `created_at` for the tests (the Q6.1 reasoning above); `tsa_time` (null for a run without a token; and a Worker's signed `ended_at` is the test's own word of when it ended); listing pending runs (an interim report would say "queued", which is no evidence).
5. **The data: eight repo reads, each with `msp_id` first, one statement each, a fixed count whatever the rows, and three new methods in the isolation table.** `MspRepo.get`, `ClientRepo.get` (`None` → `client_id: no such client`, never another MSP's), `ConnectorRepo.list(msp_id, client_id=)` (the backup source's wording from the types; one type expected, several listed), `PlanRepo.list(msp_id, client_id=)` (the Method's sizes, per plan), `WorkerRepo.list(msp_id)` (names and `key_id` for the runs' Workers, matched in Python), and three new: **`RunRepo.period(msp_id, client_id, *, start, end) -> list[TestRun]`** (the finished runs by `coalesce(finished_at, created_at)` in the span and the `expired` ones by `created_at`, oldest first by that time then id), **`ItemRepo.counts_by_type_in_period(msp_id, client_id, *, start, end) -> list[TypeCount]`** (`run_id`, `type`, count, from `test_item` joined to `test_run` on `(msp_id, run_id)` under the same span, grouped; no list of ids travels to the database, so a month of 8,928 runs is still one statement), **`ItemRepo.unmatched_in_period(msp_id, client_id, *, start, end) -> list[TestItem]`** (the items of the span's `fail` and `error` runs whose `match` is not true, by run then `position`). The span's condition lives once, in `app/repo/runs.py` (`period_filter`), and `items.py` imports it. Then `ReportRepo.create` (its new signature: `period_start`, `period_end`, `storage_key`, `content_sha256`, `file_sha256`, `interim`, `generated_at`) and one `AuditRepo.write`: ten statements, held by a test on a month of three runs and a month of sixty. `unmatched_in_period` and `counts_by_type_in_period` go in the isolation table as reads (the count read as a `COUNTS` entry, like `daily_states`); `ReportRepo.create`'s row in `make_world` takes the new columns. **What the sections hold:** *Summary:* client and MSP names, the period, "Interim" when it is, the overall line ("All N tests passed", or "N of M tests failed" and, kept apart, "K of M tests could not run (error)"; fail and error never add up into one number), tests run, average and maximum recovery time over the runs with `recovery_ms` (a dash when none has it), the did-not-run line when N > 0, the backup source, restore points covered (count, first, last), and C6.5's sentence *"This report does not test full disaster recovery. It shows that the sampled items listed here were restored and verified on the dates shown."* (the issue's exact text, put in now so the first PDF carries it; C6.5's review may change it). *Test log:* one row per run, oldest first: date, restore point time, items tested as `mail / SP / OD`, result (`pass`, `fail`, `error`, or "did not run"), recovery time, the run id's first eight hex digits. *Failures:* one block per `fail` or `error` run, oldest first: the date, the result, for an `error` its `error_code` and `error_message`, the unmatched items (type, name, what was found: "missing", "mismatch", "not checked", and the `reason` word), and **"re-tested and passed on <date>"** when a later `pass` run of the client is in the period, else "no later test in this period passed"; a report with no such run says "No test failed or errored in this period." *Method:* the fixed paragraph: the plans' sizes ("each test restored up to M mails, S SharePoint files and O OneDrive files"; one sentence per plan when there are several), canary plus random selection, the three restore targets by role (the `restoretest` mailbox, the `RestoreTarget` library, the `/RestoreTarget` OneDrive folder, by name alone, never an id), the comparison fields (a canary's content hash; a random mail's subject, received time and sender; a random file's name and size), and the issue's exact "Verification levels covered: 1, 2, 3; level 4 partially (files opened and read via Microsoft Graph)". *Integrity:* the content hash and the file-hash sentence (point 6), the Workers (name, id, `key_id` as the fingerprint), the runs (id, `bundle_sha256`, "timestamped <tsa_time>" or "not timestamped"), and the generation time. *Framework mapping:* point 3. Every time in the PDF is `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC`, as the pages print it.
6. **Two passes, one difference, held by the test: the content hash is the SHA-256 of pass 1, the file hash the SHA-256 of pass 2, and WeasyPrint's defaults embed nothing that varies.** `render_html(data, content_hash)` renders the one template; pass 1 with the hash cell reading "computed after this report was rendered; see the note below", pass 2 with the hex. `render_pdf(html) -> bytes` is the one WeasyPrint call (`HTML(string=..., base_url=the report directory).write_pdf(stylesheets=[the css])`, defaults otherwise: no `pdf_identifier`, no `dcterms` meta in the template, so no date and no id in the file). `render_report(data) -> Rendered(html_1, content_sha256, html_2, pdf, file_sha256)`. The one sentence, in the Integrity section: *"A file cannot contain its own hash. The content hash above is the SHA-256 of this report rendered without it; the file hash, which the Cloud stores beside this report and which you can check yourself, is the SHA-256 of the file you are reading."* The test holds: `sha256(render_pdf(html_1)) == content_sha256` (the renderer gives the same bytes again, in the test's own process), `sha256(pdf) == file_sha256`, `html_2` equals `html_1` with the placeholder replaced and nothing else, the hex appears in `pypdf`'s text of `pdf` and the placeholder does not, and two `render_report` calls on one `ReportData` give one `content_sha256` and one `file_sha256`. The generation time is part of `ReportData` (the generator's clock, once), so both passes print one time. *Rejected:* `pdf_identifier` set to the content hash (a second place the hash lives, and the trailer's md5 beside it; nothing reads it); scrubbing dates after render (there are none).
7. **Where the code lives, guarded; rendering in a thread; the object through `Storage.put`.** `app/report/` is a package: `data.py` (`ReportData`, `RunLine`, `Failure`, `period_of("YYYY-MM") -> Period`, `gather(session, msp_id, client_id, period, *, now) -> ReportData`: the eight reads and the pure arithmetic — the overall line, the averages, the restore points, the re-test lookup, the did-not-run count), `render.py` (`render_html`, `render_pdf`, `render_report`, the environment: `ui.py`'s factory given `app/report/` as its folder, so the report template autoescapes with `StrictUndefined` and has the pages' filters; `tests/test_login.py`'s "every template autoescapes" extends to it), `frameworks.py` (point 3), `generate.py` (`generate(session, storage, msp_id, client_id, period, *, user_id, ip) -> Created`: `gather`, `render_report` in `asyncio.to_thread` (CPU work of seconds; never on the loop), the `report` row, one audit row **`report.create`** `report:<id>` (the generator's word, written as the CLI's are, `user_id` and `ip` from the caller: null from the CLI, the user from C6.6's button), then `Storage.put(key, pdf, "application/pdf")` in a thread, in that order, so a refused row writes no object and a failed put rolls the row back), `template.html` and `report.css` (the issue's two files, A4, the six sections in the issue's order, page numbers from CSS counters, the Summary on the first page by itself for Q6.1's 30-second check, no script, no image, no link). `tools/check_coverage.py` gains **`app/report`** (every branch of the decisions above has a test; `render_pdf`'s one call is covered by the real renderer). `ui.py` gains `make_environment(folder)` and keeps `environment()` over it. **The key:** `msp/{msp_id}/reports/{client_id}/{YYYY-MM}.pdf` for a final report, the issue's; `msp/{msp_id}/reports/{client_id}/{YYYY-MM}-interim-{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ}.pdf` for an interim one (its generation time, so a second one is a second object; a second in the same second meets `uq_report_storage_key`). **`manage.py generate-report --msp-id --client-id --period YYYY-MM`** (the period defaults to the previous month) prints `report_id`, `storage_key`, `period`, `interim`, `content_sha256`, `file_sha256`; a refusal is one `<key>: <reason>` line and exit 1 as every command's; it is the one way to make a report before C6.6 and the way the Done-when is shown on the stack. It needs the bucket, so **`settings.storage_settings_from_environment()`** reads `S3_ENDPOINT`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_SECRET_KEY`, `S3_BUCKET` and `S3_REGION` alone (`StorageSettings`, held to the same shapes, a fault naming the variable), and `make_s3_client` takes either settings object (it reads the five `s3_*` fields); the CLI and, in C6.6, the scheduler read no `SECRET_KEY`. *Rejected:* rendering on the loop; streaming the PDF back from the CLI (the object is the report; the page of C6.6 hands it out); a route in this task (C6.6's).
8. **No secret, no link, nothing of another tenant.** The PDF holds no token, no key PEM (the `key_id` alone), no pre-signed URL, no bucket name, no `http` at all, no tenant id (the client is named by its name; the Worker by its name and id), and no address of a person: a mail item's `name` is its subject, as the run page shows it (the W4.1 rule holds the result, so the row), and a file's its name. A test scans both passes' HTML and the PDF's text for `Bearer`, `BEGIN `, `X-Amz`, `http`, `?`, the lab's tenant id and the test key's PEM. A planted `<script>` in a client's name, an MSP's name, a Worker's name, an item's name and an `error_message` is escaped in both passes (a test renders each). The four banned phrases (`fully recoverable`, `guarantee`, `certified`, `accepted by insurers`) are held out of `template.html`, `report.css`, `frameworks.py`, both passes' HTML and the PDF's text by one parametrised test, in any case; C6.5's review adds to the list, not to the test.
9. **Status vocabulary in the report.** `pass`, `fail`, `error` are printed as the words the pages print, with the pages' colours (green, red, amber) and, once in the Summary, their meaning in one line each: a `pass` "every sampled item was restored and matched", a `fail` "an item was missing or did not match", an `error` "the test itself could not run (the backup product, the tenant or the Worker was not available); it says nothing about the backup". The Failures section keeps the two apart by the result word and its block's heading; "N of M tests failed" never counts an `error`. An infrastructure problem is never a `fail` (the Worker decides; the Cloud files; the report prints).
10. **Finding 8 of the C6.1–C6.3 review, fixed here.** `make_world` places its hand-written audit row **30 days after the newest audit row of the MSP** (one `UPDATE` from `max(at)`), not after the fixed `NOW`, so the connectors' rows are before it on any day; and `make_world` takes `clock=` which, given, first moves every audit row of the world to that time, so `test_the_audit_reads_hold_on_a_moved_clock` runs the two `AuditRepo.page` reads of the table on worlds whose clock is 2027-06-01 (past the fixed date) and 2040-01-01 and shows they answer the world's own rows and nothing of the other's. The finding is marked closed in `CLAUDE.md`.
11. **Left to the neighbours, by name.** C6.6: the scheduler's job on the 1st at 03:00 UTC calling `generate` per client with a run in the previous month (through `storage_settings_from_environment` in the scheduler's process), `/clients/{id}/reports`, "Generate now" (an interim report of the current month: `generate` with the user), `report.download` and the "Reports" nav entry, a cap or a page limit for a month of thousands of runs, and whether a final report may be re-made. C6.5: the wording review. C6.7: the two columns of point 3 and the reviewer's comments. Q6.1: the two tests (the file hash against the object, each run's `tsa_time` within the period) and the 30-second check; `docs/report-usability.md`. C7.3: `report` rows kept a year longer than runs. Not in this task: a signature over the PDF (the issue stores hashes; the bundle is the signed evidence), a locale or a client's time zone (UTC), a report over more than one month.

**Tests first** (`tests/test_report.py` over `tests/pages_lab.py`'s world, with `tests/report_lab.py` for the month's runs: the Worker-written vector landed as the month's `pass`, and runs made by hand in the three other states with items). The Done-when by name, `test_a_pdf_renders_for_a_client_with_one_failure_and_one_error_in_the_period_and_every_section_is_populated`: a month with a `pass` (the vector's), a `fail` with a missing and a mismatched item, an `error` with its code, a later `pass`, an `expired` run; `generate` answers the lines, the row holds both hashes, the object is put under the final key with the PDF's bytes (the Stubber's exact body), the audit row is written, and `pypdf`'s text of the PDF holds the six headings in order and, section by section, the client's and MSP's names, "1 of 4 tests failed", "1 of 4 tests could not run", the average and maximum, the did-not-run line, the restore points, the four log rows with their counts and short ids, the two failure blocks with the item names, reasons and "re-tested and passed on", the Method's sizes and levels sentence, both hashes, the Workers' ids and fingerprints, each run's `bundle_sha256` and TSA line, the four controls. Failure paths first: another MSP's client is `client_id: no such client` with nothing written (both directions); a month that hasn't begun, a period text outside `YYYY-MM` and a month with no run each refused with nothing written; a second final report of one month refused by `uq_report_final_period` with no put (the Stubber sees none); a put that fails leaves no row (the transaction rolls back); the banned phrases; the planted `<script>`; the secret scan; a run of another client of the same MSP in the same month not in the report; a `queued` and a `dispatched` run not in it; a run that ended on the first second of the month in it and one that ended on the last second of the month before not; `finished_at` null falling back to `created_at`; a `fail` with no later `pass` ("no later test in this period passed"); no `recovery_ms` anywhere giving dashes; the statement count the same for three runs and sixty. Then point 6's hash tests, the interim key and title for the current month, two interim reports of one month as two rows and two objects, the repo methods by themselves (`period`'s span edges and order, `counts_by_type_in_period`, `unmatched_in_period`, the isolation table), the CLI (`generate-report` through `CliRunner` on a database of its own with the Stubber, the lines printed, each refusal one line and exit 1, `S3_*` read and `SECRET_KEY` not), `storage_settings_from_environment` (each variable missing or malformed named, never a value), `tests/test_schemas.py` for the dependency and the Dockerfile's packages, `tests/test_check_coverage.py` for the new guarded path, and point 10's moved-clock test. Red before green on the empty package, the old `report` columns and the old isolation world.

**Done-when, as it will be run.** With the Compose Postgres up, from `cloud/`: `uv run --locked pytest`, the two coverage commands (the gate, in the background), `uv run python tools/dump_openapi.py` and the document unchanged (no route changes). Then on the Compose stack (`docs/api/cloud-lab/c6.4-harness/c64-live.ps1`, its text `docs/api/cloud-lab/c6.4-done-when.txt`, the C6.1–C6.3 harness's screening rules): (1) the stack rebuilt with the four packages and the font (`dpkg -l` in the container), `downgrade -1`, `upgrade head`, `check`; (2) MSP A as the C6.1–C6.3 harness makes it, the kept C5.7 bundle landed as the month's `pass`, and by SQL two more runs of that client given the shapes of a `fail` (two unmatched items) and an `error` (a code) with `finished_at` in the same month, and one `expired`; (3) `docker compose exec api python manage.py generate-report --msp-id … --client-id … --period <that month>`: the six lines; the row; the object listed in MinIO and fetched (`mc` or a pre-signed GET from the harness), its SHA-256 equal to `file_sha256`, its page count and text (`pypdf` on the host) with the six headings; the PDF kept beside the evidence as `docs/api/cloud-lab/c6.4-sample-report.pdf` **only if** it names no person and no tenant id (the harness scans it; the kept bundle's items are canary subjects and lab file names), else its text alone; (4) the same command again → `period: already reported`, exit 1, no second object; the current month → an interim report, its key with the time and "Interim report" in its text; (5) the api's lines with nothing of the bucket in them. Not in CI: no job has started since 2026-10-03.

**Alternatives rejected, beyond the points.** *A report built from `result.json` objects* (one object read per run; the columns C5.7 and C6.2 filed are the report's reads, and the bundle stays the evidence a verifier takes). *HTML reports with a print stylesheet* (the issue says PDF with stored hashes; a browser's print is not one file). *ReportLab* (a layout API instead of the template the issue names; WeasyPrint takes the same HTML and CSS the pages are written in). *Signing the PDF with the Cloud's own key* (nothing asks; the Worker's signature is on the evidence, and a Cloud key would be a new secret with no verifier).
