## 2026-10-12 — C5.11 (#64): versioning, the OpenAPI document and the contract test. Every response carries `X-RestoreProof-API: 1`; `GET /v1/version` answers the contract's number and the Cloud's version without a token; the three routes that take the Worker's bearer token say so in the OpenAPI document by the dependency itself; a CI job regenerates `docs/api/openapi-v1.json` and fails on a difference; a 64 KiB cap on every request body but the upload's; "No test, no merge" also looks at `cloud/manage.py` and `shared/tools/`; and the contract test posts a bundle the C++ Worker made from a job of the Cloud's shape, byte for byte, to 202 (recorded before the build)

C5.11 (#64) is built on its own branch, `c5.11-contract`, in one PR with two commits (the code, then the docs), as C5.7 (#173) and C5.8 (#174) were. Done when: "The contract test passes against a fixture generated by the C++ Worker." This entry works from issue #64, the guide's C5.11, W5.1 and W7.2 text, the 2026-10-10 entries "C5.5 and C5.6" (point 7, the first committed document and what it left to this task; point 10, the W5.1 proposal), "C5.7" (points 15, 17 and 18; its open list: the security scheme on "the three Worker routes", `shared/tools/` under the guard, the fixture bundle, and "a vector written by the Worker's hidden case from a job of the Cloud's shape"), the 2026-10-11 entries "C5.8" (point 8, point 12, its open list: the security scheme on "the four Worker routes", the JSON body cap) and "C5.10 and C5.9" (its open list: `manage.py` under the guard), each with its build notes and code review, `docs/testing.md` "Cloud" and "The shared signing vectors", and the code (`cloud/app/main.py`, `logging.py`, `health.py`, `auth/dependency.py`, `routers/*.py`, `results.py`, `tools/dump_openapi.py`, `tests/test_openapi.py`, `tests/test_app.py`, `tests/results_lab.py`, `tests/test_results_vectors.py`, `.github/workflows/cloud.yml`, `.github/workflows/pr-guards.yml`, `.github/scripts/tests_touched.py`, `worker/tests/worker_body_lab.hpp`, `worker/tests/worker_body_test.cpp`, `worker/tests/signer_test.cpp`, `worker/src/outbox.cpp`, `worker/src/uploader.cpp`). No code is written yet; the build notes will record what the build finds. **The Worker's product code is not changed** (`worker/src`, `worker/include`, `worker/app` untouched); **one hidden test case is added under `worker/tests/`** and one shared vector under `shared/testdata/`, for the reason point 7 gives.

**Where issue #64 is stale against the code, settled from the code.** (a) "All routes under /v1": built since C5.1 and held by `tests/test_app.py` (`/healthz` the one route outside, by design); nothing to build, the test stays. (b) "OpenAPI JSON committed to docs/api/openapi-v1.json": committed since C5.6 and held equal to what the app serves by `tests/test_openapi.py`, regenerated by `tools/dump_openapi.py`; what is left is the CI job's own diff (point 4) and the security scheme (point 3). (c) "the Worker's recorded fixture bundle (from Q2.1/W4.1)": there is no recorded *bundle* under `worker/tests/fixtures/`; Q2.1's recordings are HTTP exchanges with Veeam and Graph, and W4.1's result is what the Worker's pipeline makes from them (`shared/testdata/result-v1/valid.json`, written by `rptests "[.write_shared_result]"` from the whole pipeline's run on the test Harness), which W4.3 signed into `shared/testdata/signing-v1/bundle.json`. That bundle is Worker-made but can't reach 202 (below), so point 7 has the Worker make one that can. (d) The issue's step 3 is already half built: `tests/test_results.py::test_the_tests_pass_and_a_real_worker_bundle_lands_as_pass_in_the_db` posts `bundle.json` to 202, **re-keyed and re-signed in Python** (`tests/results_lab.py`: `run_id` and `client.client_id` replaced, the canonical bytes signed again with the published key through `cryptography`). The result's bytes and the signature are then Python's, not the C++ Worker's; the Done-when wants the Worker's.

**What the investigation found, since the points below rest on it.**

- **No shared vector can reach 202 as it is.** `POST /v1/results` names the run only after the whole verification, by the exact text `str(test_run.id)` (a lower-case hyphenated uuid; the C5.7 review's finding 10), and holds `result.client.client_id` to `str(client.id)` (C5.7 point 9 (a); null is a mismatch). `signing-v1/bundle.json`'s result has `run_id` `rp-20261004T100000Z-0a1b2c3d` and `client_id` null (written before C5.6 made `run_id` the run's uuid and before W4.10 gave a job its `client_id`); `closed-folder.json`'s has `closed-run-1` and null. So every verified case through the route is 404 `run_id: no such run` (`tests/test_results_vectors.py`, by design), and the one 202 is on a re-signed copy.
- **The one Worker harness that makes a run with a `client_id` is the service's.** `rpworker test` at a prompt writes `client_id` null (W4.8 point 3, W4.10); the job gives it. `worker/tests/worker_body_lab.hpp`'s `BodyLab` runs `rp::make_worker_loop_env`'s real env (the pipeline in process on the restore tests' Harness, the record, the outbox, the close, the uploader to a `FakeHttpClient` Cloud) from a `jobs.json` the test writes; `worker_body_test.cpp` already runs a job to `ended pass; queued`, `sent`, with `result.client.client_id` `"client-7"` and the five parts posted to the fake Cloud's `/v1/results`. `closed-folder.json` is written from that lab (`[.write_shared_closed]`), so a second vector from it is the established way. `RP_SHARED_DIR` is `<repo>/shared` for `rptests`. The Harness's client is result-v1's made-up tenant (`11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555`, `contoso.onmicrosoft.com`), which `tests/results_lab.py` already uses as the client row's tenant, and the signing key is RFC 8032's published test key 1. The result names `worker_version` `0.0.0` (`RP_VERSION`), as every vector does.
- **The Worker reads nothing of an answer but its status.** `CloudUploader::upload` tests `response.status == kUploadAccepted` and nothing else (no header, no body); `send_heartbeat` takes any 2xx; the jobs reader takes a document. So a response header costs the Worker nothing today, and what it should do with one is W5.1's (point 8).
- **Nothing bounds a JSON request body.** uvicorn 0.54 has no body-size setting and starlette's parser caps only multipart parts (the C5.7 entry's investigation); `POST /v1/results` holds its own cap on the bytes (96 MiB, `_Body`, the C5.7 review's finding 1); registration's body is a parameter FastAPI reads whole (`await request.body()`) before validation, and `heartbeat_body` reads it whole after the token. An honest registration body is about 500 bytes (a key file of about 120 characters and a 43-character token), an honest heartbeat under 200. The Compose stack has no proxy in front of the api, and `cloud/docker-compose.yml` and `cloud/.env.example` name none.
- **The document shows no security scheme.** FastAPI writes `components.securitySchemes` and an operation's `security` only for a dependency that is a `SecurityBase` (`fastapi.security.HTTPBearer` and its kin); `current_worker` reads the header itself (`_presented_token`, the one strict parse: `Bearer <token>`, one space), so the three routes that depend on it (`GET /v1/jobs`, `POST /v1/results`, `POST /v1/heartbeat`) show no scheme. `HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)` returns `None` for a missing or non-bearer header and never raises (`fastapi/security/http.py`); it reads the header and changes nothing. **`POST /v1/workers/register` takes no bearer token:** the install token is a field of its body (C5.5 point 3), so the C5.8 entry's "the four Worker routes" is three plus one whose credential is in the body, which the document already shows as `RegisterBody.install_token`.
- **The CI diff.** `tests/test_openapi.py::test_the_committed_document_is_what_the_app_serves` already fails the test job on a stale file; what it doesn't give is a check named for the contract and the diff itself in the job's output. `cloud.yml` has two jobs (`test` with a Postgres service, `compose`); neither has run since 2026-10-03. `tools/dump_openapi.py` needs no database (closed-loopback placeholders) and takes a path.
- **"No test, no merge"** (`.github/scripts/tests_touched.py`, L0.5): two `Side`s, `worker/src|include|app` → `worker/tests/` `.cpp|.hpp|.h`, `cloud/app/` → `cloud/tests/` `.py`; a prefix match on directories ending in `/`. `cloud/manage.py` (C5.10) is outside `cloud/app/` and `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` (the Cloud's verifier since C5.7) is outside both; neither change needs a test today. The script's tests (`.github/scripts/test_tests_touched.py`, run by `pr-guards.yml`'s `guard-tests` job with `uvx pytest`) are a `CASES` table.
- **The six routers are held by name** (`tests/test_app.py`, `ROUTER_NAMES`), each a module under `app/routers/` with a `router`; `main.ROUTERS` wires them under `/v1`. `app/__init__.py`'s `__version__` is `0.0.0` and is the document's `info.version`. `/v1/openapi.json` and `/v1/docs` are served to anyone (no token), so the Cloud's version is public already.
- **The middleware.** `RequestLogMiddleware` is pure ASGI, the one middleware, and rewrites `http.response.start`'s headers to echo `x-request-id`; it also makes its own 500 when a route raises. Starlette runs the last-added middleware outermost.
- **CI has not run since 2026-10-03.** Every gate is run locally and its figures go into the build notes, as for C5.1 to C5.10.

**Decision.**

1. **`X-RestoreProof-API: 1` on every response the app sends, by one outermost pure-ASGI middleware.** `app/contract.py` (new; **guarded under `tools/check_coverage.py` at 100% line and branch**, since it answers every request) holds `API_VERSION = 1` (the contract's number: the `1` of `/v1`, and `main.API_PREFIX` is held equal to `f"/v{API_VERSION}"` by a test), `API_HEADER = "X-RestoreProof-API"`, and `ApiVersionMiddleware`, which adds the header to every `http.response.start` message and touches nothing else. It is added **last**, so it is outermost and stamps every answer: a route's, FastAPI's 404, 405 and 422, `RequestLogMiddleware`'s own 500, `/healthz` (both verdicts), `/v1/openapi.json`, `/v1/docs`, and point 5's 413. The value is the contract's number, not the Cloud's version: it changes when `/v2` exists and the document breaks, not when a field is added; a Worker that reads `1` knows the four routes it was built for are there in the shape it knows. The header's meaning: *this answer came from a RestoreProof Cloud speaking contract 1*, which is what a Worker pointed at a wrong host, a captive portal or a proxy's error page cannot otherwise tell from a 202.
   - *Rejected:* the header on the four Worker routes alone (the point of it is to mark what isn't one of them: an error page, a 404 from another service on the same host); the Cloud's version in the header (that is `/v1/version`'s; a header read on every answer should say one stable thing); a semantic version (`1.0`) or a date (nothing in the contract is negotiated; one number, bumped with the path); the header added in `RequestLogMiddleware` beside `x-request-id` (one middleware for logging and one for the contract; the log's middleware would then carry a rule that isn't about logging); a `Server` header (a proxy rewrites it).

2. **`GET /v1/version`, no token, a closed body `{"api": 1, "version": "<the Cloud's>"}`.** `app/routers/version.py` (new), the seventh router in `main.ROUTERS` (`tests/test_app.py`'s `ROUTER_NAMES` grows to seven; nothing else is wired), one route: `response_model=VersionBody` with `extra="forbid"`, `api: Literal[1]` (`API_VERSION`), `version: str` (`app.__version__`, the same text as the document's `info.version`, held equal by a test), `Cache-Control: no-store` as `/healthz` has. No statement, no session (the route takes neither `SessionDep` nor `current_worker`; a test counts zero statements and holds that a token, a wrong token and no token all answer 200 the same). It is in the OpenAPI document (it is under `/v1`; `/healthz` stays out) with its 200 alone. **Why no token:** it must answer before a Worker has one (W7.2's `rpworker doctor` checks `cloud_url` with it before registration, point 8), and it says nothing the anonymous `/v1/openapi.json` doesn't already say (`info.version`). **Why not in `/healthz`:** `/healthz` is the probe outside the contract, 503 when a dependency is down, and the version is true whether the bucket answers or not.
   - *Rejected:* `GET /v1/` (a root that will want to grow into an index); the version under a token (above); a git commit or build date in the body (C5.12's image is pinned by digest and the operator reads the deployment; the Cloud's `__version__` is what W7.4 gives a number to, and a commit hash in an anonymous answer is more than anyone needs); `min_worker_version` or any policy field (the Worker's upgrade is the operator's; the heartbeat carries the Worker's version up, and the page shows it).

3. **The security scheme in the document, by the dependency itself: `current_worker` depends on `HTTPBearer(auto_error=False, scheme_name="workerToken")`, so the three routes that take the bearer token carry `security: [{"workerToken": []}]` and the document gains `components.securitySchemes.workerToken` of type `http`, scheme `bearer`, with a description naming registration as where the token comes from.** The dependency's result is **not read**: `_presented_token`'s strict parse stays the one rule (one space, nothing else; `HTTPBearer` would take `Bearer  x` and `bearer x`), the one 401 stays as C5.4 made it after the same work, and `auto_error=False` means the library never answers (it would answer 403 for a missing header, against C5.4's rule). The parameter is there so the document follows the code: a fifth route that depends on `current_worker` is documented as taking the token with no second edit, and one that doesn't isn't. **Three routes, not four:** `POST /v1/workers/register` takes the install token in its body and shows it as `RegisterBody.install_token` already; it gets no `security` entry, and the entry's description of `workerToken` says that registration answers the token once. `tests/test_openapi.py` holds: the scheme's type and name, exactly `/v1/jobs`, `/v1/results` and `/v1/heartbeat` with `security`, `/v1/workers/register` and `/v1/version` without, and (the test that couples document to code) the set of operations with `security` equal to the set of routes whose dependency tree contains `current_worker` (walked through `route.dependant`). `tests/test_auth.py` holds that the scheme dependency changes no answer: the C5.4 cases (no header, `Basic`, `Bearer` with two spaces, `bearer x`, an unknown token, a revoked Worker) are the same one 401, and `app/auth/dependency.py` stays at 100% line and branch.
   - *Rejected:* `openapi_extra={"security": ...}` written on each route by hand with the component added by an `app.openapi` override (a fifth Worker route could forget it, and an override of the document's maker is a second place the contract is shaped); `HTTPBearer` *as* the authentication (`auto_error=True` answers 403 with its own text, and the parse is looser than C5.4's); a scheme on registration (its credential is not a bearer token; documenting it as one would be false).

4. **A CI job of its own, `contract` ("OpenAPI document is current"), in `.github/workflows/cloud.yml`: regenerate and diff, fail on a difference, and show a PR's contract change.** Steps: checkout (`fetch-depth: 0` for the base), `astral-sh/setup-uv`, `uv run --locked python tools/dump_openapi.py` (in place), then `git --no-pager diff --exit-code -- docs/api/openapi-v1.json`, which fails the job and prints the difference when a route changed without the regenerated file (the message names the command to run). No Postgres service: the tool connects to nothing. **Then, on `pull_request` only,** `git --no-pager diff "$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA" -- docs/api/openapi-v1.json` written into `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` under "Contract change in this PR" (or "none"): a deliberate contract change is shown to the reviewer where the check is, and **never fails** the job (every intended change would otherwise need an override). The job is a named check beside "Cloud tests", so a stale document is a red check that says what it is, not one failing test among two thousand. **Said plainly: the job is written and run step by step on the laptop (the two commands, and the base diff by hand against `main`), and has not been seen to run on a runner;** no job has since 2026-10-03.
   - *Rejected:* failing on any change of the committed file against the base (above); the diff inside the `test` job (it is there already as a test; the check wants its own name and the diff in the log); a `paths:` filter so the job runs only when `cloud/` changed (the document also changes when `shared/schemas/` changes a model the document embeds; cheap enough to run always).

5. **A cap on every request body but the upload's: `MAX_BODY_BYTES` = 64 KiB, held in the app on the header and on the bytes, 413 `{"detail": "body: too large"}`.** `app/contract.py`'s `BodyCapMiddleware` (pure ASGI, guarded) takes the set of paths that bound their own body, `{f"{API_PREFIX}/results"}` from `create_app` (a test holds that set equal to the document's operations with a `multipart/form-data` request body, so a second large-body route can't be added without naming it), and for every other request: a `Content-Length` of ASCII digits over the cap is **413** before the app is called and before a byte is read; otherwise `receive` is wrapped to count the bytes the app pulls, and the first byte over the cap ends the read in the middleware's own exception, caught by the same middleware, answered **413** when the response hasn't started (it never has for a body FastAPI reads) and re-raised otherwise. The body is `{"detail": "body: too large"}`, the words `POST /v1/results` answers for the same fault (`results.BODY_TOO_LARGE`, imported, so the two are one text), `Content-Type: application/json`, the two headers of points 1 and the request ID. The 413 is in the document on the two routes that take a body (`POST /v1/workers/register`, `POST /v1/heartbeat`, as `refusal(...)` through `responses=`); on a `GET` it is the server's answer to a body the contract has no place for, like the 404 and the 405, and is not written per route. **What this keeps of C5.8's rule:** the token still comes before the body: the header check reads no byte, and the byte counter counts only what the app pulls, which for a request without a token is nothing (`test_the_body_of_a_request_without_a_token_is_never_read` stays green); a 413 on the header before the 401 tells a caller nothing of any token (it is a header-only answer). It sits **inside** `RequestLogMiddleware` (added before it), so its 413 is logged as a request line with its ID, and **outside** the routers, so a 90 MiB `multipart/form-data` body sent to registration is 413 at the header and never buffered, where today FastAPI would hold it whole before its 422. `POST /v1/results` keeps its own checks unchanged (415, 411, 413 on the header and on the bytes, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`); the middleware leaves its path alone. **Why in the app and not C5.12's proxy:** the Compose stack and any deployment without a proxy stay unbounded otherwise, and C5.7's finding 1 showed the cap has to be on the bytes, which a proxy's `client_max_body_size` is a second line of, not the first; C5.12 may add the proxy's cap in front, and the entry says both are wanted. **Why 64 KiB:** a registration body is bounded by its model at about 4.5 KB (`public_key_pem` 4096 characters, `install_token` 256, `worker_name` 128, `version` 64) and a heartbeat at about 300 bytes; 64 KiB is a hundred times the largest honest body and small enough that buffering it for a 422 costs nothing.
   - *Rejected:* leaving it to C5.12's proxy with an entry (above: unbounded in the stack and in any deployment without one); a cap by media type (a non-multipart body at 64 KiB, a multipart one at 96 MiB: a 90 MiB multipart body to registration would then be buffered by FastAPI before its 422); reading registration's body in a dependency as `heartbeat_body` does, to cap it there (right, and C5.5's route would change for a hole only an over-cap body reaches; the middleware closes it for every route at once, this one included); a setting (`MAX_BODY_BYTES` is a constant like `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`; a deployment tunes the proxy); 413 raised as an `HTTPException` from inside the router through an exception handler (two places answer the same 413; one middleware answers both the header's and the bytes').

6. **"No test, no merge" also looks at `cloud/manage.py` and `shared/tools/`.** `.github/scripts/tests_touched.py`'s Cloud `Side` gains the file `cloud/manage.py` (matched as a path, not a prefix: `cloud/manage.pyc` or `cloud/manage.py.bak` is not it), and a third `Side` is added: `shared/tools/` → `cloud/tests/` `.py`, since the Cloud imports the verifier (C5.7 point 3) and the script's tests live in `cloud/tests/` (`test_verify_bundle*.py`); `rptests` runs the script nowhere. The message names the file or directory as it names the others. `test_tests_touched.py`'s `CASES` gains the rows, failure paths first (`cloud/manage.py` alone blocked; with `cloud/tests/test_manage.py` allowed; `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` alone blocked, with a `cloud/tests/*.py` allowed, with a `worker/tests/*.cpp` alone still blocked; `shared/tools/README.md` is source too, as `worker/tests/README.md` is not a test; `shared/toolsfoo/x.py` and `cloud/manage.pyc` not source). **Left as it is, and why:** `shared/schemas/` (a schema change is read by both builds, and the rule would want a test on each side; the schemas are held today by both vector suites and the W4.10 line-break guard; its own change when the owner wants it); `cloud/tools/` (`dump_openapi.py` is held by `tests/test_openapi.py` and `check_coverage.py` by `tests/test_check_coverage.py` already, and neither runs in the product); `shared/testdata/` (vectors are fixtures, written by hidden `rptests` cases and run by both builds' tests). `pr-guards.yml` is unchanged; the guard's own tests run as before. **Said plainly:** the widened guard is run locally (`uvx --python 3.12 pytest .github/scripts`, and the script by hand over this PR's own `git diff --name-status`) and has not been seen on a runner.

**Reason.** The contract is three things: the number a client can read on every answer, the document the code is held to, and a request the Worker really sends landing as 202. The header and `/v1/version` give a Worker and an operator the one fact nothing else carries, that the thing at `cloud_url` is a RestoreProof Cloud speaking contract 1; the security scheme and the CI job make the document follow the code and the build fail when the file doesn't; the cap closes the one hole every entry since C5.7 has carried forward, in the place every deployment has; and the fixture is made by the C++ Worker's own service loop from a job of the Cloud's shape, because a contract test that re-signs the Worker's bytes tests the test's own signature.

**Alternatives rejected, beyond the points.** *API versioning by header negotiation (`Accept: application/vnd.restoreproof.v1+json`)* (the path carries the version and the Worker's client is curl-shaped; one number in a response header is the whole need). *A contract test suite in a third language or tool (Pact, Schemathesis)* (the three verifiers and the shared vectors are the contract machinery this repository already runs on both sides; one more Worker-written vector extends it). *Running the Worker's `rptests` in the Cloud's CI to make the fixture* (the vector is committed, as every shared vector is; the Worker's CI holds it to the code and the Cloud's reads it). *A `GET /v1/jobs` answer carrying the version* (the jobs document is the Worker's closed reader; the version has its route).

**Open, left to the tasks named.**

- W5.1: point 8 (a) to (d), `upload_not_cloud`, and the C5.5, C5.7 and C5.8 proposals as before.
- W7.2: point 8 (e), `rpworker doctor`'s `cloud:` line.
- C5.12: the proxy's `client_max_body_size` as the second line in front of point 5's cap; `request.client.host` behind a proxy; the TSA root and the verifier checked at start (C5.7's finding 13); the image with `shared/tools` and `shared/tsa`.
- `shared/schemas/` under "No test, no merge" (point 6), if the owner wants a rule for both sides.
- The result schema's arrays without `maxItems` (the C5.7 review's finding 2), unchanged by the cap: the upload's own cap is the 96 MiB one.
- The Worker's `last_error` shared vector (C5.8's list), the Worker's to write.

**Done-when, as it will be run.** From `worker/`, in a VS 2022 Developer PowerShell with `VCPKG_ROOT` set back to `C:\vcpkg`: `cmake --build --preset dev`, then `build\dev\rptests.exe "[.write_shared_dispatched]"` once to write `shared/testdata/signing-v1/dispatched-run.json`, then `ctest --preset dev` (the holding test green; the figures in the build notes), and `python tools/fixture_secret_scan.py` over the new file. Then `uv run --locked pytest --cov=app --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=json:coverage.json --cov-fail-under=80` and `uv run --locked python tools/check_coverage.py coverage.json` with `app/contract.py` among the guarded files at 100/100; `uv run python tools/dump_openapi.py` and `tests/test_openapi.py` green; the CI job's two commands by hand (`tools/dump_openapi.py`, `git diff --exit-code -- docs/api/openapi-v1.json`) and the base diff against `main`; `uvx --python 3.12 pytest .github/scripts` and the guard over this PR's own diff; `docker compose up -d --wait --build` with `/healthz` 200 carrying `X-RestoreProof-API: 1` and `curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/version` answering `{"api":1,"version":"0.0.0"}` with the header, recorded as `docs/api/cloud-lab/c5.11-done-when.txt`. ## 2026-10-11 — C5.10 and C5.9 code review: findings 1 to 6 of ten fixed, 7 to 10 open; finding 4 fixed only as far as the issue's Done-when lets it be, the rest of it the owner's rule (proposed)

The review of the branch `c5.9-c5.10` against `main` (`/code-review high`) gave ten findings. The owner chose the six correctness findings to fix now. Each has a test that reproduces it; the tests were written beside the fixes, not before them, and only the old MSP-failure test was seen to fail on the way. Nothing is committed or pushed until the owner asks.

**Fixed.**

1. **croniter's random field is refused.** `parse` took `R 2 * * *` and `0 2 R(1-5) * *`: croniter draws such a field anew for every `croniter(...)`, so `due_at` gave a different period start on each tick, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` never met a conflict and a plan could get a run per tick. `parse` now refuses an `r` that is no letter of a name (`_RANDOM`; `MAR`, `FRI`, `apr` and `thu` still pass) as `not a cron expression`. Tests: eight `R` forms in `test_a_text_that_is_not_a_five_field_cron_is_refused`, `test_a_name_with_an_r_in_it_is_no_random_field`, `test_two_readers_of_one_cadence_agree_on_the_period`, and the CLI's and the onboarding's refusal rows.
2. **A cron that never occurs is a `CadenceError`, `never occurs`.** `0 0 31 2 *` passes `croniter.is_valid` and then raises `CroniterBadDateError` from `get_next` and `get_prev`, which nothing caught: the CLI printed `internal: CroniterBadDateError`, and a planted row lost its MSP's whole tick on every tick. `Cadence.next_after` and `previous_before` now raise `CadenceError(NEVER_OCCURS)`, so `PlanRepo.create` answers `cadence_cron: never occurs`, and the scheduler's `due_at` is inside the `except CadenceError` that skips a plan with one line. Tests: `test_a_cron_that_never_occurs_is_refused_with_its_own_word`, `test_a_planted_cron_that_never_occurs_is_skipped_and_the_others_run`.
3. **A run is counted and named after its MSP's commit, and a plan that raises is rolled back alone.** `summary.created` and the `run created` line came before the commit, so a later plan's failure reported runs that were rolled back, and one failing plan starved the MSP's other plans. **Against the entry's point 7** ("`None` is the app's failure, logged, the MSP's tick rolled back"): each plan's connector read and insert now run under a savepoint (`session.begin_nested()`), a plan that raises is logged as `plan failed` (`msp_id`, `plan_id`, the exception's type) and counted in `failed`, and the next plan runs; `_plans_of` returns the runs it made and `tick_plans` counts and logs them only once the `session.begin()` block has left. The plans' values are read into `DuePlan` tuples first, since a rolled-back savepoint may expire the session's rows. An MSP's own failure (its plans can't be listed, the commit fails) is `tick failed` as before, with nothing of it counted or named. Tests: `test_a_plan_whose_run_fails_is_rolled_back_alone_and_the_msp_s_other_plans_run`, `test_a_plan_the_database_refuses_is_rolled_back_alone` (a statement the database refused, so the savepoint is what holds), `test_an_msp_whose_tick_fails_is_rolled_back_and_the_next_msp_runs` (rewritten: the fault after two runs were made, neither's id in any line), `test_a_run_is_named_only_after_its_msp_s_commit`, `test_a_connector_the_keys_say_exists_but_is_gone_is_the_plan_s_failure`.
4. **A cadence is at most every five minutes; the finding's larger half is open.** `* * * * *` was accepted and every tick was a new period. `check_spacing` (new, in `app/cadence.py`, called by `PlanRepo.create` before `check_monthly`) refuses, as `more often than every 5 minutes`, a cron whose minute field has two values less than five apart, or whose last minute of an hour and first of the next are, when its hours can follow each other; `MIN_PERIOD` is the scheduler's tick, held equal to `TICK_S` by a test, so every period a plan may have can get its own run. It reads the minute and hour fields alone: `0,58 0,23 1 * *` is refused though its days never follow. **Not fixed, and not mine to fix:** the finding's example `*/5 * * * *` (288 runs a day) still passes, because the issue's Done-when is "a plan with a 5-minute cron creates queued runs on schedule" and its test and harness make that plan through the CLI. A real floor (hourly, daily) is the owner's rule; it needs the Done-when's plan made another way. The scheduler does not re-check spacing on a planted row. Tests: `test_a_cron_no_finer_than_five_minutes_passes`, `test_a_cron_finer_than_five_minutes_is_refused`, `test_the_floor_is_the_scheduler_s_tick`.
5. **`constraint_refusal` reads the driver's `constraint_name`.** It scanned every quoted token of the message, DETAIL included, so a name or label in the failing row that quoted a constraint's name could word another refusal. It now reads `error.orig.__cause__.constraint_name` (SQLAlchemy's asyncpg error is raised from asyncpg's own) and nothing of the message. Tests: `test_a_row_value_that_quotes_a_constraint_s_name_words_nothing`, `test_a_real_refusal_whose_row_quotes_another_constraint_is_worded_by_its_own` (on the database), the unknown-name table with no driver error, a null name and a name that is no text.
6. **`--run-now`'s insert is worded like every other.** `RunRepo.create` ran outside `_refused_by_the_database` and `connector.worker_id` was read from a value that could be `None`. The insert is now inside it, and a connector that is gone is `connector_id: not the client's connector`. Tests: `test_run_now_s_refusal_by_the_database_is_worded_like_any_other`, `test_run_now_with_a_connector_that_is_gone_is_the_key_s_refusal`.

**Open.**

7. `serve` shuts down with `scheduler.shutdown(wait=False)` and disposes the engine at once, under a tick that may still run. Less to lose since finding 3: a run is named only after its commit.
8. One `ConnectorRepo.get` and one no-op `INSERT` per enabled plan per tick; a savepoint and its release are now two statements more per plan that reaches the insert.
9. The Compose `scheduler` service mounts `./app` and never reloads: after an edit it runs the old code until restarted. **The stack's scheduler was not restarted for this review, and the by-hand Done-when was not run again** on the changed code; `docs/api/cloud-lab/c5.9-c5.10-done-when.txt` is the build's run.
10. `Created.values` beside `lines` on a frozen dataclass.

**The gate, locally** (no CI run has started since 2026-10-03): `uv run --locked pytest` 2098 passed, coverage 99.77% combined, `tools/check_coverage.py` `OK` on every guarded file at 100% line and branch (`app/cadence.py` and `app/repo/errors.py` among them). `docs/api/openapi-v1.json` unchanged.

## 2026-10-11 — C5.10 and C5.9 build notes: built as the entry says, with the plan's first period the first after its creation (the entry's own test sketch was wrong against its rule), the connector held by the plan's key rather than a read before it, the MSP's own key worded on every table, one module-level function allowed under the repo's walk, and a harness whose first tick landed on the old schema and said so; the gate green locally and both Done-whens shown on the stack (proposed)

The owner approved the entry below as written on 2026-10-11. These notes say where the build left the entry or went beyond it. The points marked **against the entry** are the ones to read.

1. **Point 11's Done-when sketch, against point 7's rule.** The entry's `tests/test_scheduler.py` sketch had the tick at 12:00:30 make a run for the 12:00 period of a plan made at 12:00:30. Point 7 says a period that began before the plan was made is not the plan's, and the build held the rule: the 12:00:30 tick makes nothing, the 12:05 tick the first run, 12:05:10 nothing, 12:10:01 the second. The test, `test_a_plan_with_a_5_minute_cron_creates_queued_runs_on_schedule`, says so in a comment, and `test_a_plan_made_at_its_own_minute_gets_that_period` holds the edge (`created_at` equal to the period's start is taken). The by-hand run shows the same: the plan made at 20:21:33Z got its first run for the period 20:25:00Z and its second for 20:30:00Z.
2. **Point 4, `create-plan`'s connector (against "the connector must be the client's (the key's word)" as built first).** The first cut read the connector before the insert and refused `no such connector` or `not the client's connector` itself; the CLI's cron tests then met the connector's refusal before the cadence's. Now `PlanRepo.create` runs first (the cadence's refusal comes first, as the entry's point 6 wants), and the database's key `fk_test_plan_msp_id_connector_id_client_id_connector` holds the connector to the client, an absent connector included, worded `connector_id: not the client's connector`; `--run-now` reads the connector afterwards for its Worker, when the key has already said it exists. The word `no such connector` is gone. Another MSP's client is `client_id: no such client` from the plan's own key to `client` (`fk_test_plan_msp_id_client_id_client`), added to the table.
3. **Point 2's table, grown.** The MSP's own key is one per table (`fk_client_msp_id_msp`, `fk_install_token_msp_id_msp`, `fk_worker_msp_id_msp`, `fk_connector_msp_id_msp`, `fk_test_plan_msp_id_msp`, `fk_test_run_msp_id_msp`), each `msp_id: no such MSP`, since `create-worker-token` meets the install token's and not the client's; and the plan's key to `client` (point 2 above). `tests/test_repo_errors.py` holds the table complete against the metadata and shows every word on the database.

The test now names `MODULE_FUNCTIONS = {("errors.py", None, "constraint_refusal")}`, holds it to its one `error` parameter, and leaves it out of the `msp_id` walk; the planted sub-package test is unchanged by it.
5. **Point 1, the CLI's errors.** `typer.Exit` is what `run()` raises, not `SystemExit`, and a command's `asyncio.run` can't be called from the tests' session loop, so the `internal: <type>` test is a plain `def`. A database on a closed port reaches `run()` as `OSError` through SQLAlchemy's asyncpg adapter and is `database: unreachable`, held by `test_a_database_that_cannot_be_reached_is_one_line_without_the_driver_s_text` with a sentinel user and password in the URL.

The scheduler's `tick` lines are matched as `event.: .tick` for the same reason.

## 2026-10-11 — C5.10 and C5.9 (#63, #62), with C5.13's remainder (#136): the hand-onboarding CLI and the job dispatcher. `cloud/manage.py` (Typer) makes an MSP, a client by its tenant, an install token shown once, a connector from a profile file, a plan, and revokes a Worker, each through the repos in one committed transaction, the database's refusals worded by constraint name and never a value; a plan's `cadence_cron` is five fields, UTC, at least monthly, held by the repo; the scheduler (APScheduler, the Compose `scheduler` service) ticks every five minutes, makes one queued run per enabled plan and cron period under a unique on `(msp_id, plan_id, scheduled_for)` so two ticks or two processes make one, and sweeps `RunRepo.requeue_stale` per MSP over `MspRepo.list`; `create-user` is left to C6.1 (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written)

C5.10 (#63) and C5.9 (#62) are built on one branch, `c5.9-c5.10`, in that order (the CLI first: the scheduler's Done-when needs a plan the CLI made), in one PR, with what is left of C5.13 (#136) beside them, as C5.5/C5.6 (#172) were. Done when: "A new MSP with one client and plan is created in under 5 minutes by CLI" and "A plan with a 5-minute cron creates queued runs on schedule in the local stack"; C5.13's "Parametrised tests show: a second client with the same tenant ID in one MSP is rejected; a connector whose profile names another tenant is rejected; a bundle for a different client than dispatched gets 409." This entry works from the three issues, the 2026-10-10 entries "C5.3 and C5.4" (point 2's repo methods and its open list: `MspRepo.list` for C5.9, the `IntegrityError` words for C5.10, the route-level 409s and `create-connector --profile-file` for C5.13), "C5.5 and C5.6" (point 1's `install_token.label` for `create-worker-token --label`, point 8's `requeue_stale`, point 10), "C5.7" (its open list) and 2026-10-11 "C5.8" with their build notes and reviews, the 2026-09-29 entry "Clients live in the Cloud" (point 5), the guide's C5.9, C5.10, C6.1, C6.2 and C6.4 text, `docs/testing.md` "Cloud", and the code. No code is written yet; the build notes will record what the build finds. **The Worker is not changed** (`worker/` untouched).

**What the investigation found, since the points below rest on it.**

- **Every row the CLI must make has its repo method, and none commits.** `MspRepo.create(name, retention_days)`, `ClientRepo.create(msp_id, name, tenant_id: UUID, screenshots_enabled)`, `issue_install_token(session, msp_id, now, *, label, created_by)` (`app/auth/tokens.py`: the token minted, its hash stored with `expires_at = now + 7 days`, the token answered once), `ConnectorRepo.create(msp_id, client_id, worker_id, config_json, type, *, user_id, ip)` (the profile held to `client-profile.v1` and to the client's tenant, the client and the Worker read with `msp_id`, one `connector.create` audit row, each refusal a `RepoError(key, reason)` with no value), `PlanRepo.create(msp_id, client_id, connector_id, *, sample_mail, sample_sp, sample_od, cadence_cron, enabled)` (the sizes held by the database's four CHECKs; **`cadence_cron` held to nothing**: any text is stored), `WorkerRepo.revoke(msp_id, worker_id, at)` (once; 0 for a Worker already revoked). The one transaction per command is the caller's (C5.3 point 2: "`get_session`, the CLI"). `UserRepo.create(msp_id, email, password_hash, role)` stores whatever hash and role it is given: no hashing exists in `app/`, `user.role` has no words (C6.1's open point since C5.1), and nothing reads `user` until C6.1's login.
- **The database's refusals an onboarding can meet, by constraint name** (`app/models.py`, migration `0001`): `uq_client_msp_id_tenant_id` (a tenant twice in one MSP), `uq_connector_worker_id_client_id` (a client twice on one Worker), `uq_worker_key_id` (worded by registration as 409 already), `ck_test_plan_sample_mail_range`, `_sp_range`, `_od_range` and `ck_test_plan_sample_not_empty` (the Worker's J3 rule), `ck_msp_retention_days_positive`; the foreign keys `fk_test_plan_msp_id_connector_id_client_id_connector` (a plan on another client's connector) and `fk_test_plan_msp_id_client_id_client`. asyncpg puts the constraint's name in `IntegrityError.orig`'s text (`registration.py` reads it so; `tests/test_models.py`'s `refused` holds every refusal to its name). An `IntegrityError` leaves the session failed, so a command that meets one has nothing to commit.
- **`PlanRepo.list(msp_id, *, client_id)` answers enabled and disabled plans alike**, ordered by id; a plan's `enabled` is a boolean the database defaults to true. There is no `test_plan.created_at`: nothing says when a plan was made, so "the first period after the plan was made" can't be told from "a period the plan missed". `test_run` has `created_at`, `state` (`queued` by default), `dispatched_at`, `attempt`, and **nothing that says which cron period a run is for**: two ticks that both find a plan due would each `RunRepo.create` a run, and nothing in the schema stops the second.
- **`RunRepo.requeue_stale(msp_id, now)` is built and held** (C5.6 point 8; `tests/test_repo_runs.py`; `sweep=True` in `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`): two statements per MSP, `(requeued, expired)`. **`MspRepo.list` does not exist**, and `tests/test_tenant_scope.py`'s `WITHOUT_MSP_ID` names exactly three methods, so a fourth fails the AST walk until it is added there with its reason; `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`'s table must name it too.
- **The lint holds `app/**` and nothing outside it.** `tests/test_tenant_scope.py` walks `APP_DIR.rglob("*.py")`; `cloud/manage.py` at `cloud/` would be outside the walk and could `select(` unseen. `tools/dump_openapi.py` and `tools/check_coverage.py` are outside too, by design (they run no statement).
- **The Compose `scheduler` service runs the api's image with a placeholder command** (`echo 'scheduler: the dispatcher is C5.9; nothing runs yet'; exec sleep infinity`), the same `*app-environment`, `depends_on: api: service_healthy`; the C5.1 entry's point 5 says it never migrates. The image carries `app/`, `shared/schemas`, `shared/tools`, `shared/tsa`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `alembic.ini` and nothing else (the root `.dockerignore`'s seven allows, held by `tests/test_schemas.py`): a `cloud/manage.py` is not in the image until the allow-list and the Dockerfile say so. The api's settings need every variable (`load_settings`); a migration reads `DATABASE_URL` and `LOG_LEVEL` alone (`database_url_from_environment`, `log_level_from_environment`), the pattern for a process that needs no bucket.
- **The libraries, resolved today against the locked tree** (`uv pip compile` in a scratch folder, Python 3.12): `typer` 0.27.3 (brings `rich`, `shellingham`, `annotated-doc`), `apscheduler` 3.11.3 (`tzlocal`), `croniter` 6.2.4 (`python-dateutil`). APScheduler 3's `AsyncIOScheduler` runs jobs on the loop with `max_instances` and `coalesce`; its `CronTrigger` answers the **next** fire time only, so "the latest cron occurrence at or before now", which the period of point 7 needs, is a search with it. **croniter measured** (6.2.4): `croniter(expr, now).get_prev()` is the latest occurrence **strictly before** `now` (at `now` = `02:00:00` exactly it answers yesterday's; at `02:00:00.5` and `02:00:30` today's), `get_next()` the first strictly after; `0 2 31 * *` from 2026-02-01 answers 2026-03-31 next (58 days); `L` is taken; the empty string, `nonsense`, four fields and a minute of 60 are `CroniterBadCronError`; **six fields (`0 2 * * * *`, seconds) and `@daily` are accepted**, which the guide's cron (five fields: the default `0 2 * * *`) is not.
- **What the shared tests already hold of C5.13's Done-when.** Line 1: `tests/test_models.py::test_a_second_client_with_the_same_tenant_in_one_msp_is_refused` (one case, the refusal held to `uq_client_msp_id_tenant_id`) and `test_the_same_tenant_in_the_other_case_is_the_same_tenant`; not parametrised. Line 2: `tests/test_repo_connectors.py::test_a_profile_naming_another_tenant_is_refused_without_either_value` and `test_the_other_msp_s_tenant_in_a_profile_is_refused_the_same_way`; two tests, not one parametrised. Line 3: `tests/test_results.py::test_a_bundle_whose_client_is_not_the_run_s_is_409`, **parametrised over seven patches** (`other_client_id`, `null_client_id`, `other_tenant`, `tenant_no_guid`, `other_organisation`, `organisation_no_guid`, `pass_without_the_check`), and `test_an_unknown_tenant_excuses_nothing_else` over three. The issue's other steps are built: the constraints (C5.2), the repo's checks and audit rows (C5.3), the profile in the job (C5.6), the 409 (C5.7). Left: the two CLI commands, the route-level 409s (below), and the first two lines as one named parametrised test each.
- **The test rig.** pytest-asyncio in auto mode with one session loop; the `session` fixture rolls back; `own_database` gives a migrated database of a test's own for rows that must be committed. A sync test can't take the async `own_database` fixture; Typer's `CliRunner.invoke` is synchronous and a command's `asyncio.run` can't be called from the session loop's thread. `app.routers.heartbeat.now` is the pattern for a clock a test moves.
- **CI has not run since 2026-10-03.** Every gate is run locally and its figures go into the build notes, as for C5.1 to C5.8.

**Decision.**

1. **`cloud/manage.py`: a Typer app whose commands are thin, over `app/onboarding.py`, which holds the logic as `async` functions over a session.** `manage.py` parses the options, makes one engine from `DATABASE_URL` alone (`app/db.py` gains `make_engine_for_url(url)`, which `make_engine(settings)` calls; `database_url_from_environment()` as the migration reads it, so the CLI needs no bucket and no `SECRET_KEY`; a missing or malformed variable is `settings error: DATABASE_URL is missing|is not valid` on stderr, exit 1, as the migration says it), opens one session, runs the command's function inside `session.begin()` (committed when it returns, rolled back when it raises), prints the function's answer, disposes the engine. Each function in `app/onboarding.py` (`create_msp`, `create_client`, `create_worker_token`, `create_connector`, `create_plan`, `revoke_worker`) takes the session and plain values, calls the repos (and `issue_install_token`) and answers a small dataclass of ids; it builds no statement, so `tests/test_tenant_scope.py`'s lint holds it as it holds the routers, and **the lint's walk grows by `cloud/manage.py`** (one more path beside `APP_DIR.rglob`), so the CLI can't come to `select(` either. The functions are the seam the tests use with the rolled-back `session` fixture; the Typer layer is tested by `CliRunner` in a thread (point 11). Run from `cloud/` as `uv run python manage.py <command> ...` with `DATABASE_URL` in the shell (the stack's database is `postgresql+asyncpg://restoreproof:local-only-postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/restoreproof` from the host), or inside the stack as `docker compose exec api python manage.py <command> ...` with the container's own environment; `docs/onboarding.md` shows both. `typer` joins the runtime dependencies (the image runs the CLI); `uv.lock` changes.
   - **The image carries `manage.py`**: the Dockerfile gains `COPY cloud/manage.py ./` and the root `.dockerignore` an eighth allow, `!cloud/manage.py`; `tests/test_schemas.py`'s test of the allow-list and the Dockerfile grows to eight paths.
   - **Output: one `<name> <value>` line per thing made, nothing else on stdout**, in a fixed order, so a person reads it and a script takes it with `split(' ')`: `create-msp` prints `msp_id`; `create-client` `client_id`; `create-worker-token` `install_token_id`, `expires_at` and then `install_token <token>` with one line after it on **stderr**, `shown once; the Cloud stores its hash alone`; `create-connector` `connector_id`; `create-plan` `plan_id` (and `run_id` when `--run-now`, point 4); `revoke-worker` `revoked_at`. A refusal is one line on stderr, `<key>: <reason>` (point 2), exit 1; a usage fault is Typer's own, exit 2; a database that can't be reached is `database: unreachable` on stderr, exit 1, never the driver's message (which names the host and the user). Exit 0 means every row of the command is committed. No `--json`: nothing scripts the CLI but the harness, which reads the lines.
   - **The CLI logs nothing and prints no secret but the token it exists to print.** `configure_logging` is not called (the CLI has no request and no library line to format); the engine is `hide_parameters=True` as the app's. The install token appears on stdout once and in no row, no file, no log line and no command line of the CLI's own (a test captures stdout and stderr and holds the token to stdout alone and its hash nowhere). The options take no secret: `create-worker-token` takes `--label`, never a token; `create-user` would take a password and is not built (point 3).
   - *Rejected:* the logic inside `manage.py` (then the lint would have to hold a Typer module, and the admin routes of C6.x would import a command-line program for the same work); `click` alone (the issue names Typer); a `--database-url` option (a URL with a password on a command line, in every shell history); the CLI through the api's HTTP routes (there are no admin routes, C6.x; and the CLI is for the operator with the database, before any user exists); the commands' `asyncio.run` with the app's `Settings` (the bucket's four variables for a command that touches no object).

2. **The database's refusals are worded once, in `app/repo/errors.py`, by constraint name and never a value; the CLI prints them now and the admin routes answer them as 409 later.** `constraint_refusal(error: IntegrityError) -> RepoError | None` reads the constraint's name out of `error.orig`'s text (as `registration.py` reads `uq_worker_key_id`) and answers a `RepoError` from a fixed table, `None` for a name it doesn't know (the caller re-raises: the app's 500, the CLI's `internal` line): `uq_client_msp_id_tenant_id` → `tenant_id: already a client of this MSP`; `uq_connector_worker_id_client_id` → `client_id: already a connector of this Worker`; `uq_worker_key_id` → `public_key_pem: already registered` (registration's words, so the two agree; registration keeps its own 409 and does not change); `ck_test_plan_sample_mail_range` → `sample_mail: not 0 to 100`, the same for `_sp` and `_od`; `ck_test_plan_sample_not_empty` → `sample sizes: all 0`; `fk_test_plan_msp_id_connector_id_client_id_connector` → `connector_id: not the client's connector`; `ck_msp_retention_days_positive` → `retention_days: not positive`; `uq_test_run_msp_id_plan_id_scheduled_for` → `scheduled_for: a run exists for the period` (point 8 never raises it, but the word exists). The words are the `RepoError` form `<key>: <reason>`, as `ConnectorRepo`'s are, so a CLI line and a future 409's `detail` are one text. The table is held complete by a test that reads every named unique, CHECK and foreign key of the metadata that a CLI command can meet and finds its word, and shows each word on the database by making the row refused (through the repos, the C5.13 lines among them).
   - **The route-level 409s, settled:** `POST /v1/results` answers 409 `client_mismatch` for a bundle whose client or tenant isn't the dispatched run's (C5.7, the issue's one route step; built and held by the parametrised test). The other 409s the C5.3 entry left "for the route or the CLI to word" (a tenant twice, a connector twice) have no route to live on: `app/routers/admin.py` is empty and the admin routes are C6.x's. This task gives them their words, which the CLI prints; the admin routes answer `409 {"detail": "<key>: <reason>"}` from the same function when they are built, and **that is recorded as C6.x's open item, not left as C5.13's**.
   - *Rejected:* the words in `manage.py` (a second table for the routes later); catching the `IntegrityError` inside each repo `create` (the repos' rule is to leave the database's refusals to the caller, C5.3 point 2; and a repo that caught it would hide the failed session); a pre-check `SELECT` before each insert (two statements for a race the unique settles; `get_by_tenant` exists for whoever wants to ask first).

3. **`create-user` is not built here; C6.1 builds it with the login.** The issue lists it, and three things it needs are C6.1's open questions since C5.1: the words for `user.role` (and their CHECK, which would edit `0001`), the password hash (an algorithm and a library, `argon2-cffi` or `bcrypt`, that nothing in `cloud/` has and nothing but the login verifies), and what `SECRET_KEY` signs. A `create-user` built now would fix all three for a login that doesn't exist, or store a hash no login can check. The Done-when of #63 needs no user (an MSP with one client and plan), the install token's `created_by` is null for the CLI (C5.5 point 1), and every audit row of point 5 has `user_id` null, as `audit_log.user_id`'s comment says of the CLI. `docs/onboarding.md` says so under the sequence; the command name is reserved for C6.1 (Typer prints the commands it has; a `create-user` typed today is Typer's "no such command", exit 2).
   - *Rejected:* `create-user` with a placeholder hash (`"x"`) and any role text (a row a login would have to migrate or refuse); `--password` on the command line (a secret on a command line, against the CLI's own rule); the role words decided here (C6.1's, with the pages that check them).

4. **The six commands, their options and what each holds.**
   - `create-msp --name <text> [--retention-days N]` (default the model's 1095): `MspRepo.create`; prints `msp_id`.
   - `create-client --msp-id <uuid> --name <text> --tenant-id <guid> [--screenshots-enabled]`: `--tenant-id` is parsed as a uuid by Typer (a text that isn't one is exit 2 naming the option, never the value in a line of ours), so the same tenant in another case is the same tenant (the C5.13 rule); `ClientRepo.create`; a second client of the tenant in the MSP is `uq_client_msp_id_tenant_id`'s word (point 2), exit 1; prints `client_id`. An MSP that doesn't exist is `fk_client_msp_id_msp` → `msp_id: no such MSP` (added to point 2's table, the one foreign key every command can meet).
   - `create-worker-token --msp-id <uuid> --label <text>`: `issue_install_token(session, msp_id, now, label=label, created_by=None)`; prints `install_token_id`, `expires_at` (`now + 7 days`, ISO 8601 UTC) and `install_token <token>` once, with the stderr line of point 1. `--label` is 1 to 128 characters without a control character (registration's `worker_name` rule, as the label is shown beside the Worker on C6.2's page). The token is 43 characters of base64url as `new_token()` makes it; nothing is retried.
   - `create-connector --msp-id <uuid> --client-id <uuid> --worker-id <uuid> --profile-file <path> [--type <name>]` (default `veeam_m365`): the file is read as UTF-8 and parsed as JSON by the CLI (not a file, not UTF-8, not JSON: `profile_file: not readable|not JSON`, exit 1, no path and no text of the file in the line), then `ConnectorRepo.create(msp_id, client_id, worker_id, config_json, type, user_id=None, ip=None)`, whose own order of refusals stands (`config_json: not a client-profile.v1`, `client_id: no such client`, `graph_tenant_id: not the client's tenant`, `worker_id: no such worker`), then the unique's word; prints `connector_id`. The profile is the same file `rpworker client check --profile-file` reads (W4.10); the CLI holds it to nothing the repo doesn't. A connector on a revoked Worker is taken (the C5.5 open point "whether a connector's `worker_id` may name a revoked Worker": nothing refuses it; the operator revokes a Worker to stop it, and its connectors and plans are what C6.2 shows as stuck; see point 9).
   - `create-plan --msp-id <uuid> --client-id <uuid> --connector-id <uuid> --mail N --sp N --od N [--cron "<five fields>"] [--disabled] [--run-now]`: the cron defaults to `0 2 * * *` (the guide's: daily at 02:00 UTC for pilots); `PlanRepo.create(..., cadence_cron, enabled=not disabled, now=now)`, which holds the cron (point 6); the sizes are the database's CHECKs worded by point 2 (the Worker's J3 rule, 0 to 100 and not all 0); the plan's connector must be the client's (the key's word); prints `plan_id`. **`--run-now` also makes one queued run** through `RunRepo.create` (no `scheduled_for`: a run made by hand, as C5.7's harness made one) and prints `run_id`: a pilot's first test without waiting for 02:00, since point 7 makes no run for a period that began before the plan was made. Strike the option if unwanted; nothing else depends on it.
   - `revoke-worker --msp-id <uuid> --worker-id <uuid>`: `WorkerRepo.revoke(msp_id, worker_id, now)`; 0 rows is `worker_id: no such Worker or already revoked` (one line for both, as the repo answers 0 for both), exit 1; prints `revoked_at`. From that commit the Worker's token is `current_worker`'s 401 on every route (C5.4), its heartbeat included; the Worker's queued runs stay queued (point 9).
   - **Every uuid option is parsed by Typer**, so a malformed id is exit 2 and never reaches a statement; every text option is held to a length (`--name` 1 to 128, the `worker_name` rule). The `now` of a command is one `dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc)` taken at its start (through a module-level `now()` in `app/onboarding.py` a test moves, as `heartbeat.now`).
   - *Rejected:* `create-plan --enabled/--no-enabled` (`--disabled` says what it does; the default is the model's); `create-client` taking the tenant from a profile file (the tenant is the client's identity; the profile comes later with the connector); an `--ip` for the audit rows (the CLI has no caller address; `ip` is null as `created_by` is); `delete-*` commands (nothing in Stage 1 deletes a client, a connector or a plan from the command line; `PlanRepo.delete` and the others exist for the admin pages).

5. **One audit row per command that changed a row, `user_id` and `ip` null, through `AuditRepo.write` in the same transaction.** `msp.create` `msp:<id>`, `client.create` `client:<id>`, `install_token.create` `install_token:<id>` (the row's id; never the token or its hash), `plan.create` `plan:<id>` (and `run.create` `run:<id>` for `--run-now`), `worker.revoke` `worker:<id>`; `connector.create` is the repo's own (C5.3), so `create-connector` writes none of its own. A command that is refused writes none (the rollback). The audit log is "what a person or a Worker did to the MSP's data" (C5.8 point 6), and the onboarding is the first thing a person does to it; C6.3's page shows it. Nothing of a profile, a label or a name goes into a row.
   - *Rejected:* no audit rows for the CLI (the registration writes one, and an MSP whose client appeared from nowhere would be the one gap on C6.3's page); the label in the token's row (`install_token.label` already holds it).

6. **`cadence_cron` is held by the repo: five fields, UTC, at least monthly; `PlanRepo.create` takes `now` and refuses as a `RepoError`.** `app/cadence.py` (new, pure, **under `tools/check_coverage.py`'s guard at 100% line and branch**, since it decides whether a run is made): `parse(expr) -> Cadence` holds the text to **exactly five space-separated fields** (`^\S+( \S+){4}$`; the guide's form, so croniter's six-field seconds form and `@daily` are refused: one form, as the heartbeat has one time form) and then to croniter (`croniter.is_valid`), refusing with `not a cron expression`; `check_monthly(cadence, now)` walks **from the start of each of the 400 days after `now`** and refuses with `less than monthly` when the next occurrence after any such day start is more than 31 days on (400 day starts, 400 `get_next` calls, under a millisecond each; 400 days cover a leap year and every month's length; a gap of more than 32 days between two occurrences always leaves a day start more than 31 days before the later one). So `0 2 * * *`, `*/5 * * * *`, `0 2 1 * *` (the 1st), `0 2 15 * *`, `0 2 L * *` and `0 2 * * 1` pass; `0 2 31 * *` (58 days from February), `0 2 1 */2 *` (bi-monthly), `0 2 1 1 *` (yearly) and `0 2 29 2 *` are `less than monthly`. The cron is read in UTC and nothing else: the Cloud's clock is UTC, the Worker's times are UTC, and a client's local time is a column no task has asked for (Open). `PlanRepo.create(..., cadence_cron: str, *, now: dt.datetime, enabled=True)` runs both before the insert and raises `RepoError("cadence_cron", reason)`; `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`'s `make_world` and the labs pass `now`. **Why the repo and not the CLI alone:** the CLI is the first writer of a plan and the admin pages the second; a rule held in the repo holds every writer, as the profile's does (C5.3 point 2). **Why monthly:** the guide's "monthly minimum" is C6.4's monthly report, which wants at least one run in every period it covers; a plan that can't give one is refused where it is made. The scheduler re-checks nothing of this: a row planted past the repo (SQL) is point 7's to skip.
   - *Rejected:* APScheduler's `CronTrigger` as the parser (no previous occurrence, and it takes six fields); a `CHECK` on `cadence_cron` (a regular expression can't say "monthly"); the monthly rule in the scheduler (a plan the operator made would be silently never run); a looser bound (62 days) "for `0 2 31 * *`" (a cron that skips every February is not monthly); a fixed reference date instead of `now` (the rule is "from the plan's creation", which the row records from this task, point 8).

7. **The dispatcher: every five minutes, for each MSP and each of its enabled plans, the period that is current now, and one queued run for it unless one exists, decided by a unique and one `INSERT`.** `app/scheduler.py` (new): `tick_plans(session_factory, now)` runs, **one transaction per MSP** (so one MSP's failure rolls back and logs that MSP's tick alone and the next MSP runs): `MspRepo.list()` (point 10) once, outside; then per MSP `PlanRepo.list(msp_id, enabled=True)` (point 10), and per plan: `app.cadence.parse` (a plan whose text the parser refuses is skipped with one `warning` line `plan skipped` carrying `msp_id`, `plan_id` and `reason: cadence_cron`, never the text, and the loop goes on: a bad cron stops no other plan), `due = cadence.due_at(now)` (**the latest occurrence at or before `now`**: croniter's `get_prev` from `now`, then its `get_next`, and the `next` when it is at or before `now`; measured above), `due < plan.created_at` → nothing (a period that began before the plan was made is not the plan's; `test_plan.created_at`, point 8), else `ConnectorRepo.get(msp_id, plan.connector_id)` for the Worker (by the keys it exists; `None` is the app's failure, logged, the MSP's tick rolled back) and `RunRepo.create_scheduled(msp_id, plan_id=, client_id=, connector_id=, worker_id=, scheduled_for=due) -> TestRun | None` (point 8): a row is `run created` at `info` with `msp_id`, `plan_id`, `run_id` and `scheduled_for`; `None` is nothing (the period has its run: the common case on four ticks of five for a 5-minute cron and on 287 of 288 for a daily one). **One run per period, the current period only:** a scheduler that was down for a day makes today's run when it comes back, not yesterday's (a run for a period that has passed would restore a point nobody asked for at a time nobody chose). The period is `[due, next occurrence)` and its key is `due`. A plan re-enabled after a month makes its current period's run at the next tick. **A plan whose Worker is revoked still gets its runs** (point 9).
   - **The sweep, the second job:** `tick_sweep(session_factory, now)`: `MspRepo.list()`, then per MSP in its own transaction `RunRepo.requeue_stale(msp_id, now)`, one `info` line `runs swept` with `msp_id`, `requeued`, `expired` when either is not 0, nothing when both are.
   - **The process:** `main()` reads `DATABASE_URL` and `LOG_LEVEL` as the migration does (no bucket, no `SECRET_KEY`), calls `configure_logging`, makes the engine (`make_engine_for_url`) and the session factory, builds an `AsyncIOScheduler` (UTC) with the two jobs on an `IntervalTrigger` of **`TICK_S = 300`**, each `max_instances=1`, `coalesce=True`, `misfire_grace_time=60`, and each with `next_run_time=now` so a fresh process evaluates at once (a plan made a minute before a restart doesn't wait five minutes more), logs `scheduler started` with the interval, and waits on an event that `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` set (Compose's stop), then shuts the scheduler down and disposes the engine. The tick's `now` is one module-level `now()` per tick (the test's clock). A tick that raises outside an MSP's transaction (the database gone) is logged `tick failed` with the exception's type and frames (the logging's rule) and the next tick runs in five minutes: the process never exits on a tick's failure. **Statements per tick:** one `SELECT` (the MSPs) plus, per MSP, one `SELECT` (its enabled plans) and, per plan due with no run yet, one `SELECT` (the connector) and one `INSERT`; the sweep one `SELECT` plus two `UPDATE`s per MSP; held by a test with `before_cursor_execute` as the poll's are.
   - **The Compose service** runs `python -m app.scheduler` with the same environment and `depends_on: api: service_healthy` (the api migrates first; the scheduler never migrates, as before); the placeholder command goes. Two scheduler containers make one run per period (point 8).
   - *Rejected:* every missed period made up (above); the tick as an api background task (a second api instance would be a second scheduler with no lease, and the api's process is the request's); APScheduler's job store in Postgres (its table is outside the model and the migration, and it would schedule the plans' crons as jobs, which point 8's unique makes unnecessary); a cron job per plan registered with APScheduler (a plan made or changed by the CLI in another process would never reach the scheduler's store without a job store, and the two-process rule would be APScheduler's lock, not the database's); the scheduler reading the plan's profile or anything of the connector but `worker_id` (nothing of a profile reaches the scheduler's lines by construction); a lease row so one scheduler runs (the unique makes a second one harmless).

8. **The schema, migration `0001` edited in place: `test_run.scheduled_for` with a unique, `test_plan.created_at`; `RunRepo.create_scheduled` is one `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.** `test_run` gains `scheduled_for timestamptz NULL` (`UtcDateTime`: the period's start; null for a run made by hand, `RunRepo.create` as before and `--run-now`) and **`UNIQUE (msp_id, plan_id, scheduled_for)`** (`uq_test_run_msp_id_plan_id_scheduled_for`; Postgres treats nulls as distinct, so hand-made runs never collide and the unique is the period rule alone). `test_plan` gains `created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` (`msp`, `test_run`, `install_token`, `report` and `audit_log` have one; the plan needs it for point 7's "not before the plan was made"). `RunRepo.create_scheduled(msp_id, *, plan_id, client_id, connector_id, worker_id, scheduled_for) -> TestRun | None` is `INSERT INTO test_run (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT uq_test_run_msp_id_plan_id_scheduled_for DO NOTHING RETURNING *` (SQLAlchemy's `insert(...).on_conflict_do_nothing(constraint=...).returning(TestRun)`), answering the row or `None` for a period that has its run: **the constraint and the statement decide together, so two ticks or two scheduler processes make one run** without a lock, a read before the write, or a retry (a conflict is no error, so the MSP's transaction goes on). `0001` is edited in place as C5.3 to C5.8 did; a database that ran the old `0001` needs `downgrade -1`, `upgrade head`, `check` once (`docs/testing.md`; the harness stops, never downgrades, point 12). `tests/test_models.py` holds the column, the unique on the database (two rows of one plan and period refused, two plans or two periods taken, two null `scheduled_for` taken) and `created_at`'s default; `tests/test_migrations.py`'s `alembic check` and the CHECK count hold the rest; `UtcDateTime` columns become seventeen.
   - *Rejected:* a locked statement (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the plan row, then a check and an insert: three statements and a lock held per plan, and a second process on another connection still needs the unique to be sure); a `test_plan.last_run_at` advanced by the tick (a cursor that drifts from the runs it stands for, and two ticks would race on it); `scheduled_for` as the period's end or a text key (the start is the cron's own time, and a `timestamptz` compares as a time); a migration `0002` (the rule since C5.3 while nothing is deployed).

9. **A revoked Worker's plans still make runs; nothing here disables a plan or expires a queued run.** A run for a plan whose connector's Worker is revoked sits `queued` with `dispatched_at` null: nothing polls it, the sweep leaves it (it sweeps `dispatched` runs), and C6.2's page shows a run that was never handed out beside a Worker with `revoked_at`. That is the truth of the plan, and the operator's next step is `revoke-worker`'s counterpart (a new install token, a new Worker, a new connector, a plan on it; the old plan disabled by the admin pages, or deleted). A rule that stopped the runs would hide the plan that nobody moved. Open for C6.2: showing it; for C7.3 or a later sweep: expiring a `queued` run older than some span.
   - *Rejected:* `revoke-worker` disabling the Worker's plans (a command that changes rows the operator didn't name); the dispatcher skipping a revoked Worker's plans (above: a silent stop).

10. **The repo methods this task adds, and the two tests that hold the repo's shape.** `MspRepo.list() -> list[Msp]` (by name then id): **the one read across every MSP**, the scheduler's, with no `msp_id` by its nature; added to `tests/test_tenant_scope.py`'s `WITHOUT_MSP_ID` as its fourth name, with its reason there and in `app/repo/msps.py`'s docstring, and to `tests/test_repo_isolation.py` as a `CROSS_MSP` row held to answer both worlds' MSPs and nothing else of either. `PlanRepo.list(msp_id, *, client_id=None, enabled: bool | None = None)` (a third `where` when given; a `Read` row with `enabled=True`). `RunRepo.create_scheduled` (in `CREATES`; the unique's refusal through it is `None`, held by `tests/test_repo_runs.py`). `PlanRepo.create` gains `now` (point 6; its row in `CREATES` unchanged). `constraint_refusal` in `app/repo/errors.py` is no method and is held by its own test. Every file of `app/repo/` stays at 100% line and branch under `tools/check_coverage.py`, which **gains `app/cadence.py`** in `GUARDED` (point 6); `app/onboarding.py`, `app/scheduler.py` and `manage.py` are aimed at 100% like the routers and their figures go into the build notes (`manage.py` is outside `--cov=app`; its tests run it through `CliRunner` and the build notes record its own `coverage run` figure or say why not).

11. **Tests, failure paths first, each Done-when by name, C5.13's three lines parametrised.** New files `tests/test_onboarding.py` (the functions over the `session` fixture), `tests/test_manage.py` (the Typer layer through `typer.testing.CliRunner` run in a thread by `asyncio.to_thread`, on `own_database` with `DATABASE_URL` set for the call through `monkeypatch`, since a command commits), `tests/test_cadence.py`, `tests/test_scheduler.py`, `tests/test_c513_done_when.py`; changed `tests/test_repo_runs.py`, `test_repo_isolation.py`, `test_tenant_scope.py`, `test_models.py`, `test_migrations.py`, `test_schemas.py`, `test_check_coverage.py`.
    - **C5.10's Done-when by name, `test_a_new_msp_with_one_client_and_plan_is_created_in_under_5_minutes_by_cli`** (`tests/test_manage.py`): the six commands in `docs/onboarding.md`'s order through `CliRunner` (`create-msp`, `create-client`, `create-worker-token`, a Worker registered through the app with the printed token and RFC 8032's test-1 key, `create-connector` with the shared valid profile naming the client's tenant written to a temp file, `create-plan` with the default cron, `revoke-worker` last), each exit 0 with its id lines, the rows read back through the repos, the whole under a `time.perf_counter` held to 300 s (and recorded; expected under 5 s); the install token on stdout once, its hash and the token in no stderr line and no row but as the hash.
    - **C5.9's Done-when by name, `test_a_plan_with_a_5_minute_cron_creates_queued_runs_on_schedule`** (`tests/test_scheduler.py`): a plan with `*/5 * * * *` made at `T` = 12:00:30; `tick_plans` at 12:00:30 makes one run `scheduled_for` 12:00; at 12:03:00 none; at 12:05:00 and 12:05:10 one run 12:05 (the second tick nothing); at 12:10:01 one 12:10; the runs `queued` with the plan's client, connector and Worker; a disabled plan none; the other MSP's plan its own; the log's `run created` lines with the ids and nothing else. The local stack's run of it is point 12.
    - **C5.13's Done-when, one named parametrised test per line** (`tests/test_c513_done_when.py`, over the `session` fixture and the C5.7 lab): `test_a_second_client_with_the_same_tenant_id_in_one_msp_is_rejected`, parametrised over the second tenant's spelling (the same text, upper case, and through `create_client` of `app/onboarding.py`, each refused with the word of point 2, and as the control the same tenant in another MSP taken); `test_a_connector_whose_profile_names_another_tenant_is_rejected`, parametrised over the tenant named (another client's of the same MSP, another MSP's client's, a GUID nobody has, each `graph_tenant_id: not the client's tenant` through `ConnectorRepo.create` and through `create_connector`, with the same tenant in the other case taken as the control); `test_a_bundle_for_a_different_client_than_dispatched_gets_409`, which is `tests/test_results.py`'s seven-way parametrised test moved under this name (the old name kept as an alias so the C5.7 docs stay true, or the docs updated: the build notes say which). The PR says `Closes #136` only if all three pass.
    - **Failure paths, before the happy ones.** The CLI: each command without a required option (exit 2); a uuid option that isn't one (exit 2, the value in no line of ours); `--tenant-id` twice in one MSP, a profile naming another tenant, a profile that isn't one, a file that isn't there, isn't UTF-8 or isn't JSON, a client, a Worker or a connector that isn't the MSP's, a plan on another client's connector, sizes of 101 and of 0, 0, 0, a cron of four fields, six fields, `@daily`, `nonsense`, `0 2 31 * *`, `0 2 1 1 *`, a `--label` with a tab or of 129 characters, `revoke-worker` twice: each exit 1 with the one line, nothing committed (the counts of every table before and after), no value of the input in the line; `DATABASE_URL` unset, malformed, or a closed port: exit 1 with the fixed line and no driver text. The cadence: the table above as `parametrize`, the day-start rule's edge (a gap of 31 days taken, 32 refused), `due_at` at an occurrence, a half second after it, between two, at 23:59 for a daily cron, across a month's end. The scheduler: a plan with a cron planted by SQL that the parser refuses skipped with its line and the MSP's other plan's run made; an MSP whose connector `get` raises (the seam) rolled back and logged while the next MSP's run is made; a period before `created_at` skipped; the unique on `own_database` with two sessions inserting one plan's period at once (one row, both transactions commit); `create_scheduled` answering `None` the second time; the statement counts; nothing of a profile, a token or a tenant value in any line (a sentinel in the connector's profile and the plan's client's name); `MspRepo.list` answering every MSP; `PlanRepo.list(enabled=True)` leaving the disabled one; the sweep per MSP with its line and its silence; `main()`'s wiring by a test that runs it with the scheduler's `start` and the wait replaced (the seam), and the signal handlers' absence on Windows tolerated (`NotImplementedError` caught: the test runs on the laptop, the process in the image).
