## 2026-10-10 — C5.7 (#60): `POST /v1/results`. The Worker's multipart upload of a signed run folder is verified by the auditor's own verifier under the token's Worker's registered key, held to the run the Cloud dispatched and to that run's client, filed as the run's `pass`, `fail` or `error` with its items in one transaction and its files under `msp/<msp_id>/runs/<run_id>/`; every refusal is one fixed word, a bad token is refused as the two verifiers refuse it, a missing one is "not timestamped", and a second upload of the same bundle is 202 with no change (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written)

C5.7 (#60) is built on its own branch, `c5.7-results`, in one PR with two commits (the route, then the docs), as C5.3/C5.4 (#171) and C5.5/C5.6 (#172) were. Done when: "The tests pass and a real Worker bundle lands as pass in the DB." This entry works from issue #60, the 2026-10-10 entries "C5.5 and C5.6" with its build notes and code review, "C5.3 and C5.4" with its build notes and review, "C5.1 and C5.2" with its review, the Worker-side entries W4.1 (the result and its canonical form), W4.2 (the run folder and `attachments`), W4.3 (the signature, the trust rule, the key-file rule, its build notes and its two review entries), W4.4 (the timestamp), W4.6 (the outbox and the exact request), W4.8 (results written afterwards), `docs/verification.md`, `docs/testing.md` "Cloud", the whole of `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py`, and the code. No code is written yet; the build notes will record what the build finds. **The Worker is not changed in this task** (`worker/` untouched): the request is what `rp::Outbox::flush` and `rp::CloudUploader` send today, and what W5.1 must do with each answer is recorded in point 15 for its entry.

**Where issue #60 is stale against the code, settled from the code.** (a) "Check `worker_id` matches the token's worker": there is no `worker_id` in the result and never was (`shared/schemas/result.v1.json` has seventeen required top-level keys, none of them `worker_id`; W4.3 point 2: "`worker_id` is issued by the Cloud at registration and isn't needed in the result: the Cloud knows the Worker from its API token"). The Worker is the token's (`current_worker`), and the run must be that Worker's (point 6). (b) "canonicalise as the Worker does (sorted keys, no whitespace, signature and tsa_token removed)": nothing is removed. `result.json` is the result's `canonical-json-v1` bytes with nothing taken out, `bundle_sha256` is the SHA-256 of those bytes, the signature is in `signature.json` beside it and the token in `timestamp.tst` (W4.3 point 2, W4.4 point 1; `rp::Outbox::flush` checks exactly that before it sends, `worker/src/outbox.cpp`). A verifier that re-serialised would accept bytes nobody signed, so the file's bytes must *be* the canonical form (`result_not_canonical`). (c) "Verify TSA token with rfc3161ng": not used; the W4.4 entry measured it ("unmaintained since 2020, pulls `requests`, builds no chain") and the script's `asn1crypto` + `cryptography` check is the one held to OpenSSL's answer on 898 one-bit changes (`timestamp-v1/cases.json`, `one_bit_changes`). (d) "a failed or missing token does not reject the run, it is flagged": a missing token is flagged (`tsa_ok` null); a bad one is refused, point 8 says why.

**What the investigation found, since the points below rest on it.**

- **The request, as the Worker sends it** (`worker/src/outbox.cpp` lines 186 to 203, `worker/include/rp/outbox.hpp` `UploadPart`, `worker/src/uploader.cpp`; the W4.6 entry point 3 and its build note 6 (d), which saw the stub Cloud's log of a real upload): `POST <cloud_url>/v1/results`, `multipart/form-data`, the parts in this order: `result` (file name `result.json`, `application/json`), `signature` (`signature.json`, `application/json`), `timestamp` (`timestamp.tst`, `application/octet-stream`, **only when the manifest says `timestamped`**), then one part per entry of the result's `attachments` under the entry's own name as the part's name and file name (`items.csv`, `veeam-session.log`, `screenshot.png`), `application/octet-stream`. `manifest.json` is never a part. Sent once per attempt, 120 s, at most 64 KiB of the answer read, no `Authorization` header until W5.1. Before it sends, the flush has already held `result.json` to 16 MiB and to a JSON object whose `run_id` is the folder's name, `signature.json` to 4096 bytes and to `bundle_sha256` = the SHA-256 of `result.json`, the token to 64 KiB and to one TimeStampToken with that imprint, and every listed attachment to its size and hash (`folder_changed` otherwise, nothing sent). **The uploader reads nothing of the answer but its status** (`CloudUploader::upload`: `response.status == kUploadAccepted` is the one test; the body is neither parsed nor logged): 202 is `sent`, any other status is `upload_http_<status>` and the run is retried by the schedule, for good (W4.6 point 3). So no body the Cloud answers reaches the Worker today, and W5.1 decides what, if anything, it reads.
- **The sizes.** The Worker's limits are `kMaxResultFileBytes` 16 MiB and `kMaxSignatureFileBytes` 4096 (`rp/signer.hpp`), `kMaxTimestampFileBytes` 64 KiB (`rp/rfc3161.hpp`); the script's `MAX_RESULT_FILE_BYTES`, `MAX_SIGNATURE_FILE_BYTES`, `MAX_TIMESTAMP_FILE_BYTES` are the same numbers. An attachment has no limit on the Worker's side but its listed `size_bytes` (a count up to 2^53 − 1); the screenshot is at most 10 MiB (W4.2), C7.2 "caps an attachment at 25 MB" (W4.2 point 1) and isn't built. **Nothing in the stack bounds a request body today:** uvicorn 0.54 has no body-size setting (`uvicorn/config.py`: `limit_concurrency`, `limit_max_requests`, `h11_max_incomplete_event_size` for headers only), and starlette 1.7's multipart parser (`starlette/formparsers.py`) caps a part *without* a file name at `max_part_size` (1 MiB) and spools a part *with* one to a `SpooledTemporaryFile` with no cap at all (`on_part_data`: the cap is checked only when `self._current_part.file is None`); `max_files` (1000) and `max_fields` (1000) bound the counts. A multipart body that doesn't parse is `MultiPartException`; a request whose `Content-Type` isn't multipart gives `request.form()` an empty `FormData`, not an error. `request.form()` needs `python-multipart`, which is not in `cloud/uv.lock` (checked: no `name = "python-multipart"` entry; `starlette/requests.py` imports `python_multipart`).
- **The verifier is importable as it is.** `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` imports `asn1crypto`, `cryptography` and `jsonschema` at module level (lines 95 to 105) under a `try` whose `except ImportError` re-raises unless the file runs as `__main__`; the only code outside functions is constants, so importing it has no side effect (the tests already load it by path with `importlib`, `cloud/tests/test_verify_bundle.py` `load_verify_bundle`). Its API fits bytes held in memory: `verify(result: bytes, signature: bytes | None, key: PublicKey, schemas: Schemas) -> Verification` runs the eight words of the result and the signature and reads no attachment (`_check` answers the listed attachments beside the verdict); `check_timestamp(raw: bytes, digest: bytes, ca_pem: bytes | None) -> (word, time)` is the token's three words; `public_key_from_pem(pem: bytes)` reads a key file by the two verifiers' one rule; `load_schemas(folder)` builds the two `Draft202012Validator`s from `result.v1.json` and `signature.v1.json`. Only the attachment check, `_check_attachment(read, attachment)`, is private and takes a reader of the folder (`read(name, limit) -> (state, bytes)`); `verify_folder` is the disk-bound composition of all of it. The words are `WORDS` (fifteen, in the checks' order) and `VERIFIED`. **The three verifiers are held to one answer today by two vector files run on both sides:** `shared/testdata/signing-v1/cases.json` (38 cases: `result_unreadable` 1, `result_not_canonical` 12, `result_schema` 1, `attachment_twice` 1, `screenshot_missing` 1, `signature_file` 10, `hash_mismatch` 2, `wrong_key` 2, `signature_invalid` 4, `attachment_missing`, `attachment_size`, `attachment_hash` 1 each, `verified` 1), run by `worker/tests/signer_test.cpp` and `cloud/tests/test_verify_bundle.py`, and `shared/testdata/timestamp-v1/cases.json` (23 cases: `timestamp_file` 7, `timestamp_mismatch` 3, `timestamp_invalid` 5, `attachment_hash` 1, `verified` 7), run by `worker/tests/timestamp_verify_test.cpp` and `cloud/tests/test_verify_bundle_timestamp.py`; plus `signing-v1/closed-folder.json`, a folder the service closed as `error interrupted`, `verified` on both sides (`test_verify_bundle_closed.py`). Every case is a replacement, addition or removal of a file of `signing-v1/bundle.json`, one signed run folder as texts, whose `run_id` is `rp-20261004T100000Z-0a1b2c3d` and whose `client.client_id` is `null` (it was written before C5.6 made `run_id` the run's uuid and before W4.10 gave a job its `client_id`); its key is RFC 8032's published test key 1, whose private half is in `signing-v1/keys.json`, and the test TSA's private key and certificates are in `timestamp-v1/keys.json`, published and "not a secret".
- **The result's shape, where the rows come from** (`shared/schemas/result.v1.json`). `status` is `{status: pass|fail|error, error_code (exactly when error), message (≤1000, the Worker's fixed words and counts), restore_sent, counts, verified, failed_items, unchecked_items, warnings}`. `started_at` and `ended_at` are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ` or null; `restore_point.backup_time` is `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` or null; `timings.spans.total` is null, `{ms}` (a count), `{ms, note: stopped}` or `{note}`; `cleanup` is null or `{cleanup_ok, restore_may_still_run, before, after}`. The items are three arrays joined by `index`: `expected.items[]` (`index`, `kind` mail|sharepoint|onedrive, `source`, `expected_kind` manifest|fields|metadata, `subject` for a mail or `name` for a file, `sha256` for a `manifest` item only; no found value is ever written, W3.2), `check.items[]` (`index`, `outcome` match|mismatch|missing|error, `found`, `mismatches`, `reason` (fixed words), `error_code`, `ms`, which may be negative when the clock went back), `restore.items[]` (`outcome` restored|failed|not_in_backup). `expected` and `check` may each be null (an `error` run stopped before them; every result written afterwards). The schema cannot say that `index` equals the item's position, that the three arrays are the same length, or that a check item exists per expected item (W4.1 build note 10: "C5.7 must not read the schema as checking these"). `client` is `{client_id (string or null), tenant_id, veeam_org_name, targets, scope, resolved}`: `scope` is `same_tenant` exactly when the Worker's client check passed and `resolved.organization.tenant_id` is then the tenant ID the backup product reported for the organisation (W4.11); both are null when the run stopped in or before the check and in every result written afterwards; `client_id` is the job's (`str(client.id)` from C5.6's document) and null for a run made at a prompt (W4.8 point 3, W4.10). `tenant_id` and `resolved.organization.tenant_id` are strings held to a length alone, not to a GUID's shape.
- **The database as it stands** (`cloud/app/models.py`, migration `0001`). `test_run` has `state` with `CHECK state IN ('queued','dispatched','received','pass','fail','error','expired')`, `dispatched_at`, `attempt`, `restore_point_at`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `total_ms` (`CHECK >= 0`), `bundle_key`, `bundle_sha256` (64 hex when set), `signature_ok`, `tsa_ok`, `cleanup_ok` (nullable booleans: null is "not known", never false), `error_code`, `error_message`; **no column for the token's time**. `test_item` has `type`, `name`, `expected_kind`, `expected_sha256`, `found_sha256`, `found`, `match`, `reason`, `ms` (`CHECK >= 0`), and **no position** (the C5.3 build notes left "a position column if a result's order matters" to C5.7; `ItemRepo.list` orders by `name` then `id`). `RunRepo` has `create`, `get`, `list`, `set_state`, `dispatch`, `requeue_stale`; `ItemRepo` `create` (one row) and `list`; `AuditRepo.write(msp_id, action, target, user_id, ip)`; `ClientRepo.get`. `requeue_stale` (C5.6 point 8) puts a run dispatched six hours ago or more back to `queued` with its `dispatched_at` and `attempt` kept, or to `expired` at three attempts; a run that was never dispatched has `dispatched_at` null and `attempt` 0. Nothing sets `received`; the C5.6 entry named it as "the state C5.7 sets when the bundle arrives".
- **The transaction and the refusals.** `get_session` (`app/db.py`, `SessionDep`, `scope="function"`) commits when the route returns and rolls back when it raises, an `HTTPException` included, before the response starts (the C5.5/C5.6 review's finding 1). So **a refusal raised as an `HTTPException` commits nothing**: registration's 400 and 409 write no audit row by that very mechanism. A refusal that must leave an audit row behind has to return rather than raise (point 6).
- **The image carries `shared/schemas` and nothing else of `shared/`** (`cloud/Dockerfile`, the root `.dockerignore`): neither `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` nor `shared/tsa/tsa-ca.pem` (DigiCert Trusted Root G4, the one root the Worker pins by default, W4.4 point 4) is in it. `app/schemas.py` finds `shared/schemas` by walking up from `app/` (`<repo>/shared/schemas` in the tree, `/srv/shared/schemas` in the image). `app/storage.py` has the data client (botocore's own limits and standard retries) and the check client; "put and get are C5.7's". `tools/check_coverage.py` guards `app/auth`, `app/results.py` and `app/repo` at 100% line and branch; `app/results.py` prints `SKIP does not exist yet`.
- **The Cloud's key for a Worker** is `worker.public_key_pem`, the library's one three-line serialisation (C5.5 point 2), which the verifiers' key-file rule accepts (`key-files.json` row `as-keys-json-has-it`; `tests/test_public_keys.py` holds the stored text equal to the library's), and `worker.key_id` is the SHA-256 of the DER, unique across MSPs, the same computation as `signature.json`'s `key_id` and the script's `PublicKey.key_id`.
- **Upstream of this route, nothing changes.** The Worker's jobs reader, `job_rules`, the five-key heartbeat, the signing contract and the outbox are as W4.6 to W4.11 left them; `GET /v1/jobs` answers `run_id` = `str(test_run.id)` (36 characters, a plain file name), which names the folder the Worker uploads, and `client_id` = `str(client.id)`. A run the sweep requeues is dispatched again under the same `run_id`, which the Worker skips while its folder is in `runs\`, `outbox\` or `sent\` (W4.8 J2), so a bundle can arrive for a run that is `dispatched` (attempt 1 or more), `queued` (requeued, not yet polled) or `expired` (three attempts, at least eighteen hours), and never for a run that was never handed out, since a uuid4 can't be guessed.
- **CI has not run since 2026-10-03.** Every gate is run locally and its figures go into the build notes, as for C5.1 to C5.6.

**Decision.**

1. **The request: the Worker's parts, read by the route itself under explicit limits, every fault one fixed answer.**
   - **The body** is `multipart/form-data` with exactly these parts, identified by the part's *name* alone: `result`, `signature`, `timestamp` (optional), and one part per attachment the result lists, named as the attachment is (`items.csv`, `veeam-session.log`, `screenshot.png`). The part's file name and content type are **not checked** (the Worker's are fixed and nothing the signature covers depends on them; a check would add refusals for nothing). The route reads the form itself (`await request.form(max_files=6, max_fields=0, max_part_size=4096)`), never through FastAPI's `File(...)` parameters, which would silently take the first of two parts of one name and drop a part they don't declare; the body is described in the OpenAPI document by hand (`openapi_extra`), so the contract still shows it.
   - **Before the body is read:** a `Content-Type` that isn't `multipart/form-data` is **415** `{"detail": "body: not multipart/form-data"}`; no `Content-Length`, or one that isn't a number, is **411** `{"detail": "body: no Content-Length"}`; a `Content-Length` over **`MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` = 96 MiB** is **413** `{"detail": "body: too large"}`. The cap must be checked before the body is read because nothing else in the stack bounds it (above), and the Worker's curl always sends a `Content-Length` for a multipart body. The cap is 16 MiB for the result plus three attachments at the 25 MiB C7.2 names, with room for the framing; an honest run today is under 11 MiB (a 10 MiB screenshot at most).
   - **While and after it is read:** a body the parser refuses (a bad boundary, a seventh file part, a part without a file name, a part header the parser won't take) is **400** `{"detail": "body: malformed"}`; a part name seen twice is **400** `part_twice`; the `result` part missing or over 16 MiB is **400** `result_unreadable` (the verifier's word for a result that "isn't there, can't be read or is too large"); the `signature` part missing or over 4096 bytes is **400** `signature_file`; a `timestamp` part over 64 KiB is **400** `timestamp_file`; a listed attachment whose part is larger than its listed `size_bytes` is **400** `attachment_size` without being read (the verifier reads at most the listed size), and a listed `size_bytes` over **`MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` = 25 MiB** is **413** `body: too large` (not a verifier's word: the bundle may be honest and the Cloud won't hold it); a part whose name is none of the three and not among the listed attachments is **400** `part_unexpected`, checked after the attachments (point 7). A part's size is `UploadFile.size`, known after the parse, so nothing over a limit is read into memory.
   - **`python-multipart` joins the runtime dependencies** (starlette's form parser needs it and asserts otherwise); **`cryptography` and `asn1crypto` move from the dev group to the runtime dependencies** (the verifier imports both, point 3; `jsonschema` moved in C5.3). `uv.lock` changes. Nothing else is added: `rfc3161ng` is not wanted (above).
   - *Rejected:* FastAPI `File(...)` parameters with aliases for the dotted names (above: a duplicate or stray part passes unseen, and a part's absence is FastAPI's 422 naming the field, not the verifier's word); a cap enforced by counting the stream (the parser owns the stream; a `Content-Length` is what every honest sender gives and what a proxy enforces too); reading the body without a cap "since the Worker's files are small" (anyone with a token could post gigabytes to the spool); taking the `Content-Type` and file name as part of the contract (nothing checks them on the Worker's side either).

2. **Authentication: `Depends(current_worker)` through `SessionDep`, as `GET /v1/jobs`.** The route is `async def results(request, worker: Annotated[Worker, Depends(current_worker)], session: SessionDep)`; `msp_id` is `worker.msp_id` and the key is `worker.public_key_pem` and `worker.key_id`; **nothing in the body names the MSP, the Worker or the key**, and nothing in it is believed about them. A missing, unknown or revoked token is the dependency's one **401** before any byte of the body is parsed (FastAPI resolves the dependency before the handler runs; the body is still received by the server, which is why the cap of point 1 is a header check and the 401 costs no parse). Never a bare `Depends(get_session)`.

3. **The verifier's home: the Cloud imports `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` from the image; the script's logic is not copied.** The Dockerfile gains `COPY shared/tools ./shared/tools` and `COPY shared/tsa ./shared/tsa`, the root `.dockerignore` allows the two paths (`!shared/tools`, `!shared/tsa`), and `tests/test_schemas.py`'s test of the file and the Dockerfile grows to the seven paths. `app/results.py` loads the script once by path (`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, as the tests do) from `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` beside the `shared/schemas` folder `app/schemas.py` already finds (`shared_schemas_dir().parent / "tools"`), and calls `load_schemas(shared_schemas_dir())` once; a script or a schema that can't be found is the app's failure at the first upload (a `FileNotFoundError` naming `shared/tools`, no path), as a missing schema is for a connector, never a skipped check. The Cloud then *is* the Python verifier: `verify()` for the eight words of the result and the signature, the module's attachment check for the three attachment words, `check_timestamp()` for the three token words, `public_key_from_pem()` for the Worker's stored key, `WORDS` as the vocabulary a test holds the route's 400s to. **One change to the script, its behaviour untouched:** `_check_attachment` becomes public as `check_attachment(read, attachment)` and joins `__all__`, so the route checks an attachment part through the same three lines the folder is checked through, with a reader over the parts in place of a reader over the folder; `verify_folder` calls it as before. The script's tests and both vector files are unchanged by it; `rptests` doesn't run the script.
   - **Why import and not copy.** The signing contract says the two verifiers run the same checks in the same order with the same words; the Cloud as a third must agree on every shared vector, and the cheapest agreement is to be the same code. A copy under `app/` would be a second Python verifier held equal by the vectors alone, and the C5.5 entry already paid that price for forty lines; the W4.3 reasons for keeping the script one self-contained file for an auditor all stand, and importing it costs the auditor nothing. The three libraries the script brings are wanted here anyway. The schemas stay the only copies (read by path on both sides). The one thing the script lacks for this route, a reader over bytes instead of a folder, is the three-line attachment check, which point 3 exposes rather than duplicates.
   - **What this does to the gates.** The script stays outside `--cov=app` and mutmut (W4.3 left "a coverage floor for `verify_bundle.py`" open; it stays open): its lines are held by its own 150-odd tests and the 61 shared cases, and by this PR's route tests that run every case through the route. `app/results.py` is the part the gate measures at 100% line and branch: the mapping from an upload's parts to the verifier's calls, the order, the run and tenant rules, the mapping to rows. A change to the script is a change to the Cloud's verification; `.github/workflows/pr-guards.yml`'s "No test, no merge" looks at `cloud/app/` and `worker/` and not at `shared/tools/`, which is as it was since W4.3 and is C5.11's to widen if the owner wants (Open).
   - **C5.5's reader stays a copy.** `app/auth/public_keys.read_key_file` is not folded into the script's `public_key_from_pem`: the registering side deliberately asks the library nothing before its own checks, and the two are held equal row by row by `tests/test_public_keys.py` already. Folding would couple enrolment to the auditor's file for forty lines.
   - *Rejected:* a copy of the verifier in `app/` (above); `shared/tools` on `PYTHONPATH` with a plain `import verify_bundle` (an environment setting that is right in the image and in pytest and wrong at a developer's prompt; the by-path load works everywhere the schemas are found); a package under `shared/` with a `pyproject` (W4.3 rejected a third lock file for one script); `rfc3161ng` (above); the schema validation through `app/schemas.load_schema` beside the script's own `load_schemas` (two readers of one file for one route; the script's `Schemas` are what `verify()` takes).

4. **The result's checks come first and in the verifiers' order; every refusal is 400 with the verifier's word as `detail`, and no refusal's text ever quotes the document.** With the parts in hand: `verify(result_bytes, signature_bytes_or_None, key, schemas)` answers, first failure wins, `result_not_canonical` (the canonical form before the schema, W4.3 point 5: Python's `integer` takes `1.0`), `result_schema` (against `shared/schemas/result.v1.json` by path), `attachment_twice`, `screenshot_missing`, `signature_file`, `hash_mismatch`, `wrong_key`, `signature_invalid`; each is **400** `{"detail": "<word>"}`. The word is the whole body: no pointer, no key, no value, no library message (the script's `Refusal` carries a slug and nothing else, and `jsonschema`'s message, which quotes the document, is never read: `is_valid` alone). A test holds every 400 the route can answer to `WORDS` plus the four request words of point 1 (`part_twice`, `part_unexpected`, `body: malformed`, and `body: too large` on a 413), and holds that no response body and no log line holds any string of the uploaded result or signature (a sentinel in `expected.items[].subject` and in a stray key).
   - *Rejected:* 422 for a result that isn't the schema (422 is FastAPI's word for a body that isn't the route's model; the result is the verifiers' document and `result_schema` is their word); a 400 that names the failing JSON pointer "to help the operator" (the Worker's own `result error:` line names it at the run, and a pointer can name a tenant value's key; the operator runs `rpworker signer verify` on the queued folder and gets the same word).

5. **The run: looked up after the bundle has verified, by the result's `run_id`, held to this Worker and to a state the Cloud handed out; `received` is dropped.**
   - **The order.** The run is read only once the result, the signature, the attachments and the timestamp have all verified (points 4, 6, 7, 8), so nothing of the database is read for, and nothing but a 400 is answered to, a bundle that doesn't verify under this Worker's key; and every 400 is answered before any run is named, so a 400 tells a caller nothing about what runs exist. Then: (a) `run_id` that is not a uuid (`uuid.UUID()` refuses it), `RunRepo.get(worker.msp_id, run_id)` answering `None` (no such run, or another MSP's), or a run whose `worker_id` isn't `worker.id` (another Worker's of the same MSP) is **one 404** `{"detail": "run_id: no such run"}`: as with `current_worker`, nothing tells a caller which. A run of another Worker is refused because a run's Worker is a fact of the run (C5.3 point 1: a run names its plan's connector's Worker and nothing moves it), and a folder copied from one machine to another is not that Worker's word. (b) A run that was never handed to the Worker, `dispatched_at IS NULL` (so `queued` with `attempt` 0), is **409** `{"detail": "run_id: not dispatched"}`: the only way a Worker has a run's uuid is a poll. (c) A run that is `dispatched`, or `queued` with `dispatched_at` set (requeued by the sweep and not yet polled again), or **`expired`** is taken: the bundle is signed evidence of what happened to the job the Cloud handed out, however late it arrives, and the W4.8 case (a service that died mid-run uploads `error interrupted` at its next start, which may be after the sweep requeued or expired the run) ends the run `error` with that evidence instead of leaving `expired` beside a bundle the Cloud refused. The run's state becomes the bundle's status (point 11), `attempt` and `dispatched_at` are kept. (d) A run that is already `pass`, `fail` or `error` holds a bundle: point 13 (202 for the same bundle, 409 `bundle_conflict` for another).
   - **`received` is dropped from `RUN_STATES` and from `test_run`'s CHECK, migration `0001` edited in place** (nothing is deployed; the stack's database is re-migrated once as `docs/testing.md` says). The bundle's status is known in the very request that receives it, so the run goes from `dispatched` (or `queued`/`expired`, (c)) to `pass`, `fail` or `error` in **one `UPDATE` whose `WHERE` holds the state rule** (point 11), and no row is ever `received`. A word in a CHECK that nothing writes is a lie waiting for a reader; a later streaming design adds its state with its migration. The C5.6 entry's sentences that name `received` ("the state C5.7 sets") are superseded here; `app/models.py`'s and `app/repo/runs.py`'s comments and CLAUDE.md's "Dispatch" rule say so.
   - *Rejected:* refusing an `expired` run (above: evidence lost for a late Worker, and the Worker would retry the 409 hourly for good or file it under `failed\`, both wrong for an honest bundle); a 403 for another Worker's run or a 404 that says "another Worker's" (it names the case; C5.4's rule); the run looked up before the signature (a forged, unsigned result could then probe run ids under a stolen token; and the audit row of point 6 would carry a `run_id` taken from an unverified body); `received` kept "for later" (above); a run keyed by a text `run_id` column so the shared vectors' `rp-…` ids could land (C5.6 made `run_id` the run's uuid, and a second key for a run is a second place for it to be wrong).

6. **The signature: the token's Worker's key and nothing in the body; one audit row per refusal, committed by returning the refusal rather than raising it.**
   - **The key** is `public_key_from_pem(worker.public_key_pem.encode())` — the stored three-line form, which the rule takes — and `wrong_key` is `signature.key_id != worker.key_id`; `signature_file`, `hash_mismatch` and `signature_invalid` are the script's (point 4). The body's `key_id` is compared, never used to look anything up (the W4.3 trust rule: a verifier takes the key from its caller, and here the caller is the token).
   - **A refusal after authentication writes one `audit_log` row and stores nothing.** `action` is `result.rejected`, `target` is `worker:<worker.id>` with the word after a space, `worker:<uuid> <word>` (the word is one of a fixed list: `WORDS`, the four request words, `no such run`, `not dispatched`, `client_mismatch`, `bundle_conflict`; never text of the body), `user_id` null, `ip` the request's client address as registration records it. For a refusal made after the run is known (points 5 (b), 9, 13) the target is `run:<run.id> <word>`, the run's own uuid from its row. **The row must be committed, so a refusal is answered as a response, not raised:** `app/results.py` answers a `Refused(status, word)` and the router writes the audit row through `AuditRepo` and *returns* `JSONResponse(status, {"detail": word})`, so `get_session` commits the one row; nothing else was written, by the order of point 10 (every write comes after every check). The 401 stays raised (the dependency's, before anything of this route runs) and writes no row, as it does nowhere. A test holds that a 400 leaves exactly one new audit row and no other new row, no changed run and no object put; and a planted refusal placed after a row was written would be caught by the same test, which counts rows of every table.
   - *Rejected:* raising the refusal and writing the row in a second session of the request's own (a second transaction per refusal, and a route that commits; `get_session` is the one owner); the word in a column of its own on `audit_log` (a column for one caller; the target text is read by people and by C6.3's log page); no audit row for a 400 (the issue asks for one, and a bundle that fails under a Worker's own key is the one signal of tampering or of a Worker bug the Cloud ever gets).

7. **The attachments: every listed file as a part with the listed size and SHA-256; an unlisted part is refused.** For each entry of the result's `attachments` in the result's order, the module's `check_attachment` over a reader of the parts answers `attachment_missing` (no part of that name), `attachment_size` (the part's size isn't `size_bytes`; a larger one isn't read), `attachment_hash`; each **400**. Then any part left whose name is not `result`, `signature`, `timestamp` or a listed attachment is **400** `part_unexpected`. **The Cloud refuses where the verifiers note:** a verifier reads a folder that can hold the Worker's own `manifest.json` and whatever an operator put there, and a note is the honest answer for a file nobody uploaded; an upload is the Worker's own request, which lists exactly the attachments (`outbox.cpp` builds the parts from the result's list and nothing else), so a part the result doesn't cover is bytes nobody signed, and storing them beside evidence or dropping them without a word are both wrong. The schema holds `attachments[].name` to the enum `items.csv`, `screenshot.png`, `veeam-session.log` (`$defs/attachment`), so `result.json`, `signature.json`, `timestamp.tst` and `manifest.json` can't be listed; confirmed. An attachment's `size_bytes` of 0 (an empty log, as the closed folder has) is a part of 0 bytes with the empty hash, and verifies.
   - *Rejected:* ignoring an unlisted part (above); `attachment_missing` for a listed part the Worker sent under another case of the name (the part's name is compared byte for byte, as the verifiers compare a folder's listing since the W4.3 review's finding 9; `TIMESTAMP.TST` is a `part_unexpected`).

8. **The timestamp: a missing token is "not timestamped"; a token that is there is checked under `shared/tsa/tsa-ca.pem` from the image and a bad one is refused, as both verifiers refuse it; the token's time gets a column.**
   - **No `timestamp` part:** the run is accepted with `tsa_ok` **null** and `tsa_time` null; never a refusal (W4.4 point 2: a folder without a token is "not timestamped, whatever the reason", and the outbox never asks the TSA again).
   - **A `timestamp` part:** `check_timestamp(token, sha256(result_bytes), tsa_ca_pem)` with the CA the image carries, read once from `shared/tsa/tsa-ca.pem` beside `shared/schemas` (`app/results.py` `tsa_ca_pem()`, cached; held by the app on `app.state.tsa_ca_pem` so a test can hand the route the vectors' test root). `timestamp_file`, `timestamp_mismatch`, `timestamp_invalid` are each **400**, nothing stored. **Refused, not flagged, because:** (i) the three verifiers must agree on every shared vector, and `timestamp-v1/cases.json` expects those three words as refusals; a Cloud that filed such a bundle as `pass` with `tsa_ok` false would be the one verifier calling verified what the other two call not verified, and `verify_bundle.py` run later over the stored objects under the same CA would say `not verified`; (ii) an honest Worker never sends one: the run verified the token's chain under the pinned root before it wrote the file (W4.4 point 4) and the flush holds the token to its imprint before every upload, so a bad token at the Cloud is a change in transit or at rest, or a Worker whose `tsa_url`/`tsa_ca_file` name a TSA the Cloud doesn't trust; (iii) that last case is real and is the reason to refuse loudly: the Cloud holds one root today, and a Worker configured for another TSA would otherwise have every run quietly filed as "timestamp not verified" for months. A Cloud-side list of trusted TSA roots is the task that wants it (Open). `tsa_ok` is therefore **true or null** after this task; `false` stays what the column allows for a later re-check (Q6.1), never written here.
   - **`test_run` gains `tsa_time timestamptz NULL`, migration `0001` edited in place:** the token's `genTime`, UTC, whole seconds (the verifiers' third field), set with `tsa_ok` true. C6.4's "timestamped at <time>" and Q6.1's "its time is within the period" need it and would otherwise parse the token out of S3 for every report.
   - *Rejected:* `tsa_ok` false with the run accepted (above); `unchecked` (the Cloud always has the CA; the script's third answer exists for an auditor without `--tsa-ca`); the CA file as a setting (`TSA_CA_FILE`: a path that is wrong only in production, the C5.3 reason against `SCHEMAS_DIR`); checking the token's time against the result's `ended_at` or against now (no verifier does; the Worker's clock was 80 s off in the lab and the token's time is the better one).

9. **The tenant: the bundle's client is the run's client, three comparisons and one word, 409 `client_mismatch`.** With the run known, `ClientRepo.get(worker.msp_id, run.client_id)` (by the keys of C5.3 it exists; `None` is the app's 500, never an empty answer). Then, each refused as **409** `{"detail": "client_mismatch"}`: (a) `result.client.client_id != str(client.id)` (null included: the Cloud gave the job its `client_id` and the Worker signs the job's, W4.10; a run made at a prompt has null and is not the Cloud's job); (b) `result.client.tenant_id`, parsed as a uuid (a string that isn't one is a mismatch), `!= client.tenant_id` (parse, then equality, as `ConnectorRepo` compares the profile's `graph_tenant_id`, C5.3 point 2); (c) when `result.client.scope` is `same_tenant`, `result.client.resolved.organization.tenant_id` parsed as a uuid `!= client.tenant_id` (what the backup product said the organisation is, held to the client the run is filed under; the Worker held it equal to the profile's tenant already, W4.11, and the Cloud holds it to its own row); (d) a `status.status` of `pass` or `fail` whose `scope` isn't `same_tenant` (a verdict the Worker never writes without the client check having passed; "never claim more than was tested": the Cloud files no verdict for a client it wasn't shown to be about). The audit row's target is `run:<id> client_mismatch`. The result's `connector.type` is not compared with the connector's: it is the Cloud's own job field echoed, and a `connector_unknown` result names the type the job asked for by design (W4.11).
   - *Rejected:* comparing `veeam_org_name` or the targets' IDs (the profile's, which the Cloud wrote into the job; nothing a check protects); a `uuid` CHECK on the result's `tenant_id` (the schema holds it to a length alone on purpose, W4.1 point 3); accepting a null `client_id` "for hand-made runs" (a hand-made run isn't a job the Cloud dispatched; its `run_id` is no uuid either).

10. **Storage: the rows first, then the objects, in the request's one transaction; nothing on any refusal.** After every check (points 4 to 9): (a) `RunRepo.receive(...)` (point 11), whose rowcount decides the race; (b) `ItemRepo.create_many(...)` (point 12); (c) `AuditRepo.write(msp_id, "result.received", f"run:{run.id}", ip=...)`; (d) the objects, through `Storage.put(key, body, content_type)` (new, synchronous boto3 `put_object` on the data client, run with `asyncio.to_thread` as `/healthz` runs `check`), under **`msp/<msp_id>/runs/<run_id>/<file name>`**: `result.json` and `signature.json` as `application/json`, `timestamp.tst` when there and each attachment under its own name as `application/octet-stream`; (e) return 202, and `get_session` commits before it leaves. A put that raises (the bucket down, a credential wrong) propagates: the app's 500, the transaction rolled back, no row; the objects already written sit under a key the next upload of the same bundle overwrites with the same bytes, which is why **rows before objects**: the `UPDATE`'s rowcount settles the race (point 13) before any byte goes to the bucket, so a second upload of a bundle already received puts nothing, and a put that fails leaves no row that claims a bundle the bucket doesn't hold. `Storage.get(key) -> bytes` is added beside `put` (a `get_object` and `read()`) for the live Done-when's read-back and for C6.2; both are tested on botocore's `Stubber` (the data client, `expected_params` with the exact key, body and content type) and on a closed port, as the check is; **no MinIO runs in the unit tests** (the C5.1 rule), the real bucket is the by-hand Done-when's on the Compose stack. `bundle_key` is the prefix **`msp/<msp_id>/runs/<run_id>/`**, under which C6.2 reads `result.json` and the names the stored result lists.
    - *Rejected:* objects first (a failed row write would leave objects without a row that names them, and the race would be settled after the puts); a put per table row or a manifest object (the stored result lists the attachments; `manifest.json` is the Worker's and never sent); the result's key as `bundle_key` (the folder is the bundle, W4.3; a prefix names it and every file beside it); the Compose MinIO in a `db` test (a second container every test run and CI job would need, for what `Stubber` shows of the client's calls; the C5.1 entry's reason).

11. **`test_run`, one `UPDATE` with the state rule in its `WHERE`, `RunRepo.receive`.** `receive(msp_id, run_id, *, worker_id, update: ReceivedRun) -> int` is `UPDATE test_run SET … WHERE msp_id = :msp_id AND id = :run_id AND worker_id = :worker_id AND state IN ('dispatched', 'queued', 'expired') AND dispatched_at IS NOT NULL`, answering the rowcount (0 or 1). The columns, each from the named field of the result by the schema:

    | Column | From the result | Rule |
    |---|---|---|
    | `state` | `status.status` | `pass`, `fail` or `error`, the bundle's own word |
    | `error_code` | `status.error_code` | there exactly when `error`; else null |
    | `error_message` | `status.message` | when `error`; else null (a `pass` message is counts the dashboard computes; the stored result has it) |
    | `started_at` | `started_at` | `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ` parsed as aware UTC; null when null; a text the pattern takes and the calendar refuses (a 30th of February) is null, never a refusal (the verifiers say verified) |
    | `finished_at` | `ended_at` | the same |
    | `total_ms` | `timings.spans.total.ms` | when the span is an object with `ms`; null for null or `{note}`; a negative `ms` is null (the column's CHECK) |
    | `restore_point_at` | `restore_point.backup_time` | `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` parsed; null when null |
    | `bundle_key` | — | `msp/<msp_id>/runs/<run_id>/` |
    | `bundle_sha256` | `signature.bundle_sha256` | equal to the SHA-256 of the `result` part's bytes (verified in point 4) |
    | `signature_ok` | — | true: a bundle that didn't verify is never stored |
    | `tsa_ok`, `tsa_time` | the token | true and its time with a token that verified; null and null without one (point 8) |
    | `cleanup_ok` | `cleanup.cleanup_ok` | when `cleanup` isn't null; else null |

    **No column, stays in the stored `result.json`:** `worker_version`, `connector`, `client` (held in point 9), `restore_point.id` and `backup_time_raw`, `sample` (the seed, the pools, the keys), `expected.counts`, `restore` (the sessions and per-item outcomes), `check.counts` and `stale_copies`, `status.restore_sent`, `counts`, `verified`, `failed_items`, `unchecked_items` and `warnings`, `cleanup.restore_may_still_run`, `before` and `after`, every span but `total`, `attachments` (the names are the objects beside the result), `screenshot`. `worker.version` isn't touched (C5.8's heartbeat sets it). `dispatched_at` and `attempt` are kept.
    - **A rowcount of 0** means the run isn't in a state the statement takes any more: by point 5 the route has just read it as one, so another transaction changed it meanwhile (a second upload of the same run, or the sweep). The route reads the row again (`RunRepo.get` now runs `populate_existing`, so a `get` always answers the row as the database has it and never the identity map's stale copy; a test holds it) and decides by point 13: the same `bundle_sha256` is 202 with no change, another is 409 `bundle_conflict`, and a run the sweep just requeued or expired is taken by running the `UPDATE` once more (the second try is the only loop, and it is bounded: the sweep moves a run once per six hours). Under Postgres' read-committed rules the second `UPDATE` sees the row as the other transaction left it, which is what the `WHERE` is for.
    - *Rejected:* `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the run at the start of the route (the row lock would be held through the signature, the hashing and the puts, and the sweep's `UPDATE` would wait on an upload); `set_state` (no `WHERE` on the state: a race would overwrite a bundle's verdict); the statement in the router (every statement lives in `app/repo/`).

12. **`test_item`: one row per `expected.items[]` entry, joined to `check.items[]` by `index`, in one `INSERT`; a `position` column, migration `0001` edited in place.** `test_item` gains `position integer NOT NULL` with `CHECK (position >= 0)` (`ck_test_item_position_not_negative`), no unique (the Cloud files what the signed result says; the schema can't hold `index` to its position and the Worker always writes it so); `ItemRepo.list` orders by `position` then `id`, and `ItemRepo.create` takes `position` as a required keyword (the isolation test's `make_world` passes one). The mapping, in `app/results.py`:

    | Column | From | Rule |
    |---|---|---|
    | `position` | `expected.items[i].index` | the item's own index |
    | `type` | `.kind` | `mail`, `sharepoint`, `onedrive` |
    | `name` | `.subject` for a mail, `.name` for a file | what the Worker expected; the CSV's `name` is the same value guarded for a spreadsheet |
    | `expected_kind` | `.expected_kind` | `manifest`, `fields`, `metadata` |
    | `expected_sha256` | `.sha256` | a `manifest` item's; null otherwise |
    | `found_sha256` | — | **null, always:** no found value is ever written in the result (W3.2, W4.1), and the Cloud files what the signed document says. The canaries' found hashes are in `items.csv`, stored as an object for a person to read; a report that wants them reads the CSV (C6.x), the Cloud doesn't parse it into rows |
    | `found` | `check.items[j].found` where `j` has the same `index` | null when `check` is null or no check item carries the index |
    | `match` | `check.items[j].outcome` | `match` → true; `mismatch` and `missing` → false; `error` → null (not known; the C5.1 build notes' rule) |
    | `reason` | `check.items[j].reason` | the fixed words; null for a `match` |
    | `ms` | `check.items[j].ms` | null when absent or negative (the CHECK; the schema allows a clock that went back) |

    `ItemRepo.create_many(msp_id, run_id, rows: Sequence[ItemRow]) -> int` adds every row and flushes once (`session.add_all`, one `INSERT` of many under asyncpg's `insertmanyvalues`), answering the count; an empty sequence runs no statement and answers 0. A result whose `expected` is null (an `error` run that never sampled; every result written afterwards) files no items. `restore.items[]` is not mapped (no column; the stored result has it).
    - *Rejected:* a unique on `(msp_id, run_id, position)` (an `IntegrityError` for a signed result the verifiers accept, with a 500 as its only word); `index` as the column's name (a keyword, quoted everywhere, read as "an index"); parsing `items.csv` for `found_sha256` (an attachment is held by its hash, not read as a document; the first reader of CSV in the Cloud would be this one, for a value the result withholds on purpose).

13. **Idempotency: by the run row, no index or unique on `bundle_sha256`.** A run that already holds a bundle (`state` in `pass`, `fail`, `error`; `bundle_sha256` set) answers, after the whole verification of points 4 to 9 has passed again (cheap, and a repeat that doesn't verify is refused like any other): **202** with the stored state when the upload's `bundle_sha256` (the `result` part's SHA-256) equals the row's, writing nothing, no second audit row, no put; **409** `{"detail": "bundle_conflict"}` with one audit row `run:<id> bundle_conflict` when it differs (a second signed result for one run: the Worker never makes one, since a run ID's folder can't be made twice, W4.3 point 2). W4.6 point 3 says why the same bundle comes twice: a 202 whose manifest couldn't be written is uploaded again, and the next flush after a lost answer tries again. **The first upload's 202 is committed before the response starts** (`SessionDep`; `tests/test_app.py` holds the mechanism, and this task's test holds it on the route from a second connection inside `send`), so the Worker's move to `sent\` never outruns the row. No index on `bundle_sha256`: nothing looks a bundle up by hash (the run is the key, and C6.x reads by run and client), and a unique would hold trivially (every result names its own `run_id`, so two runs can't have one hash) while refusing nothing a route doesn't.

14. **The response: 202 with a closed body `{"run_id": "<uuid>", "state": "pass" | "fail" | "error"}`**, the run's state as filed (the idempotent repeat answers the stored one). Never a 200: the Worker's `kUploadAccepted` is 202 and a 200 would be `upload_http_200`, retried hourly for good. The body is for a person at a prompt (the live Done-when's curl); the Worker reads nothing of it today and W5.1 needn't (point 15).

15. **What W5.1 (#66) does with each answer, recorded here for its entry and built nowhere in `worker/`.** The status alone decides; the Worker may log the body's `detail` word (printable ASCII, under 64 characters, from a fixed list) beside `upload_http_<status>` and must rely on nothing else in a body: not `run_id`, not `state`, not the absence of a body. (a) **202**, first or repeated: `sent`, the move to `sent\`, as today. (b) **401**: never retried by schedule; one `warning` line once; the run stays queued and is sent when the token is right (the C5.5 entry's point 10 (c): the heartbeat keeps going). (c) **400** (any word), **404**, **409** (`run_id: not dispatched`, `client_mismatch`, `bundle_conflict`), **415**, **422**: permanent; the folder goes to the issue's `failed\<run_id>` with its manifest's `last_error` (`upload_http_400` and the word), untouched otherwise, for the operator's `rpworker signer verify`; never retried, never deleted by the Worker. (d) **411**, **413**, **5xx**, a timeout, no connection: retried by today's schedule (a 413 is most often a proxy's `client_max_body_size`, fixed on the Cloud's side, after which the retry lands). A `failed\` folder counts under the 500 MB cap as `sent\` does but is never pruned (it is the operator's to look at); W5.1 decides its ACL with W7.1. `manifest.json`'s `last_error` vocabulary gains nothing here: `upload_http_<status>` stays the word, the detail is a log line.

16. **The files, and what is where.** `app/results.py` (new; **guarded, 100% line and branch**): `load_verifier()` (the script by path, once) and `tsa_ca_pem()` (the root by path, once); `Upload` (the parts as bytes by name, with their sizes); `verify_upload(upload, *, public_key_pem, key_id, tsa_ca) -> Verified | Refused` (points 1's part rules, 4, 6, 7, 8 in that order; `Verified` carries the parsed result, the signature's `bundle_sha256`, the token's time or `None`, the attachment names; `Refused` carries the status and the word); `check_run(result, run, client, worker_id) -> Refused | None` (points 5 and 9); `run_update(verified, bundle_key) -> ReceivedRun` and `item_rows(result) -> list[ItemRow]` (points 11 and 12), with the time, span and item mappings as pure functions; the words as constants beside the script's `WORDS`. `app/routers/results.py`: the header checks (415, 411, 413), the form read under the limits, the parts into an `Upload`, the calls above in order, the audit row and the `JSONResponse` for a `Refused`, the repos and `Storage.put` for an accepted one, the `Accepted` response model and the `responses` for the document. `app/repo/runs.py`: `receive`, `ReceivedRun`, `get` with `populate_existing`; `app/repo/items.py`: `create_many`, `ItemRow`, `position`; `app/storage.py`: `put`, `get`; `app/models.py` and `0001`: `tsa_time`, `position`, `received` gone; `app/main.py`: `app.state.tsa_ca_pem` set from `tsa_ca_pem()` (a test replaces it); `cloud/Dockerfile`, the root `.dockerignore`, `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`; `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` (`check_attachment` public, `__all__`); `docs/api/openapi-v1.json`. Every new repo method is in `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`'s table (`receive` as a `Write`: A's `msp_id` on B's run answers 0 and leaves it; `create_many` in `CREATES`), the lint holds the router and `app/results.py` statement-free, and the AST walk holds `msp_id` first.

17. **Tests, failure paths first, the shared vectors through the route.** `tests/test_results.py`: **the Done-when by name, `test_the_tests_pass_and_a_real_worker_bundle_lands_as_pass_in_the_db`.** "A real Worker bundle" in a test without the Veeam VM is `shared/testdata/signing-v1/bundle.json`: the files of a run folder the Worker's own pipeline wrote (the test Harness's run through `rptests "[.write_shared_signing]"`, `status` `pass`, 6 of 6, two attachments) and signed with RFC 8032's published test key 1. Its `run_id` is `rp-20261004T100000Z-0a1b2c3d` and its `client_id` null, so as it is it can't be a run the Cloud dispatched (point 5); the test takes its `result.json`, puts the dispatched run's uuid in `run_id` and the client's id in `client.client_id`, writes the canonical bytes, and signs them with the same published private key (`keys.json`'s `private_pkcs8_base64`, through `cryptography`) into a `signature.json` of the Worker's five keys; the two attachments are the bundle's own bytes. Posted under the registered Worker's token (the Worker row made with that key's PEM through `WorkerRepo.create`, the client with the result's `tenant_id` `11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555`, the run dispatched through `RunRepo.dispatch`): **202** `{"run_id", "state": "pass"}`, the row `pass` with every column of point 11, six `test_item` rows as point 12 maps them (positions 0 to 5, three `manifest` with their hashes, every `match` true), one audit row `result.received`, and `Stubber` having seen four `put_object` calls under `msp/<msp_id>/runs/<run_id>/` with the exact bytes. The same test posts the same bundle again: 202, the same state, no new row of any table, no put. A second Done-when test does the same with a token: the test makes an RFC 3161 token over the re-signed result's hash with the published test TSA key and certificate of `timestamp-v1/keys.json` (`asn1crypto` builds the TSTInfo and the CMS SignedData; `cryptography` signs it with ECDSA; the same shape the Worker's test TSA makes, held by `check_timestamp` saying `verified` with the test root before the route is asked), and shows `tsa_ok` true and `tsa_time` the token's time. **If that token can't be built in the test's budget, the fallback is recorded in the build notes:** the token's acceptance is then shown by the vector `token` reaching the run lookup (below), and `tsa_ok`/`tsa_time` by a unit test of `run_update` on a `Verified` carrying a time.
    - **`tests/test_results_vectors.py`:** every case of `signing-v1/cases.json` and `timestamp-v1/cases.json` built as a folder of bytes by the vector tests' own `write_folder` and posted as the Worker would post it (`result.json` as `result`, `signature.json` as `signature`, `timestamp.tst` as `timestamp`, every other name as a part under its name; a removed file is a missing part); under the registered Worker holding the case's `public_key` (test 1 or test 2) and, for the timestamp cases, the app's CA set to the case's `tsa_ca` (`root`, `other_root`, `tsa_certificate`, `both_roots`; a case with `tsa_ca` null runs under `root`, since the Cloud never leaves a token unchecked). **Every failing case answers 400 with the case's own word**, exactly, with one audit row and nothing stored; **every `verified` case passes the whole verification and is then 404 `run_id: no such run`**, since its `run_id` is no uuid, which is what the Cloud can show for a folder it didn't dispatch: the 404 comes after the fifteen words, and a test holds the order by planting a stale key for one of them. **Two cases differ by design and the test says so:** `token-under-another-name` (`TIMESTAMP.TST`, a note to the verifiers) is `part_unexpected` as an upload (point 7); `token-and-no-ca` (`unchecked` to the script) is `verified` under `root` here. Also `closed-folder.json` (the service's `error interrupted` result) through the route: it verifies and is then 404 for the same reason, and `item_rows` of it is empty.
    - **The rest of `tests/test_results.py`:** the request words (415, 411, 413 before any byte is parsed, held by a body the parser would refuse; `body: malformed` for a bad boundary, a seventh file part and a part without a file name; `part_twice`; the three size words at the limit and one byte over; an over-cap listed size 413); 401 before the body is parsed (no header, a revoked Worker); the run words (not a uuid, unknown, another MSP's, another Worker's of the same MSP: one 404 body; `dispatched_at` null 409; `dispatched`, requeued `queued` and `expired` each taken, the W4.8 case as `closed-folder.json`'s result re-keyed and re-signed, landing `error interrupted` on an `expired` run with `attempt` 3 kept); the tenant words (each of (a) to (d) a 409 `client_mismatch`, the tenant in the other case accepted); the mapping table of point 11 row by row (an `error` result with `expected` null files no items and null columns; `create_many` of 0, 1 and 6 rows in one statement, the order of `list`). `tests/test_openapi.py`: the three paths, the responses `202, 400, 401, 404, 409, 411, 413, 415, 422` on the new route each as `ErrorBody` but the 202, the multipart body in the document. `tests/test_verify_bundle.py`: `check_attachment` in `__all__` and unchanged in its three words.
    - **The by-hand live Done-when, the evidence step, from the Veeam VM to the Compose stack** (`docs/api/cloud-lab/c5.7-done-when.txt`). The Worker sends no `Authorization` header until W5.1, so the Worker's own flush can't land a bundle yet; the real Worker bundle is made by the Worker on the VM and posted by hand with the token, exactly as the Worker will post it. The commands, in order: (1) `cd cloud; docker compose up -d --wait --build`, then the three migration commands of `docs/testing.md` on the stack's database once (the edit of `0001`), `alembic check` clean. (2) The rows, through the repos from a short `uv run python` script against the stack's `DATABASE_URL` (C5.10's `manage.py` doesn't exist; the script is kept in the evidence file, not the repository): one MSP, one client with the lab tenant's id (`lab/tenant.md`), one install token (its label `c5.7 done-when`), printed once. (3) On the VM, `rpworker signer public-key > %TEMP%\rp-c57\worker.pub.pem`, and `curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/workers/register -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @register.json` (the token, the PEM, `worker_name` `veeam-vm`, `version` from `rpworker --version`): 201 with the API token, kept in a file under `%TEMP%\rp-c57` for the session. (4) The connector (the lab's `client-profile.v1` file, as `rpworker client check --profile-file` reads it), a plan (10, 10, 10) and one run through the repos; `curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/jobs -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"`: the `restoreproof.jobs.v1` document with the run's uuid, saved as `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RestoreProof\lab\jobs.json`. (5) The service by hand as `docs/testing.md` "The service's loop by hand" does it, with `jobs_file` naming that document: within one poll the run lands under `outbox\<run uuid>\` with `result.json`, `signature.json`, `timestamp.tst`, `items.csv`, `veeam-session.log` and `manifest.json`; the service's own flush gets `upload_http_401` (expected until W5.1; recorded as such); the service stopped and uninstalled. (6) From that folder, `curl.exe -s -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/results -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -F "result=@result.json;type=application/json" -F "signature=@signature.json;type=application/json" -F "timestamp=@timestamp.tst;type=application/octet-stream" -F "items.csv=@items.csv;type=application/octet-stream" -F "veeam-session.log=@veeam-session.log;type=application/octet-stream"`: **202 `{"run_id": "<uuid>", "state": "pass"}`**; the same command again: 202, the same body. (7) `docker compose exec postgres psql -U restoreproof -d restoreproof -c "SELECT state, error_code, bundle_sha256, signature_ok, tsa_ok, tsa_time, cleanup_ok, total_ms, started_at, finished_at, restore_point_at FROM test_run"` (one row, `pass`, `tsa_ok` true), `SELECT position, type, name, expected_kind, found, match FROM test_item ORDER BY position` (30 rows), `SELECT action, target FROM audit_log` (`worker.register`, `result.received`, nothing for the repeat); the bucket listed (`docker compose run --rm minio-bucket ls` through `mc`, or boto3 from the script) showing the five objects under `msp/<msp_id>/runs/<uuid>/`; the five objects downloaded into a folder and `uv run shared/tools/verify_bundle.py <folder> --public-key worker.pub.pem --tsa-ca shared/tsa/tsa-ca.pem` printing `verified <bundle_sha256> key <key_id> timestamp <time>` with the row's `bundle_sha256` and `tsa_time`. (8) A tampered copy (one byte of `items.csv`) posted: 400 `{"detail": "attachment_hash"}`, one audit row `result.rejected`, the row unchanged, no sixth object. (9) `graph list` 0 in all three targets; the folder moved from `outbox\` to `sent\` by hand (the Worker will do it after W5.1); the API token file and `%TEMP%\rp-c57` removed; the stack's rows left for the next task or `docker compose down -v`. The run folder, the profile and the token stay outside the repository.

18. **The OpenAPI document.** `tools/dump_openapi.py` regenerates `docs/api/openapi-v1.json`; the route declares `responses` for 400, 401 (with `WWW-Authenticate`), 404, 409, 411, 413 and 415 as `ErrorBody` through `refusal(...)` (the C5.5/C5.6 review's finding 3), 202 as `Accepted`, and the multipart body with its named parts through `openapi_extra` (a `requestBody` of `multipart/form-data` with `result`, `signature`, `timestamp` and the three attachment names as `binary` strings, `result` and `signature` required). `tests/test_openapi.py`'s path set becomes the three routes, with the new route's status set and the `ErrorBody` reference on each refusal held as the two existing ones are. FastAPI's own 422 stays in the document (a body FastAPI refuses before the handler is one this route never reaches, since it declares no body model; the test holds the set as generated).

19. **Open review findings: none closed here.** C5.3/C5.4's finding 4 (the lint's wider names), 8 (the dead `compare_digest`), 9 (the two walk-up helpers: `app/results.py` finds `shared/tools` and `shared/tsa` through `app/schemas.shared_schemas_dir()`'s parent and adds no third helper, so the finding neither grows nor closes) and 10 (the slow isolation test) stay open, each its own change. The C5.5/C5.6 build notes' open point (the jobs route's unreachable `RuntimeError`) is untouched; this route's `ClientRepo.get` answering `None` for a run of this MSP is the same unreachable 500 and is noted the same way.

**Reason.** The product is a signed result the Cloud can't alter; the route's job is to take exactly what the Worker signed, refuse anything else with a word the operator can reproduce at a prompt, and file the verdict once. So the verifier is the auditor's own file, the words are its words, the key is the token's and nothing in the body is believed until the signature under that key says so, the run is named only after that, the rows are written in one transaction whose `UPDATE` settles the race, and the objects follow the rows. A refusal leaves one audit row and nothing else; a repeat leaves nothing.

**Alternatives rejected, beyond the points.** *A streaming verifier that hashes parts as they arrive* (the result must be whole before its attachments are known, and 16 MiB plus three files fit in memory; a cap and a spool do the rest). *Verifying in a background job and answering 202 at once* (the Worker's `sent\` would then hold bundles the Cloud later refused, against W4.6's "202 means the Cloud has the run"). *The key by the body's `key_id` with a `Lookup.find_worker_by_key_id`* (a fourth method without `msp_id`, and the trust rule reversed). *An `attempt`-keyed state `received`* (above). *`test_run.worker_version`* (the stored result has it; the Worker row's `version` is the heartbeat's).

**Open, left to the tasks named.**

- C5.8: the heartbeat; `worker.version`, `last_seen_at`, `last_error`.
- C5.9: the sweep calling `requeue_stale` per MSP (unchanged by this task; a run it requeues or expires is still taken by point 5 (c)).
- C5.11: the security scheme on the three Worker routes; whether "No test, no merge" should look at `shared/tools/` now that the Cloud imports it; the fixture bundle (`signing-v1/bundle.json` serves).
- C5.12: the image pinned by digest with `shared/tools` and `shared/tsa` in it; a deployment's TSA roots (one root today).
- C6.2: reading `bundle_key`'s objects, the audit row for a download; C6.4 and Q6.1: `tsa_time` against a report's period; C7.2: the attachment cap as a setting; C7.3: what retention deletes under `bundle_key`.
- A coverage floor for `verify_bundle.py` (W4.3's open point, now that the Cloud runs it).
- The shared vectors' `run_id`s are no uuids and their `client_id` null, so no shared case can reach 202 as it is; a vector written by the Worker's hidden case from a job of the Cloud's shape (a uuid `run_id`, a `client_id`) would let one, and is the Worker's to write (not this task: `worker/` untouched).
- `request.client.host` behind a proxy (C5.12), as for registration.

**Done-when, as it will be run.** With the Compose Postgres up, from `cloud/`: `uv run --locked pytest`, in which `tests/test_results.py::test_the_tests_pass_and_a_real_worker_bundle_lands_as_pass_in_the_db` posts the Worker-made bundle re-keyed to a dispatched run and finds the row `pass` with its items, its audit row and its four objects, and again with no change; `tests/test_results_vectors.py` answers every failing shared case with its word and every verified one with the run's 404 after the whole verification. Then the two coverage commands with `app/results.py`, `app/repo` and `app/auth` at 100/100, `docker compose up -d --wait --build` with `/healthz` 200, `/srv/shared/tools/verify_bundle.py` and `/srv/shared/tsa/tsa-ca.pem` in the image and `alembic check` clean on the stack's re-migrated database, `tools/dump_openapi.py` leaving `docs/api/openapi-v1.json` unchanged, the by-hand live upload of point 17 recorded in `docs/api/cloud-lab/c5.7-done-when.txt`, and the real numbers in the PR.

## 2026-10-10 — C5.5 and C5.6 code review: all ten findings fixed; the commit runs before the response by the dependency's scope, the contract names every refusal, a key off the curve is refused at enrolment, and a poll is two statements (proposed)

The review of the branch `c5.5-c5.6-register-and-jobs` against `main` (`/code-review xhigh`, PR #172) gave ten findings. The owner chose all ten; each has its test written first and seen to fail on the code as it was (the two that mattered most were also shown red with their fix taken out again). This entry supersedes point 5 of the "C5.5 and C5.6" entry where that point said the commit "runs before the response is sent": it did not, in this FastAPI, until finding 1.

1. **`get_session` committed after the response had been sent.** FastAPI 0.143 gives a `yield` dependency the scope `request` unless told otherwise (`fastapi/dependencies/models.py`, `_get_computed_scope`), and a request-scoped dependency's exit runs on the stack that closes after `await response(scope, receive, send)` (`fastapi/routing.py`); only `scope="function"` exits before. So a 201 left with its API token while the Worker's row and the token's `used_at` were still uncommitted, and a poll's runs were still `queued` when the document left. Now `app/db.py` has `SessionDep = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session, scope="function")]`, the three use sites (`current_worker`, the two routes) take it, and the docstring says why a bare `Depends(get_session)` is never to be written. Tests: `test_get_session_commits_before_the_response_starts_and_rolls_back_when_the_route_raises` reads the row from a second connection inside the ASGI `send` of `http.response.start` (1 at that moment for the route that returns, 0 rows left by the route that raises), `test_the_session_dependency_exits_before_the_response_by_its_scope` holds the alias to `get_session` and `function`, and `test_the_worker_row_is_committed_before_the_201_leaves` does the same on the real registration route; all three fail with the scope put back to `request`.
2. **The `get_session` test could not see the ordering and wrote into the shared database.** httpx's transport awaits the whole app call, exit stacks included, so the old test passed with the commit after the response; and it committed through the real dependency into `restoreproof_test`, cleaning up only on the happy path. Replaced by the test of finding 1, on `own_database`.
3. **The committed OpenAPI document named no refusal.** `app/routers/errors.py` has `ErrorBody` (`{"detail": str}`) and `refusal(description, header=…)`; `register` declares 400, 401 (with `WWW-Authenticate`) and 409, `jobs` 401; `docs/api/openapi-v1.json` regenerated; `tests/test_openapi.py` holds the status sets and the `ErrorBody` reference on each.
4. **The two-polls-at-once test over-specified the split** as five and one; two backends locking row by row can split 4/2 or 3/3. Now disjoint, six in all, none over five.
5. **A busy poll was up to seventeen statements and an idle one two.** `RunRepo.dispatch` returns `[]` before any second statement when the CTE took nothing, and otherwise answers `Dispatched(run, plan, connector, client)` tuples from one select joined on keys that start with `msp_id` (`Repo._rows` added for a select of several entities); the route builds the jobs from them. Tests count statements through `before_cursor_execute`: a busy poll is `SELECT` (the token), `WITH` (the dispatch), `SELECT` (the join), an idle one the first two; the repo's own test holds `WITH, SELECT` and `WITH`.
6. **The route read `request.state.msp_id` and repeated the limit.** It takes `worker.msp_id` from the Worker it was given, so an override of `current_worker` works (a test), and `JobsDocument.jobs` is `Field(max_length=DISPATCH_LIMIT)` (a test holds the constant).
7. **Two 401s.** `not_authenticated()` lives in `app/auth/dependency.py`; `current_worker` and `register_worker` both raise it; a test holds the two names to one object.
8. **A value that is no point of the curve registered with 201 and used the token.** `registered_key` now refuses it with the same 400, by RFC 8032 section 5.1.3's recovery of x from y (the two candidates; no x is no point), after the canonical rule and before the small-order list. A one-character slip of RFC 8032's test-1 key (`SLIPPED_KEY` in the test, off the curve as about half of all slips are) is refused though it is a well-formed key file; the module's answer is held equal to an independent Legendre-symbol check on 200 random values and the vectors; RFC 8032's tests 2 and 3 pass. This goes beyond the entry's "not refused: a point off the curve", for the reason the reviewer gave: nothing could ever verify under such a key, and the operator should hear so at enrolment rather than at the first bundle's `wrong_key`.
9. **`own_database` leaked its admin connection when `CREATE DATABASE` failed.** The body is `own_database_context`, an async context manager that connects inside its `try` and closes in `finally`; a test with a fake connection whose CREATE raises sees it closed.
10. **The body patterns repeated the lengths.** `^[^\x00-\x1f\x7f]+$` and `^[ -~]+$` beside the fields' `min_length`/`max_length`, so a name of 129 characters is `string_too_long` and not a pattern mismatch (a test holds both kinds).

**Docs touched:** `docs/testing.md`'s rows for the tests above and its note on `session_override`; CLAUDE.md's `db.py` line, "Worker tokens" and "Dispatch" rules and open-findings line; this entry.

**The gate after the fixes** (the branch, the dev laptop, the Compose `postgres:16`): `uv run --locked pytest --cov=app --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=json:coverage.json --cov-fail-under=80`: **1553 passed** (1535 before; the eighteen new tests above), coverage **99.75%** combined (1065 statements, 2 missed; 116 branches, 1 partial; the two lines still `app/migrations/env.py`'s command-line path, and `app/routers/jobs.py` is now at 100%), in 620 s. `uv run --locked python tools/check_coverage.py coverage.json`: exit 0, every file of `app/repo` and `app/auth` `OK` at 100% line and branch; `app/results.py` skipped as absent. `uv run python tools/dump_openapi.py` leaves `docs/api/openapi-v1.json` unchanged.

## 2026-10-10 — C5.5 and C5.6 build notes: built as the entry says, with a materialised CTE where the entry wrote `id IN (subquery)`, the version stored at registration, a sweep's row in the isolation table, and the test override on a savepoint; both Done-whens shown locally, not in CI (proposed)

The owner approved the entry below as written on 2026-10-10. These notes say where the build left the entry or went beyond it. The points marked **against the entry** are the ones to read.

1. **`RunRepo.dispatch` picks its rows through a `MATERIALIZED` CTE, not `id IN (subquery)` (against point 4).** The entry's statement, `UPDATE … WHERE id IN (SELECT … LIMIT 5 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING`, took six rows of six with the limit at five. `EXPLAIN` showed why: Postgres runs it as a nested-loop semi join whose inner side, the locking subquery, is rescanned per outer row, and `LockRows` re-checks each candidate's latest version, so the rows this very statement had already set to `dispatched` no longer pass `state = 'queued'` and the limit slides to the next ones. The raw probe of the entry's SQL on a scratch table had passed only because its plan was different. Now `WITH chosen AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT id … LIMIT :n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) UPDATE test_run … FROM chosen WHERE test_run.id = chosen.id RETURNING test_run.id`, then one `SELECT` of those ids ordered `(created_at, id)` with `populate_existing`, since the session may already hold stale instances of the rows (a first version returned the identity map's instances with `attempt` still 0). `test_a_dispatch_takes_the_oldest_five_in_order_and_marks_them` is the test that caught both. `RunRepo.dispatch` also refuses a `limit` outside 1 to 5 (`ValueError`).
2. **`worker.version` is set at registration (beyond point 3).** The body carries `version` and the column exists, so `WorkerRepo.create` takes `version=None` and the route stores it; C5.8's heartbeat updates it later.
3. **The test override is a savepoint, not `session.begin()` (against point 5's wording).** The test's session already has its transaction open (the fixture's), so `session_override` wraps the yield in `begin_nested()`; the real `get_session` uses `begin()`. The real one is shown committing and rolling back from a second connection (`tests/test_app.py`). After a rolled-back savepoint every row the session holds is expired, and an expired attribute can't be loaded outside the driver's greenlet, so the route tests keep ids as plain values and read rows back through the repos.
4. **A sweep in the isolation table (beyond point 6).** `requeue_stale` names no row: called with A's `msp_id` it legitimately touches A's own stale run, so `Write` gained `sweep=True`, under which the crossed call's count isn't held to 0 and B's row is still held unchanged; `make_world` makes one dispatched-at-`NOW` run per MSP for it, and `rows_touched` reads a count from an int, a list (`dispatch`) or a pair (`requeue_stale`).
5. **The empty-hash Worker is planted by SQL in `tests/test_auth.py`.** `WorkerRepo.create` now refuses `sha256("")` (point 3), so the C5.4 review's finding-2 test inserts its row with `text()`; the dependency's own refusal is still what it shows.
6. **`tests/registration-keys.json` holds fourteen encodings, not the entry's "fourteen the paper lists, the eight canonical and the six non-canonical"** in the strict sense: eight canonical small-order points, four with `y` at or above p, and two with the sign bit set where x is 0 (the identity and the point of order 2), which the canonical rule doesn't catch and the list does. The module's `SMALL_ORDER` holds all fourteen so it is the paper's list and not a derivation.
7. **The jobs route's required rows.** A `None` from `PlanRepo.get`, `ConnectorRepo.get` or `ClientRepo.get` for a dispatched run is a `RuntimeError` (the app's 500), as the entry says; it can't be reached through the database's keys and is not covered (the routers are outside the guarded paths).
8. **Red before green.** The model tests (13 cases), the key-reader tests (on import), the repo tests (on import), the registration route (404 → the first test), the `get_session` test, the planted sub-package tests, the run-repo tests and the jobs route were each seen failing before their code existed; two tests of the C5.6 batch were then wrong and fixed with the code they test (the Done-when's first sweep counts the other Worker's run too, the sweep's row in the isolation table).
9. **Finding 5 of the C5.3/C5.4 review is closed** (`rglob`, `walk_packages`, the planted `app/repo/sub/x.py` seen by both walks and removed whatever happens); **finding 6** by the phrase in CLAUDE.md. Finding 4 stays open.
10. **Small things the entry didn't name:** `own_database` in `tests/conftest.py` (a migrated database of a test's own, for the three races); `test_a_body_that_is_not_the_model_is_422_before_any_lookup` counts lookups to show the 422 comes before any statement; `tools/dump_openapi.py`'s placeholders are closed loopback ports and visible placeholder strings, held by a test; the stack's own database was re-migrated once (`downgrade -1`, `upgrade head`, `check`).

**The runs, on the branch, on the dev laptop** (Windows, Python 3.12.9, Docker Desktop 29.4.3, the Compose `postgres:16`):

- `uv run --locked pytest --cov=app --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=json:coverage.json --cov-fail-under=80`: **1535 passed**, none skipped, in 580 s; coverage **99.57%** combined (1043 statements, 3 missed; 114 branches, 2 partial: `app/migrations/env.py`'s command-line path as before, and `app/routers/jobs.py`'s unreachable `RuntimeError`). Before this PR: 1341.

**The Done-whens** (`docs/api/cloud-lab/c5.5-c5.6-done-when.txt`):
