## 2026-10-10 — C5.5 and C5.6 (#58, #59): `POST /v1/workers/register` and `GET /v1/jobs`. A Worker registers once with an install token and its Ed25519 public key, held to the two verifiers' one key-file rule, refused when small-order or not canonical, stored in one form under a `key_id` unique across the Cloud, and is given its API token once, all in one transaction; a poll moves the Worker's oldest queued runs, at most five, to `dispatched` in one locked statement and answers them as a `restoreproof.jobs.v1` document whose `run_id` is the run's own id; a run not received within six hours goes back to the queue, after three attempts to `expired` (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written)

C5.5 (#58) and C5.6 (#59) are built on one branch, `c5.5-c5.6-register-and-jobs`, in that order, in one PR with two commits, as C5.3 and C5.4 were (#171). Done when: "The Worker's registration flow succeeds and the token cannot be reused" and "Two polls return the same job only if the first attempt expired." This entry works from the two issues, #66 (W5.1, for what the Worker will do with the answers), the 2026-10-10 entries "C5.3 and C5.4" with their build notes and code review, "C5.1 and C5.2" with its review, the 2026-10-05 W4.3 entry (the trust rule and the key-file rule), the 2026-10-08 W4.8 entry (the jobs document), the W4.10 and W4.11 entries (the job's `client` and `connector`), and the code. No code is written yet; the build notes will record what the build finds.

**What the investigation found, since the points below rest on it.**

- **`key_id` is one computation on three sides already.** The Worker's `SigningKey::key_id()` and `PublicKey::key_id()` are the SHA-256 of the public key's 44-byte SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER in lower-case hex (`worker/include/rp/signer.hpp`); `shared/tools/verify_bundle.py`'s `PublicKey.key_id` is `hashlib.sha256(der).hexdigest()` over the same 44 bytes; `lab/seeder/signing_key.py` computes it the same way; `shared/schemas/signature.v1.json` says so in its description. The Cloud can compute it in Python from the DER alone, and `shared/testdata/signing-v1/key-files.json` pins the answer for RFC 8032's test 1 (`accepted_key_id` `06e3fd8f…2fa9`) and for the identity key (`identity_key_id` `d0fbfbb4…9b4c`).
- **The text of a key file is not canonical; its DER is.** `key-files.json` accepts eleven layouts of one key (LF, CRLF, mixed, no final newline, the body wrapped in two lines, the padding on a line of its own, blank lines and white space around) and refuses thirty-five others, all by the one rule of the W4.3 review (finding 4): the body lines joined are strict Base64 of exactly the 44 bytes of an Ed25519 SubjectPublicKeyInfo as the library writes it. So a unique on the PEM text as it was sent would let one key in eleven times; a unique on the DER's hash lets it in once.
- **The Worker's own PEM and `cryptography`'s are one text.** `rp::Ed25519::public_key_pem` writes `-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----`, one body line, `-----END PUBLIC KEY-----`, each line ending in LF (`worker/include/rp/ed25519.hpp`), which is what `rpworker signer public-key` prints (`docs/worker-config.md`, "`signer public-key`") and `key-files.json`'s row `as-keys-json-has-it`. Measured today with the locked `cryptography` 50.0.2 (OpenSSL 4.0.3): `Ed25519PublicKey.public_bytes(PEM, SubjectPublicKeyInfo)` for RFC 8032 test 1 is byte for byte that text, and its DER's SHA-256 is `accepted_key_id`. There is one serialisation to store, and the library gives it.
- **`cryptography` refuses no small-order key.** Measured today: `Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes` takes all eight small-order points (the identity `01 00…`, its negative, the two of order 2 and 4 by sign, and the four of order 8), and under the identity key `verify(R = the identity's encoding, S = 0, any message)` passes. The W4.3 entry measured the same on OpenSSL 3.5.5 and left the refusal to C5.5, rejecting a list kept equal in two languages ("for a key that only the registering side can vouch for"). Nothing in the library stands between a registration and a key under which every signature verifies; only a list does.
- **The Python reader of a key file is not in the image.** `cloud/Dockerfile` copies `shared/schemas` beside `app/` and nothing else of `shared/`; `verify_bundle.py` imports `asn1crypto` at module level, a dev dependency of `cloud/`. W4.3's open point "whether the Cloud loads `verify_bundle.py` or keeps a copy" is C5.7's, which needs the whole verifier; C5.5 needs its first forty lines.
- **Nothing in `app/` commits.** `get_session` (`app/db.py`) opens a session and yields it; the repos flush (`app/repo/base.py`); `/healthz` uses the engine directly. The C5.3 entry's "one transaction per request or command is the caller's (`get_session`, the CLI)" named the owner and nothing implements it yet. C5.5 is the first route that writes, so the owner is settled below. FastAPI 0.143.0 (locked) throws an exception raised in a route into a `yield` dependency and runs the dependency's exit code before the response is sent (both since 0.106), so a `session.begin()` around the `yield` rolls back on an `HTTPException` and commits before a `201` leaves.
- **The Worker acknowledges no job.** `rp::read_jobs` reads the document and the loop runs it (`worker/include/rp/service_jobs.hpp`, `service_loop.hpp`); the heartbeat body has exactly five keys, none naming a run (`worker/src/heartbeat.hpp`); the only thing the Cloud ever hears of a run is its bundle at `POST /v1/results` (`worker/include/rp/uploader.hpp`). So "received" can only mean "its bundle arrived", and the W5.1 proposal (point 10) asks the Worker for no acknowledgement.
- **A `test_run.id` is a `run_id` the Worker takes.** The Worker's rule is `job_rules::is_folder_run_id` (`worker/src/job_rules.hpp`): 1 to 128 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -` and a plain file name (no `:`, no `.` at the end, not `.` or `..`, not a DOS device's name, `worker/src/atomic_file.hpp`); the schema's pattern is `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`. A `uuid4` written in its usual form is 36 characters of lower-case hex and hyphens: it passes both, names `outbox\<run_id>` (J2) and `runs\<run_id>`, and is the one id the Cloud already has for the run. `str(client.id)` likewise passes `client_id`'s `^[ -~]{1,128}$`.
- **The database already says what a job may say.** `connector.type`'s CHECK is the schema's `^[a-z0-9_]{1,64}$`; `test_plan`'s three CHECKs are the schema's 0 to 100 and not all 0; `connector.config_json` is held to `client-profile.v1.json` and to the client's tenant by `ConnectorRepo` (C5.13); `client.screenshots_enabled` is a boolean; `RUN_STATES` already holds `received` and `expired` (`app/models.py`). What `test_run` lacks is `dispatched_at` and an attempt count, and its one index is `(msp_id, client_id, created_at)`.
- **Two fixtures hold a placeholder key.** `tests/test_auth.py` and `tests/test_repo_isolation.py` make Workers with `PEM = "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\nMCowBQYDK2VwAyEA\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----\n"` (not a key) and a made-up `api_token_hash`. A `key_id` column that is `NOT NULL` and unique touches every such fixture.
- **The lint already holds the routers**, and `session.begin()`, `session.commit()` and `session.rollback()` are not in its list of calls (`tests/test_tenant_scope.py`, `SESSION_CALLS`), so a dependency that owns the transaction passes it. `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`'s `test_the_table_names_every_repo_method` fails for every repo method this PR adds until it is in `READS` or `WRITES`.
- **No OpenAPI document is committed.** `tests/test_app.py` holds the document's path and that `/healthz` is not in it; `docs/api/` has no `openapi-v1.json`; CI diffs nothing (C5.11).
- **CI has not run since 2026-10-03.** Every gate below is run locally and its figures go into the build notes, as for C5.1 to C5.4.

**Decision.**

1. **The schema, in migration `0001` edited in place** (nothing is deployed; `alembic check`, `tests/test_models.py` and `tests/test_migrations.py` hold it, red first on today's schema; the stack's own database gets the three commands of `docs/testing.md` once).
   - **`worker` gains `key_id text NOT NULL`** with `CHECK (key_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$')` (`ck_worker_key_id_hex`) and **`UNIQUE (key_id)` across all MSPs** (`uq_worker_key_id`, a single-column unique like `uq_worker_api_token_hash`). "The public key is already registered" is this unique refusing the row. `public_key_pem` stays `text NOT NULL` and holds the one serialisation of point 2, so it is also one text per key; it is the file a verifier is given (C5.7) and what C6.4 prints a fingerprint of. The unique is on `key_id` because that is the name `signature.json` carries and C5.7 compares (`wrong_key`), and because it is a hash of canonical bytes, where the text is canonical only by the app's doing. **`worker` also gains `install_token_id uuid NULL`** with the key `(msp_id, install_token_id) → install_token (msp_id, id)` (`fk_worker_msp_id_install_token_id_install_token`), set at registration and null for a Worker made any other way: which token made this Worker, in the row the insert writes, with no second statement.
     - *Rejected:* a unique on `public_key_pem` alone (true only while every writer normalises; the hash is what the signature names); a unique per MSP (`(msp_id, key_id)`: one key in two MSPs has no honest case, and the issue says "already registered", not "in this MSP"; the global unique tells a caller a key is known elsewhere only after a valid install token, point 3); `key_id` nullable "for old rows" (there are none).
   - **`install_token` gains `label text NOT NULL`** (what the MSP admin typed when the token was made; C5.10's `create-worker-token` takes `--label`), **`created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`**, **`created_by uuid NULL`** with the key `(msp_id, created_by) → user (msp_id, id)` (`fk_install_token_msp_id_created_by_user`; null for the CLI, as `audit_log.user_id` is), and **`UNIQUE (msp_id, id)`** (`uq_install_token_msp_id_id`, what the new key above points at, by the model's rule for every table another one points at). **It names no client:** a Worker is an MSP's, and connectors bind clients to it later (C5.13); a token that named a client would have to be re-checked against every later connector, for nothing the issue asks.
   - **`test_run` gains `dispatched_at timestamptz NULL`** (the last dispatch's time; null while never dispatched) **and `attempt integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`** with `CHECK (attempt >= 0)` (`ck_test_run_attempt_not_negative`): how many times the run has been handed to its Worker. **No `received_at`:** "received" is the state `received`, which C5.7 sets when the run's bundle is accepted at `/v1/results` (and then `pass`, `fail` or `error` by the verdict); the Worker sends nothing else and is asked for nothing else. "Dispatched but not received within 6 hours" is therefore `state = 'dispatched' AND dispatched_at <= now - 6 h`, with no new column.
   - **The poll's index is `(msp_id, worker_id, state, created_at)`** (`ix_test_run_msp_id_worker_id_state_created_at`): `msp_id` first as every `where` has it, then the two equalities, then the order, so the oldest five queued runs of a Worker are one index walk. The six-hour sweep (point 8) filters on `(msp_id, state, dispatched_at)` and gets no index of its own: dispatched rows are at most a handful per MSP; an index comes with a measurement.
     - *Rejected:* `(worker_id, state, created_at)` without `msp_id` (an index that doesn't start with the tenant is one a future statement can be tempted to use without it); a partial index `WHERE state = 'queued'` (`alembic check` doesn't compare the predicate, so a test couldn't hold it).

2. **The key: one reader, one stored form, two refusals beyond it, `app/auth/public_keys.py`** (guarded, 100% line and branch).
   - **`registered_key(pem: str) -> RegisteredKey | None`** applies the key-file rule of the W4.3 review exactly as `verify_bundle.py`'s `public_key_from_pem` does (white space around; the two armour lines; body lines of Base64 characters only; LF or CRLF; the body joined strict Base64 of exactly the 44 bytes with the prefix `302a300506032b6570032100`), on the UTF-8 bytes of the body's string, and the library is handed the 32 key bytes only. **Held to `key-files.json` row by row** (the 46 rows, as `tests/test_verify_bundle.py` already reads them: the eleven accepted rows all give `accepted_key_id`, the identity row gives `identity_key_id` from the reader and is then refused by the next step, the thirty-five refused rows give `None`) **and to the script's answer**: a test runs both readers over every row and requires the same DER or the same `None`. A copy of forty lines, not an import: the script is not in the image and brings `asn1crypto` with it; C5.7 decides the verifier's home and may fold this reader into it then.
   - **Then two refusals the verifiers don't make.** (a) **A non-canonical encoding:** the 32 key bytes read little-endian with the top bit cleared give `y`; `y >= 2^255 − 19` is refused (RFC 8032 §5.1.3 decodes it, libraries differ, and it would let one point in under two `key_id`s). (b) **A small-order point:** the eight canonical encodings of the points of order 1, 2, 4 and 8, as a fixed list of 32-byte values in the module with the paper named ("Taming the many EdDSAs", Chalkias, Garillot, Nikolaenko, 2020, table 1), compared after (a) so each point has one encoding to compare. Under such a key the library verifies forgeries (measured above), so a Worker registered with one could have any bundle "verified" by C5.7; the registering side is the one place to refuse it, as W4.3 left it. **The list lives in the Cloud alone, with its vector in `cloud/tests/`** (the fourteen encodings the paper lists, the eight canonical and the six non-canonical ones, each as a PEM made by the library, plus RFC 8032's test 1 as the accepted control): the verifiers keep accepting such a file as a well-formed key (`key-files.json`'s `small-order-identity-key` row stays `accepted: true` and `rptests` isn't touched), since the W4.3 reason stands: only the registering side can vouch for a key, and a list kept equal in C++ and Python would guard nothing the Worker does. **Not refused:** a point off the curve (no private key signs under it, so nothing it is registered for can ever verify; refusing it would need the curve's arithmetic in Python for no attack) and a published key such as RFC 8032's test vectors (the API token, not the key, is what lets a Worker upload; the key names who signed).
   - **What is stored:** `public_key_pem` is the library's own serialisation of the DER that was read (`public_bytes(PEM, SubjectPublicKeyInfo)`: the three-line form with LF, shown above to be the Worker's own text), `key_id` the SHA-256 of that DER. A key sent with CRLF or wrapped is accepted and stored in the one form; a test registers the eleven accepted layouts of `key-files.json` and finds one stored text and one `key_id` for all.
     - *Rejected:* `cryptography`'s `load_pem_public_key` (it takes what the rule refuses: a block on one line, header lines, text on the armour lines, and re-encodes); a shared vector under `shared/testdata/signing-v1/` for the small-order list (every file there is written by a hidden `rptests` case and run by both builds; this one would be run by one); a proof of possession at registration (a challenge the Worker signs: W5.1 would gain a round trip for what the first bundle's signature proves anyway, and the Worker side is not to change here).

3. **`POST /v1/workers/register`, in `app/routers/workers.py` over `app/auth/registration.py`** (the logic in the guarded package, the route a few lines mapping its answers to statuses).
   - **The body** is a closed Pydantic model (`extra="forbid"`): `install_token` (a string of 1 to 256 characters, deliberately *not* held to the token's 43-character shape: whatever is sent is hashed and looked up, so a token of another shape gets the same 401 as an unknown one), `public_key_pem` (1 to 4096 characters; a key file is about 120), `worker_name` (1 to 128 characters, no control character: `^[^\x00-\x1f\x7f]{1,128}$`), `version` (1 to 64 printable ASCII characters, `^[ -~]{1,64}$`, what `rpworker --version` prints). A body that isn't the model is FastAPI's own **422**, which names the field and the rule; the model is in the OpenAPI document, so it tells a caller nothing it can't read there.
   - **The order of checks, and the one answer each gives.** (1) `accept_install_token(session, body.install_token, now)`: `None` is **401** `{"detail": "not authenticated"}` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, one body for a token that is unknown, used or expired (the C5.4 rule; the `UPDATE`'s conditions decide, `app/auth/tokens.py`). (2) `registered_key(body.public_key_pem)`: `None` is **400** `{"detail": "public_key_pem: not an accepted Ed25519 public key"}`, one body for a file that breaks the rule, a non-canonical encoding and a small-order point (nothing says which; an operator's real key passes, and no honest key fails any of the three). (3) `WorkerRepo.create(...)` with the key's `key_id`: the database's `uq_worker_key_id` refusing the flush is **409** `{"detail": "public_key_pem: already registered"}`, recognised by the constraint's name in the `IntegrityError` (any other `IntegrityError` is re-raised and is the app's 500). (4) **201** `{"worker_id": "<uuid>", "api_token": "<43 characters>", "key_id": "<64 hex>"}`, a closed response model. The token comes first so that **no 400 and no 409 is ever answered to a caller without a valid install token**: what keys are registered, and whether a key is well-formed, is told only to someone the MSP admin gave a token to; `current_worker`'s rule, "one 401 after the same work for every failure to authenticate", holds here too (one hash, one lookup, one `UPDATE`, whatever the token). `key_id` is in the answer so an operator can compare it with the `key <key_id>` line `rpworker signer public-key` prints; the Worker may ignore it.
   - **One transaction, both or neither.** The token's `UPDATE`, the Worker's `INSERT` and the audit row (below) run in the request's one transaction and are committed by `get_session` (point 5) when the route returns 201; a 400, a 409 or anything else raised after the `UPDATE` rolls it back, so **a failed registration leaves the token unused**: an operator who pasted a wrong key tries again with the same token. Single use under concurrency is the `UPDATE`'s (`used_at IS NULL` in the statement): two registrations with one token at once are one 201 and one 401, whichever order they run in, and two with the same key and two tokens are one 201 and one 409 with the loser's token unused. A test shows each with two sessions on a database of its own (as `tests/test_migrations.py` makes one), since rows must be committed for a second connection to see them.
   - **The token is minted here.** `new_token()` once, `token_hash()` of it into `WorkerRepo.create`, the token itself into the response and nowhere else: not in a row, not in a log line, not in an audit row. `tests/test_auth.py`'s log test is extended to registration: a 201, a 401, a 400 and a 409 through `create_app` with the log captured, and neither the install token, nor the API token, nor either hash, nor the word `Bearer` in any line (the request line has no body; the secret-name rule covers `install_token` and `api_token` by their endings).
   - **The empty token's hash is refused by the repo** (the C5.4 review's finding 2, its second half): `WorkerRepo.create` raises `RepoError("api_token_hash", "the empty token's hash")` for `hashlib.sha256(b"").hexdigest()`, a constant computed in `app/repo/workers.py` from the standard library, so `app.repo` imports nothing of `app.auth`. The dependency's own refusal stays; this is the second line.
   - **One audit row per registration**, through `AuditRepo.write` in the same transaction: `action` `worker.register`, `target` `worker:<id>`, `user_id` null, `ip` the request's client address when FastAPI has one (`request.client.host`) else null. Nothing of the body goes into it. A registration that fails writes none (the rollback).
   - **The repo methods this changes:** `WorkerRepo.create(msp_id, name, *, public_key_pem, key_id, api_token_hash, install_token_id=None)`, `InstallTokenRepo.create(msp_id, *, token_hash, expires_at, label, created_by=None)`, and `issue_install_token(session, msp_id, now, *, label, created_by=None)` passing them on. The repo stores the `key_id` it is given and holds it to nothing but the CHECK and the unique: the reader of point 2 is the one place that makes a `key_id` from a key, and the fixtures that make Workers by hand give a distinct hash per Worker (`a_hash(f"{name} key")`) as they do for `api_token_hash`.
     - *Rejected:* a 404 or 403 for a bad token (it names the case; C5.4's one 401); a 422 for a bad PEM (a well-formed string that isn't a key is the issue's 400, and the 422 is FastAPI's word for the body's shape); a pre-check of the key by a `Lookup.find_worker_by_key_id` (a fourth method without `msp_id` in the AST allowance, for a race the unique settles anyway); refusing a used token before the key is parsed by a `SELECT` and then marking it after (two statements where one `UPDATE` is the single-use rule); the token's hash compared with `compare_digest` here (the review's open finding 8 applies: a row found by equality on the hash is equal; the 256 random bits are the mitigation).

4. **`GET /v1/jobs`, in `app/routers/jobs.py`, `Depends(current_worker)`.**
   - **Selection, in one statement, `RunRepo.dispatch(msp_id, worker_id, now, limit=5) -> list[TestRun]`:** `UPDATE test_run SET state = 'dispatched', dispatched_at = :now, attempt = attempt + 1 WHERE msp_id = :msp_id AND id IN (SELECT id FROM test_run WHERE msp_id = :msp_id AND worker_id = :worker_id AND state = 'queued' ORDER BY created_at, id LIMIT 5 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING *`, built with SQLAlchemy's `with_for_update(skip_locked=True)` on the inner select and `.returning(TestRun)`, the rows then ordered `(created_at, id)` in Python since `RETURNING` promises no order. Two polls at once can't take one row (the second skips what the first holds and sees `dispatched` once it is committed), and a poll holds nothing after its transaction. `msp_id` is `request.state.msp_id`, `worker_id` the row `current_worker` returned, `limit` fixed at five (`kMaxJobs` in the Worker, `maxItems` in the schema).
   - **The document, field by field** (`shared/schemas/jobs.v1.json` as it stands; nothing in the schema or the Worker's reader changes): `format` `restoreproof.jobs.v1`; `jobs` the dispatched runs in their order, each `run_id` = `str(test_run.id)` (36 characters, passes `is_folder_run_id` and the pattern); `client_id` = `str(test_run.client_id)` (the Cloud's label for the client, W4.10; never null from the Cloud); `client` = `connector.config_json` as stored (a `client-profile.v1` whose `graph_tenant_id` is the client's tenant, held by `ConnectorRepo` at every write); `connector` = `{"type": connector.type}`; `sample_mail`, `sample_sp`, `sample_od` = the plan's; `restore_point` = `"latest"` (the only value a run has today; `test_run.restore_point_at` is what the result reports back, C5.7); `screenshots_enabled` = `client.screenshots_enabled`; **`canary_cursor` omitted** (the Worker defaults it to `0,0,0`; the cursor is the Cloud's to keep, W2.6, and no table holds one yet: the task that rotates canaries adds the column and the advance rule). The plan, connector and client of each run are read through `PlanRepo.get`, `ConnectorRepo.get` and `ClientRepo.get` with the same `msp_id`; by the keys of C5.3 every one exists for a run of this MSP, so a `None` there is the app's 500, never an empty job. **The response is validated against the schema in a test, not per request:** `tests/test_jobs_route.py` validates every document the route answers with `Draft202012Validator` over `load_schema("jobs.v1.json")` and the profile schema (`app/schemas.py`, by path, with the registry `tests/test_jobs_schema.py` already builds), and runs it through the shared vectors' `base` for the shape; at run time every field comes from a column the database already holds to the schema's rule, so a check per request would refuse nothing the writes didn't.
   - **A Worker with nothing queued answers 200 `{"format": "restoreproof.jobs.v1", "jobs": []}`** (no connectors, no plans, no runs, or all of them dispatched): the Worker's reader takes an empty `jobs` (the vector `no-jobs`) and runs nothing. **A revoked Worker is `current_worker`'s 401**, before any statement; nothing is added. The poll doesn't touch `worker.last_seen_at`: the heartbeat is the liveness signal (W4.8 point 11, C5.8).
   - **Done-when, as a test:** two queued runs for Worker A and one for Worker B of the same MSP, one for another MSP's Worker; A's first poll answers A's two, oldest first, each now `dispatched` with `dispatched_at` = now and `attempt` 1; A's second poll answers `[]`; B's poll answers B's one; the other MSP's run is nowhere. Then `requeue_stale` at now + 6 h puts A's two back (`attempt` still 1) and A's third poll answers them again (`attempt` 2); after the third dispatch the sweep makes them `expired` and a fourth poll answers `[]`. Six queued runs and two concurrent polls on a database of their own answer five and one, disjoint.
     - *Rejected:* `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` then an `UPDATE` per row (two statements and a per-row loop for what one does); a per-request schema validation (above); `restore_point` as a per-run column now (no writer of it exists); `last_seen_at` on the poll (above); the jobs as a bare array (the Worker's reader wants the closed document).

5. **`get_session` owns the request's transaction.** `app/db.py`'s dependency becomes `async with session_factory() as session: async with session.begin(): yield session`: committed when the route returns, rolled back when it raises (an `HTTPException` included, which FastAPI 0.143 throws into the generator), and the commit runs before the response is sent. The repos keep flushing and never committing (the isolation test holds it); a route calls neither `commit` nor `rollback`. The tests' override is the same generator over the test's session (`join_transaction_mode="create_savepoint"` makes `begin()` a savepoint under the test's outer transaction), so a test sees what a 400 rolled back. `tests/test_auth.py`'s "the dependency takes its session from `get_session`" stays as it is.
   - *Rejected:* the route committing (every writing route would repeat the three lines and one would forget the rollback); a middleware that commits on 2xx (the session is the dependency's; a middleware doesn't hold it).

6. **The isolation table and the lint.** Every new repo method goes into `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`: `RunRepo.dispatch` as a `Write` (A's `msp_id` with B's Worker answers `[]` and B's runs stay `queued`), `RunRepo.requeue_stale` as a `Write` (A's `msp_id` leaves B's stale run `dispatched`); the two `create`s keep their rows in `CREATES` with their new keywords; `make_world` gives each Worker its own `key_id`. The two routers are under the lint already and stay statement-free. **Of the review's open findings 4 to 6: 5 and 6 are closed in this PR** (5: the AST walk and the isolation test's module scan become `rglob` and `pkgutil.walk_packages`, with a test that plants `app/repo/sub/x.py` holding a `select(` without `msp_id` and sees both catch it; 6: the one phrase in CLAUDE.md names `app/migrations/` as the second exemption); **4 stays open** (the wider name set, `text(`, the multi-line import: its own lint-hardening change with its own table rows, not mixed into two routes).

7. **The first `docs/api/openapi-v1.json` is committed now**, since these are the first routes: `cloud/tools/dump_openapi.py` writes `create_app(settings).openapi()` with sorted keys, two-space indentation and LF (the settings built in the tool from the same closed-loopback placeholders `tests/conftest.py`'s `make_settings` uses, so nothing in `app/settings.py` gains a default), and `tests/test_openapi.py` holds the file equal to what the app serves at `/v1/openapi.json`, so a route change without the regenerated file fails the existing test step. C5.11 keeps what it had left: the CI job's wording, the `HTTPBearer` security scheme on the Worker routes in the document (today the document shows `current_worker`'s routes with no security scheme, since the dependency reads the header itself), and the fixture bundle.
   - *Rejected:* waiting for C5.11 (two routes' shapes settled without the artefact that holds them); the document written by the test on a flag (a test that writes a file).

8. **What C5.9 gets from this PR: `RunRepo.requeue_stale(msp_id, now) -> tuple[int, int]`**, written and tested here as pure repo (the scheduler that calls it per MSP, over `MspRepo.list`, is C5.9's). Two statements in order: `UPDATE test_run SET state = 'expired' WHERE msp_id = :msp_id AND state = 'dispatched' AND dispatched_at <= :now − 6 h AND attempt >= 3`, then the same condition with `attempt < 3` `SET state = 'queued'` (`dispatched_at` and `attempt` kept, so the next dispatch counts 2 and 3); the answer is `(requeued, expired)`. The constants `DISPATCH_TIMEOUT = 6 h` and `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` live beside the method in `app/repo/runs.py`; the time is the caller's. The edge is held by a test: a run dispatched at `t` is left alone at `t + 6 h − 1 s` and requeued at `t + 6 h`. `set_state` stays for C5.7.
   - *Rejected:* leaving it to C5.9 (the Done-when's "only if the first attempt expired" can't be shown without it, and C5.9 would then write the statement that decides what C5.6's counter means).

9. **Tests and coverage.** Failure paths first, each refusal held to its status and body: `tests/test_public_keys.py` (the 46 rows, the script's agreement, the fourteen small-order encodings and the non-canonical rule, the one stored form), `tests/test_registration.py` (the Done-when; the four answers in order; a used, an expired and an unknown token one 401; the token unused after a 400 and after a 409; two tokens and one key; one token twice at once; the audit row; the log), `tests/test_jobs_route.py` (the Done-when; the document against the schema; the empty answer; the other MSP's and the other Worker's runs; the revoked Worker; two concurrent polls), `tests/test_repo_runs.py` (`dispatch` and `requeue_stale` by themselves: the order, the limit, the counter, the edge, the other MSP), the model and migration tests for the new columns, keys and index (red first), `tests/test_openapi.py`, and the extended `test_auth.py`, `test_tokens.py` (`label`, `created_by`) and `test_repo_isolation.py`. `app/auth/public_keys.py`, `app/auth/registration.py`, `app/repo/runs.py`, `app/repo/workers.py` and `app/repo/install_tokens.py` are under `tools/check_coverage.py` at 100% line and branch; the 80% gate on `app/` stays; both commands of `cloud/Makefile`'s `cov` go into the build notes.

10. **What W5.1 (#66) does afterwards, recorded here for its entry and built nowhere in `worker/`.** The Worker already reads `restoreproof.jobs.v1`, names its folders by `run_id`, signs under its vault key and sends the heartbeat body and the results POST; **none of that changes**: not the reader, not `job_rules`, not the five-key heartbeat, not the signing contract, not `rpworker signer public-key`'s text (which is exactly what `public_key_pem` takes). What W5.1 adds, as this entry proposes it: (a) two vault names, `cloud_install_token` (set by the operator with `rpworker vault set`, as the five are) and `cloud_api_token` (written by the service after a 201, which needs the vault's own write path used from the service; both names end in `token`, so the Cloud's log rule covers them, and the Worker's `kSecretNames`, `secret_values` and the secret audit's list grow by two); (b) the first-start flow of #66: no `cloud_api_token` → `POST <cloud_url>/v1/workers/register` with `{"install_token", "public_key_pem": <the vault key's PEM>, "worker_name": <a config key or the machine's name>, "version": rp::version()}`, read the closed answer `{"worker_id", "api_token", "key_id"}` with strict JSON, store the token, keep `worker_id` somewhere that isn't a secret (`state\worker.json`, or the config), remove the install token; on 401 or 400 stop with one fixed line (the operator makes a new token; the Worker never registers twice by itself), on 409 the same (the key is already another Worker's); (c) `Authorization: Bearer <cloud_api_token>` on `GET /v1/jobs`, `POST /v1/results` and `POST /v1/heartbeat`, and what a 401 from any of them does (nothing retries it; one `warning` line once; the heartbeat keeps going, since it is the Cloud's only word of a Worker whose token was revoked); (d) the poll replacing `jobs_file`: the same document through the same reader, with the file's owner rule replaced by TLS to `cloud_url`, and the J2 rule unchanged (a `run_id` the Cloud dispatches twice is skipped by the Worker when its folder is still there, which is why a requeued run should carry the same `run_id`: it does, point 4). What the outbox does with a 4xx that will never succeed is C5.7's to define by status and W5.1's to act on.

**Files.** New: `app/auth/public_keys.py`, `app/auth/registration.py`, `tools/dump_openapi.py`, `docs/api/openapi-v1.json`, the tests of point 9. Changed: `app/models.py`, `app/migrations/versions/0001_initial.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/auth/tokens.py`, `app/repo/workers.py`, `app/repo/install_tokens.py`, `app/repo/runs.py`, `app/routers/workers.py`, `app/routers/jobs.py`, `tests/conftest.py` (the override that mirrors `get_session`), `tests/test_auth.py`, `tests/test_tokens.py`, `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`, `tests/test_tenant_scope.py`, `tests/test_models.py`, `tests/test_migrations.py`, `docs/testing.md` ("Cloud"), `docs/worker-config.md` (one sentence under "The jobs file": the Cloud's `run_id` and `client_id` are the run's and the client's ids), `docs/glossary.md` ("Tokens": `key_id` at registration, the install token's label, `dispatched`), CLAUDE.md. No runtime dependency is added: `cryptography` is needed for nothing here (the reader hands the library nothing; `key_id` is `hashlib`; the one serialisation is the twelve-byte prefix, the key and Base64, which the test holds equal to the library's). Unchanged: everything under `shared/` and `worker/`.

## 2026-10-10 — C5.3 and C5.4 code review: findings 1, 2, 3 and 7 of ten fixed, 4 to 6 and 8 to 10 open (proposed)

The review of the branch `c5.3-c5.4-repo-and-tokens` against `main` (`/code-review xhigh`) gave ten findings. The owner chose 1, 2, 3 and 7 to fix now; each has its test written first and seen to fail on the code as it was. The rest are listed open with what each would take. Nothing is committed until the owner asks.

**Fixed.**

1. **`ConnectorRepo.update` writes its audit row only when the `UPDATE` touched a row.** The row was read, the profile checked, then the `UPDATE` run and the `connector.update` audit row written whether or not the `UPDATE` reached anything; a delete between the read and the statement left an audit row for a change that never happened. Now `if touched:` guards the row as the delete path already did, and the method answers 0. Test: `test_an_update_of_a_connector_deleted_meanwhile_touches_nothing_and_writes_no_update_row` deletes the connector from inside the repo's own `_client` seam and finds `create` and `delete` rows and no `update` row. This supersedes the build notes' "an audit row per create, update and delete": per one that touched a row.
2. **The empty token authenticates nothing, whatever the database holds.** A missing or malformed `Authorization` header was the empty token, whose hash was looked up like any other; a Worker row stored under `sha256("")` would have answered every request without a header. `current_worker` still does the same work for every request (one hash, one lookup, one comparison; the test that counts lookups is unchanged) and then also refuses when the presented token is empty. Test: `test_no_token_authenticates_nothing_whatever_the_database_holds` makes such a Worker and sends no header, `Bearer ` and `Basic …`. *Rejected:* refusing `token_hash("")` in `WorkerRepo.create` alone (it would leave the dependency trusting the database to hold the line, and `app.repo` would import a constant of `app.auth`'s, the wrong way round); it can still be added by C5.5, which mints the token.
3. **`ConnectorRepo.create` holds the Worker as it holds the client, and checks in the entry's order.** `worker_id` was left to the foreign key, so another MSP's Worker or an absent one surfaced as an `IntegrityError` with the session failed, while `client_id` was a `RepoError`; and the client was read before the schema was checked, against the entry's "the schema first, then the client". Now the order is the schema (`config_json`), the client (`client_id`), its tenant (`graph_tenant_id`), the Worker (`worker_id: no such worker`), each a `RepoError` naming the key and no value. `_client` and the new `_worker` go through `ClientRepo.get` and `WorkerRepo.get` rather than a `select` of their own, which closes the first half of finding 9. Tests: `test_a_worker_that_is_not_the_msp_s_is_no_worker` (the other MSP's Worker and an absent id; the session still answers afterwards) and `test_the_refusals_come_in_one_order_schema_client_tenant_worker` (four cases, each carrying every later fault too).
4. **Finding 7: `tests/test_auth.py`'s probe route can no longer leak.** `Lab.__init__` put the route on the shared `workers.router` and the fixture's `try/finally` began only after `Lab.make` had also made the rows, so a database failure while making them left the route on the router for the rest of the session. The fixture is now `open_lab`, an async context manager that constructs the `Lab`, then inside its `try` fills the rows and yields, and closes in `finally`. Test: `test_a_lab_that_fails_to_open_leaves_no_probe_route_behind` makes `WorkerRepo.create` raise and finds the router clean.

**Open, for the owner.**

- **4. The lint is bypassable** (`tests/test_tenant_scope.py`): it matches `session.` alone, not `db.`, `conn.`, `connection.` or `engine.`; never `text("UPDATE …")`; and its import regex is single-line, so a parenthesised multi-line `from sqlalchemy import (…)` escapes. A fix is a wider name set, a `text(` pattern and a multi-line import match, with each added to the lint's table of refused lines. Best done together with 5 and 6 as one lint-hardening change.
- **5. A module under `app/repo/<sub>/` escapes all three checks**: the AST walk's `glob("*.py")` and `test_repo_isolation.py`'s `pkgutil.iter_modules` are non-recursive while the lint exempts everything under `app/repo/`. A fix is `rglob` and `pkgutil.walk_packages`, or a test that `app/repo/` has no sub-package.
- **6. CLAUDE.md says the lint holds everything outside `app/repo/`; `app/migrations/` is exempt too.** `docs/testing.md` names the exemption. One phrase in CLAUDE.md's "Cloud tenant isolation" rule.
- **8. `hmac.compare_digest` in `current_worker` compares a row found by SQL equality on the same hash, so it is always equal when a row exists**; the constant-time step guards nothing, and the real mitigation is the 256-bit random token, which makes the lookup's timing uninformative. Either drop the compare and say why in the module docstring, CLAUDE.md and the C5.4 entry, or look the row up by a non-secret key and compare the stored hash. The entry and CLAUDE.md still describe the compare as a property; a reader should not rely on it.
- **9. Duplication, half closed here**: `_client` now calls `ClientRepo.get` (fixed under 3). Still open: `app/schemas.py`'s `shared_schemas_dir` and `tests/test_result_schema.py`'s `shared_dir` are two walk-up helpers; the tests could import the app's.
- **10. `tests/test_repo_isolation.py` rebuilds two worlds per case** (50 cases, about 44 inserts each) and is a large share of the suite's 175 s. A module-scoped pair of worlds under a savepoint per case, or one multi-row insert per table, would cut most of it. Not a correctness matter.

**Docs touched:** `docs/testing.md`'s rows for `test_repo_connectors.py` and `test_auth.py`; CLAUDE.md's "Cloud tenant isolation" and "Worker tokens" rules and its open-findings line; this entry.

**The gate after the fixes** (the branch, the dev laptop, the Compose `postgres:16`): `uv run --locked pytest --cov=app --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=json:coverage.json --cov-fail-under=80`: **1341 passed** (1336 before; the five new tests above), coverage **99.68%** combined (853 statements, 2 missed; 90 branches, 1 partial; the two lines still `app/migrations/env.py`'s command-line path), in 396 s with the laptop otherwise busy. `uv run --locked python tools/check_coverage.py coverage.json`: exit 0, every file of `app/repo` and `app/auth` `OK` at 100% line and branch (`connectors.py` 68/68 lines, 18/18 branches; `dependency.py` 25/25, 2/2); `app/results.py` skipped as absent. `python worker/tools/fixture_secret_scan.py`: 1163 files, 0 findings. The five new tests were each seen to fail on the code as it was (`5 failed, 33 passed` on `test_repo_connectors.py` and `test_auth.py`) before the fixes.

The world is built through the repos (so every `create` runs twice per test), and `test_the_table_names_every_repo_method` holds the table to the 42 public methods it inspects; 25 reads and 9 writes each run both ways round.

## 2026-10-10 — C5.3 and C5.4 (#56, #57): the tenant-scoped repository layer and the tokens. Every database statement in `app/repo/`, every method `msp_id` first but two named lookups and the MSP's own create; a run keyed to its plan's connector's Worker (finding 3 of the C5.1/C5.2 review); install and Worker tokens as 32 random bytes stored as their SHA-256; `current_worker` answering one 401 for every failure (recorded before the build; the owner approved it as written)

C5.3 (#56) and C5.4 (#57) are built on one branch in that order, in one PR. Done when: "The scope test passes and the lint test is in CI" and "A revoked token gets 401 and a valid one passes." This entry works from the two issues, issue #136 (C5.13, whose repo-layer rules land here), the 2026-10-10 "C5.1 and C5.2" entry with its build notes and code review (finding 3 is settled below), the 2026-09-22 entry "Cloud tenant isolation through repository classes", the 2026-09-29 entry "Clients live in the Cloud", and the code. No code is written yet; the build notes will record what the build finds.

**What the investigation found, since the points below rest on it.**

- **Nothing in `app/` selects, inserts, updates or deletes today.** `app/db.py` runs `SELECT 1` through a connection in `/healthz`; `app/models.py` is the metadata; the six routers are empty. So the lint of point 3 starts green on everything but `app/repo/`, and the repo layer is the first code to issue a statement.
- **`test_run.worker_id` is held to the MSP alone.** `test_run (msp_id, worker_id) → worker (msp_id, id)`; the plan's connector's Worker is reachable only through `test_plan.connector_id → connector.worker_id`, and nothing ties the two. The review's finding 3. Nothing is deployed and migration `0001` has run on no database but the tests' and the local stack's.
- **The image doesn't carry `shared/`.** `cloud/Dockerfile` copies `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `alembic.ini` and `app/` from a build context of `cloud/`, and `cloud/.dockerignore` allows those four paths and nothing else. The Cloud's tests find the schemas by walking up from `tests/` (`shared_dir()` in `tests/test_result_schema.py`); the app has no such function and, in the container, no such folder. A repo method that validates against `shared/schemas/client-profile.v1.json` by path would raise `FileNotFoundError` in the api container the first time it is called. Point 7 settles it.
- **`jsonschema` is a dev dependency.** The C5.1/C5.2 entry (point 3) kept it there "until C5.7 verifies a bundle in `app/`". C5.13's validation in the repo layer brings it into `app/` now.
- **The secret-name rule already covers the header.** `app/logging.py` redacts the value under any key ending in `authorization` or `token`; the request line has no header, no query string and no body. What C5.4 adds is a test that the bearer value and its hash appear in no line of a failed request's log and a passed one's.
- **`check_coverage.py`'s guarded paths are all absent today.** `app/auth`, `app/results.py` and `app/repo` print `SKIP does not exist yet`. This is the first PR where the 100% line-and-branch gate has files to measure; a branch without a test fails the step.
- **asyncpg gives a rowcount for `UPDATE` and `DELETE`** (SQLAlchemy reads the status tag), so an update or delete that touched no row can say so, which point 2's "reports zero rows" and point 5's single use rest on.

**Decision.**

1. **Finding 3: a run is keyed to its plan's connector and to that connector's Worker, in migration `0001` edited in place.** `test_run` gains `connector_id uuid NOT NULL`. Two keys hold it:
   - `test_run (msp_id, plan_id, connector_id, client_id) → test_plan (msp_id, id, connector_id, client_id)`, **replacing** today's `(msp_id, plan_id, client_id) → test_plan (msp_id, id, client_id)` and its unique. One key says both "the run's client is its plan's" and "the run's connector is its plan's".
   - `test_run (msp_id, connector_id, worker_id) → connector (msp_id, id, worker_id)`, new, with the new `UNIQUE (msp_id, id, worker_id)` on `connector`.
   So a run's Worker is its connector's, and its connector is its plan's: the run can only name its plan's connector's Worker. The direct keys `(msp_id, worker_id) → worker` and `(msp_id, client_id) → client` stay (redundant now, cheap, and they keep each column's meaning readable in the catalogue). **The simpler way, taken over the brief's:** the brief kept the `(msp_id, plan_id, client_id)` key and added a second one to `test_plan (msp_id, id, connector_id)`; folding `connector_id` into the existing plan key is one key and one unique fewer for the same guarantee. The constraint names follow from the convention: `fk_test_run_msp_id_plan_id_connector_id_client_id_test_plan`, `fk_test_run_msp_id_connector_id_worker_id_connector`, `uq_connector_msp_id_id_worker_id`, `uq_test_plan_msp_id_id_connector_id_client_id`.
   - **A consequence to know:** `connector.worker_id` can't change once a run names the connector (no key cascades). Moving a client to another Worker is a new connector, which is also what `UNIQUE (worker_id, client_id)` says a connector is. `ConnectorRepo.update` therefore changes `config_json` alone, never `worker_id` or `client_id`.
   - **Edited in place, not a `0002`:** nothing is deployed, so a second migration would exist only to correct a schema no one has run; `0001` stays the one hand-written file that makes the eleven tables. `tests/test_migrations.py` holds the models to it (`alembic check` compares foreign keys and uniques), and `tests/test_models.py` shows, red first on today's schema, that a run on plan A with another Worker of the same MSP is refused by `fk_test_run_msp_id_connector_id_worker_id_connector`, and a run on plan A naming another connector of the same MSP by `fk_test_run_msp_id_plan_id_connector_id_client_id_test_plan`; the two existing tests that name the replaced key move to the new name.
   - *Rejected:* dropping `test_run.worker_id` and reading the Worker through the plan (C5.6 dispatches and C5.8 reports by `worker_id`, and a run's Worker is a fact of the run that must not move when a connector is re-pointed later); a trigger (a rule in procedural SQL that `alembic check` can't see).

2. **The repository layer, `app/repo/`.** One module per aggregate: `msps.py`, `users.py`, `clients.py`, `workers.py`, `connectors.py`, `plans.py`, `runs.py`, `items.py`, `reports.py`, `audit.py`, `install_tokens.py`, plus `base.py` (`Repo.__init__(self, session: AsyncSession)`, nothing public), `errors.py` (`RepoError`) and `lookup.py` (the exception below). Each is a class over an `AsyncSession`:
   - **Every public method takes `msp_id: UUID` first** and every statement it issues has `.where(Model.msp_id == msp_id)`: `select`, `update` and `delete` alike. A `get` that finds nothing answers `None`, and another MSP's row is "nothing". An `update` or `delete` answers the number of rows it touched (`0` for another MSP's row or an absent one) and never raises for zero. A method takes plain values, never a `select` or a model row from its caller. `list` methods answer in a fixed order (a name, a time, else the id), so a later page is stable; paging itself is the task that needs it.
   - **The repos flush and never commit.** One transaction per request or command is the caller's (`get_session`, the CLI); so "an audit row in the same transaction" is by construction.
   - **The methods of this PR** (the later tasks add theirs): `MspRepo.create(name, retention_days=None)` — the one method in `app/repo/` with no `msp_id`, since it makes the MSP — and `get(msp_id)`; `UserRepo.create/get/list`; `ClientRepo.create(msp_id, name, tenant_id: UUID, screenshots_enabled=False)/get/get_by_tenant/list/update(name, screenshots_enabled)/delete`; `WorkerRepo.create(msp_id, name, public_key_pem, api_token_hash)/get/list/revoke(msp_id, worker_id, at)` (a Worker is revoked, never deleted: its runs are evidence); `ConnectorRepo.create/get/list(msp_id, client_id=None, worker_id=None)/update/delete`; `PlanRepo.create/get/list(msp_id, client_id=None)/set_enabled/delete`; `RunRepo.create(msp_id, plan_id, client_id, connector_id, worker_id)/get/list(msp_id, client_id=None)/set_state` (no delete: retention is C7.3's); `ItemRepo.create/list(msp_id, run_id)`; `ReportRepo.create/get/list`; `AuditRepo.write(msp_id, action, target, user_id=None, ip=None)/list` (append-only: no update, no delete); `InstallTokenRepo.create(msp_id, token_hash, expires_at)/get/list/mark_used(msp_id, token_id, at)`. No `MspRepo.list` and no `UserRepo.find_by_email`: the first is a cross-MSP read for the scheduler (C5.9) and the second the login's lookup before an MSP is known (C6.1); each is that task's to add with its reason.
   - **The one documented exception, `app/repo/lookup.py`:** `Lookup.find_worker_by_token_hash(token_hash)` and `Lookup.find_install_token_by_hash(token_hash)`, the two reads that happen before any MSP is known, over the model's two single-column uniques (`uq_worker_api_token_hash`, `uq_install_token_token_hash`). Each answers the row, which carries its `msp_id`; everything after it goes through a repo with that `msp_id`. A test in `tests/test_tenant_scope.py` walks the AST of every file under `app/repo/` and holds that every public function or method (no leading underscore, `__init__` excluded) has `msp_id` as its first parameter after `self`, annotated `UUID`, but for exactly these three: `Lookup.find_worker_by_token_hash`, `Lookup.find_install_token_by_hash`, `MspRepo.create`.
   - **C5.13's rules that are the repo's.** `ConnectorRepo.create` and `update` validate `config_json` against `shared/schemas/client-profile.v1.json` with `jsonschema`'s `Draft202012Validator` (the file read by path, point 7, as `tests/test_client_profile_schema.py` reads it), then read the client with `msp_id` and require `uuid.UUID(config_json["graph_tenant_id"]) == client.tenant_id` — **parse, then equality**: the schema has already held the string to a GUID's shape, `UUID()` reads either case, and `client.tenant_id` is a `uuid`, so the same GUID in upper and lower case is one tenant, as the Worker compares them. A refusal is `RepoError(key, reason)` with `str()` `"<key>: <reason>"` from fixed words: `config_json: not a client-profile.v1` (never the validator's message, which quotes the document), `graph_tenant_id: not the client's tenant` (never either value), `client_id: no such client` (an absent client and another MSP's client are the same answer). The database's own refusals (a tenant twice in one MSP, a connector twice for one Worker and client, a key into another MSP) stay `IntegrityError` naming their constraint, for the route or the CLI to word (C5.10, C5.13). **Every connector create, update and delete writes one `audit_log` row through `AuditRepo` in the same transaction**: `action` `connector.create|update|delete`, `target` `connector:<id>`, `user_id` and `ip` as the caller gives them (`None` for the CLI); a delete or update that touched no row writes none. Nothing of the profile goes into the audit row.
   - *Rejected:* one generic `Repo[Model]` with `get`/`list`/`delete` for every table (it would hand `AuditRepo` a delete and `RunRepo` a delete for free); methods that take a caller's `select` (the scope is then the caller's again); Postgres row-level security (the 2026-09-22 entry's reason stands; and the two lookups before an MSP is known would need a bypass role).

3. **The lint test, `tests/test_tenant_scope.py`, plain pytest, so CI's existing `uv run --locked pytest` step runs it.** Every `.py` under `app/` except `app/repo/` and `app/migrations/` is held, line by line, against: a bare call `select(`, `update(`, `delete(` or `insert(` not preceded by a `.` or a word character (so a dict's `.update(` passes and SQLAlchemy's constructors don't); the same four qualified as `sqlalchemy.` or `sa.`; `session.execute`, `.get`, `.get_one`, `.add`, `.add_all`, `.delete`, `.merge`, `.scalar`, `.scalars`, `.stream`; and `from sqlalchemy… import` lines that bring any of the four names in. `app/migrations/` is left out on purpose: a migration runs on every MSP's rows by design and never from a request. The test is shown to work by planting `select(` in a router, watching it fail, and removing the plant (the build notes record it), and it holds its own patterns against a short table of allowed and refused lines, and that `app/repo/` itself contains at least one `select(`, so it can't pass by matching nothing. A file under `app/repo/` that forgets `msp_id` in a `where` is not the lint's to catch: that is point 4's.
   - *Rejected:* a flake8 plugin or ruff rule (another tool in CI for one regex); an AST walk for the lint (the names to catch are tokens, and the plant-and-remove check is clearer on text).

4. **The two-MSP isolation test, `tests/test_repo_isolation.py`, on the real test Postgres.** Through the repos themselves, MSP A and MSP B each get one user, client, worker, connector, plan, run with two items, report, audit row and install token. Then a table, parametrised over every repo class and every `get` and `list` method (an inspection of `app.repo` collects the public methods, and the test fails if one is missing from the table, so a method added later must be added here): called with A's `msp_id` and B's ids it answers `None`, `[]` or nothing of B's; with A's `msp_id` and A's ids it answers A's rows and every row's `msp_id` is A's; and the other way round. Every `update`, `delete`, `revoke`, `set_enabled`, `set_state` and `mark_used` called with A's `msp_id` on B's row answers `0` and B's row, read back with B's `msp_id`, is unchanged. The two lookups are held the other way: each finds its row by hash alone and the row carries its own `msp_id`.

5. **C5.4, `app/auth/`:** `tokens.py` and `dependency.py` (and `__init__.py`). **`current_user` (sessions, C6.1) is not here.**
   - **`tokens.py`.** `new_token()` is `secrets.token_bytes(32)` in base64url without padding: 43 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 - _`, two calls never equal. `token_hash(token)` is the SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes as 64 lower-case hex digits; the database holds hashes only. **Install tokens:** `issue_install_token(session, msp_id, now)` makes a token, stores its hash through `InstallTokenRepo.create` with `expires_at = now + 7 days`, and answers the token once (the caller shows it; it is never stored). `accept_install_token(session, token, now)` hashes, finds the row through `Lookup.find_install_token_by_hash`, then `InstallTokenRepo.mark_used(row.msp_id, row.id, now)`, whose `UPDATE … SET used_at = now WHERE msp_id = … AND id = … AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now`; zero rows is a refusal, so an unknown, a used and an expired token are refused alike and **single use holds under two concurrent accepts** (the second `UPDATE` re-reads the row after the first's lock and sees `used_at` set). Expiry is strict: at exactly `created + 7 days` the token is refused, one second before it is accepted; a test holds both edges. **Worker tokens:** stored as their hash on `worker.api_token_hash` (C5.5's registration mints one with `new_token()` and `WorkerRepo.create`); `revoked_at` set to anything blocks use.
   - **`dependency.py`: `current_worker(request, session = Depends(get_session))`.** It reads `Authorization`, takes the token only from `Bearer <token>` with exactly one space and nothing before or after (`Basic …`, two spaces, a missing header and a header of another shape all give no token), hashes what it got (an empty string when there was no token), looks the hash up through `Lookup.find_worker_by_token_hash`, compares the stored and computed hashes with `hmac.compare_digest` (against a fixed string of the same length when no row was found), and refuses when the row is missing, the digests differ or `revoked_at` is not null. **Every failure is one 401**, body `{"detail": "not authenticated"}`, header `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, and every failure runs the same work — one hash, one lookup, one comparison — so a missing header, an unknown token and a revoked Worker have one body and one timing shape; nothing tells a caller "revoked" from "unknown". On success it sets `request.state.worker` and `request.state.msp_id` and returns the Worker row. The lookup by equality already finds the row; the `compare_digest` is the constant-time step the issue asks for over the stored and computed hashes, so a difference in the stored value's bytes can't be timed.
   - **The token never reaches a log line.** By construction (the request line has no header) and by the secret-name rule (`authorization`, `*_token`); and `tests/test_auth.py` sends a request that fails and one that passes through `create_app` with its log stream captured and finds neither the bearer value nor its hash in any line.
   - **Tests.** `tests/test_tokens.py`: the shape (43 characters, the alphabet, no `=`), the hash (SHA-256 hex of a known string), two creations never equal, expiry at exactly seven days and a second before, single use (a second accept answers nothing and `used_at` is unchanged), an unknown token. `tests/test_auth.py`: a probe route under `/v1` added to the `workers` router for the test (as `tests/test_app.py` adds its wiring probe) guarded by `Depends(current_worker)`, with `get_session` overridden to the test's own session so the Worker rows the test made are the ones the dependency sees: no header, `Basic`, `Bearer` with two spaces, a token of the right shape that is unknown, a revoked Worker's token, a valid one; the five refusals' status, body and `WWW-Authenticate` compared for equality with each other; the valid one answering 200 with the Worker's id and `msp_id` from `request.state`; and the log assertion.
   - *Rejected:* refusing a malformed header before the lookup (a different timing shape for one of the three); a 403 for a revoked Worker (it names the case); JWTs for Workers (a random token looked up by hash can be revoked at once; a signed token can't without a list); storing the token's bcrypt (the token is 256 random bits, so a fast hash is right and lets the lookup be by index).

6. **Coverage.** `app/repo` and `app/auth` are two of `tools/check_coverage.py`'s three guarded paths and must be at 100% line and branch; this is the first PR where the gate measures anything (every guarded path printed `SKIP` until now). So every branch of both needs a test: every `None` from a `get`, every zero rowcount, every `RepoError`, both sides of the header parse, the missing row and the revoked row. The 80% combined gate on `app/` stays; both commands of `cloud/Makefile`'s `cov` are run and their numbers go into the build notes.

7. **The image carries `shared/schemas/`, and the app finds it as the tests do.** The repo layer reads `client-profile.v1.json` by path at run time, so the file must be in the container. `cloud/docker-compose.yml` builds with the repository root as context (`context: ..`, `dockerfile: cloud/Dockerfile`), the Dockerfile copies `cloud/pyproject.toml`, `cloud/uv.lock`, `cloud/alembic.ini`, `cloud/app` to `/srv/` as before and `shared/schemas` to `/srv/shared/schemas`, and `cloud/.dockerignore` becomes a `.dockerignore` at the repository root allowing those five paths and nothing else (so no evidence file, fixture or `.env` can reach the image). `app/schemas.py` has `shared_schemas_dir()`: the first `shared/schemas` found walking up from `app/`, which is `<repo>/shared/schemas` in the tree and `/srv/shared/schemas` in the image, and `load_schema(name)`; a missing folder is a `FileNotFoundError` naming `shared/schemas` and no path. `jsonschema` moves from the dev group to the runtime dependencies (`uv.lock` changes). The CI `compose` job runs `docker compose up` from `cloud/` and so builds with the new context unchanged; the local Done-when of C5.1 (`/healthz` 200 on `--build`) is run again as this change's evidence.
   - *Rejected:* a copy of the schema under `cloud/` (the schemas in `shared/schemas/` are the only copies, by the Signing contract); a `SCHEMAS_DIR` setting (a path that is wrong only in production, found the first time a connector is made); embedding the schema into a Python module at build time (the Worker embeds at build because it ships as one exe; the Cloud ships as an image with a file system).

**Open, left to the tasks named.**

- C5.5: minting the Worker token at registration and answering it once; `409` on a public key already registered; what `install_token` carries beyond the hash (a name, a client?), which the model lacks.
- C5.6: `RunRepo` methods for dispatch (`dispatched_at`, the attempt count, the poll's index on `(msp_id, worker_id, state)`), all through the repo.
- C5.9: `MspRepo.list`, the one read across MSPs the scheduler needs, with its own entry line. C6.1: `UserRepo.find_by_email`, the login's lookup before an MSP is known, which would be a third method in `lookup.py`.
- C5.10: wording the database's `IntegrityError`s for the CLI. C5.13: the route-level 409s and the CLI's `create-connector --profile-file`, both over `ConnectorRepo`.
- C5.12: the image pinned by digest, and whether the root `.dockerignore` stays once there is a second image to build.
- Paging of the `list` methods, when a dashboard needs it (C6.2).

**Done-when, as it will be run.** With the Compose Postgres up, from `cloud/`: `uv run --locked pytest`, in which `tests/test_repo_isolation.py` (the scope test) and `tests/test_tenant_scope.py` (the lint, run by CI's existing test step, with the plant-and-remove recorded in the build notes) pass; `tests/test_auth.py` shows a revoked Worker's token answered 401 and a valid one 200 on the probe route. Then the two coverage commands of `cloud/Makefile`'s `cov` with `app/repo` and `app/auth` at 100/100, `docker compose up -d --wait --build` with `/healthz` 200 on the image built from the new context, and the real numbers in the PR.

## 2026-10-10 — C5.1 and C5.2 code review: findings 1, 2 and 4 to 15 of fifteen fixed, 3 open for the owner (proposed)

The review of the branch `c5.1-c5.2-cloud-stack` against `main` gave fifteen findings. Fourteen are fixed, each with its test written first and seen to fail on the code as it was; 3 is a choice about the schema and stays with the owner. Nothing is committed until the owner asks.

1. **A library's log line is its first line only, and a failed lifespan is logged by type and frames.** Only `exc_info` lost its message; a message that *is* a traceback passed. Starlette sends a failed startup or shutdown as `traceback.format_exc()` and uvicorn logs what it is sent; asyncio's "Task exception was never retrieved" has the exception's repr on its second line. `RequestLogMiddleware` now takes the `lifespan` scope: it puts `the app's startup failed` or `the app's shutdown failed` in the text's place and writes `lifespan failed` with `exc_type` and `stack`. And `first_line_only` cuts every standard-library record at its first line break. Tests run uvicorn's own `LifespanOn` and asyncio's own handler. Rejected: scrubbing by pattern, since a message can hold anything. Not covered: a library that puts an exception's text on the first line of its message.
2. **`audit_log.ip` is read back as the text it was given.** asyncpg answers an `inet` with an `ipaddress` object while the model says `str`. `InetText` (a `TypeDecorator` over `INET`, beside `UtcDateTime`) makes the model's word true under any engine. Rejected: `native_inet_types=False`, which is per engine (the app's, the tests', the migration's) and so easy to hold on two of three. The column is still `inet`; the migration is unchanged.
3. **Open: `test_run.worker_id` is held only to a Worker of the same MSP**, not to the Worker of the plan's connector. To settle before C5.6 dispatches by it: drop the column, or key `(msp_id, connector_id, worker_id)` to `connector`. Either changes migration `0001`, so it is the owner's.
4. **/healthz asks through an S3 client of its own.** The 2 s limits and the single attempt were on the app's one client, which C5.7's put and get will use. `make_s3_client(settings, for_check=True)` is the probe's; the data client keeps botocore's limits and its standard retries. `Storage.check_client`.
5. **`uv run mutmut run` finds `alembic.ini`.** `also_copy` names it; a test holds that. Not run: mutmut needs `fork()` and this laptop's WSL has Docker's distribution only. The Makefile's and `docs/testing.md`'s "exits 1 until app/ has functions" notes are gone.
6. **`LOG_LEVEL` reaches uvicorn's lines and the migration's.** uvicorn gives `uvicorn.error` a level of its own before it calls the factory; `configure_logging` sets it. `env.py` reads `log_level_from_environment()` in place of a fixed `info`, and refuses a word that is no level before it connects.
7. **The wiring probe's teardown takes away the probe alone**, not every route of the module's router.
8. **The app and a migration read one environment the same way.** `_settings_in` is the one lookup: names in any case, an empty value a missing one. `database_url_from_environment` took the first match, even an empty one.
9. **`test_the_checks_run_side_by_side` fails for a route that awaits one check after the other.** Both checks are slow and the answer must take as long as one. Seen to fail with `gather` taken out.
10. **The Compose healthcheck asks Postgres over TCP** (`pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1`): on a fresh volume the image's first server listens on its unix socket alone. The same in `cloud.yml`'s service. Shown by `docker compose -p rpfresh up -d --wait --build` on new volumes: every service healthy, `/healthz` 200.
11. **`LOG_LEVEL=INFO` is `info`.** The value is lower-cased before it is held to the four words; `WARN` is still not one of them.
12. **The command-line test searches what all four runs printed** for the URL's password, its database and its driver, not the last run's alone.
13. **`HEAD /healthz` answers as `GET` does.**
14. **`alembic check` compares server defaults** (`compare_server_default=True`); a test plants one and the check finds it. No false difference on the migrated database.
15. **The three bare `IntegrityError`s name their constraint.** Doing so showed that "filed under B, with A's worker and client" was refused by `uq_connector_worker_id_client_id` and never reached a key; the test now uses a pair with no connector yet. A delete is held to a key that points at the table deleted from.

Runs (local, 2026-10-10; no CI): `uv run --locked pytest` 1181 passed (101 on the Compose Postgres), coverage 99.49% combined with `app/logging.py`, `settings.py`, `storage.py`, `health.py` and `models.py` at 100%.

## 2026-10-10 — C5.1 and C5.2 build notes: built as the entry says but for MinIO's image, a time without a zone, two nullable columns and the libraries' log level; both Done-whens shown on the Compose stack; green locally, not in CI (proposed)

The owner approved the entry below as written on 2026-10-10 and gave the go-ahead to start Docker Desktop. These notes say where the build left the entry or went beyond it. The points marked **against the entry** are the ones to read.

1. **MinIO's own images don't pull at all (against the entry's point 8 and its Open list).** The entry expected to pin `minio/minio` and `minio/mc` to an existing release. `docker.io/minio/minio`, `docker.io/minio/mc` and both on `quay.io` answer "pull access denied" or 401 for every tag, `latest` included. The local stack uses Chainguard's builds of the same programs, `cgr.dev/chainguard/minio` (MinIO `RELEASE.2026-09-22T19-25-18Z`) and `cgr.dev/chainguard/minio-client`, **pinned by digest**, since their free tier has the `latest` tag only. What that changed in `docker-compose.yml`: the images carry no `/bin/sh`, so the bucket maker is `mc mb --ignore-existing local/restoreproof` with the alias given as `MC_HOST_local` (no shell line), and MinIO's health check asks its own `/minio/health/ready` with bash's `/dev/tcp` (no curl in the image); MinIO runs as root in the local stack, because the image's user can't write a fresh named volume. It is still MinIO, so the 2026-09-22 entry "Local stack: Postgres 16 and MinIO" stands. The app knows nothing of this: it talks S3. Open for C5.12, which may replace MinIO by a real bucket anyway.
2. **asyncpg does not refuse a time without a zone (against point 4).** The entry said "a naive one is refused by the driver (a test holds that)". The test was written and failed: asyncpg takes a naive `datetime` for a `timestamptz` column and reads it as the local time of the machine the app runs on. So the model refuses it instead: `app.models.UtcDateTime`, a `TypeDecorator` over `DateTime(timezone=True)` that raises `ValueError` for a value without an offset before the driver sees it; every time column is one, and a test holds that no bare `DateTime` is left. The migration is unchanged by it (`timestamptz`).
3. **`test_item.found` and `match` are nullable (against point 4's list).** The entry listed `found_sha256`, `expected_sha256` and `reason` as `test_item`'s nullable columns and said the rest is NOT NULL. A result's unchecked item (the check's outcome `error`) has no answer to "was it found" or "did it match", and the entry's own rule for the three `_ok` columns is that null is "not known", never false. So `found`, `match` and `ms` are nullable too.
4. **Every library but our own is held to warnings, whatever `LOG_LEVEL` is (beyond point 7).** The logging test caught it: httpx logs each request's URL, query string included, at `info`, through the root logger. botocore logs its signed requests at `debug`. So `LOG_LEVEL` sets the level of `app`, `uvicorn` and `alembic` alone, and the root logger stays at `warning`. uvicorn's handlers, which it installs before it calls the factory, are cleared so its lines go through the JSON formatter, and `uvicorn.access` is disabled as well as switched off on the command line.
5. **The secret-name rule's words.** A key is a secret's name when it contains `secret` or `password`, or ends in `token`, `authorization`, `cookie`, `api_key`, `access_key` or `private_key` (`-` read as `_`, any case). The entry's list would have missed `S3_SECRET_KEY`. A name that only starts like one (`token_count`) is not one.
6. **FastAPI 0.143 has a route at the root the entry didn't know of,** `/docs/oauth2-redirect`; it is off (`swagger_ui_oauth2_redirect_url=None`), which the "every route under `/v1` but `/healthz`" test found. In this FastAPI an included router is one entry of `app.routes` and stays live, so that test holds the factory's own routes by their paths and the seven included routers by which they are, and a second test adds a probe route to each of the six routers and requires it at `/v1/...` and nowhere else.
7. **A migration run from the command line logs in the app's form.** `env.py` calls `configure_logging` when the URL comes from the environment, so the api container's log shows `Running upgrade  -> 0001` as a JSON line before uvicorn's. With `--reload` (the local stack only) uvicorn's reloader process prints three plain lines before the app is loaded; the image's own command, without reload, logs JSON only, which a run of the bare image showed.
8. **Small things the entry didn't name:** `database_url_from_environment()` in `app/settings.py` (the migration's one setting, held to the same shape and the same names-only fault); `app/migrations/script.py.mako`; `cloud/docker/postgres-init/01-test-database.sql` (a `.sql`, so no line-ending trouble); `build: .` on the scheduler too, or Compose tries to pull the image; the `Makefile`'s `db`, `up` and `down`; `.gitignore` gained `!.env.example`, which `.env.*` was hiding; `alembic.ini`'s `path_separator = os`; the test role must be allowed to create a database (the migration tests make their own). `report` got no CHECK that its period's end isn't before its start: not in the entry, left to C6.4.
9. **Red before green, with one exception.** The logging, `/healthz`, app, migration and model tests were each run and seen failing before their code was written. The settings test was written first but its first run was already with `app/settings.py` in place, so it was never seen red.
10. **What the tests found beyond the above:** nothing else in the model. `alembic check` passes with the functional index `uq_user_email_lower`, and a planted table makes it fail, so the check is not vacuous.
